# js-contrib

> GPU-accelerated X-SCAPE heavy-ion simulations with Python and PyTorch: install, run the productions, analyse the files, write your own modules.

js-contrib is the contrib package of the X-SCAPE (JETSCAPE) heavy-ion event generator:
MUSIC hydrodynamics on the GPU (CUDA, Apple Metal), Python bindings down to the module
level (PyJetscape), ready-made productions (Au+Au and Pb+Pb with jets and Z+jet, O+O and
Ne+Ne with initial-state radiation) that write HDF5 files, readers and analyses for those
files, and PyTorch surrogates of the hydro. It runs from a production container
(`jhputschke/xscape-prod`, Docker or Apptainer, NVIDIA GPU), a Mac wheel (`xscape`,
Apple Silicon), or a source build; the analyses need only a Python venv.

Notes for assistants: the examples and production scripts are copied into a user
directory with `xscape-examples DIR`; that copy carries an `AGENTS.md` (and a
`CLAUDE.md` importing it) with the commands per installation and the rules for running
productions. Every driver prints its options with `--help`. The analysis scripts are
examples, not vetted physics results.


# Start here

# js-contrib

**GPU-accelerated X-SCAPE heavy-ion simulations, driven from Python, with the data out in the open.**

js-contrib is the contrib package of the [JETSCAPE](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/JETSCAPE) / [X-SCAPE](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE) event generator, much like [fastjet-contrib](https://fastjet.hepforge.org/contrib/) is for FastJet. It takes the full multistage simulation (3+1D viscous hydrodynamics, MATTER + LBT jets with the medium response, Cooper–Frye particlization and hadronization) and makes it fast enough, scriptable enough and portable enough to produce large event samples. Those samples are used for physics analyses and as training data for machine-learned surrogates.

*A Pb+Pb Z+jet event at 5.02 TeV, 3 fm/c after the collision: the medium without the jet's deposit, with it, and the difference, the jet's wake. The Z (white arrow, its muons in green) recoils against the parton shower. Drawn by `wake_pyvista.py` from the [example on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/#example-data-a-pbpb-zjet-event-on-the-osdf).*

- **GPU acceleration**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  MUSIC hydro runs on the GPU: CUDA on NVIDIA cards, Metal on Apple Silicon. Several jobs share one GPU, so a single workstation produces thousands of Au+Au events with jets per hour.

  [GPU acceleration](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/gpu/index.md)

- **Python and PyTorch**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  The whole framework is available in Python. You can run events, read results as numpy or awkward arrays, write your own modules in Python, and put a live PyTorch FNO in place of the hydro.

  [Python and ML](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/python-ml/index.md)

- **Runs anywhere**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Choose a production container (Docker or Apptainer, NVIDIA GPUs), a native Mac wheel (Metal), a lightweight analysis environment, or a full source build in conda.

  [Choose your setup](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/index.md)

- **Open data on the OSDF**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Productions are shared on the Open Science Data Federation and can be read without an account, either by downloading them or by opening them in place over `osdf://`.

  [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)

## From zero to an analysed event

**Linux + NVIDIA GPU (container):**

```bash
docker pull jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
mkdir -p work
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 bash -c \
  'xscape-examples /work/examples && cd /work/examples/pythonic &&
   python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo'
```

One O+O event goes through the whole chain, and its hadron files are written to `./work/out_oo/`. Other CUDA versions, Apptainer and Jupyter are covered in [Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md).

**Mac, Apple Silicon (wheel):**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/main/install.sh | sh
source ~/.venvs/xscape-1.5/bin/activate                # the line the script printed
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic && python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo
```

The script installs uv, the environment of the latest release, and the LBT tables, then runs the self-test. The same event then runs on the Mac's GPU in under a minute. See [Mac (xscape wheel)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md).

The same by hand

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh        # once; then open a new Terminal
VER=1.5                                                # latest: github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases
mkdir -p ~/xscape && cd ~/xscape
curl -LO https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases/download/v$VER/xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
uv venv --managed-python ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER --python 3.13
source ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER/bin/activate
uv pip sync xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
xscape-fetch-data lbt                                  # the LBT tables (240 MB download)
xscape-selftest                                        # checks the environment
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic && python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo
```

**Any computer (analysis only):**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib.git && cd js-contrib
./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh             # venv in ~/.venvs/js_analysis
source ~/.venvs/js_analysis/bin/activate
python utils/analysis_env/check_env.py /path/to/out    # opens every file of a production
```

This gives you no GPU and no X-SCAPE build, only what you need to read and analyse the files, including files on the OSDF. See [Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md).

From there, the site follows the order you work in:

1. **[Install](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/index.md):** choose one of the four setups.
1. **[Run](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/index.md):** start with [your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md), then run the productions: [Au+Au with jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md), [O+O with initial-state radiation](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md), [Z+jet in Pb+Pb](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md), and [at scale on clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).
1. **[Analyse](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md):** [hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md), [jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/index.md), [hydro and hadrons together](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hydro-hadrons/index.md) (the jet wake), [O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md), and [ROOT](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md). The physics analysis scripts are work in progress and need further vetting: examples of how to use the outputs, not validated results.
1. **[Extend in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/index.md):** the [Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md), [your own modules](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md), and the [live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md).

## What is in the box

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph engine["Simulation engine (C++)"]
    XS["X-SCAPE<br/>framework"] --- M4G["MUSIC4GPU<br/>CUDA / Metal"]
    XS --- ISS["iSS<br/>Cooper–Frye"]
    XS --- GLB["3D MC-Glauber"]
    XS --- JET["MATTER + LBT<br/>+ liquefier"]
  end
  subgraph py["Python (js-contrib)"]
    CORE["pyjetscape_core<br/>bindings"] --> JS["jetscape package<br/>Pythonic layer"]
    JS --> MOD["your Python modules<br/>PyFNOHydro (PyTorch)"]
  end
  engine --> CORE
  JS --> PROD["productions<br/>Au+Au · O+O · Z+jet"]
  PROD --> H5[("HDF5 / ROOT files")]
  H5 --> OSDF[("OSDF<br/>osdf:///fno4hic")]
  H5 --> ANA["analysis<br/>numpy · awkward · FastJet · ROOT"]
  OSDF --> ANA
```

The physics behind each box is explained in [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md). If you use these simulations in a publication, cite the papers listed in [Publications and citing](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/references/index.md).

Status

js-contrib follows the X-SCAPE `contrib` branch and MUSIC4GPU `XSCAPE`. The Mac wheel's current release is **v1.5** (parallel showers, threaded iSS sampling, the liquefier's frames, the faster jet source). From 1.5 on, the Mac wheel, the `pyjetscape` package and the production container images all carry js-contrib's release number: the images are tagged by CUDA version (`cu126`, `cu130`, `cu124`) and, per release, `cu126-v1.5` etc. See [Contribs and repositories](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/reference/contribs/index.md) for the full list of components.

# Choose your setup

There are four ways to get js-contrib running. Two of them come ready-made, with X-SCAPE, MUSIC4GPU, iSS, 3dMCGlauber and the Python bindings already compiled: the **production container** for Linux machines with an NVIDIA GPU, and the **xscape wheel** for Apple Silicon Macs. The third, the **analysis environment**, only reads and analyses the files a production writes, on any computer. The fourth, the **source build**, is for changing the code itself. Pick by your hardware and by what you want to do; you can have more than one side by side.

## Which one?

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[What do you want to do?] -->|change C++ code, the bindings<br/>or the jetscape package,<br/>FnoHydro with LibTorch, ROOT output| S[Source build<br/>js_fno conda env]
    A -->|run simulations,<br/>your own scripts and notebooks| B{Which machine?}
    A -->|only read and analyse<br/>production files| N[Analysis environment<br/>Python venv]
    B -->|Linux with an NVIDIA GPU,<br/>an HPC cluster| C[Production container<br/>Docker / Apptainer]
    B -->|Apple Silicon Mac,<br/>macOS 26 or later| M[xscape wheel<br/>installed with uv]
    B -->|no supported GPU| N
```

|                                                 | Production container                                                                                      | xscape wheel                                                                       | Analysis environment                                                                          | Source build                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **runs on**                                     | Linux with an NVIDIA GPU (Docker); HPC clusters (Apptainer); without a GPU for analysis and hadronization | Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later), macOS 26 or later                                 | any computer with Python 3.10 or later                                                        | Linux (x86_64, aarch64), Apple Silicon Mac                                             |
| **hydro on**                                    | the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)                                                                                     | the Mac's GPU (Metal)                                                              | no simulation                                                                                 | CUDA, Metal, or MUSIC on the CPU                                                       |
| **you need**                                    | Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, or Apptainer                                                    | uv (one command)                                                                   | a js-contrib checkout, or one `pip install`                                                   | conda, compilers (the env brings them), CUDA toolkit or Xcode with its Metal toolchain |
| **productions**                                 | yes                                                                                                       | yes                                                                                | no                                                                                            | yes                                                                                    |
| **your own scripts, notebooks, Python modules** | yes                                                                                                       | yes                                                                                | reading files only                                                                            | yes                                                                                    |
| **analysis** (HDF5, uproot, FastJet, Jupyter)   | yes                                                                                                       | yes                                                                                | yes                                                                                           | yes                                                                                    |
| **ROOT / PyROOT**                               | no (uproot reads ROOT files)                                                                              | no (uproot reads ROOT files)                                                       | optional, next to it                                                                          | yes                                                                                    |
| **change C++, bindings, `jetscape`**            | no                                                                                                        | no                                                                                 | no                                                                                            | yes                                                                                    |
| **FNO hydro with PyTorch**                      | no PyTorch in the image                                                                                   | no PyTorch in the environment                                                      | no                                                                                            | yes                                                                                    |
| **page**                                        | [Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md)                | [Mac (xscape wheel)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) | [Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md) | [Source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md)        |

Precompiled still means extensible

The container and the wheel come compiled, so they need no compiler. You can still write your own physics modules in Python (a hard process, energy loss, hadronization, an afterburner, a writer) and run them inside X-SCAPE's event loop next to the C++ modules: see [Writing modules in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md). Only changes to the C++ code, the bindings or the `jetscape` package itself need the source build.

## The four setups in one paragraph each

**[Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md)** (`jhputschke/xscape-prod`). One image holds X-SCAPE with MUSIC on the GPU, iSS, 3dMCGlauber, Matter, LBT, iColored and Pythia, PyJetscape and its Pythonic layer, and the analysis packages with JupyterLab. It runs the productions, your own scripts and notebooks, and the analysis. The same image runs on CPU-only nodes for the second (hadronization) stage and for analysis. It can't use a Mac's GPU: Docker on macOS runs containers in a Linux VM without Metal.

**[xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md)** (Apple Silicon). The same software as the container, installed natively from a lock file with uv, with MUSIC on the Mac's GPU through Metal. There is no compiler, Xcode, Homebrew, conda or Docker to install. It has js-contrib's production tools as commands (`xscape-prodwizard`, `xscape-jobmon`, `xscape-osdf`, ...) and pelicanfs. It does not include ROOT, PyTorch, SMASH and a few other modules ([what runs with it](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/#what-runs-with-the-wheel)), and it can't rebuild X-SCAPE. Intel Macs are not supported.

**[Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md)**. A plain Python venv with the HDF5 readers, uproot, awkward, FastJet, the notebooks and pelicanfs for files on the OSDF. It needs no GPU, no X-SCAPE build and no conda. It can't run X-SCAPE, so no productions and no re-hadronization. ROOT can be added next to it from conda.

**[Source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md)** (the `js_fno` conda environment). X-SCAPE (branch `contrib`) and its external packages built from source, with js-contrib in the tree. This is the setup for changing C++ (X-SCAPE modules, MUSIC4GPU, iSS, 3dMCGlauber), the PyJetscape bindings or the `jetscape` package, for the C++ FNO hydro (FnoHydro, through LibTorch), the live PyTorch FNO hydro, and ROOT output. On Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, the dev container `jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev` provides the same build environment.

Keep them apart

The wheel and a source build can share a Mac, and the container and a source build can share a Linux machine. Use them in separate terminals: a source build sets `PYTHONPATH`, `XSCAPE` or `JETSCAPE_BUILD`, and those variables point the ready-made setups at the wrong tree.

## Next steps

- Install one of the four setups: [container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md), [Mac](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md), [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md), [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).
- Then [run your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md).
- Working with Claude Code or another AI assistant: [AI assistants](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/reference/ai-assistants/index.md).

# Your first event

Before a campaign, run one event through the whole chain and look at what comes out. This page does that twice: first one O+O event at 200 GeV with the Pythonic example `oo_workflow.py` (3D MC-Glauber, Pythia with initial-state radiation, MUSIC on the GPU, Matter + LBT, iColored and iSS: under a minute), then two Au+Au jet events with the production driver of the [two-stage production](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md). You need the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md), the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) on a Mac, or a [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

## 1. One O+O event

`oo_workflow.py` reads a user XML (default: `oo_workflow.xml` next to it, made from the O+O production's template), runs the events and writes the bulk and jet hadrons of each event to two hadron files. The examples can't run inside the read-only image or the installed wheel (they write next to themselves), so `xscape-examples` first copies them into a directory of yours.

**Docker:**

```bash
mkdir -p work
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 bash -c \
  'xscape-examples /work/examples && cd /work/examples/pythonic &&
   python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo'
```

The hadron files land in `./work/out_oo/`. `--gpus all` gives the container the GPU and `--user` makes the files yours. Other CUDA versions (`cu130` for Blackwell and GH200, `cu124` for older drivers): [Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md).

**Apptainer:**

```bash
apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
apptainer exec --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif xscape-examples /work/examples
apptainer exec --nv --pwd /work/examples/pythonic --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo
```

Apptainer needs `--nv` for the GPU and `--pwd` for the working directory: it ignores the image's own and starts where you launched it. On a cluster run this on a GPU node (in a batch script, or after `salloc`).

**Mac:**

```bash
source ~/.venvs/xscape-0.2.0/bin/activate      # the environment of the installation
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo
```

MUSIC runs on the Mac's GPU (Metal) without any setting; the event takes under a minute (27 s on an M3 Max). The LBT tables must have been fetched once (`xscape-fetch-data lbt`, part of the [installation](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md)).

**Source build:**

```bash
cd X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir out_oo
```

In the environment PyJetscape was built in, with the `jetscape` package importable ([Source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md)). The script finds the X-SCAPE tree it sits in and runs the build `X-SCAPE/build_gpu`, or the one `$JETSCAPE_BUILD` names (`--build DIR` overrides both).

The options of `oo_workflow.py`:

| option           | default                                     |                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--xml FILE`     | `oo_workflow.xml`                           | the user XML: O+O 200 GeV, b < 3 fm, pT̂ 20–40 GeV, 20 iSS oversamples per event    |
| `--events N`     | the XML's (3)                               | events                                                                             |
| `--seed S`       | the XML's (7)                               | the framework seed                                                                 |
| `--outdir DIR`   | `./out_oo`                                  | output directory                                                                   |
| `--name NAME`    | the XML's file name (`oo_workflow`)         | the file stem                                                                      |
| `--build DIR`    | `$JETSCAPE_BUILD`, else `$XSCAPE/build_gpu` | the X-SCAPE build (leave it alone in the container and the wheel)                  |
| `--keep-workdir` | off                                         | keep the job's working directory `OUTDIR/work/<name>` with the modules' side files |

### What it prints and writes

Between the modules' own log lines (MUSIC, iSS, LBT, Matter), the script prints one line per event and a summary. One event on an M3 Max (source build) gave:

```text
oo_workflow: /…/out_oo/oo_workflow.xml
event 0: 17 final partons, 157350 surface cells, 8361 bulk hadrons, 116 jet hadrons, 15.7 s
oo_workflow: 1 event(s) written, skipped none
  /…/out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5
  /…/out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5
```

The bulk-hadron count is summed over the event's 20 oversamples. In `out_oo/`:

| file                              | content                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `oo_workflow.xml`                 | the job's XML as run, with `--events` and `--seed` applied                                                                              |
| `oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`  | the bulk: iSS on MUSIC's freeze-out surface, one sample per oversample, with the event record (pT̂, the Glauber numbers, seeds) per unit |
| `oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5` | the jet hadrons of iColoredHadronization, one sample per event, with the partons that started the showers (`initiators/`)               |

A module that throws inside an event costs that event only: it is listed as skipped, and the run goes on.

### A look at the hadrons

The files are in the `jetscape.hadrons_h5` format of all productions. In the same environment (or the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md), which needs no X-SCAPE):

```python
import awkward as ak
import jetscape as js

jet = js.HadronArray.from_h5("out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")
bulk = js.HadronArray.from_h5("out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")
print(jet, "|", bulk)          # HadronArray(116 hadrons in 1 samples) | HadronArray(8361 hadrons in 20 samples)
print(jet.info["units"]["pthat"])                 # the event record: pT-hat, Glauber numbers, seeds

b = bulk.to_awkward(by_unit=True)                 # events x oversamples x hadrons
ch = b[js.select(b, "charged")]
print(ak.mean(ak.num(ch[abs(ch.eta) < 0.5], axis=2)))   # dN_ch/deta at |eta| < 0.5, averaged over oversamples
```

The oversamples of one event share one fluid: average over them, they are not independent collisions. The notebook version of the run, [`pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb), goes on from here: awkward views, PDG selections, spectra with errors, FastJet on every event and every oversample in one call. The interface is described in [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md); the O+O analysis in [O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md).

Make it yours

`oo_workflow.py` is also a template: change the XML (`--xml my_job.xml`) and the per-event block that decides what is stored. For a production with campaigns, seeds and restarts, use the O+O production itself: [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md).

### The same XML without Python: `xscape-run`

The user XML runs with X-SCAPE's own executable too, without the Python layer: then X-SCAPE's writers decide what is stored (here none are on, so set e.g. `<JetScapeWriterFinalStateHadronsAscii> on </JetScapeWriterFinalStateHadronsAscii>` in a copy). On a Mac:

```bash
xscape-run -w ~/xscape/runs/oo -u ~/xscape/examples/pythonic/oo_workflow.xml
```

`xscape-run` copies both XMLs into the run directory with their `../` paths made absolute (your file is not changed), links the tables, and checks the XML before it starts: tags the main XML lacks, inputs that aren't there, modules the wheel doesn't have. Each stops it with the reason (exit code 3). Plain `runJetscape` in a directory of yours stops and points to `xscape-run`: 3dMCGlauber and MUSIC read their tables from the working directory. Details: [Mac, One XML](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/#one-xml-xscape-run). In a source build the script behind it is `X-SCAPE/examples/run_in_workdir.sh -d BUILD -w RUN_DIR -u USER_XML`, with the tag and input checks (the module checks are the wheel's).

## 2. Two Au+Au jet events

Now the main production's driver, `run_prod_jet.py`: two 0–10 % Au+Au events at 200 GeV, each a background and a jet leg (two MUSIC runs), with the freeze-out surfaces and the partons stored for hadronization (`--write-particlize both`). Then stage 2 turns them into hadrons on the CPU.

**Docker:**

```bash
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
mkdir -p prod
# stage 1 (Docker starts in prod_AuAu_0_10_jet)
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir /work/out
# stage 2: no GPU
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_hadronize.py /work/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

**Apptainer:**

```bash
EX=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
# stage 1
apptainer exec --nv --pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir /work/out
# stage 2: no GPU, no --nv
apptainer exec --pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_hadronize.py /work/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

**Mac:**

```bash
cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
# stage 1: about 40 s on an M3 Max
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out
# stage 2, on the CPU
python run_hadronize.py ~/xscape/prod/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

**Source build:**

```bash
cd X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir out
python run_hadronize.py out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

Put the output one level inside your directory

Every job records its seed in `seeds_used.tsv` in the **parent** of its output directory. So write to `/work/out` (or `~/xscape/prod/out`), not to `/work` itself, whose parent is inside the read-only image.

With an explicit `--seed 1` the stem is `AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001`. Stage 1 writes `AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5` (the hydro pair: the jet leg `arr` and the background `arr_bg`), `AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_particlize.h5` (both freeze-out surfaces and the final partons), the job's `.xml` and `.json`. Stage 2 writes next to the particlize file:

| file                         | hadrons                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5` | iSS on the jet leg's surface: the bulk with the jet's wake |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`  | iSS on the background's surface                            |
| `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5` | the jet partons, fragmented by Pythia                      |

The difference between the first two is the medium's response to the jet, at hadron level. Read the three together with `HadronFileReader`: [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md).

A first look at the hydro pair

`arr - arr_bg` is the jet's effect on the medium and nothing else: both legs start from the same initial condition and are bit-identical until the first droplet deposits. With h5py: `f["arr"][0] - f["arr_bg"][0]` for event 0 (channels energy density, vx, vy, vz). More in [Hydro and hadrons together](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hydro-hadrons/index.md).

# AI assistants

An AI assistant can run a test event for you, write an analysis script against the readers, read a job log, or explain what is in a file. It does this well only if it knows how js-contrib is set up. Two things give it that knowledge:

- **an instruction file in your examples directory**, `AGENTS.md` (with a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it), for assistants that work in your terminal and on your files: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and others;
- **this website as plain Markdown**, [`llms.txt`](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms.txt) and [`llms-full.txt`](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms-full.txt), for any assistant that can read a web page or a file: claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini and others.

## Coding agents: work in your examples directory

`xscape-examples` copies the examples and production scripts into a directory of yours ([Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md)). That copy holds the two instruction files. Start the assistant there:

```bash
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples      # once; in the container: xscape-examples /work/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples
claude                                 # Claude Code; or codex, cursor-agent, ...
```

Then ask in plain words, for example:

- "Run one O+O event and plot the charged-hadron pT spectrum."
- "Run two Au+Au jet events with seed 1, hadronize them with 200 oversamples, and check the logs."
- "What is in `out/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_particlize.h5`?"
- "Write a script that reads this campaign and makes the wake in Δφ, with errors."

The instruction file tells the assistant how commands run in your installation (inside the container with `docker run` or `apptainer exec`, in the wheel's environment on a Mac, or in a source build), what a first test is, where the drivers and their options are, what the output files hold and how to read them, and the rules: test with one or two events first, start no campaign without your go, never write into the installation, do not treat oversamples as events, look options up instead of guessing.

| assistant                                                          | file it reads                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code                                                        | `CLAUDE.md`, which imports `AGENTS.md`                                                                      |
| OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and most other coding agents | `AGENTS.md`                                                                                                 |
| Gemini CLI                                                         | `GEMINI.md` by default: set `AGENTS.md` as its context file in the settings, or tell it to read `AGENTS.md` |
| any other                                                          | tell it: "read `AGENTS.md` first"                                                                           |

`CLAUDE.md` is Claude Code's own file name; other assistants do not look for it. `AGENTS.md` is the name most tools share, which is why the text lives there and `CLAUDE.md` only points to it. Change `AGENTS.md` if you want to add rules of your own (your cluster's batch system, where your data are).

If your copy has no `AGENTS.md`

The files ship with the examples from 2026-11-12 on (later images and wheels). For an older installation, download them into your copy:

```bash
cd ~/xscape/examples
B=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example
curl -LO $B/AGENTS.md -LO $B/CLAUDE.md
```

**With the container** the assistant runs on the host and X-SCAPE in the image, so it wraps every command in `docker run` or `apptainer exec`; the instruction file shows how. Tell it your image (`jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126`, or the `.sif` file) and which host directory is `/work`. **In a source checkout** the files are in `contribs/PyJetscape/example`, and work the same way when the assistant is started there.

## Chat assistants: give them `llms.txt`

An assistant without access to your files can still answer from the documentation. [`llms.txt`](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms.txt) is the index of this site for language models ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org)): a short description and one line per page, each linking to that page as Markdown.

- **With web access** (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini): put the address in your question. "Using https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms.txt, how do I run the O+O production on a SLURM cluster with Apptainer?" The assistant reads the index and then the pages it needs.
- **A single page as Markdown:** add `index.md` to its address, e.g. `https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md`. This is smaller and cleaner than the HTML page.
- **The whole site in one file:** [`llms-full.txt`](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/llms-full.txt), 1.2 MB, roughly 300 000 tokens. That is more than most chat models take in one conversation. Use it where the assistant searches an uploaded file instead of reading all of it (a Claude project, a custom GPT, NotebookLM), or with a model that has a context of a million tokens.
- **For commands,** also paste [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/AGENTS.md): it is short and holds the rules and the per-installation command forms.

## What to check yourself

- **Physics numbers.** The analysis scripts are examples, not vetted results ([Analyse](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md)). Ask the assistant for the cuts, the number of events and the error it used, and check a result against a second method before you rely on it.
- **Options and names.** Assistants invent plausible options, XML tags and dataset names. The truth is `--help`, the folder's `README.md`, and `h5_inspect.py` for a file.
- **What actually ran.** Ask for the exact command and the log lines that show the result. A line `No CUDA device found` means the run was on the CPU, which is slow and not the same numbers.
- **Cost.** A campaign takes hours of GPU time and many GB of disk. Decide that yourself; the instruction file tells the assistant to ask first.

How the two `llms` files are made: [Building this site](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/reference/site/#llmstxt).
# Install

# Production container

The production image `jhputschke/xscape-prod` is the ready-made setup for Linux machines with an NVIDIA GPU: workstations, cloud VMs (Docker) and HPC clusters (Apptainer). It holds X-SCAPE with MUSIC on the GPU (MUSIC4GPU, CUDA), iSS, 3dMCGlauber, Matter, LBT, iColored and Pythia, all compiled, together with PyJetscape and its Pythonic layer and the analysis packages (awkward, vector, fastjet, particle, hist, mplhep, matplotlib, scipy, pandas, uproot, JupyterLab). Nothing is compiled on your machine. One image serves three uses:

| use                                                                                                          | GPU                             | you bring                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **the production scripts** (`run_prod_jet.py`, `run_prod_oo_isr.py`, `run_jobs.sh`, `run_hadronize.py`, ...) | yes; stage 2 (hadronization) no | an output directory                             |
| **your own scripts and notebooks** (the O+O workflow, the examples, Python modules of your own)              | yes                             | your scripts, notebooks and XMLs in a directory |
| **analysis only** (hadron and pair files, FastJet, plots, notebooks)                                         | no                              | the files, or OSDF paths                        |

On a Mac

Containers on macOS can't reach the GPU: Docker runs them in a Linux VM without Metal. Use the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) there; the scripts, notebooks and outputs are the same.

## 1. Requirements

- **For simulations:** an NVIDIA GPU with a driver recent enough for the image's CUDA version (table below), and either
  - **Docker** with the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html) (workstation, cloud VM), or
  - **Apptainer** (or Singularity) on an HPC cluster; it needs no extra toolkit.
- **For analysis and hadronization only:** any Linux machine with Docker or Apptainer; no GPU.
- **Disk:** the full image is about 5.4 GB (5.36 GB for `cu130` on arm64); the `-slim` variant is 0.6 GB smaller.

Pick the tag by the CUDA version your driver supports. `nvidia-smi` on the host prints it in the top right corner ("CUDA Version").

| tag     | CUDA | GPUs                                                               | host driver                         | CPU architectures |
| ------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `cu126` | 12.6 | V100, RTX 20xx–40xx, A100, A40, L4, H100, GH200                    | supports CUDA 12.6 or later (R560+) | amd64, arm64      |
| `cu130` | 13.2 | GH200, B200/GB200, RTX 50xx / RTX PRO Blackwell, GB10; **no V100** | supports CUDA 13.2 or later (R580+) | amd64, arm64      |
| `cu124` | 12.4 | as `cu126`                                                         | older drivers (R550)                | amd64 only        |

Each tag is a multi-architecture manifest: `docker pull` and `apptainer pull` take the image for the machine's CPU (x86_64 or ARM, e.g. GH200 and GB10). There is no performance difference to expect between `cu124` and `cu126`.

For a campaign, pin the image

`cu126` is a **moving** tag: it always points at the latest build. For a production campaign take a fixed tag: a release's, `cu126-v1.5` (`cu130-v1.5`, `cu124-v1.5`; the number is js-contrib's release, the same as the Mac wheel's), a dated one, `cu126-<YYYYMMDD>-<xscape commit>`, or the image digest, and use the same one on every machine. Physics fixes change results, so don't mix images of different builds in one campaign, and record which image you used: the output files don't say. The image's `/opt/X-SCAPE/BUILD_INFO.txt` lists the commits it was built from.

## 2. Pull the image and check it

**Docker:**

```bash
docker pull jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
docker run --rm --gpus all jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 nvidia-smi       # the GPU is seen
docker run --rm jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  python /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/utils/container/image_check.py --analysis
```

**Apptainer:**

```bash
apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
apptainer exec --nv xscape_prod.sif nvidia-smi
apptainer exec xscape_prod.sif \
  python /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/utils/container/image_check.py --analysis
```

`image_check.py` ends with `image_check: all ok`. To confirm that the bindings were built against the GPU MUSIC:

```bash
docker run --rm jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  python -c "import jetscape as js; print(js.HAS_CORE, js.pyjetscape_core.MUSIC_BACKEND)"
# -> True music4gpu-cuda
```

## 3. The rules of the container

Everything else on this page follows from four rules.

1. **The image is read-only; your files live in `/work`.** The X-SCAPE tree is `/opt/X-SCAPE` (read-only in Apptainer, owned by root in Docker). Mount a directory of yours at `/work` (Docker `-v "$PWD/work:/work"`, Apptainer `--bind "$PWD/work:/work"`) and write every output there. A file written anywhere else is gone when the container ends.
1. **Run as yourself.** With Docker, pass `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`, or the outputs belong to root. Apptainer runs as you anyway.
1. **GPU access is explicit.** Docker `--gpus all` (or `--gpus device=1`), Apptainer `--nv`. Without it MUSIC falls back to its CPU path: about 10× slower, and its numbers are not the GPU's.
1. **Everything finds the tree by itself.** `import jetscape` works everywhere; scripts and notebooks find the build through `$XSCAPE=/opt/X-SCAPE` (`jetscape.paths`), and each job runs in a private working directory under its output directory, so jobs never share files and nothing writes into the image. Leave `XSCAPE` and `JETSCAPE_BUILD` as the image sets them.

Where things are inside the container:

|                                 | path                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| X-SCAPE tree, build             | `/opt/X-SCAPE`, `/opt/X-SCAPE/build_gpu`                                             |
| js-contrib                      | `/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib`                                          |
| examples and production scripts | `/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example`              |
| start directory                 | Docker: `.../example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`; Apptainer: the directory you start it from |
| your files                      | `/work` (you mount it)                                                               |
| X-SCAPE's default parameters    | `/opt/X-SCAPE/config/jetscape_main.xml`                                              |

## 4. Your first event

`xscape-examples` copies every example into a writable directory (the examples write next to themselves, so they can't run inside the read-only image). Then one O+O event runs through the whole chain: 3dMCGlauber, Pythia with initial-state radiation, MUSIC on the GPU, Matter + LBT, iColored + iSS. It takes under a minute on a GPU and leaves two hadron files in `./work/out_oo/`.

**Docker:**

```bash
mkdir -p work
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 bash -c \
  'xscape-examples /work/examples && cd /work/examples/pythonic &&
   python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo'
```

**Apptainer:**

```bash
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
apptainer exec --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif xscape-examples /work/examples
apptainer exec --nv --pwd /work/examples/pythonic --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo
```

`work/examples/` now holds the production scripts, the Pythonic examples (`pythonic/`), the toy Python modules (`python_modules/`), the analysis notebooks and their XMLs, editable on the host with your own editor. `xscape-examples` never overwrites: for a fresh copy, give it a new directory. What the event does and what the files contain: [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md).

## 5. Running the productions

The production scripts run from the image's own copy, with their outputs in `/work`. Docker starts in `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`; for O+O, change the directory with `-w`.

```bash
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
mkdir -p prod

# Au+Au 0-10 % with a jet: 2 events
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir /work/out

# stage 2 (hadronization) needs no GPU
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_hadronize.py /work/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

# O+O with initial-state radiation
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" \
  -w /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr $IMG \
  python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 2 --seed 5 --outdir /work/out_oo
```

Put OUTDIR one level inside `/work`

Use `/work/out`, not `/work`: every job records its seed in `OUTDIR/../seeds_used.tsv`, so the parent of OUTDIR must be writable too.

Your own physics settings go in a user XML that you mount and pass: `-v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro"` and `--user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10.xml`. Campaigns, several jobs per GPU, SLURM arrays and the two stages are explained in [Au+Au jets (two stages)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md), [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md), [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md) and [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).

## 6. Your own scripts and notebooks

### A script of your own

Put the script and its user XML in `work/` (start from a copy of `examples/pythonic/oo_workflow.py` and `oo_workflow.xml`). Every such script has the same skeleton:

```python
# work/my_job.py
import jetscape as js
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronH5Writer

with js.JobDir("/work/out_mine", "/work/my_job.xml") as job:      # private working directory
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml) as driver, \
         HadronH5Writer("/work/out_mine/my_job_hadrons.h5", tag="jet_frag", n_samples=1) as out:
        for i in driver.events():                                 # one iteration per event
            jets = driver.hadronization_manager.hadron_array()
            out.append_unit(jets.to_dict(), unit=i, event=i)
            print(i, len(jets), "jet hadrons")
```

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 python my_job.py
```

`js.JobDir(out_dir, user_xml)` copies your XML to `out_dir/`, makes its relative paths (such as iSS's tables) absolute for the image's build, runs the job in a private directory `out_dir/work/<name>` and removes that directory after a successful run. Inside the `with` block the current directory is that working directory, so use absolute output paths. The interface (`driver.events()`, `hadron_array()`, the hadron files) is described in [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md); writing physics modules in Python in [Writing modules in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md).

### Python packages that are not in the image

Install them once into `/work` and put that directory on the path:

```bash
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  pip install --target /work/pylib seaborn
docker run ... -e PYTHONPATH=/work/pylib:/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/python ...
```

Don't upgrade numpy or h5py this way: `pyjetscape_core` is compiled against the image's numpy. For a group, a small Dockerfile of your own is cleaner: `FROM jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126-<date>-<commit>` plus `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir seaborn`.

### Changing js-contrib's Python code

The image uses its own `jetscape` package unless yours comes first on the path. For changes to pure Python, mount your js-contrib checkout and put its package in front:

```bash
docker run ... -v "$HOME/js-contrib:/src/js-contrib:ro" \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/src/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/python ...
```

This works only if your checkout is close to the image's js-contrib commit (`BUILD_INFO.txt`), and the compiled `pyjetscape_core*.so` must come from the image (copy it from the image's `python/jetscape/` into your checkout's). Changes to C++ need the [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

## 7. Analysis without a GPU

Without `--gpus` (Docker) or `--nv` (Apptainer) the image is an analysis environment. It also runs stage 2 (hadronization) on CPU-only nodes, unchanged.

```bash
# a script of yours on your files
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 python my_analysis.py /work/data

# open every file of a production directory
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/prod:/work:ro" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  python /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/utils/analysis_env/check_env.py /work/out --no-render
```

pelicanfs reads `osdf://` paths in place; public namespaces need no token, a protected one takes `-e BEARER_TOKEN_FILE=/work/token`. Notebooks to start from (in the `xscape-examples` copy):

| notebook                                                              | reads                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `pythonic/oo_analysis.ipynb`                                          | the O+O hadron files, streamed from the OSDF |
| `pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb` (sections 4–6)                           | the hadron files of your own run             |
| `analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb`, `jet_fastjet*.ipynb` | a production directory                       |
| `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/jet_wake.ipynb`                                   | a pair file and its hadron files             |
| `prod_OO_isr/oo_isr_overview.ipynb`                                   | an O+O production                            |

How to read the files: [Analyse](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

## 8. Jupyter

`xscape-jupyter [DIR]` starts JupyterLab on port 8888 with `DIR` (default `/work`) as its root and prints the URL with its access token.

```bash
docker run --rm -it --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -p 8888:8888 \
  -v "$PWD/work:/work" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 xscape-jupyter
```

Open the `http://127.0.0.1:8888/lab?token=...` line it prints. Notebooks run with the image's Python ("Python 3 (ipykernel)"), and simulations in a notebook use the GPU as scripts do. Stop it with Ctrl-C twice.

- **Another port:** `-p 8890:8888`, then open `127.0.0.1:8890`.
- **On a remote GPU server:** start it there as above, then on your laptop run `ssh -N -L 8888:localhost:8888 user@server` and open the URL locally.
- **Keep Jupyter's settings and history:** `$HOME` is a temporary directory with `--user`; add `-e HOME=/work/.home`.
- **Analysis only:** the same command without `--gpus all`.

## 9. HPC clusters with Apptainer

Apptainer runs the same image as you, with your home directory mounted and the host's network. It differs from Docker in three ways: `--nv` for the GPU, `--bind` for `/work`, and it starts in the current directory, not the image's start directory, so pass `--pwd` or full paths.

```bash
apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126-<date>-<commit>
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
EX=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example

# a production
apptainer exec --nv --pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --outdir /work/out

# a script of your own
apptainer exec --nv --pwd /work/examples/pythonic --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python oo_workflow.py --events 3 --outdir /work/out_oo

# analysis, no GPU
apptainer exec --pwd /work --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif python my_analysis.py
```

In a SLURM batch script these lines run as they are (after `#SBATCH --gpus=1` or your site's equivalent). Job arrays, several GPUs and the LBT table cache: [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).

- **Mixed clusters:** a `.sif` file holds one CPU architecture. Where the login nodes are x86 but the GPU nodes are ARM (GH200), pull with `apptainer pull --arch arm64`, or pull on a compute node.
- **Home directory:** Apptainer mounts it, but write outputs to `/work` on scratch, not to `~`.

**Jupyter on a compute node:**

```bash
salloc --gpus=1 --time=2:00:00                  # your site's options; you land on a node
apptainer exec --nv --bind $SCRATCH/xscape:/work xscape_prod.sif xscape-jupyter
```

In Apptainer, `xscape-jupyter` listens on 127.0.0.1 only, since the node is shared. Tunnel from your laptop through the login node to the compute node:

```bash
ssh -N -L 8888:localhost:8888 -J user@login.cluster user@<node>   # if nodes accept ssh
ssh -N -L 8888:<node>:8888 user@login.cluster                     # otherwise, with JUPYTER_IP=0.0.0.0
```

For the second form start Jupyter with `apptainer exec --env JUPYTER_IP=0.0.0.0 ...`; the token still protects it.

## 10. Image variants

Each CUDA tag comes in flavours, marked by a suffix; suffixes combine (`cu126-slim-gcs`).

| suffix  | what changes                                                            | for                                                                                       |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (none)  | the full image: productions, analysis packages, JupyterLab, the helpers | everything on this page                                                                   |
| `-slim` | no analysis packages and no Jupyter; 0.6 GB smaller                     | production runs only                                                                      |
| `-viz`  | adds pyvista/vtk with off-screen rendering                              | [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md) |
| `-gcs`  | adds Google Cloud Storage for Python (`gcsfs`, `google-cloud-storage`)  | reading and writing `gs://`                                                               |

Which variants are published at a given time is visible on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/jhputschke/xscape-prod/tags). Every image has Pelican/OSDF support (`pelicanfs` and the `pelican` command-line tool). The images contain neither ROOT nor PyTorch.

Images built before 2026-10-28 (the date is in the dated tag) lack the analysis packages, the helpers (`xscape-examples`, `xscape-jupyter`) and the preset `PYTHONPATH`; they only run the production scripts.

## 11. Troubleshooting

| symptom                                                                | cause and fix                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Permission denied` or `Read-only file system` when writing            | writing into the image, or into `/work` itself where OUTDIR's parent must be writable: write to `/work/<something>`; with Docker use `--user` and a directory you own |
| outputs owned by root                                                  | Docker without `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`; fix once with `sudo chown -R $USER work/`                                                                                |
| `No CUDA device found ... falling back to CPU`                         | no `--gpus all` / `--nv`, or the driver is older than the image's CUDA: check `nvidia-smi`; take `cu124` for R550 drivers                                             |
| `docker: could not select device driver "" with capabilities: [[gpu]]` | the NVIDIA Container Toolkit is not installed on the host                                                                                                             |
| `no kernel image is available for execution on the device`             | the image has no code for this GPU (e.g. V100 with `cu130`): take `cu126` or `cu124`; discard files written by such a run                                             |
| `python: can't open file 'run_prod_jet.py'`                            | Apptainer: add `--pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet` or use the full path                                                                                                    |
| `xscape-examples: ... exists and is not empty`                         | it never overwrites: give another directory                                                                                                                           |
| `JobDir: not found: .../music_input`                                   | `JETSCAPE_BUILD` or `XSCAPE` set to something else; in the image leave them as they are                                                                               |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: awkward` (fastjet, Jupyter, ...)                 | a `-slim` image, or an image built before 2026-10-28                                                                                                                  |
| Jupyter page does not load                                             | Docker: `-p 8888:8888` missing; Apptainer: tunnel to the compute node, not the login node                                                                             |
| Matter warnings `Second instance ... el_vector` for ISR partons        | harmless: an ISR parton before t = 0 outside the light cone, where there is no medium                                                                                 |

Full reference (helpers, environment variables, the image build): [`utils/README_Container_Usage.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/README_Container_Usage.md), [`utils/BuildContainerProd.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/BuildContainerProd.md).

## Next: run your first event

You ran one event above; [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md) explains what it did, what the output files hold and where to go from there.

# Mac (xscape wheel)

On an Apple Silicon Mac, X-SCAPE runs natively with MUSIC on the Mac's own GPU through Metal. It comes as a Python wheel, `xscape`, installed with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) from a lock file. There is no compiler and no container involved. Docker on a Mac can't reach the GPU, so on a Mac the wheel takes the place of the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md); the scripts, notebooks and outputs are the same. The environment holds X-SCAPE with MUSIC (MUSIC4GPU, Metal), iSS, 3dMCGlauber, Matter, LBT, iColored and Pythia, PyJetscape and its Pythonic layer, and the analysis packages (awkward, vector, fastjet, particle, hist, mplhep, matplotlib, scipy, pandas, uproot, JupyterLab), pelicanfs for `osdf://` paths, and js-contrib's production tools as commands (`xscape-prodwizard`, `xscape-jobmon`, `xscape-osdf`, ...).

**What it can't do:** rebuild X-SCAPE or the bindings (that needs the [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md)), ROOT/PyROOT (uproot, included, reads ROOT files), and PyTorch (not in the environment). Some modules and data are not in it: [What runs with the wheel](#what-runs-with-the-wheel). Intel Macs are not supported.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later) on **macOS 26** or later (Apple menu → About This Mac).
- About 3 GB of disk, 1 GB of it uv's download cache (`uv cache clean` frees it).
- Internet access during the installation.

You do **not** need Xcode, Homebrew, conda, Docker, git or an Apple developer account.

Releases

The wheels are published on the [Releases page of jhputschke/xscape-macos](https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases). The current release is **v1.5**; check that page for the latest. Each release is a set of three files: the `xscape` wheel (X-SCAPE, 175 MB), the `pyjetscape` wheel (the Python package), and a **lock file** `xscape-<version>-cp313.lock.txt`, which names every package of the environment with its exact version and checksum. You install from the lock file, so every Mac gets exactly the same software.

**Version numbers:** from 1.5 on, a release has the number of the js-contrib release it is built from (xscape 1.5 = js-contrib `v1.5` = pyjetscape 1.5), the same number as the production containers of that release (`cu126-v1.5`, `cu130-v1.5`, `cu124-v1.5`), which are built from the same commits. Earlier releases were numbered on their own (0.1.0, 0.2.0); 1.5 follows 0.2.0.

## Install with one command

```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/main/install.sh | sh
```

The script, [`install.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/blob/main/install.sh), does steps 1–4 below for the latest release:

1. checks the Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later, 3 GB free) before downloading anything;
1. installs uv, unless a recent one is already there;
1. creates the environment `~/.venvs/xscape-VER` from the release's lock file;
1. fetches the LBT tables and runs `xscape-selftest`.

It takes a few minutes (93 s on an M3 Max with a fast connection, everything downloaded) and ends with `xscape VER is installed in ...` and the line that activates the environment. Then run your first event (step 5):

```bash
source ~/.venvs/xscape-1.5/bin/activate       # the line it printed; in every new Terminal window
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo
```

Options go after `sh -s --`, for example `... | sh -s -- --version 1.5 --examples ~/xscape/examples`:

| option                      | does                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--version VER`             | installs this release (default: the latest on the Releases page) |
| `--venv DIR`                | puts the environment in `DIR` (default: `~/.venvs/xscape-VER`)   |
| `--examples DIR`            | also copies the examples to `DIR` (never overwrites)             |
| `--force`                   | deletes an existing environment first                            |
| `--no-lbt`, `--no-selftest` | skips the LBT tables, the self-test                              |

Running it again is safe: it reuses the environment and the LBT tables, and the lock file makes the environment exactly the release again (`--force` builds it new). Apart from the environment it writes only uv (in `~/.local/bin`; uv's installer adds that directory to your shell's `PATH`), uv's cache and Python, and the LBT tables in `~/Library/Caches/xscape`.

The steps below do the same by hand.

## Step 1: install uv

uv is Astral's Python package manager: a single program in `~/.local/bin`.

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Then open a new Terminal window (or run `source ~/.local/bin/env`) so that `uv` is found. With Homebrew, `brew install uv` works too.

## Step 2: create the environment from the lock file

```bash
VER=1.5                       # the latest: github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases
mkdir -p ~/xscape && cd ~/xscape
curl -LO https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases/download/v$VER/xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
uv venv --managed-python ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER --python 3.13
source ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER/bin/activate
uv pip sync xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
```

uv downloads Python 3.13 and about 200 MB of packages, which takes seconds to a few minutes depending on the connection.

- `--managed-python` makes uv use its own Python, never one from Homebrew, conda or python.org that happens to be installed, so nothing outside the environment is used.
- `uv pip sync` installs exactly what the lock lists, hash-checked, and removes anything else.
- `source ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER/bin/activate` is needed in **every new Terminal window** where you use X-SCAPE. Your prompt then starts with `(xscape-1.5)`.

## Step 3: fetch the LBT tables

LBT, the jet energy-loss module, needs its scattering tables: a 240 MB download, 1.1 GB on disk. They are kept in `~/Library/Caches/xscape` and shared by all your environments.

```bash
xscape-fetch-data lbt
```

It checks every file against the release's checksums and ends with `xscape-fetch-data: LBT tables ... (checked) -> ...`. If you already have the tables on disk, `xscape-fetch-data lbt --from DIR` uses them instead of downloading.

## Step 4: check the environment

```bash
xscape-selftest
# ... image_check: all ok
python -c "import jetscape as js; print(js.HAS_CORE, js.pyjetscape_core.MUSIC_BACKEND)"
# -> True music4gpu-metal
```

`xscape-selftest` checks the bindings, the HDF5 filters, pelicanfs, the paths to the installed X-SCAPE, the analysis packages, MUSIC's EoS table and the LBT tables, and sends one synthetic event through awkward, FastJet and mplhep. It stops at the first failure. `True` means the compiled bindings load; `music4gpu-metal` means they were built with the Metal MUSIC. The first `import` after the installation takes a little longer, because matplotlib builds its font cache once.

When an event runs, MUSIC prints the GPU it uses when it starts: `[MUSIC-GPU] Metal device: <your chip>`. There is nothing to switch on. If instead you see `[MUSIC-GPU] Metal init failed, falling back to CPU.`, MUSIC runs on the CPU; that happens inside a virtual machine or a container, so run natively in Terminal.

## Step 5: copy the examples and run one event

```bash
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
xscape-utils ~/xscape/utils          # optional: js-contrib's utils/, to read or adapt
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo
```

`xscape-examples` copies every example into a directory of yours: the production scripts, the Pythonic examples (`pythonic/`), the toy Python modules (`python_modules/`), the analysis notebooks and their XMLs. The examples write next to themselves, so they run from this copy. `xscape-utils` does the same for js-contrib's `utils/` (`jobmon.py`, `prodwizard.py`, `h5_inspect.py`, `remote_transfer/`, ...); you don't need the copy to use them, they are commands of the environment ([Command reference](#command-reference)). Neither ever overwrites: for a fresh copy, give a new directory.

The event is one O+O collision through the whole chain: 3dMCGlauber, Pythia with initial-state radiation, MUSIC on the GPU, Matter + LBT, iColored + iSS. It takes under a minute (27 s on an M3 Max) and writes two hadron files to `~/xscape/out_oo/`. What it did: [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md).

## The rules

1. **Your files live in your own directories** (e.g. `~/xscape`). The installed X-SCAPE inside `~/.venvs/...` is not edited; the examples run from your copy.
1. **Activate the environment** in every new Terminal window: `source ~/.venvs/xscape-VER/bin/activate`.
1. **One environment per release.** A release fixes all the software. For a campaign, keep to one release, and don't mix files of two releases, since physics fixes change results. The commits a release was built from: `cat "$(python -c 'import xscape; print(xscape.TREE)')/BUILD_INFO.txt"`.
1. **Everything finds the installed X-SCAPE by itself** (`jetscape.paths`). Leave `XSCAPE`, `JETSCAPE_BUILD`, `PYTHONPATH` and `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` unset in this environment: they belong to a source build and would point it elsewhere.
1. **Results agree statistically, not bit for bit,** across Macs and macOS versions.

|                                                           | where                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the environment                                           | `~/.venvs/xscape-VER`                                               |
| the installed X-SCAPE (data, `config/`, `BUILD_INFO.txt`) | `python -c "import xscape; print(xscape.TREE)"`                     |
| X-SCAPE's default parameters                              | `config/jetscape_main.xml` in that tree                             |
| the examples                                              | your copy, e.g. `~/xscape/examples` (`xscape-examples`)             |
| js-contrib's `utils/`                                     | inside the installed tree (`utils/`); your copy with `xscape-utils` |
| the LBT tables                                            | `~/Library/Caches/xscape/LBT-tables-<commit>`                       |

## One XML: `xscape-run`

`xscape-run` runs X-SCAPE's `runJetscape` on a user XML in a directory of its own, and takes any XML as it is: one of the installed X-SCAPE's `config/`, one of the examples, or your own.

```bash
xscape-run -w ~/xscape/runs/oo -u ~/xscape/examples/pythonic/oo_workflow.xml
xscape-run -w ~/xscape/runs/pp -u "$(python -c 'import xscape; print(xscape.TREE)')/config/jetscape_user.xml"
```

- It copies both XMLs into the run directory (`jetscape_main.xml`, `<name>.run.xml`; your file is not changed), with every `../` path made absolute. A `../` path with no file behind it is looked up in the installed X-SCAPE by its last parts: `../external_packages/iSS/iSS_tables` becomes its `iSS_tables`, `../config/HH_LightExcitedMesons.xml` its `config/...`. Give inputs of your own as absolute paths.
- It links the tables 3dMCGlauber and LBT read from the working directory and gives the run a private `music_input`, so several runs can go at once.
- **Before anything runs it checks the XML** and stops (exit code 3) with the reason:
  - a tag the main XML lacks: X-SCAPE would stop at the first with `User XML tag <...> is unrecognized`. Either the tag is misspelled or the XML is newer than the environment (`<extraHard>` in an environment before 0.2.0);
  - an input with no file behind it (the test hydro files, SMASH's configuration);
  - a module this wheel does not have ([below](#what-runs-with-the-wheel)), which X-SCAPE would only warn about and then run without;
  - automatic module setup turned off (`<enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination> false`): such XMLs are written for C++ test programs, and `runJetscape` would run nothing;
  - an LHAPDF6 set for Pythia (`PDF:pSet = LHAPDF6:...`), which the wheel's Pythia can't load.

`xscape-run -f ...` runs anyway.

`runJetscape USER_XML` runs X-SCAPE in the current directory, as it is. When the XML needs files there that the directory lacks (3dMCGlauber's `tables/`, MUSIC's `music_input`, `../` paths), it stops and points to `xscape-run`, rather than failing in the middle with `sh: ./Metropolis.e: No such file or directory` (`XSCAPE_RUN_HERE=1` runs it anyway). Use `xscape-run`.

## Running the productions

The productions run from your copy of the examples, with the same options as on a GPU server or in the container.

```bash
cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet

# Au+Au 0-10 % with a jet: 2 events (about 40 s on an M3 Max)
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out

# a campaign: 20 jobs x 25 events, unique seeds, 3 jobs at a time on the GPU
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign test 20 25 0 ~/xscape/prod/out

# stage 2 (hadronization) on the CPU
python run_hadronize.py ~/xscape/prod/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

# O+O with initial-state radiation
cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_OO_isr
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 2 --seed 5 --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out_oo
```

- **Put OUTDIR one level inside a directory of yours** (`~/xscape/prod/out`): every job records its seed in `OUTDIR/../seeds_used.tsv`.
- **Your own physics settings:** copy a user XML from `~/xscape/examples/config/`, edit it and pass it with `--user-xml my.xml`.
- **Several jobs at once:** on an M3 Max, `-j 3` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=5` and `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive` gave the most events per hour; aim for `-j` × threads ≈ the number of performance cores. Without `passive`, idle OpenMP threads spin and slow the other jobs down.
- **Long campaigns:** keep the Mac awake, e.g. `caffeinate -i ./run_jobs.sh ...`.
- **ROOT output** (`run_h5toROOT.py` with ROOT) needs PyROOT, which this environment does not have; uproot writes and reads the ROOT files instead.
- **The extra hard scatterings, minimum bias, O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV** (`run_prod_jet.py --extra-hard`, `--hard none`, `../config/OO_5360_jet.xml`, `NeNe_5360_jet.xml`) need the 0.2.0 environment or later. An older one stops with the unknown-tag message for `<extraHard>`: install the new release next to it.

**Plan, watch and upload with the tools.** `xscape-prodwizard` writes the launch commands for this Mac with the measured settings (machine `mac_wheel`: this environment, your copy of the examples, `run_jobs.sh`) and estimates the duration, disk and memory; it never starts jobs. `xscape-jobmon` watches the campaign.

```bash
xscape-prodwizard --preset auau_jet --machine mac_wheel --events 300 --campaign test
xscape-prodwizard --preset oo_hadrons --machine mac_wheel --events 1000 --save launch_oo.sh
xscape-jobmon ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/out/test --tui     # while it runs
xscape-check-deposition ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/out/test
xscape-upload-follow ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/out AuAu_test --follow   # to the OSDF
```

`mac_wheel` takes the environment from `$VIRTUAL_ENV` (default `~/.venvs/xscape`) and the examples from `$XSCAPE_EXAMPLES` (default `~/xscape/examples`); inside this environment the wizard picks it by itself. The rates are the M3 Max's. The tools and their options: [Tools](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/reference/tools/index.md); the OSDF: [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/#on-a-mac-the-xscape-wheel).

The productions themselves: [Au+Au jets (two stages)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md), [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md), [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md), [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md).

## Your own scripts and Python modules

Put your script and its user XML in a directory of yours, starting from a copy of `examples/pythonic/oo_workflow.py` and `oo_workflow.xml` (`oo_workflow.py` takes any user XML with `--xml`). The skeleton every such script has:

```python
# ~/xscape/mine/my_job.py
import os
import jetscape as js
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronH5Writer

out = os.path.expanduser("~/xscape/out_mine")
with js.JobDir(out, os.path.expanduser("~/xscape/mine/my_job.xml")) as job:  # private working dir
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml) as driver, \
         HadronH5Writer(f"{out}/my_job_hadrons.h5", tag="jet_frag", n_samples=1) as h5:
        for i in driver.events():                                         # one iteration per event
            jets = driver.hadronization_manager.hadron_array()
            h5.append_unit(jets.to_dict(), unit=i, event=i)
            print(i, len(jets), "jet hadrons")
```

`js.JobDir(out_dir, user_xml)` copies your XML to `out_dir/`, points it at the installed X-SCAPE's tables, runs the job in a private directory `out_dir/work/<name>` and removes it after a successful run. Inside the `with` block the current directory is that working directory, so use absolute output paths. Details: [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md).

**Physics modules in Python** (a hard process, energy loss, hadronization, an afterburner, a writer) run inside X-SCAPE's event loop with this environment as it is, next to the C++ modules.
