Start from `examples/python_modules/` (`python run_by_hand_pythonic.py --style new`) and read [Writing modules in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md).

**More Python packages:** `uv pip install seaborn`. A later `uv pip sync` (of the same or a new lock) removes them again, so keep your additions in a file and run `uv pip install -r my_packages.txt` after each sync. Don't change numpy or h5py this way.

## Analysis

The same environment is an analysis environment; analysis needs no GPU. Notebooks to start from, in your copy of the examples:

| notebook                                                              | reads                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb` (sections 4–6)                           | the hadron files of your own run                                              |
| `pythonic/oo_analysis.ipynb`                                          | the O+O hadron files streamed from the OSDF (pelicanfs is in the environment) |
| `analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb`, `jet_fastjet*.ipynb` | a production directory                                                        |
| `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/jet_wake.ipynb`                                   | a pair file and its hadron files                                              |
| `prod_OO_isr/oo_isr_overview.ipynb`                                   | an O+O production                                                             |
| `analysis/bulk/` (`bulk_obs.py`, notebooks)                           | Nch, [pT] and vₙ of extras or minimum-bias files                              |

`osdf://` paths work as they are (`fsspec`, `uproot`, `h5py` through pelicanfs), and `xscape-osdf download` fetches whole productions: [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md). `xscape-h5-inspect FILE.h5` shows any HDF5 file, with js-contrib's formats decoded.

To analyse on another computer (Linux, an Intel Mac, a cluster) you need only the Python package, not X-SCAPE: see [the analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/#without-a-checkout-the-pyjetscape-wheel).

3D visualization is not in the wheel

The wheel has neither PyVista nor the [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md) scripts (`wake_pyvista.py`, `hydro_jet_particles_pyvista.py`). For movies of the medium, the jet wake and the hadrons, clone js-contrib and create the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md) next to this one, with `setup_analysis_env.sh --python /opt/homebrew/bin/python3`: its visualization stack is installed by default. [How, step by step](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/#requirements).

## Jupyter and VS Code

```bash
source ~/.venvs/xscape-VER/bin/activate
cd ~/xscape/examples
jupyter lab
```

JupyterLab opens in your browser. Notebooks run with the environment's Python ("Python 3 (ipykernel)"), and simulations in a notebook use the GPU as scripts do. Stop it with Ctrl-C twice in the Terminal.

**VS Code:** open `~/xscape/examples`, then "Python: Select Interpreter" (for notebooks also "Select Kernel") and choose `~/.venvs/xscape-VER/bin/python`.

## Command reference

In the activated environment:

| command                                  | does                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `xscape-fetch-data lbt [--from DIR]`     | the LBT tables into `~/Library/Caches/xscape` (or `$XSCAPE_CACHE`), checked and linked into this environment                                                              |
| `xscape-selftest`                        | checks the environment: bindings, HDF5 filters, pelicanfs, paths, analysis packages, EoS table, LBT tables, one synthetic event                                           |
| `xscape-examples [DEST]`                 | copies the examples to `DEST` (default `./examples`); never overwrites                                                                                                    |
| `xscape-utils [DEST]`                    | copies js-contrib's `utils/` to `DEST` (default `./utils`); never overwrites                                                                                              |
| `xscape-run -w RUN_DIR -u USER_XML [-f]` | X-SCAPE's `runJetscape` on any user XML, in a directory of its own; checks the XML first ([above](#one-xml-xscape-run))                                                   |
| `runJetscape USER_XML`                   | X-SCAPE's executable with this environment's data, in the current directory; stops if the directory lacks what the XML needs                                              |
| `xscape-prodwizard`                      | plans a production (`utils/prodwizard.py`; `--machine mac_wheel`)                                                                                                         |
| `xscape-jobmon OUTDIR`                   | watches a `run_jobs.sh` production (`utils/jobmon.py`; `--watch`, `--tui`)                                                                                                |
| `xscape-check-deposition DIR`            | flags Au+Au jet jobs with far too little deposition (`utils/check_deposition.py`)                                                                                         |
| `xscape-h5-inspect FILE.h5`              | any HDF5 file, js-contrib's formats decoded (`utils/h5_inspect.py`)                                                                                                       |
| `xscape-osdf`                            | `ls`, `du`, `download`, `upload`, `rm` on the OSDF, `osdf:///fno4hic` (`utils/remote_transfer/js_osdf.py`), in this environment                                           |
| `xscape-upload-follow OUTBASE REMOTE`    | uploads a running production's finished jobs to the OSDF (`utils/upload_follow.py`)                                                                                       |
| `xscape-gcs`                             | the same transfers for Google Cloud Storage (`utils/remote_transfer/js_gcs.py`); makes its own environment in `~/.cache/js_gcs` on first use; needs a service-account key |

The tool commands run the copies of the `utils/` scripts installed with the wheel, with the same options; `--help` shows them under the command's name.

## What runs with the wheel

The wheel is built without ROOT, HepMC, SMASH, FreestreamMilne, CLVisc, IPGlasma and the FNO hydro (PyTorch); its Pythia has no LHAPDF6, and Martini's data and X-SCAPE's test hydro files are not installed. `xscape-run` names what an XML needs of these and stops. For them use the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) or a [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

|                                               | runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | does not run (why)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **productions**                               | `prod_AuAu_0_10/run_prod.py`, `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_prod_jet.py` (also `--extra-hard`, `--hard none`, the 5.36 TeV O+O and Ne+Ne XMLs), `run_prod_vacuum.py`, `hadronize.py`, `run_hadronize.py`, `prod_OO_isr/run_prod_oo_isr.py`, `run_jobs.sh` | `run_h5toROOT.py` with ROOT (PyROOT)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **examples**                                  | `pythonic/` (scripts and both notebooks), `python_modules/`, `per_event_loop.py`, `python_bulk_h5_writer.py`, `inspect_bulk_info.py`, `python_bulk_root_writer.py` (uproot), `analysis/`                                                            | `python_fno_test.py` (PyTorch), `python_fast_bulk_root_writer.py`, `validate_h5_vs_root.py`, `analysis_root/` (ROOT), `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/music_cpu_gpu_hydro.py` (a CPU MUSIC), `prod_OO_isr/hadro_compare/run_hadro_compare.sh` (two builds), the movie step of `analysis/zjet/test/make_data.sh` (Visualization)                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **X-SCAPE's test XMLs** (installed `config/`) | `jetscape_user.xml`, `_MUSIC`, `_DIS`, `_photoproduction`, `_twostagehydro`, `_brick_hybrid_hadronization`, `_OO_ISR_MatterLBT_iColored`                                                                                                            | the rest: the HepMC writer (`_rMatterLbt`, `_root_test`; `-f` runs them without it), ROOT writers (`BulkFastTest/`, `_dAu3d`), SMASH, FreestreamMilne (`_AA_dukeTune*`, `_FSFileTest`, `_sims`), CLVisc, IPGlasma, test hydro files (`_HydroFile`, `_PbPb_hard_nPDF`), LHAPDF6 (`_nPDF_test`), automatic module setup off (`FVvsMUSIC/`, `_iMATTERMCGlauber*`, `_MUSICMainClockTest`, `_SMASH*`, `_test`); `_MCGlauberMUSIC` and `3D/` use a tag no main XML has (`<nEvents_MCGla>`) |

## Updating and removing

**A new release** goes into a new environment next to the old one, so a running campaign keeps its software. With the script (the latest release, or `sh -s -- --version VER`):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/main/install.sh | sh
source ~/.venvs/xscape-<new version>/bin/activate
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples-<new version>   # the examples of this release
```

or by hand:

```bash
VER=<new version>
cd ~/xscape
curl -LO https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases/download/v$VER/xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
uv venv --managed-python ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER --python 3.13 && source ~/.venvs/xscape-$VER/bin/activate
uv pip sync xscape-$VER-cp313.lock.txt
xscape-fetch-data lbt                    # reuses the cached tables when they match
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples-$VER   # the examples of this release
```

**Removing:**

```bash
rm -rf ~/.venvs/xscape-VER               # one environment
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/xscape           # the LBT tables
uv cache clean                           # uv's downloads
rm ~/.local/bin/uv ~/.local/bin/uvx      # uv itself
```

## Troubleshooting

| symptom                                                                                          | cause and fix                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zsh: command not found: uv`                                                                     | open a new Terminal window, or `source ~/.local/bin/env`                                                                                                             |
| `install.sh: this shell runs under Rosetta (x86_64)`                                             | Terminal is set to open using Rosetta: Finder → Applications → Utilities → Terminal → Get Info → untick "Open using Rosetta"                                         |
| `install.sh: ... exists but is no environment`                                                   | `--venv` names a directory that is not an environment: give another directory, or `--force` to replace it                                                            |
| `... has no wheels with a matching platform tag`                                                 | macOS older than 26, or an Intel Mac: update macOS; Intel Macs are not supported                                                                                     |
| `zsh: no matches found: pyjetscape[analysis]...`                                                 | quote the argument: `"pyjetscape[analysis] @ ..."`                                                                                                                   |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jetscape'`                                                | the environment is not active: `source ~/.venvs/xscape-VER/bin/activate`                                                                                             |
| `import jetscape` picks up a source checkout, or `JobDir: not found: .../music_input`            | `PYTHONPATH`, `XSCAPE` or `JETSCAPE_BUILD` set (e.g. in `~/.zshrc`): `unset PYTHONPATH XSCAPE JETSCAPE_BUILD`                                                        |
| LBT: `cannot open ... LBT-tables`                                                                | step 3 not done for this environment: `xscape-fetch-data lbt`                                                                                                        |
| `xscape-fetch-data: ... file(s) missing or different`                                            | an interrupted download: `rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/xscape/LBT-tables-*` and run it again                                                                              |
| `xscape-examples: ... exists and is not empty`                                                   | it never overwrites: give another directory                                                                                                                          |
| `python: can't open file 'run_prod_jet.py'`                                                      | run it from your copy, `~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`                                                                                                        |
| MUSIC slow, no GPU                                                                               | inside a virtual machine or a container there is no Metal GPU: run natively in Terminal                                                                              |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: ROOT`                                                                      | ROOT is not part of this environment; uproot reads ROOT files                                                                                                        |
| `sh: ./Metropolis.e: No such file or directory` (3dMCGlauber), from `runJetscape`                | an environment before 0.2.0, run in a directory without `tables/`: use `xscape-run -w RUN_DIR -u USER_XML`                                                           |
| `runJetscape: ... reads files relative to the current directory`                                 | the same, caught: use `xscape-run`                                                                                                                                   |
| `User XML tag <extraHard> is unrecognized`, or `xscape-run: tags of ... that the main XML lacks` | the XML is newer than the environment (the extra hard scatterings need 0.2.0), or a tag is misspelled: install the current release                                   |
| `xscape-run: ... needs modules this xscape wheel does not have`                                  | the XML uses ROOT, SMASH, FreestreamMilne, CLVisc, IPGlasma or HepMC: [What runs with the wheel](#what-runs-with-the-wheel)                                          |
| `xscape-run: ... turns automatic module setup off`                                               | an XML of an X-SCAPE C++ test program: run it with its program in a source build                                                                                     |
| `JobDir` / `enter_workdir` raise `XMLProblem`                                                    | the same checks from Python, before X-SCAPE starts: the message names the tags or inputs                                                                             |
| `ValueError: Protocol not known: osdf`                                                           | an environment before 0.2.0 has no pelicanfs: install the current release (or `uv pip install pelicanfs`)                                                            |
| `AttributeError: 'Client' object has no attribute 'info'` on an `osdf://` path                   | installed after 2026-11-02, the environment has aiowebdav2 1.x, which pelicanfs (up to 1.5.0) cannot use: `uv pip install "aiowebdav2<1"` in the wheel's environment |

The same guide, with every detail: [`utils/README_Mac_Usage.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/README_Mac_Usage.md) (also the README of [jhputschke/xscape-macos](https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos)).

## Next: run your first event

You ran one event in step 5; [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md) explains what it did, what the output files hold and where to go from there.

# Analysis environment

The analysis environment is a plain Python venv for reading and analysing the files a production writes, on any computer with Python 3.10 or later. It needs no GPU, no X-SCAPE build, no compiled `pyjetscape_core`, no conda and no ROOT. Use it when someone else runs the productions and you get the files (from a disk or from the [OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)), or when you analyse on a laptop and simulate elsewhere. It holds the HDF5 readers of the `jetscape` package, uproot and awkward, FastJet, vector, particle, hist, mplhep, scipy, pandas, Jupyter, pyvista for the 3D visualization, and pelicanfs for `osdf://` files.

You may already have one

The [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) (run without `--gpus`) and the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) on a Mac carry the same analysis packages, but not the 3D visualization: the wheel has no PyVista (and the container only in its `-viz` variant). For [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md) on a Mac, create this environment (it includes PyVista by default) next to the wheel. Otherwise this page is for computers that have neither.

## What works in it, and what doesn't

| works                                                                                                                                    | doesn't                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| every HDF5 file of a production: pair, particlize and hadron files (`jetscape.hadrons_h5`, `jetscape.particlize_h5`, `jetscape.showers`) | anything that runs X-SCAPE: `run_prod_jet.py`, `run_jobs.sh`                                    |
| `run_h5toROOT.py` (hadron files → ROOT ntuples, written with uproot) and reading ROOT files with uproot                                  | re-hadronization (`hadronize.py`, `run_hadronize.py`): iSS and Pythia live in the compiled core |
| the analysis scripts and notebooks (`analysis/`, `jet_wake.ipynb`, the FastJet tutorials)                                                | the ROOT macros and the C++ reader, unless ROOT is added ([below](#4-root-next-to-it))          |
| the visualization of stored files (`wake_pyvista.py`, `hydro_jet_particles_pyvista.py --file`)                                           | the visualization of a live event                                                               |

`jetscape.HAS_CORE` is `False` in this venv. That is expected: every reader works without the compiled core.

## 1. Make the venv

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib.git
cd js-contrib
./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh           # venv in ~/.venvs/js_analysis
```

The script

1. creates the venv (default `~/.venvs/js_analysis`; give another directory as the first argument). Re-running it on an existing venv updates it;
1. installs the analysis packages from `utils/analysis_env/requirements.txt` (pelicanfs for the OSDF among them), plus pyvista/vtk (on by default), about 1.6 GB in total;
1. installs PyJetscape from your checkout in editable mode, so `import jetscape` works from anywhere and follows `git pull`;
1. downloads MUSIC's two hotQCD EoS tables (3.2 MB each, md5-checked) into the venv: EOS 91 (SMASH hadron list, the current productions) and EOS 9 (UrQMD, older files). It sets `MUSIC_EOS_TABLE` in its `activate` script to the EOS 9 file; the tools take the table of a file's EOS from the same directory. The pair files store the energy density, not the temperature; `jet_wake.ipynb`, `analysis/wake_*.py` and the visualization use the table to convert e → T. A venv made before 2026-10-29 has only EOS 9's: re-run the script;
1. runs `check_env.py`.

Nothing outside the venv directory is written, except a Jupyter kernel spec if you ask for one.

## 2. Activate and check

```bash
source ~/.venvs/js_analysis/bin/activate
python utils/analysis_env/check_env.py /path/to/out    # opens every file of a production directory
```

`check_env.py` checks the packages, the Blosc filter (the HDF5 files are Blosc-compressed and don't open without `hdf5plugin`), PyROOT if present, the EoS table and off-screen rendering. With a directory it opens its pair, hadron and ROOT files. Two flags:

| flag            | does                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--no-render`   | skips the off-screen rendering test                     |
| `--remote-test` | also reads one public object over `gs://` and `osdf://` |

## 3. Options

```bash
./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh [VENV_DIR] [options]
```

| option                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--uv`                   | create the venv and install with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): much faster (uv must be on `PATH`)                                                                                                                  |
| `--python PY`            | the interpreter for the venv (default `python3`; 3.10 or later)                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--no-viz`               | leave out pyvista/vtk/ffmpeg (about 0.6 GB of the 1.6 GB)                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--with-fasthydro`       | also install [FastHydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fasthydro/index.md), for FastHydro's own files and readers; **not needed for the production files**. Its solver also needs `pip install torch` |
| `--system-site-packages` | let the venv see the packages of the Python it is made from, e.g. PyROOT of a conda env ([§4](#4-root-next-to-it)); on an existing venv it switches this on                                                            |
| `--with-gcs`             | add Google Cloud Storage (`gcsfs`, `google-cloud-storage`): `gs://` URLs for fsspec, h5py and uproot                                                                                                                   |
| `--no-pelican`           | ignored: pelicanfs (`osdf://` and `pelican://` URLs) is part of the base list since 2026-11                                                                                                                            |
| `--eos-table PATH`       | copy the EoS tables from `PATH` (an `EOS/hotQCD` directory of a MUSIC or X-SCAPE build, or one of its `.dat` files) instead of downloading them; a table not found there is downloaded                                 |
| `--no-eos`               | neither download nor copy them                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--kernel NAME`          | register a Jupyter kernel `NAME` for the venv (for VS Code or a JupyterLab elsewhere)                                                                                                                                  |
| `--check DIR`            | at the end, open the production files in `DIR`                                                                                                                                                                         |

Full description: [`utils/analysis_env/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/analysis_env/README.md) and `./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh --help`.

## 4. ROOT next to it

ROOT isn't needed: `run_h5toROOT.py` falls back to uproot, and the ntuples hold the same hadrons. You want ROOT for PyROOT and RDataFrame, the `root` prompt and browser, the ROOT macros and the C++ reader, or the `--bits-p`/`--bits-x` options of `run_h5toROOT.py`. A venv sees ROOT only when it is made **from the Python that ROOT was built for**, with `--system-site-packages`.

**conda with ROOT + the venv (tested):**

```bash
# 1. conda, once (skip if you have it): Miniforge, conda-forge by default
curl -fLO "https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh"
bash "Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh" -b -p ~/miniforge3
source ~/miniforge3/bin/activate

# 2. an env with ROOT (ROOT >= 6.34 reads the RNTuple files run_h5toROOT.py writes)
conda create -n root -c conda-forge "root>=6.34"
conda activate root

# 3. the venv, from this env's Python
cd js-contrib
./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh ~/.venvs/js_analysis_root --system-site-packages
```

`check_env.py` then prints `ok PyROOT 6.xx ... writes with ROOT`. Afterwards PyROOT works from the venv alone; for the `root` prompt and compiled macros, `conda activate root` (without it ACLiC doesn't find the system headers: `'assert.h' file not found`):

```bash
source ~/.venvs/js_analysis_root/bin/activate
python contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_h5toROOT.py /path/to/out -j 4

conda activate root
root -l -b -q 'contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/hadron_distributions.C+("/path/to/out")'
```

The same works with any other ROOT that has PyROOT (LCG/CVMFS, Homebrew, a source build): make the venv from the `python3` in which `import ROOT` works, with `--python "$(which python3)" --system-site-packages`.

**one conda env with everything (untested):**

```bash
cd js-contrib
conda env create -f utils/analysis_env/environment.yml    # env "js_analysis"
conda activate js_analysis
python utils/analysis_env/check_env.py /path/to/out
```

Everything comes from conda-forge except the scikit-hep `fastjet` and PyJetscape (editable). The EoS tables are not part of it; add them with

```bash
mkdir -p "$CONDA_PREFIX/share/music_eos/hotQCD"
for t in binary SMASH_binary; do                         # EOS 9 and EOS 91
  curl -fL -o "$CONDA_PREFIX/share/music_eos/hotQCD/hrg_hotqcd_eos_$t.dat" \
    https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/wayne_state_nuclear_theory/hotqcd/src/main/hrg_hotqcd_eos_$t.dat
done
conda env config vars set MUSIC_EOS_TABLE="$CONDA_PREFIX/share/music_eos/hotQCD/hrg_hotqcd_eos_binary.dat"
conda activate js_analysis                               # again, to pick up the variable
```

More on ROOT, RDataFrame and the C++ reader: [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md).

## 5. FastJet

|           | Python                                                                                                                   | C++ (ROOT macros, programs)                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| package   | scikit-hep `fastjet` (the FastJet library is in the wheel): the classic SWIG interface and the array (awkward) interface | conda-forge `fastjet-cxx` (FastJet, `fastjet-config`) and `fastjet-contrib` (fjcontrib as one library, `libfastjetcontribfragile`) |
| install   | already in the venv                                                                                                      | `conda install -c conda-forge fastjet-cxx fastjet-contrib` in the ROOT env                                                         |
| fjcontrib | only SoftDrop, Lund declusterings, energy correlators and N-subjettiness, through the array interface                    | all of it (`#include <fastjet/contrib/SoftDrop.hh>`, ...; link `-lfastjetcontribfragile`)                                          |

Jet finding on the hadron files: [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/index.md).

## 6. Files on the OSDF or in Google Cloud Storage

pelicanfs (default) and gcsfs (`--with-gcs`) are fsspec file systems, so `osdf://` and `gs://` URLs work wherever fsspec does: uproot takes the URL directly, and h5py takes the file object fsspec opens (with `hdf5plugin` imported). Only the chunks you read travel over the network. Reading the public `osdf:///fno4hic` namespace needs no login or token. How to find, download and read the published productions: [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md).

## 7. Jupyter

```bash
source ~/.venvs/js_analysis/bin/activate
cd js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
jupyter notebook jet_wake.ipynb
```

The notebooks name the kernel they were saved with. If Jupyter asks, choose "Python 3 (ipykernel)": started from the activated venv, that is the venv. For a Jupyter elsewhere (VS Code, a JupyterLab of another env), register the venv with `--kernel js_analysis` and choose that kernel. The notebooks read `out/` by default; point them elsewhere with `WAKE_H5=/path/to/<stem>.h5` (`jet_wake.ipynb`) or `HADRON_DIR=/path/to/out` (the `analysis/` notebooks).

**Headless machines:** the visualization renders off-screen and `check_env.py` tests that it works. If it fails on a machine without a display, run under `xvfb-run` (Linux, `apt install xvfb`).

## Without a checkout: the pyjetscape wheel

The `jetscape` package with the same analysis packages also comes as a pure-Python wheel, part of every [xscape-macos release](https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases). It installs on any platform, in any Python 3.10+ environment:

```bash
uv pip install "pyjetscape[analysis] @ https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos/releases/download/v1.5/pyjetscape-1.5-py3-none-any.whl"
```

Quote the argument: zsh treats `[...]` as a pattern. The readers, `HadronArray`, the awkward views and the notebooks work with it; running X-SCAPE does not. Unlike the setup script, it does not install pyvista (pelicanfs is in `[analysis]` from 1.5; with the older 0.2.0 wheel, pyjetscape 1.4, add it with `uv pip install pelicanfs "aiowebdav2<1"`), and it does not fetch the EoS tables: download both as in the conda tab above and point `MUSIC_EOS_TABLE` at one of them (the tools take the other from the same directory).

## Threads and memory

The analysis tools are mostly single-threaded Python. Parallelise over files with processes, and keep processes × threads at or below the number of cores.

| tool                                               | parallel with                                             | memory                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HadronFileReader`                                 | one process; split a campaign by `events=` over processes | the units it reads: a background of 2000 oversamples is ~14 M hadrons, ~1.5 GB with the derived kinematics (estimate) |
| `wake_observables.py -j N`, `wake_hadrons.py -j N` | N processes over files                                    | about +0.5 GB per process for the read-ahead (`wake_observables.py`)                                                  |
| `run_h5toROOT.py -j N`                             | N processes                                               | ~80 B per hadron of the largest tag: ~3.5 GB for a 15-event file at 400 oversamples                                   |
| `hadron_distributions.C` (RDataFrame)              | its `threads` argument                                    |                                                                                                                       |
| numpy (OpenBLAS)                                   | `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`                                    | set it to 1 when running with `-j`, or the processes oversubscribe the cores                                          |
| Blosc decompression (h5py)                         | `BLOSC_NTHREADS`                                          | helps little; leave it unset with `-j`                                                                                |

Measured times and more: [`docs/README_analysis.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/README_analysis.md#threads-and-memory).

## Next: start analysing

[Analyse](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md) walks through what a production writes and how to read it: hadrons, jets with FastJet, hydro and hadrons together, O+O, and ROOT.

# Source build (conda)

The source build compiles X-SCAPE (branch `contrib`) with its external packages and js-contrib inside the tree, in the `js_fno` conda environment. You need it to change C++ (X-SCAPE modules, MUSIC4GPU, iSS, 3dMCGlauber), the PyJetscape bindings or the `jetscape` package, to use the C++ FNO hydro (FnoHydro, through LibTorch) or the live PyTorch FNO hydro, and for ROOT output. If you only want to run productions, write scripts and Python modules, or analyse, the [container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) or the [Mac wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) gets you there without compiling.

**Why conda.** One conda prefix holds every C++ dependency (Boost, Pythia8, HDF5, GSL, HepMC3, FastJet, ROOT) next to Python, PyTorch, pybind11 and the analysis packages, so CMake finds them all without system packages. That matters most on Apple Silicon (native ARM builds, PyTorch with MPS) and on Linux `aarch64` (AWS Graviton, ARM servers, GB10), where several JETSCAPE dependencies are missing from the usual package managers; conda-forge has native builds of all of them.

The order of the steps: get the sources, make the environment, fetch the external packages, configure and build, make `jetscape` importable, run the tests.

## Requirements

**Linux:**

- x86_64 or aarch64.
- For MUSIC on the GPU: an NVIDIA GPU with its driver and the CUDA toolkit (`nvcc`). Without them, MUSIC builds and runs on the CPU.
- git, and conda (the install script offers to install Miniconda if `conda` isn't found).
- On a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, the [dev container](#the-dev-container-linux-nvidia) is an alternative to steps 2 to 4's environment.

**macOS:**

- An Apple Silicon Mac. PyTorch from PyPI (the latest release) and MLX need macOS 14 or later.
- Xcode with its Metal toolchain, for MUSIC on the GPU (`-DUSE_METAL=ON`).
- git, and conda (the install script offers to install Miniconda if `conda` isn't found).

The Mac wheel and a source build on one Mac

They can coexist, but use them in separate Terminal windows: the source build's conda environment and variables (`PYTHONPATH`, `XSCAPE`, ...) must not be active where the wheel's environment runs.

## 1. Get X-SCAPE and js-contrib

js-contrib is built inside X-SCAPE's tree, from `external_packages/js-contrib`. X-SCAPE must be on its `contrib` branch: `get_js_contrib.sh`, the `USE_JS_*` options and the hooks the bindings use exist only there, not on `main` or in the original JETSCAPE.

```bash
git clone -b contrib https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE.git
cd X-SCAPE/external_packages
./get_js_contrib.sh            # clones https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib into js-contrib/
```

## 2. Create the `js_fno` environment

Run the scripts from the js-contrib checkout inside the tree: they finish with an editable `pip install -e` of PyJetscape and FastHydro from that checkout, so the `jetscape` package you import is the one you build.

```bash
cd X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib
bash utils/conda_install/test_js_fno_build_env.sh          # dry run: is every package reachable?
```

**Linux:**

```bash
bash utils/conda_install/install_js_fno_build_minimal.sh        # CUDA detected from nvcc / nvidia-smi
# bash utils/conda_install/install_js_fno_build_minimal.sh 12.4 # or force a CUDA version
conda activate js_fno
```

**macOS:**

```bash
bash utils/conda_install/install_js_fno_build_minimal.sh none   # CPU/MPS PyTorch from PyPI
conda activate js_fno
```

The dry run prints `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[WARN]` per package and ends with `All checks passed — safe to run install_js_fno_build_minimal.sh.` It takes the same CUDA argument (`none` on a Mac). The install script then creates the environment (Python 3.11) with:

| layer              | packages                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C++ build          | cmake, make, compilers, boost-cpp, zlib, hdf5, pythia8, hepmc3, fastjet, gsl, openmpi                                                                                 |
| ROOT               | `root>=6.34,<6.38` from conda-forge                                                                                                                                   |
| PyTorch            | torch, torchvision: CUDA wheels from download.pytorch.org, or CPU/MPS wheels with `none`                                                                              |
| analysis and tests | numpy, scipy, matplotlib, h5py, hdf5plugin, pandas, JupyterLab, ipykernel, vector, pybind11, pytest, ...; with pip: neuraloperator, uproot, awkward, pyvista, imageio |
| MLX                | Apple Silicon only                                                                                                                                                    |
| js-contrib         | `pip install -e` of PyJetscape and FastHydro                                                                                                                          |

Arguments and settings, the same for all install scripts:

|                          |                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1st argument             | the CUDA version for the PyTorch wheels (`12.4`, `13.0`, ...), or `none`; omitted: detected |
| 2nd argument             | where to install Miniconda if `conda` isn't found (default `~/miniconda3`)                  |
| `JS_FNO_ENV_NAME=<name>` | another environment name, e.g. a new install next to a working `js_fno`                     |
| `JS_FNO_FORCE=1`         | replace an existing environment of that name (otherwise the script stops)                   |
| `JS_FNO_NO_EDITABLE=1`   | skip the final editable install of PyJetscape and FastHydro                                 |
| `JS_FNO_NO_MLX=1`        | skip MLX on Apple Silicon                                                                   |

For exact reproducibility there are pinned variants in `utils/conda_install/pinned/` (`install_js_fno_build_pinned.sh`, Python 3.11.9, torch 2.4.1, ROOT 6.36.14, ...). Details: [`utils/conda_install/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/conda_install/README.md).

## 3. Fetch the external packages

Each external package has a download script in `X-SCAPE/external_packages/`, pinned to a tested commit.

```bash
cd X-SCAPE/external_packages
./get_music4gpu.sh      # MUSIC with GPU backends (CUDA, Metal), + its hotQCD EoS tables
./get_iSS.sh            # iSS particlization, + its EoS and delta-f tables
./get_3dglauber.sh      # 3dMCGlauber initial state, + LHAPDF
./get_lbtTab.sh         # LBT's scattering tables (1.2 GB), needed at run time
```

| script              | for                                                | CMake flag                                                                        |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_music4gpu.sh`  | MUSIC on the GPU (MUSIC4GPU, branch `XSCAPE`)      | `-DUSE_MUSIC=ON` with `-DUSE_CUDA=ON` or `-DUSE_METAL=ON`                         |
| `get_music.sh`      | MUSIC on the CPU only (the upstream package)       | `-DUSE_MUSIC=ON` alone                                                            |
| `get_iSS.sh`        | iSS (hadronization of the stored surfaces)         | `-DUSE_ISS=ON`                                                                    |
| `get_3dglauber.sh`  | 3dMCGlauber (also needed for iColored and iMATTER) | `-DUSE_3DGlauber=ON`                                                              |
| `get_lbtTab.sh`     | LBT tables                                         | none; run it **before** configuring, so CMake links them into the build directory |
| `get_js_contrib.sh` | js-contrib (step 1)                                | `-DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON`                                                             |

After `git pull` of X-SCAPE

The `get_*.sh` scripts carry the pinned commit of each package. When a pull changes a pin (`git diff` on `external_packages/get_*.sh`), bring that package to the new commit (or fetch it again) and rebuild; a pull alone doesn't update the packages already in `external_packages/`.

## 4. Configure and build

Build into a directory called **`build_gpu`** at the top of the X-SCAPE tree: the production scripts (`--build`) and `jetscape.paths` look there by default. With another name, pass `--build` to the scripts or set `JETSCAPE_BUILD`.

**Linux, NVIDIA GPU:**

```bash
conda activate js_fno
cd X-SCAPE
cmake -S . -B build_gpu -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DUSE_MUSIC=ON -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DUSE_ISS=ON -DUSE_3DGlauber=ON \
  -DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON -DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON
cmake --build build_gpu -j"$(nproc)"
```

MUSIC4GPU compiles for the GPU it finds at configure time (`CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` defaults to `native`). On a node without a GPU, give the architectures explicitly, e.g. `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80` for an A100. If nvcc fails to find the CUDA headers with conda's compilers, use the system GCC as nvcc's host compiler, `export CUDAHOSTCXX=/usr/bin/g++`, as the container builds do.

**macOS, Metal:**

```bash
conda activate js_fno
cd X-SCAPE
cmake -S . -B build_gpu -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DUSE_MUSIC=ON -DUSE_METAL=ON -DUSE_ISS=ON -DUSE_3DGlauber=ON \
  -DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON -DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON
cmake --build build_gpu -j"$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
```

**CPU only:**

```bash
conda activate js_fno
cd X-SCAPE
cmake -S . -B build_gpu -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DUSE_MUSIC=ON -DUSE_ISS=ON -DUSE_3DGlauber=ON \
  -DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON -DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON
cmake --build build_gpu -j"$(nproc)"
```

MUSIC without a GPU flag is the CPU MUSIC from `get_music.sh`. Its results differ systematically from the GPU path, so don't mix CPU and GPU events in one campaign.

The flags:

| flag                               | what it does                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-DUSE_MUSIC=ON`                   | builds MUSIC; **required** for the bindings, which include MUSIC's wrapper                                                                                                                   |
| `-DUSE_CUDA=ON` / `-DUSE_METAL=ON` | MUSIC from MUSIC4GPU on an NVIDIA GPU / on Apple Silicon (mutually exclusive; Metal only on macOS)                                                                                           |
| `-DUSE_ISS=ON`                     | iSS; needed for hadronization (`hadronize.py`, `run_hadronize.py`)                                                                                                                           |
| `-DUSE_3DGlauber=ON`               | 3dMCGlauber; **required** for the bindings: without it iColoredHadronization and iMATTER are not compiled and `pyjetscape_core` fails to load (`undefined symbol ... iColoredHadronization`) |
| `-DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON`              | builds js-contrib from `external_packages/js-contrib`                                                                                                                                        |
| `-DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON`           | the Python bindings `pyjetscape_core`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `-DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON`            | the C++ FnoHydro module (LibTorch, about 2 GB, and ROOT); see below                                                                                                                          |
| `-DJS_PIP_INSTALL_PYJETSCAPE=ON`   | runs `pip install -e` of PyJetscape on every build                                                                                                                                           |
| ROOT                               | used when the environment has it (`js_fno` does): adds the `FastRootBulkWriter` binding (`jetscape.HAS_ROOT`). Without ROOT everything else builds and `HAS_ROOT` is `False`                 |

CMake finds Boost, Pythia8, HDF5, ROOT and the rest in the active conda environment by itself. After a change to the bindings only, rebuild just them: `cmake --build build_gpu --target pyjetscape_core`.

**FnoHydro (C++ FNO hydro).** Add `-DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON` and PyTorch's CMake files to the prefix path:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_gpu ... -DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX;$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.utils.cmake_prefix_path)')"
```

The live PyTorch FNO hydro (`PyFNOHydro`) needs no extra flag, only PyTorch in the Python environment, which `js_fno` has: [Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md).

## 5. Make `jetscape` importable

The build writes the compiled extension `pyjetscape_core*.so` into `external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/python/jetscape/`. The install script of step 2 already installed that package in editable mode, so with `conda activate js_fno` it imports from anywhere:

```bash
python -c "import jetscape as js; print(js.HAS_CORE, js.pyjetscape_core.MUSIC_BACKEND)"
# -> True music4gpu-cuda      (Linux)    or    True music4gpu-metal   (macOS)
```

`HAS_CORE` is `True` once the compiled extension loads; `MUSIC_BACKEND` names the MUSIC it was built against (`music` for the CPU build). In another environment, make the package importable in one of two ways:

```bash
# editable install (recommended, e.g. for Jupyter)
pip install -e X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape
# or, without installing
export PYTHONPATH="/path/to/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/python:$PYTHONPATH"
```

The compiled core must match that environment's Python version (the one it was built with).

- **`PYTHIA8DATA`:** the compiled core needs it, and `conda activate js_fno` sets it. Without it `import jetscape` aborts with `Assertion 'InternalHelperPythia.particleData.isParticle(id)' failed`.
- **Import order with PyTorch and ROOT:** both ship their own `libomp`. Import `torch` before `jetscape` and ROOT (on macOS, `import jetscape` does this for you); if you see a segfault at import, check the order first.

## 6. Run the tests

```bash
cd X-SCAPE
pytest external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/tests -q
```

Most of the Python tooling is tested without a build; the tests that need the compiled core are skipped when it doesn't load. FastHydro and Visualization have their own suites in `contribs/FastHydro/tests` and `contribs/Visualization/tests`.

## The dev container (Linux, NVIDIA)

On Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, the dev image `jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev` holds the same build environment as `js_fno`, ready-made: CUDA, a conda environment (`xscape`, already on `PATH`), PyTorch and the C++ dependencies, but **no sources**. Mount your X-SCAPE checkout (with its external packages fetched, steps 1 and 3) and build inside it with the commands of step 4.

| tag     | GPUs                                   |
| ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `cu126` | GH200, H100, A100, RTX 20/30/40xx      |
| `cu132` | the above plus Blackwell (GB200, GB10) |

```bash
docker pull jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev:cu126
docker run --rm -it --gpus all -v "$PWD/X-SCAPE:/workspace/X-SCAPE" \
  jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev:cu126
# inside: cd /workspace/X-SCAPE, then step 4
```

The image starts in `/workspace` and sets `CUDAHOSTCXX` for nvcc. It is published for amd64 and arm64, but has not been tested on aarch64 yet; there, use the conda environment. Image details: [`utils/BuildContainerDev.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/BuildContainerDev.md).

## Linux aarch64

On ARM servers (AWS Graviton, GH200, GB10) the conda environment is the tested way to build: conda-forge has native `aarch64` builds of every C++ dependency, and the CUDA 12.x PyTorch wheels run on a CUDA 13 driver. To run productions without building, the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) has arm64 images (`cu126`, `cu130`).

## Other ways to build js-contrib

js-contrib can also be built standalone against an X-SCAPE build tree or an installed X-SCAPE prefix (Paths B and C of the [js-contrib README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/README.md#installation)); for the Python bindings that route does not work at present, so use the in-tree build above. For X-SCAPE checkouts older than the `contrib` integration there is a manual patch recipe (Path A′ of the same README), kept for legacy checkouts.

## Troubleshooting

| symptom                                                                                    | cause and fix                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `conda: command not found` after the install                                               | the installer doesn't edit your shell config: run the printed init command, e.g. `~/miniconda3/bin/conda init zsh`, and open a new terminal        |
| `Environment 'js_fno' exists already`                                                      | remove it (`conda env remove -n js_fno`), replace it with `JS_FNO_FORCE=1`, or install next to it with `JS_FNO_ENV_NAME=js_fno_new`                |
| CMake doesn't find ROOT on macOS                                                           | activate the environment before `cmake`; if it still fails, add `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${CONDA_PREFIX}"`                                            |
| `pyjetscape_core` fails to load: `undefined symbol ... iColoredHadronization`              | configure with `-DUSE_3DGlauber=ON`                                                                                                                |
| `Assertion 'InternalHelperPythia.particleData.isParticle(id)' failed` on `import jetscape` | `PYTHIA8DATA` not set: `conda activate js_fno`                                                                                                     |
| `MPS: False` for PyTorch on Apple Silicon                                                  | the environment was made without `none`, or Python runs under Rosetta: `python -c "import platform; print(platform.machine())"` must print `arm64` |
| `JobDir: not found: .../music_input`                                                       | the build directory is not `build_gpu`: set `JETSCAPE_BUILD` or pass `--build`                                                                     |

Step-by-step reference for the environment and the workflows it covers: [`contribs/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/README.md); the bindings: [`contribs/PyJetscape/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/README.md).
