With `build_gpu` built and `jetscape` importing, [run your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md).
# Run

# Running the productions

A *production* is a set of ready-made scripts that run one physics setup of X-SCAPE many times and write the results as HDF5 files for analysis and for training the ML hydro surrogates. This section shows how to run them: a first event, the two-stage Au+Au jet production, O+O with initial-state radiation, Z+jet and other collision systems, and how to scale up to clusters with many GPUs and share the outputs on the OSDF. You need one of the two ready-made setups, the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) (Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, or an HPC cluster) or the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) (Apple Silicon Mac), or a [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

## The productions

All productions live in [`contribs/PyJetscape/example/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example), each in a folder with a driver script, a user XML in `example/config/`, and a `run_jobs.sh` for campaigns. In the container they are under `/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example`; on a Mac `xscape-examples` copies them into a directory of yours.

| production                                                      | physics                                                                                                                                                                         | writes                                                                                                                                | page                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prod_AuAu_0_10`                                                | 0–10 % Au+Au at 200 GeV: 3D MC-Glauber strings, MUSIC on the GPU, no jet                                                                                                        | hydro evolutions on a chosen output grid, in the FNO4d training format (`run_prod.py`)                                                | [below](#hydro-only-prod_auau_0_10)                                                                                         |
| `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`                                            | the same medium with a jet: PythiaGun, Matter + LBT, the causal liquefier feeding the energy lost back into a second MUSIC run                                                  | a background/jet **pair** of hydro evolutions per event, the freeze-out surfaces and final partons, and (in stage 2) the hadron files | [Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md)                                                 |
| `prod_OO_isr`                                                   | O+O at 200 GeV with initial-state radiation (PythiaIsrGun + iMATTER), one MUSIC run per event, Matter + LBT, iColored jet hadronization                                         | the hydro evolution, the jet hadrons, the bulk hadrons (in the job or later)                                                          | [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md)                                                 |
| Z+jet (`utils/zjet/`)                                           | Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV, 0–30 %, with a Z → ee/μμ trigger, through the jet production's driver                                                                                        | hadron files with the Z and its leptons recorded per event                                                                            | [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md)                                  |
| your own system                                                 | e.g. Pb+Pb at the LHC: a copy of the jet XML with the collision changed                                                                                                         | as `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`                                                                                                               | [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/#another-collision-system-pbpb-at-the-lhc) |
| extra hard scatterings, minimum bias, O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV | any jet production plus the event's other hard scatterings (`--extra-hard`), or the bulk and its hard scatterings alone (`--hard none`); `OO_5360_jet.xml`, `NeNe_5360_jet.xml` | as `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`, plus `<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5`                                                                          | [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md)                                   |

The Pythonic example [`pythonic/oo_workflow.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/pythonic/oo_workflow.py) runs the O+O chain in about 140 lines of Python and is the quickest way to see the whole chain work: [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md).

## The general shape

Every production works the same way.

- **A driver and a user XML.** The driver (`run_prod_jet.py`, `run_prod_oo_isr.py`, `run_prod.py`) runs *one job*: one seed, N events, one set of output files. The physics is in the user XML; the driver takes it (or yours, with `--user-xml`), fills in the job (events, seed, the hard process and its pT̂ windows, what to store), checks it, and writes the XML it ran next to the output (`<stem>.xml`) and into the files.
- **`run_jobs.sh` for campaigns.** It runs many jobs, `-j P` at a time on one GPU, each in its own working directory, and is resumable: run the same command again and finished jobs are skipped.

```text
./run_jobs.sh [-j P] [--mps] [--stagger S] [--campaign NAME] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB FIRST_SEED [OUTDIR] [driver options]
```

- **Seeds.** `FIRST_SEED 0` gives every job a new seed drawn from OS entropy and checked against the seed registry `seeds_used.tsv` next to OUTDIR, so two campaigns never share a collision. `FIRST_SEED > 0` gives exactly those seeds, for reproducing a file or comparing settings on the same events. The seed that ran is stored in every file, and `--seed <it>` reproduces the file bit for bit.
- **Stages.** The expensive part, hydro and jets, runs on a GPU. Hadronization, which needs only the stored freeze-out surfaces and final partons, runs later on CPUs, as often as wanted. Productions with little oversampling can make the hadrons in the GPU job instead and skip the second stage.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    X["user XML<br/>+ driver options"] --> S1
    subgraph S1 ["Stage 1: GPU"]
        R["run_jobs.sh<br/>→ driver, one job per seed"]
    end
    S1 --> P["stem.h5<br/>hydro (pair)"]
    S1 --> Q["stem_particlize.h5<br/>surfaces + partons"]
    S1 -.->|"--hadrons-only,<br/>O+O --bulk-hadrons"| H
    Q --> S2
    subgraph S2 ["Stage 2: CPU"]
        Z["run_hadronize.py<br/>→ hadronize.py"]
    end
    S2 --> H["stem_hadrons_*.h5<br/>hadron files"]
    P --> F["FNO training,<br/>hydro analysis"]
    H --> A["analysis venv,<br/>ROOT export"]
    P & Q & H -.-> O[("OSDF<br/>osdf:///fno4hic")]
```

**Why two stages.** Hydro needs a GPU; sampling hadrons from a freeze-out surface (iSS) and fragmenting partons (Pythia) does not, and it is cheap per sample. Storing the surfaces, with their full viscous information, lets you choose the number of oversamples, the hadron selection and the precision after the expensive part is done, on any CPU nodes, without rerunning the hydro. The result is the same as hadronizing in the job, checked bit for bit.

## Hydro only (`prod_AuAu_0_10`)

The simplest production writes 0–10 % Au+Au hydro evolutions (no jet) straight to FNO4d training HDF5 on an output grid chosen in a YAML file (default `example/config/grid_fno.yaml`). It is the training-data production for the FNO surrogates and uses the same `run_jobs.sh` as the others:

```bash
cd prod_AuAu_0_10                                # in your copy of the examples
python run_prod.py --events 10 --seed 1          # -> out/AuAu_0_10_seed0001.h5
python run_prod.py --events 1 --seed 1 --grid my_grid.yaml --dry-run   # check a grid
./run_jobs.sh --campaign mb_a 20 25 0            # 20 jobs x 25 events, unique seeds
```

Each job writes `<stem>.h5` (the evolutions), `.xml`, `.json` and, through `run_jobs.sh`, `.log`. Full options: the folder's [README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10/README.md). What the files hold: [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/index.md).

## What a job writes

| file                                            | written by                                     | content                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<stem>.h5`                                     | stage 1                                        | the hydro evolution (Au+Au jet: the background and jet-leg pair) on the output grid                      |
| `<stem>_particlize.h5`                          | stage 1 (`--write-particlize`; O+O by default) | the freeze-out surfaces, the final partons and the shower initiators: the input to hadronization         |
| `<stem>_hadrons_{bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag}.h5` | stage 2, or the job itself                     | the hadrons: iSS on the jet-leg surface (bulk + wake), on the background, and the fragmented jet partons |
| `<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5`                  | as above, only with `--extra-hard`             | the fragments of the event's other hard scatterings                                                      |
| `<stem>.xml`, `.json`, `.log`                   | stage 1                                        | the job XML as run, a summary (seed, events, cross sections, checks), the log                            |

The stem is `AuAu_0_10_jet_seedNNNN` for an explicit seed and `AuAu_0_10_jet_<campaign>_NNNN` (job number) in a `FIRST_SEED 0` campaign; O+O files start with `OO_isr_`. The formats are described in [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/index.md).

## Next steps

- [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/index.md): one O+O event through the whole chain, then two Au+Au jet events.
- [Au+Au jets (two stages)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md): the main production, from the first job to a campaign.
- [Extra hard scatterings, O+O and Ne+Ne](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md): the event's other hard scatterings, minimum bias, the light ions at the LHC.
- [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md): SLURM, several GPUs, `jobmon.py`.
- [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md): download existing productions or share yours.

# Au+Au jets in two stages

`prod_AuAu_0_10_jet` is the main production: 0–10 % Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV (3D MC-Glauber strings, MUSIC on the GPU) with a hard jet whose energy loss feeds back into the medium. Each event is written as a **pair** of hydro evolutions, the background and the same event with the jet, and, for hadron-level work, as the freeze-out surfaces and partons that a second stage turns into hadrons on CPUs. Use it for the medium response to jets (the wake) in hydro and in hadrons, for jet observables with a realistic background, and as training data for the ML hydro surrogates. This page goes from a single job to a campaign; the first two events are in [Your first event](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/first-event/#2-two-auau-jet-events).

## How an event is made

```text
IS (3dMCGlauber) -> Hard (PythiaGun) -> NullPreDynamics
   -> MUSIC_1                    background leg               -> arr_bg
   -> Liquefier + Eloss          Matter + LBT on MUSIC_1's medium -> droplets
   -> MUSIC_2                    the same strings + the droplets  -> arr
```

**Why pairs.** Both legs start from the same initial condition and are bit-identical until the first droplet deposits, so `arr - arr_bg` is the jet's effect on the medium and nothing else: no event-by-event fluctuation of the bulk to subtract statistically. The same holds at hadron level: iSS on the jet leg's surface minus iSS on the background's.

The background leg doesn't depend on the jet. So a background can be **shared** by several jets (`--reuse N`, or several pT̂ windows with `--pthat-bins`): MUSIC_1 runs once per background, MUSIC_2 once per jet. MUSIC_2 also starts from MUSIC_1's saved state just before the first droplet can deposit (τ ≈ 1 fm/c), with bit-identical output; this is on by default. The physics settings (EOS, liquefier, Matter and LBT) are discussed in [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md).

## 1. Checks before a campaign

The driver `run_prod_jet.py` runs one job: one seed, N events. Run these from the production folder (in the container: `/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet`, Docker's start directory; on a Mac: your `xscape-examples` copy), with the output under a directory you can write:

```bash
# 1. the XML and the grid, checked; the job XML written, no event
python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 1 --dry-run --outdir out_val

# 2. null test: MUSIC_2 without the liquefier must reproduce the background bit for bit
python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 901 --write-particlize both --no-deposit --outdir out_val

# 3. validation: the hadrons are also made in the job, to compare with stage 2
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 900 --write-particlize both --validate-inline --outdir out_val
```

- **Null test.** `arr == arr_bg` in every frame (`diag/frames_identical == ntau` in the pair file), and the two stored surfaces are identical:

```bash
python -c "import numpy as np; from jetscape.particlize_h5 import ParticlizeFile as P; \
p = P('out_val/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0901_particlize.h5'); \
print(np.array_equal(p.surface('jet', 0), p.surface('bg', 0)))"      # True
```

- **Validation.** `hadronize.py --use-stored-seeds` on the validation file must reproduce the in-job hadrons bit for bit (run it without `--keep-bits-*` or `--eta-max`). The script is in *Checks before a campaign* of the [folder's README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md#checks-before-a-campaign). `--validate-inline` changes the jet sample of a seed (it adds tasks, which shifts the energy loss's random streams): use it for validation jobs only.
- **One event with a jet:** `diag/n_droplets > 0`, and the legs differ only after the first deposit.

With pT̂ windows, also run the null test with the windows (`--pthat-bins … --no-deposit`). For hardware checks (GPU found, settings arrived) see [Checking a run](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#checking-a-run).

## 2. Stage 1: hydro and jets on the GPU

### `run_jobs.sh`

```text
./run_jobs.sh [-j P] [--mps] [--stagger S] [--campaign NAME] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB FIRST_SEED [OUTDIR] [run_prod_jet.py options]
```

| argument          |                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NJOBS`           | number of jobs = number of output files; total events = NJOBS × EVENTS_PER_JOB                                     |
| `-j P`            | at most P jobs at once (default 1); it doesn't create jobs                                                         |
| `FIRST_SEED`      | `0`: a new seed per job, never repeated (a campaign, the usual choice); `> 0`: seeds FIRST_SEED, FIRST_SEED+1, …   |
| `--campaign NAME` | names the files `AuAu_0_10_jet_NAME_0001.h5`, …; without it, the start time                                        |
| `OUTDIR`          | the output directory: the argument after FIRST_SEED (default `./out`), **not** `--outdir`. One campaign per OUTDIR |
| after OUTDIR      | options for every job, e.g. `--write-particlize both`, `--pthat-bins …`                                            |

- **Restarting:** run the same command again. Jobs whose `.json` says complete are skipped, unfinished ones are redone (in a seed-0 campaign with a new seed). The skip test looks only at file names and event counts: give every setting its own OUTDIR.
- **Seed registry:** `seeds_used.tsv` in OUTDIR's parent, shared by the campaigns side by side there, under a lock.
- **A seed is a set of collisions.** The same seed gives the same background in every campaign, whatever the jet settings. That is what paired comparisons want, and wrong for campaigns meant as more statistics: use `FIRST_SEED 0` for those.
- `--mps` (CUDA only) lets the P jobs share the GPU through CUDA MPS; `--stagger S` starts the first P jobs S seconds apart. Both are discussed in [Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#launch-settings).
- At the end, `OUTDIR/run_jobs.finished` is written; each job leaves `<stem>.log`, `<stem>.json` and `<stem>.xml`.
- `--eloss-threads -1` runs the showers of an event in parallel (X-SCAPE `<Eloss><nThreads>`; off by default here). It changes the showers of a seed, and gains nothing measurable here: the showers take ~0.1 s of a ~19 s event. It pays for [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/#settings), where it is the default; details in the [folder's README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md#parallel-showers).

### What to store

| option                                      | stores                                                                                                                  | use                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default)                                   | the hydro pair `<stem>.h5`                                                                                              | FNO training data, hydro-level wake                                                    |
| `--write-particlize both`                   | + `<stem>_particlize.h5`: both freeze-out surfaces (full viscous information), the final partons, the shower initiators | hadron level: jet − background. **Add it to every job that should get hadrons later**  |
| `--write-particlize jet`                    | + the jet leg's surface only                                                                                            | the jet event's hadrons without background subtraction (turns the MUSIC_2 restart off) |
| `--write-particlize both --particlize-only` | only the particlize file, no pair file                                                                                  | hadrons without the hydro history: ~2.5× less disk, ~3 s per event faster              |
| `--hadrons-only`                            | only hadron files, made in the job; no stage 2                                                                          | little or no oversampling ([below](#hadrons-in-the-job-hadrons-only))                  |

The pair file is unchanged, byte for byte, by `--write-particlize`.

### pT̂ windows and shared backgrounds

A background costs about as much as a jet leg. For a real campaign, share each background among several jets in several pT̂ windows:

```bash
... --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5
```

- **How.** One Pythia per window, each with its own seed and cross section; event *i* uses window *i* mod K. `--reuse` is set to K × M (here 3 × 5 = 15), so one background serves 15 events, 5 in each window.
- **EVENTS_PER_JOB must be a multiple of K × M** (15, 30, 45, …).
- **Cost.** An event costs about (1 + 1/(K·M)) / 2 of an event with its own background: 0.53 for K·M = 15.
- **Cross sections.** Each window records its σ; combine windows with those weights ([Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md)). Results stitched over windows have errors correlated through the shared backgrounds; per-window results and jet − background don't.
- `--reuse N` alone shares a background among N jets of one window. `--pthat-min/--pthat-max` set a single window (default 50–70 GeV); `--hard pgun --pgun-pt P` shoots one parton (`--pgun-y`, `--pgun-id`, and `--pgun-grid 20,50,100:0,1,2 --pgun-per-point N` for several (pT, y) points on one background).

### The parton rapidity cut

At low pT̂ the jets spread far in rapidity, and much hydro time would go to events that cannot reach a mid-rapidity measurement. `--parton-ymax Y` keeps only events whose shower-initiating partons pass a rapidity cut; rejected events are regenerated in Pythia before any shower or hydro, and the cross sections are corrected by the kept/tried fraction.

| `--parton-y-mode`   | keeps the event if            | for |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- | --- |
| `leading` (default) | the hardest parton has        | y   |
| `both`              | the two hardest have          | y   |
| `any`               | either of the two hardest has | y   |

The cut only selects events; the analysis applies its own. So Y must be looser than the analysis acceptance: `--parton-ymax 0.6` (leading) is complete for jets up to |η_jet| ≈ 0.4–0.5; for inclusive R = 0.4 jets at |η_jet| < 0.6 use `--parton-ymax 0.7 --parton-y-mode any`. For wake hadrons at |η| < η_max, about Y ≈ η_max + 1 with `any`.

### Defaults worth knowing

- **MUSIC's late time step.** From τ = 3 fm/c MUSIC steps 0.05 fm/c instead of 0.02. The stored frames stay at 0.1 fm/c; the medium changes at 1e-3 and the hadron level by less than ±2 %. **Keep one setting per campaign**: `--late-dtau 0` gives a constant step.
- **MUSIC_2 from MUSIC_1's state.** Bit-identical output, ~25 core-s less per jet event; `--no-music2-restart` turns it off. Every job log says `restart` at the start, on or off.
- **EOS 91** (hotQCD with the SMASH hadron list), which iSS decays itself; `--eos 9` only to rerun older campaigns.
- **The liquefier's frame** is the Bjorken frame (`<CausalLiquefier><frame>bjorken</frame>`, [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/#5-energymomentum-deposition-the-causalliquefier)): forward droplets spread as midrapidity ones do. Campaigns made before 2026-11 used the lab frame, which deposits forward droplets displaced and far too narrow; `--liquefier-frame lab` reproduces them. Only droplets at η_s = 0 deposit the same in both: the lab frame pulls the others toward midrapidity (by 0.4 units already at η_s = 1), so the wake at |η_s| < 1 differs by 3 % in energy at RHIC, and by 19 % for Z+jet events at the LHC, where most droplets are made forward. `--liquefier-frame fluid` diffuses each droplet in the rest frame of the background fluid where it was made. It agrees with the Bjorken frame along η_s and in energy, but moves late deposits outward with the radial flow; FastHydro does not support it yet. **Do not mix frames in a wake analysis.** The pair file records it (`liquefier_frame`).
- **To choose it:** `run_prod_jet.py ... --liquefier-frame fluid`, or the same flag after `run_jobs.sh`'s arguments (`./run_jobs.sh -j 2 20 25 0 out_fluid --liquefier-frame fluid`).
- **Use a new output directory per frame:** `run_jobs.sh` skips completed jobs whatever their frame.
- **Needs an X-SCAPE with the option.** The script refuses an older build; images from before 2026-11 have only the lab frame.
- **The frames compared** on the same events (Au+Au, LHC Z+jet, single quarks at fixed rapidity and energy): `example/liquefier_frame_test/`. Per jet, the lab error depends on the jet's rapidity, not its energy. The fluid frame makes the wake about 1.5 % harder.
- **The output grid** of the pair file is `example/config/grid_fno.yaml` (64 × 64 × 32 cells, x, y ±12.2 fm, η_s ±4.84); `--grid FILE` for another. Never mix grids in one training set.

### The event's other hard scatterings

`--extra-hard` adds the event's other hard scatterings above a threshold p₀ (the XML's `<extraHard><pTHatMin>`, 10 GeV for Au+Au) to every jet event, showered in the jet leg with the trigger; `--hard none --extra-hard` gives minimum-bias events. At 200 GeV they are rare (~0.13 per 0–10 % event above 10 GeV), at the LHC they are not (~15 per 0–10 % Pb+Pb event above 15 GeV). Without the option nothing changes, and with it the trigger, `jet_frag` and `bulk_bg` stay bit-identical for the same seed. Everything about it: [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md).

Every option of `run_prod_jet.py`: the *Options* table of the [folder's README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md#options).

## 3. Stage 2: hadronization on CPUs

`hadronize.py` turns one particlize file into hadrons: iSS samples both stored surfaces (with viscous corrections), Pythia fragments the stored partons. It needs no GPU and no MUSIC. `run_hadronize.py` runs it over a whole campaign, `-j P` files at a time, and skips files whose hadrons are complete:

**Docker:**

```bash
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126          # the image of stage 1
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_a -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

**Apptainer:**

```bash
PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
apptainer exec --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" \
  xscape_prod.sif ./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_a -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

**Mac / source build:**

```bash
python run_hadronize.py out_had -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50
```

Inputs are directories, particlize files or quoted globs. Per production file it writes `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5`, `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5` and `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5` next to it.

| option                               |                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-j P`                               | processes at once, ~1.4–1.7 GB and one core each                                                                                    |
| `--oversample N`                     | iSS samples per jet-leg surface (default 100)                                                                                       |
| `--n-frag K`                         | Pythia fragmentations of the partons per event                                                                                      |
| `--oversample-bg auto`               | a background shared by N events gets N × the samples: the optimal split for jet − background under `--reuse`                        |
| `--oversample-bg per-pthat-bin`      | for `--pthat-bins` campaigns analysed per window: M × the samples (M = `--jets-per-bin`)                                            |
| `--correlated`                       | correlated jet/background sampling: jet − background ~8× less noisy at                                                              |
| `--keep-bits-p B`, `--keep-bits-x B` | round momenta and positions to B mantissa bits: `12` and `8` store 58 % of the bytes with no visible effect on ensemble observables |
| `--eta-max X`, `--charged`, `--no-x` | store only                                                                                                                          |
| `--tags`                             | a subset of `bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag`                                                                                             |
| `--follow`                           | keep running next to a stage 1 that is still writing; stop when its campaign is finished                                            |
| `--dry-run`                          | show the plan only                                                                                                                  |
| `--force`                            | redo complete files (e.g. with other settings)                                                                                      |

Decide the hadron settings once per campaign

The precision (`--keep-bits-*`), the selection (`--eta-max`, `--charged`, `--no-x`) and the background oversampling must be the same for every file: pass the same flags to every call, `--follow` and restarts included. Complete files are skipped whatever settings made them. Nothing is lost for good: the particlize file and the stored seeds reproduce the exact hadrons with `--force`. Keep the validation job at full precision and without cuts.

**Alongside production.** Start `run_hadronize.py --follow` next to `run_jobs.sh`; it hadronizes each file as its job completes and stops when the campaign writes `run_jobs.finished`. On a machine whose cores are the limit, its cores come out of stage 1's rate, so on clusters stage 2 usually runs separately on CPU nodes ([SLURM](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#stage-2-on-cpu-nodes)). Only the particlize files need to travel there: they are self-contained.

### Hadrons in the job (`--hadrons-only`)

For campaigns with little or no oversampling (1–10 samples per jet event), the hadrons can be made in the GPU job itself: `run_prod_jet.py --hadrons-only` writes only the three hadron files, the undecayed bulk hadrons (`*_primary.h5`, for SMASH later; `--keep-primaries 0` turns them off) and the `.json`. No pair or particlize file, no stage 2:

```bash
./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --mps 60 45 0 /work/AuAu_ho --reuse 4 --hadrons-only
```

Its options are `hadronize.py`'s (`--oversample`, default 1; `--n-frag`, default 1; `--correlated`; `--eta-max`, `--charged`, `--no-x`; the rounding is `--hadron-keep-bits-p/-x`). The hadrons equal those of the two-stage path for the same seed, bit for bit. What is lost: no surfaces (no new samples later) and no hydro history. On the GB10 it cost ~4 % in events/h against `--particlize-only` and wrote 0.64 MB per event, against ~160 MB in two stages.

## 4. A realistic campaign

The campaign setting used for the production runs: three pT̂ windows, 5 jets per window per background, the leading parton at |y| < 0.6, everything stored for hadronization.

**Docker:**

```bash
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126          # for a campaign: a dated tag or the digest
mkdir -p ~/prod/lbt_cache
docker run -d --name c1 --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 6 --mps --stagger 12 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 \
    /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
docker logs -f c1             # progress;  docker stop c1 stops it cleanly
```

`-j 6` with 3 threads each suits one GPU with ~24 cores and 64 GB; size `-j` to your machine (~2–3 cores and ~7 GB per job).

**Apptainer:**

```bash
PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
mkdir -p $SCRATCH/prod/lbt_cache
apptainer exec --nv \
  --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 6 --stagger 12 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 \
    /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
```

On a SLURM cluster use the array script instead: [Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#slurm-one-gpu-per-array-task).

**Mac:**

```bash
cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  caffeinate -i ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 ~/xscape/prod/AuAu_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
```

On a Mac, split the cores between the jobs (`-j` × threads ≈ the performance cores) and use `passive`, or several jobs gain nothing; `--mps` is CUDA only. `caffeinate -i` keeps the Mac awake.

That is 67 jobs × 15 events = 1,005 events on 67 backgrounds. Then stage 2, with the background sampled per window and the hadrons rounded:

```bash
./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 -j 16 \
  --oversample 400 --oversample-bg per-pthat-bin --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8
```

400 samples per jet event, 5 × 400 = 2,000 per background and window, 50 fragmentations.

**What to expect.** Measured with the campaign setting:

|                                          |                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores), 10 jobs per GPU | **2,160 events/h** (1,080 per GPU), ~25 s per event in a loaded job                                                                                            |
| GB10, `-j 4 --mps` (earlier code)        | 336 events/h                                                                                                                                                   |
| host memory per job                      | ~6–7 GB with the shared LBT tables; plan 7 GB (5 GB with `--particlize-only`)                                                                                  |
| disk, stage 1                            | **0.243 GB per event** (pair + particlize); 0.097 GB with `--particlize-only`                                                                                  |
| stage 2                                  | ~340 events/h per core at 500 oversamples (10.6 s per event, both legs; 8.8 s with `--correlated`): ~6–7 cores keep up with 2,000 events/h                     |
| disk, hadrons                            | ~100 MB per leg and event at 500 oversamples, full precision; 58 % of that with `--keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8`, and ~60 % of that again with `--eta-max 2` |

On a cluster, the sizing per GPU type and a 12,000-event SLURM example are in [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md); the hardware numbers in [GPU acceleration](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/gpu/index.md).

Pin the image, one per campaign

The moving tags (`cu126`) change with every build, and different builds can differ in the last digits or more. For a campaign use a dated tag (`cu126-<YYYYMMDD>-<commit>`) or the digest, the same one on every machine, and note it: the files don't record which image made them. Run the whole campaign on GPUs: MUSIC's CPU path differs systematically (~0.2 % in multiplicity).

## After the campaign

- **Watch and check it:** `utils/jobmon.py OUTDIR --watch`, and the deposition check `utils/check_deposition.py OUTDIR`, which flags the rare job whose jets deposited far less than the rest: [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#monitoring-a-campaign).
- **Move the files:** `--what h5` (particlize + hadron files) for the analysis, `--what pair` for FNO training: [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md).
- **Analyse:** [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md) (`HadronFileReader`, cross-section weights, jet − background), [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/index.md), [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md) (`run_h5toROOT.py`), [Bulk and flow](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/bulk/index.md) (Nch, [pT], vₙ{2}).

Full details, every option and the measurements: [`prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md) and [`docs/README_2stage.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/README_2stage.md).

# O+O with initial-state radiation

`prod_OO_isr` runs O+O collisions at 200 GeV with X-SCAPE's initial-state radiation (ISR) workflow: the hard scattering's incoming partons are showered backward in time by iMATTER, the 3D MC-Glauber strings are made from what the hard scattering left, MUSIC evolves that medium, and Matter + LBT shower the jets through it. The jet hadrons come from iColoredHadronization, which follows the colour flow of the ISR and the beam remnants; the bulk hadrons from iSS. Use it for small-system studies where the hard process and the bulk come from the same nucleon–nucleon collisions: multiplicity and centrality biases of hard-triggered events, flow, jets in a small medium. The tuned O+O 3D MC-Glauber and MUSIC parameters are those of X-SCAPE's O+O example, tuned at 200 GeV.

## What is different from Au+Au

```text
IS: 3dMCGlauber (O16, positions only)
 -> Hard: PythiaIsrGun at one binary collision
          -> IsrManager / iMATTER       ISR, backward in time
          -> MCGlauberGenString         strings, the hard partons' momentum subtracted
 -> MUSIC                              ONE hydro run per event
 -> Eloss: Matter + LBT in the medium   the final-state shower
 -> JetHadronization: iColored          jet hadrons, in the job
 -> SoftParticlization: iSS             bulk hadrons, in the job or later
```

- **One MUSIC run per event, no pair.** The medium is made from what each event's hard scattering left (its partons' momentum is subtracted from the colliding nucleons), so a medium belongs to one hard event: there is no background leg, no jet − background, no hydro reuse, and no jet deposition into the fluid.
- **Every event is hard-triggered:** exactly one hard scattering, at a binary collision drawn uniformly. `glauber_ncoll` is recorded per event to weight the geometry ([O+O analysis](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md)). Centrality comes from the impact parameter: the default b < 3 fm is about 0–24 % of the O+O cross section.
- **The jet hadrons are made in the job.** iColoredHadronization needs the event's beam remnants and ISR colour connections, which exist only while the job runs. The bulk can be made in the job or later from stored surfaces.
- **Events without a medium:** when the hard collision is the only one, no string is made; Matter showers in vacuum and the bulk unit is empty (`has_medium` 0).
- **The cores set the rate.** An O+O event is small (MUSIC's grid ±10.5 fm), so an O+O job needs ~1.4 GB and ~6 core-s per event; the GPU is far from full.

## Running it

The driver is `run_prod_oo_isr.py` (one job), with the same `run_jobs.sh` as the Au+Au productions: the same seeds, campaign names, seed registry and restarts ([Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/#run_jobssh)).

```bash
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 1 --seed 1 --dry-run      # check the XML/grid, print the plan
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 10 --seed 1               # pT-hat 20-40 GeV, b < 3 fm
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 30 --seed 1 --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --parton-ymax 0.6
./run_jobs.sh 20 25 0                                        # 20 jobs x 25 events, unique seeds
./run_jobs.sh -j 2 20 25 1 out_had --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize
```

The image starts in the Au+Au folder, so point it at the O+O one, or call the scripts by their full path (they find their XML and grid next to themselves):

**Docker:**

```bash
OO=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" -w "$OO" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --mps 32 60 0 /work/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file
```

**Apptainer:**

```bash
OO=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr
apptainer exec --nv --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --pwd "$OO" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 32 60 0 /work/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file
```

**Mac:**

```bash
cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_OO_isr
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 2 --seed 5 --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out_oo
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign oo_a 20 25 0 ~/xscape/prod/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize
```

That is 32 jobs × 60 events, 8 at a time on one GPU, with all hadrons made in the jobs and nothing else kept. Write the output under the bound `/work`: the default `./out` is inside the read-only image. Nothing needs to be set for iMATTER in the container (the image sets `PYTHIA8DATA`), and the LBT table cache and `--stagger` don't apply to these small jobs.

## Hadronization: in the job or afterwards

| setup                                | options                              | files                                                      | afterwards                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **A. everything in the job**         | `--bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize` | `<stem>.h5`, `_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`, `_hadrons_jet_frag.h5` | nothing to do                                   |
| **B. in the job, surfaces kept**     | `--bulk-hadrons 100`                 | A + `_particlize.h5`                                       | more oversamples or other iSS settings any time |
| **C. bulk afterwards** (the default) | none                                 | `<stem>.h5`, `_particlize.h5`, `_hadrons_jet_frag.h5`      | `hadronize.py --tags bulk_bg`                   |

Add `--no-hydro-file` to any of them to leave out the hydro evolution (MUSIC still runs and Matter still reads it). A + `--no-hydro-file` is a hadrons-only job: the usual production setting, at ~0.13 MB per event with 10 oversamples.

For setup C, the bulk is made on CPUs with the Au+Au production's `hadronize.py`, **always with `--tags bulk_bg`** (the jet hadrons were made in the job; it refuses `jet_frag` on these files):

```bash
python ../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/hadronize.py out/OO_isr_seed0001_particlize.h5 \
       --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100
python ../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_hadronize.py out -j 4 --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100
```

In the container, with `-w "$OO"` (Docker) or `--pwd "$OO"` (Apptainer) and without `--gpus`/`--nv`: `../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_hadronize.py /work/OO_a -j 8 --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100`. On SLURM: `PROD=oo` for `utils/slurm_hadronize.sh` ([Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#stage-2-on-cpu-nodes)).

The bulk made in the job and afterwards are sampled alike (both use `config/hadronize.xml`); only the seeds differ. An event at hadron level is unit *i* of the jet file plus unit *i* of the bulk file; the bulk's N oversamples share one fluid.

## Settings

| option                                                   | default                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--pthat-min`, `--pthat-max`                             | 20, 40 GeV              | one pT̂ window                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--pthat-bins A-B,C-D,…`                                 |                         | K windows in one job, one Pythia each, event *i* in window *i* mod K; no background is shared. Use a multiple of K events                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--parton-ymax Y`, `--parton-y-mode {both,any}`          | off, `both`             | regenerate the event until the two outgoing partons of the hard scattering have                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--b-min`, `--b-max`                                     | 0, 3 fm                 | the impact-parameter range (centrality)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--sqrts`                                                | 200 GeV                 | the collision energy (the parameters are tuned at 200 GeV)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--bulk-hadrons N`                                       | 0                       | iSS in the job, N oversamples per event                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--no-particlize`, `--no-hydro-file`, `--no-jet-hadrons` |                         | leave out the particlize file, the hydro file, the jet hadrons                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--eta-max`, `--charged`, `--no-x`, `--keep-bits-p/-x`   |                         | store less, as for `hadronize.py`, on both in-job hadron files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--keep-primaries N`                                     |                         | with `--bulk-hadrons`: also the undecayed bulk hadrons of the first N oversamples, for SMASH later                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--colour-closure MODE`                                  | the XML's (`reconnect`) | how iColored closes colour lines that end in the medium: `reconnect`, `reconnect_global`, `thermal`, `fake`, `none`                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--matter-only`                                          |                         | Matter alone, no LBT and no recoils: a reference for colour studies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--store-hadronization-input`                            |                         | keep what was handed to Pythia, so `rehadronize_jets.py` can redo the jet hadrons later                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--no-subtraction`                                       |                         | the reference without the hard-momentum subtraction (counts the hard pair's energy twice, on purpose); keep it in its own OUTDIR                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--late-dtau 0`                                          | late step on            | MUSIC at a constant 0.02 fm/c; keep one setting per campaign                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--eloss-threads 0`                                      | -1: in parallel         | the final-state showers of an event run in parallel on `OMP_NUM_THREADS` threads (set it: unset means all cores per job): events ~13 % faster (GB10, 4 threads). 0 runs them serially, N on N threads. Serial and parallel give other showers for a seed, the thread count does not: one setting per campaign |
| `--max-skipped N`                                        | 3                       | stop the job when more events fail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Choices that change the jets of a seed

X-SCAPE seeds each module from the order it was made. `--bulk-hadrons` and `--no-hydro-file` change that order, so the same seed gives other, equally valid jet showers (the hydro is identical). So do parallel showers, this driver's default, against `--eloss-threads 0`: every shower gets streams of its own (the thread count does not matter). Keep one choice per campaign if jets of different jobs are to be compared event by event; the files record it as `prod_eloss_threads`.

Before combining files, check the settings every file records (subtraction, b range, late time step, energy loss, colour closure): [O+O analysis](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md). Every option and the physics notes: the folder's [README](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr/README.md).

## Output and throughput

Each job writes (stem `OO_isr_seedNNNN`, or `OO_isr_<campaign>_NNNN`):

| file                          | content                                                                                                                                             | size per event        |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5`  | the jet hadrons (dijet, ISR emissions, Pythia's MPI partons, the hard pair's remnants), one unit per event, with the whole event record in `units/` | small                 |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`   | the bulk, N oversamples per event                                                                                                                   | ~13 kB per oversample |
| `<stem>_particlize.h5`        | MUSIC's freeze-out surface, the final partons, the initiators                                                                                       | ~10 MB                |
| `<stem>.h5`                   | MUSIC's evolution (e, vx, vy, vz) on `config/grid_oo.yaml` (64 × 64 × 32, x, y ±9.84 fm), with `diag/` per event                                    | ~17 MB                |
| `<stem>.xml`, `.json`, `.log` | the job XML, the summary (cross sections, skipped events), the log                                                                                  |                       |

A module that throws inside an event costs that event only; the `.json` lists it under `events_skipped`.

Measured on 2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores), 8 jobs per GPU with 3 threads, MPS, `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block`, 60 events per job:

| output                                                                  | events/h   | per job | disk per event |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------- | -------------- |
| hadron files only (`--bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file`) | **13,728** | 1.43 GB | 0.13 MB        |
| full outputs (hydro, particlize, jet hadrons)                           | 12,700     | 1.40 GB | 28 MB          |

The cores set the rate (~570 events/h per core). Full outputs write ~360 GB/h, more than an OSDF upload takes: use hadron files only, or a large local disk. On two GPUs, `utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh` runs one container per GPU with these settings, and on SLURM `PROD=oo` selects this production in `slurm_prod_array.sh`: [Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).

- [O+O analysis](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md): the per-event record, cross-section and N_coll weights, multiplicity, centrality, flow from the oversamples, jets.

# Z+jet and other collision systems

The physics of a production is in its user XML, so a new collision system or a different hard process is mostly a copy of an XML with a few lines changed. This page covers the two cases that already exist: the **Z+jet production** in Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV, made for the CMS and ATLAS Z–hadron and Z+jet measurements, and **Pb+Pb jets at the LHC** from your own XML, with the steps to take for any other system. O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV, and the event's other hard scatterings, which matter at the LHC, are on [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md). Both run through the Au+Au jet production's driver `run_prod_jet.py`, so everything in [Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md) applies. At the end, the production wizard plans the launch command for any of the productions.

## Z+jet in Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV

The Z+jet production runs Pb+Pb collisions at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, 0–30 %, with a hard process that makes a Z boson decaying to e⁺e⁻ or μ⁺μ⁻ and a recoiling parton. The Z's leptons pass through the medium untouched, so the Z tags the initial jet momentum; the recoil jet loses energy and leaves a wake. The inputs are in [`example/config/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/config) (in the image: `/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/config`):

- `PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml`: the Pb+Pb jet XML at 0–30 % (`b_max` 8.57 fm) with a Z+jet `<PythiaGun>` (Z + parton processes, Z → ee/μμ, `<trigger>Z`);
- `grid_PbPb.yaml`: the larger Pb+Pb output grid (80 × 80 × 40 cells, x, y ±15.3 fm), for the edge flags;
- `hadronize.xml`: the shared hadronization settings; its `eCMforHadronization` is set to the collision's 5020 GeV from the XML's PythiaGun automatically.

### The settings

The campaigns use six pT̂ windows with 4 jets per window per background (24 events per background), the Z's leptons inside the detector acceptance, and hadron files made in the job:

| option                                                                                   |                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user-xml …/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --grid …/grid_PbPb.yaml`                                | the Z+jet XML and the Pb+Pb grid                                                                                  |
| `--pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 --jets-per-bin 4`                     | the windows: the p_T^Z > 40 GeV cross section is spread evenly over them, so little is lost to the window weights |
| `--lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5`                                                  | both leptons p_T > 20 GeV,                                                                                        |
| `--hadrons-only --oversample 40 --n-frag 40 --correlated`                                | hadron files only, 40 correlated samples per jet event                                                            |
| `--eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --hadron-keep-bits-x 8 --keep-primaries 0` | all final particles at                                                                                            |
| `TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_30_seed` (environment)                                                | names the files `PbPb_0_30_<campaign>_…` instead of `AuAu_0_10_jet_…`                                             |

`--trigger Z` comes from the XML; `--trigger-ymax Y` would add a Z rapidity cut (the campaigns apply |y_Z| offline). There is no cut on the recoiling parton.

**The event's other hard scatterings.** A 0–30 % Pb+Pb event has ~8 other hard scatterings above 15 GeV (the XML's `<extraHard><pTHatMin>`). Add `--extra-hard` to the options above to have them: their fragments then form the B of the Z+jet analysis as CMS's minimum-bias events do, and the Z, its recoil and the background stay bit-identical for the same seed. See [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md) and, for the analyses, [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#with-the-events-other-hard-scatterings).

A current image

The Z trigger, `--hadrons-only` and `TAG_PREFIX` need an image built from the current code. Check it first: `python run_prod_jet.py --help` must list `--trigger`, and a `--dry-run` must print `trigger Z (lepton pT > 20 GeV, lepton |eta| < 2.5)`, `EOS 91` and `eCMforHadronization 5020`. Pin the image by digest for the campaign.

### Running it

Check with `--dry-run` inside the image (no GPU work), then run. In Docker:

```bash
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126                      # pinned by digest for a campaign
D=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/config
mkdir -p ~/prod/lbt_cache
docker run -d --name zjet --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_30_seed -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive \
  -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --stagger 12 --campaign zjet_test 10 96 0 /work/zjet_test \
    --user-xml $D/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --grid $D/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 --jets-per-bin 4 \
    --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 \
    --hadrons-only --oversample 40 --n-frag 40 --correlated \
    --eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --hadron-keep-bits-x 8 --keep-primaries 0
```

**The liquefier's frame.** `PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml` doesn't set `<CausalLiquefier><frame>`, so the build's default applies.

- **Published campaigns** (`zjet_c00`…, images from before 2026-11) were made in the lab frame. At the LHC that frame moves the wake of forward partons toward midrapidity: +19 % at |η_s| < 1 ([The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/#5-energymomentum-deposition-the-causalliquefier)).
- **A newer image runs the Bjorken frame by default.** Add `--liquefier-frame lab` to extend an old campaign, or `bjorken`/`fluid` for a new one.
- **Use a fresh output directory per frame:** `run_jobs.sh` skips completed jobs whatever frame made them.
- **Never combine campaigns made in different frames** in one analysis.

Ten jobs of 96 events (4 backgrounds each), three at a time: a Pb+Pb Z+jet job peaks at **14–16 GB** of host memory (2.1× an Au+Au job; measured on the GB10), mostly MUSIC's larger box. It takes 2.1× the time of an Au+Au jet job and writes 1.7× the disk.

**The scripts of the published campaigns** are in [`utils/zjet/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/utils/zjet): ten campaigns `zjet_c00` … `zjet_c09` of 9,600 events each (100 jobs × 96 events), with disjoint seed ranges (campaign C uses seeds from 1 + 1000 C), so campaigns from different machines combine. Run them from a js-contrib checkout:

| script                   | runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zjet_slurm_campaign.sh` | one campaign as a SLURM array through `utils/slurm_prod_array.sh`: `C=0 sbatch zjet_slurm_campaign.sh` (set up for NCSA Delta's A40 nodes, 3 jobs per GPU; edit the `#SBATCH` lines for your site). `C=0 NJOBS=1` is a ~1,000-event smoke test |
| `zjet_3090_campaign.sh`  | one campaign on a two-GPU workstation through `utils/launch_2gpu.sh`: `IMAGE=… ./zjet_3090_campaign.sh 0`                                                                                                                                      |
| `zjet_3090_test.sh`      | before the first campaign on a workstation: `info` (digest, commits, dry run), `bench 3`, `bench 4`, `report`, `smoke`                                                                                                                         |

After each campaign: `utils/check_deposition.py OUTDIR` ([Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#monitoring-a-campaign)), then the upload to the OSDF ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)).

### The pp reference

`prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_prod_vacuum.py` runs the same XML's PythiaGun and Matter in vacuum (no initial state, hydro, LBT or liquefier), with Colorless hadronization at the PythiaGun's energy. It runs on the CPU, ~0.02 s per event on the GB10, so 12,000 events take minutes:

```bash
python run_prod_vacuum.py --events 12000 --seed 900001 --campaign zjet_pp \
  --user-xml $D/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 \
  --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 \
  --n-frag 40 --eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --outdir /work/zjet_pp
```

It writes one `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5` (attribute `vacuum`), read like the Pb+Pb jet files. Give it seeds of its own: the Pb+Pb campaigns' seeds would give the same Pythia events.

### What to know in the files

- **The Z per event** is in `units/` of the hadron files (`z_pt`, `z_y`, `z_phi`, `z_m`, `lep{1,2}_{pid,pt,eta,phi}`); every paper's p_T^Z and mass window is applied offline.
- **Weight every event by its `n_coll`** (`units/n_coll`): the geometry is drawn with P(b) ∝ b over 0–30 % and every event has one Z, while Z production scales with N_coll. Weight also by the window's cross section.
- **The two leptons are among the jet hadrons** (`jet_frag`, pid ±11/±13) and in `initiators/`: remove them before a track or jet analysis.
- **Every background has its event plane near φ = 0** (3dMCGlauber puts the impact parameter along x). The means of a Z-frame analysis are unaffected; event mixing needs each background rotated by a random angle, which the Z-analysis scripts do by default.

The Z–hadron and Z+jet analyses, step by step: [`analysis/zjet/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet) and [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md). The campaign design (windows, cuts, expected statistics): [`utils/zjet/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/zjet/README.md).

## Another collision system: Pb+Pb at the LHC

`run_prod_jet.py` takes a copy of `AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml` with `--user-xml`, fills in the job and checks it. So another system or energy is a copy of the XML with the collision changed. Here: Pb+Pb at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, 0–10 %; the same steps apply to other nuclei and energies.

### 1. The XML

| where                                     | Au+Au 200 GeV | Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV | why                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<IS><MCGlauber><projectile>`, `<target>` | `Au`          | `Pb`           |                                                                                                                  |
| `<IS><MCGlauber><sqrts>`                  | `200`         | `5020`         |                                                                                                                  |
| `<IS><MCGlauber><b_max>`                  | `4.7` fm      | `4.95` fm      | centrality comes from b inside X-SCAPE (`cenMin`/`cenMax` are ignored): the geometric 0–10 %, π b² = 0.1 × 7.7 b |
| `<IS><grid_max_x>`, `<grid_max_y>`        | `15`          | `20`           | MUSIC's grid: the fireball is larger and lives longer                                                            |
| `<IS><grid_max_z>`                        | `6`           | `8`            | MUSIC's η_s range: the beam rapidity is 8.5 instead of 5.4                                                       |
| `<Hard><PythiaGun><eCM>`                  | `200`         | `5020`         |                                                                                                                  |
| the pT̂ windows                            | 10–40 GeV     | your choice    | `--pthat-bins`                                                                                                   |

`eCMforHadronization` follows the collision automatically, so the one `hadronize.xml` serves every system. From a js-contrib checkout:

```bash
mkdir -p xml
T=contribs/PyJetscape/example/config
sed -e 's#<projectile>Au</projectile>#<projectile>Pb</projectile>#' \
    -e 's#<target>Au</target>#<target>Pb</target>#' \
    -e 's#<sqrts>200</sqrts>#<sqrts>5020</sqrts>#' \
    -e 's#<b_max>4.7</b_max>#<b_max>4.95</b_max>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_x> 15 </grid_max_x>#<grid_max_x> 20 </grid_max_x>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_y> 15 </grid_max_y>#<grid_max_y> 20 </grid_max_y>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_z> 6  </grid_max_z>#<grid_max_z> 8  </grid_max_z>#' \
    -e 's#<eCM>200</eCM>#<eCM>5020</eCM>#' \
    $T/AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml > xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml
diff $T/AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml     # 8 lines must differ
```

The result is already in `example/config/` as `PbPb_0_10_jet.xml`, with `grid_PbPb.yaml`; use them as they are or as a start for another system.

**What the driver checks** (it refuses an XML that breaks the two-stage setup, before any event): exactly two `<Hydro><MUSIC>` blocks, `MUSIC_1` (background) and `MUSIC_2` (jet leg), all MUSIC settings in the first; the liquefier's `<dtau>` equal to MUSIC's starting step; a `<Hard><PythiaGun>` block; no `<SoftParticlization>`, `<JetHadronization>`, `<Afterburner>` or writers (the hadrons come from stage 2); an output grid inside MUSIC's grid.

**Choices to make before a production:**

- **The tune.** The 3D MC-Glauber, viscosity, freeze-out and energy-loss parameters are those of the Au+Au 200 GeV production; none is tuned at the LHC. Check the bulk against data first (ALICE: dN_ch/dη at |η| < 0.5 is 1943 ± 54 at 0–5 % and 1587 ± 47 at 5–10 %).
- **Pythia's MPI.** PythiaGun switches multi-parton interactions on, and every parton it hands over is showered and can deposit; at 5.02 TeV that is many more partons than at 200 GeV. `PartonLevel:MPI = off` in `<LinesToRead>` leaves the hard process and its ISR.
- **The output grid.** The default grid (±12.2 fm) fits, but the jet leg can reach its edge: `grid_PbPb.yaml` is larger with the same cells (files of different grids don't go into one training set).
- **Names.** `TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_10_seed` names the files `PbPb_0_10_…` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, ending in `_seed`; one per OUTDIR), or put the system into the campaign name.

### 2. Your XML from outside the container

The XML doesn't need to be in the image. Bind its directory and give the driver the path **as the container sees it**, as an absolute path:

|                                                     | bind                                                          | then                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker                                              | `-v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro"`                                       | `--user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml`               |
| Apptainer                                           | `--bind "$PWD/xml:/xml"`, or nothing for a file under `$HOME` | `--user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml`               |
| SLURM (`slurm_prod_array.sh`, `slurm_hadronize.sh`) | `BINDS="$PWD/xml:/xml"`                                       | in `EXTRA_ARGS` (stage 1) or `HAD_ARGS` (stage 2) |

The same holds for `--grid`, `--main-xml` and `--hadronize-xml`. The file is read when a job starts, and each job stores the XML it ran (`<stem>.xml`, `prod_user_xml`): don't edit it during a campaign.

### 3. A first event, then the campaign

```bash
# in the container (Apptainer; Docker with -v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro" -v "$PWD/prod:/work")
PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
apptainer exec --nv --env MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block --pwd "$PROD" \
  --bind "$PWD/xml:/xml,$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --events 3 --seed 1 \
    --write-particlize both --outdir /work/PbPb_test --out PbPb_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 --dry-run
# ... the same without --dry-run, then stage 2
apptainer exec --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$PWD/xml:/xml,$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_hadronize.py /work/PbPb_test -j 3 --oversample 100 --n-frag 20
```

One event against Au+Au, measured on the GB10 (one job alone, pT̂ 50–70 GeV, `--write-particlize both`, default output grid, 100 oversamples):

|                                       | Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV  | Au+Au 200 GeV     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| wall time of the event (both legs)    | 38.9 s          | 17.1 s            |
| peak host memory of the job           | 15.7 GB         | 6.1 GB            |
| freeze-out cells per leg              | 2.55 M          | 1.0 M             |
| showers, droplets, deposited energy   | 18, 74, 336 GeV | 2, 25, 32 GeV     |
| pair file, particlize file            | 321 MB, 395 MB  | 245 MB, 155 MB    |
| hadron file per leg (100 oversamples) | 79 MB           | 19 MB             |
| dN_ch/dη,                             | η               | < 0.5, background |

The campaign is the Au+Au one with the XML (and the grid) passed after OUTDIR:

**Docker:**

```bash
docker run -d --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  -v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro" -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 4 --stagger 12 --campaign PbPb_c1 20 15 0 /work/PbPb_c1 \
    --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid /xml/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --pthat-bins 40-60,60-80,80-100 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
```

**SLURM:**

```bash
# stage 1: ~16 GB per job, so fewer jobs per GPU than for Au+Au
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=PbPb_c1 P=5 BINDS="$PWD/xml:/xml" \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid /xml/grid_PbPb.yaml --pthat-bins 40-60,60-80,80-100 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 --cpus-per-task=20 --mem=96G utils/slurm_prod_array.sh
# stage 2
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=PbPb_c1 \
  HAD_ARGS="--oversample 200 --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 --mem=48G utils/slurm_hadronize.sh
```

- **Memory:** plan ~16 GB per job, 4–5 jobs on 96 GB; measure events/h with a short sweep of `P` on the first node.
- **Disk:** ~0.7 GB per event with a new background every event; a background shared by 15 jets saves most of the background's share. Hadrons are ~4× Au+Au per oversample, so 200 oversamples give the statistics of 400–500 in Au+Au.
- **Stage 2 memory:** ~2.3 GB per process at 100 oversamples.
- Hydro-only Pb+Pb (`prod_AuAu_0_10/run_prod.py`) takes the same `<IS>` changes in a copy of its XML.

Here the grid is bound from `xml/`: copy `grid_PbPb.yaml` there, or pass the image's own path. Full details: [`docs/README_2stage.md`, §9](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/README_2stage.md#9-another-collision-system-pbpb-at-the-lhc).

## Planning a production: the wizard

[`utils/prodwizard.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/prodwizard.py) plans a campaign before anything runs. Pick a production preset and a machine; it writes the launch command with the settings measured for that machine (`launch_2gpu.sh` on a two-GPU workstation, `run_jobs.sh` on a single machine or Mac, `slurm_prod_array.sh` on a cluster) and estimates events/h, duration, disk and memory, each marked as measured or estimated with its source. It checks the plan: events per job a multiple of the pT̂ windows × jets, memory, disk, upload rate, the image, the campaign name. It never starts jobs.

```bash
utils/prodwizard.py --list                 # presets and machines
utils/prodwizard.py --preset auau_jet --machine 2x3090 --events 2700 --campaign c5 --out /data/c5
utils/prodwizard.py --preset pbpb_zjet --machine slurm_a40 --events 19200 --gpus 20 \
    --campaign zjet_c10 --save launch_zjet_c10.sh      # a script, the plan in its header
utils/prodwizard.py                        # the interactive wizard: a form, the plan beside it
```

| presets (`--preset`)    |                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auau_jet`              | Au+Au jets, pair + particlize files (the campaign setting) |
| `auau_particlize_only`  | Au+Au jets, particlize file only                           |
| `auau_hadrons_only`     | Au+Au jets, hadron files only, in the job                  |
| `oo_hadrons`, `oo_full` | O+O with ISR: hadron files only; or the default outputs    |
| `pbpb_zjet`             | Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV 0–30 % Z+jet, hadron files only             |

The machines (`--machine`) are `2x3090`, `gb10`, `m3max` and SLURM nodes with one `slurm_v100`, `slurm_a40`, `slurm_a100` or `slurm_l40s` per array task; further options set `--events-per-job`, `--image`, `--first-seed`, `--jobs-per-gpu`, `--omp`, `--upload`, `--delete` and `--min-free`. The command-line mode needs only the standard library; the interactive wizard needs `textual` (in the analysis venv), and runs in a browser with `textual serve "utils/prodwizard.py"`. The presets and measured rates are in `utils/prod_presets.json`.
