# Extra hard scatterings, small systems and minimum bias

Without extra options, every event of the jet production has exactly one hard scattering: the trigger. A nucleus–nucleus collision has many more, N_coll × σ(p̂T > p₀)/σ_NN of them, and at the LHC they matter: their fragments are the jet background a Pb+Pb event otherwise lacks (the fake jets, the B of Z+jet, the hard tail of the underlying event), and their wakes change the bulk (Nch, [pT], vₙ). `run_prod_jet.py --extra-hard` adds these **extras** above a threshold p₀ to every event. The same option, without a trigger, gives **minimum-bias** events, and two new inputs run **O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV**. Everything on [Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md) applies; this page adds what is new. The analysis side is on [Bulk and flow](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/bulk/index.md) and in the [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/#the-events-other-hard-scatterings) page.

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks for these files (bulk and flow, v₂(p_T) against data) are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

Needs the current code

The option needs X-SCAPE with PythiaGun `<extraHard>` and the current js-contrib. Check an image first: `python run_prod_jet.py --help` must list `--extra-hard`. On a Mac, the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) has it from 0.2.0. A 0.1.0 environment stops with `User XML tag <extraHard> is unrecognized`, also for the XMLs that carry the block switched off (`AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml`, `PbPb_0_10_jet.xml`, `PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml`): install the current release next to it.

## How many extras

Per binary collision (LO Pythia 8.3, HardQCD, ISR on, MPI and FSR off):

| √s_NN    | σ(p̂T > 10 GeV) | σ(p̂T > 15 GeV) | extras per binary collision, p₀ = 10 / 15 GeV |
| -------- | -------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 200 GeV  | 0.0058 mb      | 0.00054 mb     | 1.4·10⁻⁴ / 1.3·10⁻⁵                           |
| 5.02 TeV | 2.31 mb        | 0.52 mb        | 0.034 / 0.0077                                |
| 5.36 TeV | 2.54 mb        | 0.58 mb        | 0.037 / 0.0085                                |

Per event:

| system                 | ⟨N_coll⟩ | p₀ (XML default) | extras per event                   |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Au+Au 200 GeV, 0–10 %  | ~960     | 10 GeV           | ~0.13 (at RHIC they barely matter) |
| Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV, 0–10 % | ~1,800   | 15 GeV           | ~15 (~66 at 10 GeV)                |
| Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV, 0–30 % | 1,030    | 15 GeV           | ~8 (~35 at 10 GeV)                 |
| O+O 5.36 TeV, 0–10 %   | 42       | 10 GeV           | ~1.5                               |
| Ne+Ne 5.36 TeV, 0–10 % | 51       | 10 GeV           | ~1.9                               |

Each extra hands over ~4.5–4.8 partons (its two hard partons and the ISR partons above 2 GeV), Σp_T ~40–60 GeV. The physics, and what the model leaves out, is in [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/#15-the-events-other-hard-scatterings).

## How an event is made

```text
IS (3dMCGlauber) -> Hard (PythiaGun: the trigger, then N ~ Poisson(N_coll sigma/sigma_NN) extras)
   -> MUSIC_1                    background leg: the strings alone           -> bulk_bg
   -> Liquefier + Eloss          Matter + LBT shower the trigger and the extras -> droplets
   -> MUSIC_2                    the same strings + all droplets             -> bulk_jet
   -> hadronization              trigger's partons -> jet_frag, the extras' -> extra_frag
```

- Each extra is one event of a Pythia instance of its own (HardQCD above p₀), at a binary collision drawn from the background's collisions; its partons are handed over after the trigger's, labelled with their scattering (1, 2, …).
- **The trigger is untouched.** Everything random the extras do (their Pythia, the Poisson draw, the vertices, their shower engines, their colour tags and hadronization seeds) runs on streams of their own. With the same seed, a job with extras has the same trigger showers, `jet_frag` and `bulk_bg` as a job without, bit for bit, in every event; only `bulk_jet` (their wakes) and the new records differ. Running the same seeds twice, with and without `--extra-hard`, is a paired measurement of what the extras do.
- With `--reuse` every jet event draws its own extras from its background's N_coll and binary collisions.
- Their energy is **not** subtracted from the strings, as for the trigger.

## Running it

| option of `run_prod_jet.py`                 |                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--extra-hard`                              | switch the extras on. Off (default): the files are bit-identical to before                                                                                                     |
| `--extra-pthat-min P0`                      | their threshold [GeV]; default: the XML's `<extraHard><pTHatMin>`                                                                                                              |
| `--extra-n N`                               | exactly N extras per event instead of Poisson (tests)                                                                                                                          |
| `--extra-warmup N`                          | Pythia events for their cross section at Init (default 20,000, ~1 s at the LHC)                                                                                                |
| `--extra-hadronize {groups,per_scattering}` | with `--hadrons-only`: all extras' showers in one Colorless call (default), or one call per scattering, with each hadron's scattering kept                                     |
| `--hard none`                               | no trigger: the **minimum-bias** event, the bulk and its extras (N may be 0), weight 1. Needs `--extra-hard`; refuses `--pthat-*`, `--parton-ymax`, `--trigger`. No `jet_frag` |

Everything else works as without extras: `--reuse`, `--pthat-bins`, `--trigger Z`, `--hadrons-only`, `--write-particlize`, `--correlated`, `run_jobs.sh` and the container launchers. `run_prod_vacuum.py` (pp) ignores the extras: pp has one collision and Pythia's own MPI.

```bash
cd prod_AuAu_0_10_jet                            # in your copy of the examples
# Au+Au 0-10 % with extras above 10 GeV (the XML's)
python run_prod_jet.py --events 10 --seed 1 --extra-hard --hadrons-only

# Pb+Pb 0-30 % Z+jet with extras above 15 GeV
python run_prod_jet.py --events 24 --seed 1 --user-xml ../config/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml \
    --grid ../config/grid_PbPb.yaml --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 \
    --jets-per-bin 4 --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 --extra-hard --hadrons-only

# a two-stage campaign: particlize files, then hadronize.py (which handles the extras itself)
python run_prod_jet.py --events 10 --seed 1 --extra-hard --write-particlize both --particlize-only
python hadronize.py out/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_particlize.h5 --oversample 20 --n-frag 10
```

The job prints the extras' settings once, and their number per event:

```text
  extras   pTHat > 15 GeV: sigma = 0.524 +- 0.002 mb (20000 warm-up events, Pythia seed 234669607), sigma_NN 67.57 mb, N ~ Poisson(N_coll sigma/sigma_NN)
prod_AuAu_0_10_jet: event 1/1 done in 40.5 s, ..., N_coll 1294, ..., 10 extra scattering(s) (mu 10.04, 3342 GeV)
```

The energy in that line includes the extras' forward ISR partons, which carry most of it; the summed p_T (`extra_pt` in the files) is the better measure of what they bring to mid-rapidity.

### Choosing p₀

Lower thresholds put more of the hard tail into the bulk and cost more. Below ~10 GeV the extras' energy becomes a sizeable part of what the strings already carry; that needs minijets with energy subtraction and a retuned bulk, which this option does not do. The production XMLs set 10 GeV for Au+Au, O+O and Ne+Ne, 15 GeV for Pb+Pb.

Cost on the GB10 (Pb+Pb 0–10 %, 3 events, the same backgrounds, one job alone, `--hadrons-only`; hadronization ~5 s per event either way):

|                             | extras per event | droplets | s per event  | peak memory |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | -------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| extras off                  | —                | 45       | 32.1         | 18.98 GB    |
| p₀ = 20 GeV                 | ~5               | 195      | 34.5 (+8 %)  | 19.04 GB    |
| p₀ = 15 GeV (Pb+Pb default) | ~15              | 464      | 36.4 (+13 %) | 19.08 GB    |
| p₀ = 10 GeV                 | ~66              | 1,300    | 45.6 (+42 %) | 19.16 GB    |

The time grows with the showers and with MUSIC_2's jet source (all cells × the active droplets, on the CPU); the warm-up for σ adds ~1 s per job. Memory hardly changes.

### The XML settings

The driver writes the settings into `<Hard><PythiaGun><extraHard>` of the job XML; set them there yourself to change a default for a whole campaign. The defaults are in X-SCAPE's `config/jetscape_main.xml`.

| tag             | default |                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<on>`          | 0       | 1: the extras on (`--extra-hard`)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `<noTrigger>`   | 0       | 1: no triggering scattering, the extras alone (`--hard none`). Refuses `<pTHatBins>`, `<partonYMax>`, `<trigger>`                                                                                                        |
| `<pTHatMin>`    | 15      | their p̂T threshold [GeV] (`--extra-pthat-min`). The production XMLs set their system's: 10 (`AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml`, `OO_5360_jet.xml`, `NeNe_5360_jet.xml`), 15 (`PbPb_0_10_jet.xml`, `PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml`) |
| `<sigmaNN>`     | empty   | σ_NN^inel [mb]; empty: 3dMCGlauber's parametrization at `<eCM>`, the one its N_coll is made with (40.8 mb at 200 GeV, 67.6 at 5.02 TeV, 68.3 at 5.36 TeV)                                                                |
| `<warmup>`      | 20000   | Pythia events at Init for σ(p̂T > p₀) (`--extra-warmup`); kept fixed for the job                                                                                                                                          |
| `<fixedN>`      | −1      | ≥ 0: exactly that many per event (`--extra-n`, tests); < 0: Poisson                                                                                                                                                      |
| `<LinesToRead>` | empty   | more Pythia settings for the extras' instance only (not the trigger's `<LinesToRead>`, which may hold a Z process)                                                                                                       |

The extras' Pythia runs `HardQCD:all = on` with `PhaseSpace:pTHatMin` = p₀, ISR on, MPI off, FSR as `<FSR_on>` (off in production: Matter showers), hadron level off, and the trigger's `<eCM>` and `<softMomentumCutoff>`.

## Minimum bias

`--hard none --extra-hard` makes events without a trigger: the bulk and its extras, N of them from Poisson (N may be 0), every event with weight 1. An event with N = 0 has no hard parton: the energy loss is skipped, MUSIC_2 still runs (restarted from MUSIC_1's checkpoint, so it is cheap), and `bulk_jet` differs from `bulk_bg` only by sampling. `bulk_jet − bulk_bg` is then the extras' wakes. These are the events for the bulk observables of [Bulk and flow](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/bulk/index.md); use correlated legs and several samples so that the paired differences are small-noise:

```bash
TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_10_seed ./run_jobs.sh -j 4 --campaign mb_x 20 30 0 out_mb_x \
    --user-xml ../config/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid ../config/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --hard none --extra-hard --hadrons-only --oversample 10 --correlated
```

For the 0–10 % XMLs this is minimum bias *within* 0–10 %; set `b_max` to 20 in a copy of the XML for all impact parameters. Scale the threshold with `--extra-pthat-min 20`, `15`, `10` on the same seeds (the backgrounds are the same) to see the dependence on p₀.

## O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV

`example/config/OO_5360_jet.xml` and `NeNe_5360_jet.xml` (in the image's `example/config/`) are copies of `PbPb_0_10_jet.xml` for the LHC's light-ion run:

- 3dMCGlauber's ¹⁶O and PGCM ²⁰Ne configurations (`Ne20` is 3dMCGlauber's name for neon), √s_NN = 5.36 TeV, MUSIC's transverse grid ±12 fm, the output grid `grid_oo.yaml`;
- 0–10 %: b < 2.09 fm (O+O) and 2.41 fm (Ne+Ne), the 10 % quantile of b in 80,000 minimum-bias 3dMCGlauber events, ⟨N_coll⟩ 42 / 51; set `b_max` to 20 for minimum bias;
- `<extraHard><pTHatMin>` 10 GeV.

Not refitted for the LHC or for small systems

The bulk settings are the Pb+Pb file's: the RHIC best fit of the JETSCAPE 3D calibration ([arXiv:2601.17234](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17234)), without the paper's Pb+Pb refit and without an afterburner ([The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/#7-hydrodynamics-music)). Two test events give dN_ch/dη(|η| < 0.5) ≈ 136 (O+O) and 131 (Ne+Ne), ⟨pT⟩ ≈ 0.59 / 0.65 GeV. Compare dN_ch/dη and v₂{2} with ATLAS ([arXiv:2606.20257](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20257)) and ALICE ([arXiv:2604.07184](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07184)) before quoting numbers. The 0–10 % edges are geometric, not multiplicity classes.

```bash
# 0-10 % with a jet trigger and extras
python run_prod_jet.py --events 10 --seed 1 --user-xml ../config/OO_5360_jet.xml \
    --grid ../config/grid_oo.yaml --extra-hard --hadrons-only --out OO_5360_seed0001.h5
python run_prod_jet.py --events 10 --seed 1 --user-xml ../config/NeNe_5360_jet.xml \
    --grid ../config/grid_oo.yaml --extra-hard --hadrons-only --out NeNe_5360_seed0001.h5

# minimum-bias campaigns, correlated legs, 10 samples per event
TAG_PREFIX=OO_5360_seed ./run_jobs.sh --campaign mb1 20 30 1 out_oo_mb1 \
    --user-xml ../config/OO_5360_jet.xml --grid ../config/grid_oo.yaml \
    --hard none --extra-hard --hadrons-only --oversample 10 --correlated
                                                  # -> OO_5360_mb1_seed0001.* ...
TAG_PREFIX=NeNe_5360_seed ./run_jobs.sh --campaign mb1 20 30 1 out_nene_mb1 \
    --user-xml ../config/NeNe_5360_jet.xml --grid ../config/grid_oo.yaml \
    --hard none --extra-hard --hadrons-only --oversample 10 --correlated
```

These run through the jet production's driver, so they are not the [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md) production at 200 GeV: no initial-state shower module, the two-leg pair, and the Au+Au jet production's files.

Name the files

The driver's default name is `AuAu_0_10_jet[_<campaign>]_seed<NNNN>`, whatever the XML, so without a name the O+O, Ne+Ne and Pb+Pb runs above are all written as `AuAu_0_10_jet_*`. Use `--out` for a single job and `TAG_PREFIX` for a campaign through `run_jobs.sh` (it must end in `_seed`; one prefix per OUTDIR). `launch_2gpu.sh` and `slurm_prod_array.sh` pass `TAG_PREFIX` into the container.

## What the files hold

- **`<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5`:** the extras' fragments, with the layout of `jet_frag` (unit = event, `--n-frag` samples), plus `scatterings/` and the extras' `initiators/`. `jet_frag` stays the trigger's alone and is absent with `--hard none`.
- **`scatterings/`** (pair, particlize and `extra_frag` files): one row per scattering, the trigger's first: `scatter, pthat, code, x, y, n_partons, E, pt`.
- **Per event** (`diag/`, `events/`, `units/`): `n_extra`, `extra_mu` (= N_coll σ/σ_NN), `extra_E`, `extra_pt`.
- **Attributes and the `.json`:** the threshold, σ and its error, σ_NN, the warm-up and the seeds of the extras (`extra_*`, `prod_extra_*`).

Files without extras have none of these; their layout is unchanged. Full layout: [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/#the-events-other-hard-scatterings).

# Clusters, GPUs and monitoring

A production job keeps a GPU only partly busy: much of an event is host work (string deposition, Matter and LBT, the freeze-out search, writing). So a GPU needs several jobs at once, and **the cores and host memory per GPU, not the GPU, usually set the rate**. This page covers running at scale with the production container: the launch settings, SLURM arrays with Apptainer, several GPUs in one machine, watching a campaign with `jobmon.py`, and what to do when a run goes wrong. The single-machine commands are on the production pages ([Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md), [O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md)).

## Sizing: jobs, cores, memory

For the Au+Au jet production with the current code, per job:

|             |                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| host memory | **plan 7 GB per job** (5 GB with `--particlize-only`), plus ~8 GB per node; Pb+Pb ~16 GB |
| cores       | ~1 core busy on average, with OpenMP bursts: **2–3 threads per job**                     |
| GPU memory  | ~1 GB per job: a 16 GB V100 holds 8–10 jobs                                              |
| disk        | 0.243 GB per event with pair + particlize files                                          |

An O+O job needs ~1.5 GB and, with 10 oversamples in the job, ~6 core-s per event. So set the number of jobs per GPU from the cores and memory a GPU gets: about cores / 2–3, and about (memory − 8 GB) / 7 GB. Lower the number of jobs where a node gives a GPU less, not the threads per job below 2. The measured and extrapolated rates per GPU type (V100, A40, A100, L40S, RTX 3090, GB10, M3 Max) are in [GPU acceleration](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/gpu/index.md).

**Before a large campaign**, on the first node: a 20–30 min sweep of the jobs per GPU (e.g. 8, 12, 16) at the planned cores. Record events/h by makespan, the GPU use (`nvidia-smi dmon -s u`) and the memory peak. If the GPU stays below ~75 % busy while the cores are full, more cores per GPU pay, more jobs don't.

## Launch settings

None of these changes the output; together they decide how many jobs fit and how fast they run.

| setting                   | how                                               | why                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| jobs per GPU              | `run_jobs.sh -j P`                                | the GPU needs several jobs to stay busy (10 on an RTX 3090 with 12 cores per GPU)                                           |
| threads per job           | `OMP_NUM_THREADS` ≈ cores per GPU / P, at least 2 | more threads than cores oversubscribe them                                                                                  |
| `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive` | environment                                       | idle OpenMP threads sleep instead of spinning                                                                               |
| `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block`   | environment                                       | the host sleeps while it waits for the GPU: ~30 % less CPU per event at the same throughput                                 |
| `LBT_TABLE_CACHE=FILE`    | environment; FILE in a bound, writable directory  | all jobs map one read-only copy of LBT's 0.66 GB of tables: −0.6 GB and 6–11 s of start-up per job. The first job writes it |
| `--stagger S`             | `run_jobs.sh` option                              | the first P jobs start S s apart, so their memory peaks don't coincide (12 for 8–10 jobs per GPU)                           |
| `--mps`                   | `run_jobs.sh` option, CUDA only                   | the jobs share the GPU through CUDA MPS: +5–12 % where it works                                                             |

Parallel showers (`--eloss-threads -1`, X-SCAPE `<Eloss><nThreads>`; the default of the O+O ISR driver, off in the Au+Au drivers) use the same `OMP_NUM_THREADS`: the showers start after the hydro, so the budget is not exceeded. Set `OMP_NUM_THREADS` for O+O jobs: unset, each job runs its showers on all cores of the node. Unlike the settings above they change the output (the showers of a seed), so they are a campaign choice, not a launch setting.

CUDA MPS in containers

MPS is not assured inside containers (on the GB10 the daemon does not start in one) and has never been tried on a cluster: run without it first, and test with `nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d; echo $?` inside the container. Two daemons in one container hang the second GPU's jobs. If the site runs MPS itself (`--gres=mps`), don't add `--mps`.

In Docker pass the variables with `-e`, in Apptainer with `--env A=1,B=2`. On a Mac the same rule holds without MPS: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 …` on a 16-core M3 Max.

## SLURM: one GPU per array task

[`utils/slurm_prod_array.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/slurm_prod_array.sh) runs a campaign as a job array in the production container: each task gets one GPU and runs `P` jobs on it with the launch settings above. SLURM gives whole GPUs, and only jobs in one allocation can share a GPU, so one SLURM job per production job would leave the GPUs mostly idle.

**1. Pull the image** once, on a login node (a `.sif` holds one CPU architecture; on x86 login nodes with arm64 GPU nodes such as GH200, add `--arch arm64`):

```bash
apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126-<date>-<commit>
```

**2. Make the LBT table cache once** with one 1-event job (otherwise 20 tasks starting together each write their own copy; add your site's `-p`/`-A`):

```bash
PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
WORK=$SCRATCH/xscape_prod; mkdir -p $WORK/lbt_cache
srun --gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=4 --mem=16G --time=0:20:00 \
  apptainer exec --nv --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$WORK:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 1 --outdir /work/lbt_cache/init \
    --seed-registry none 2>&1 | grep "LBT:"
rm -r $WORK/lbt_cache/init                 # the test event, not needed
```

The `grep` shows `LBT: wrote the table cache /work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin`. Where arm64 and amd64 nodes share a file system, keep one file per architecture (`LBT_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1_arm64.bin`).

**3. A trial, then the campaign** (from a js-contrib checkout):

```bash
# trial: 2 tasks, 2 jobs of 15 events each
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 NJOBS=2 EVENTS=15 P=2 \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-1 --time=2:00:00 utils/slurm_prod_array.sh

# the campaign: 20 tasks x 40 jobs x 15 events = 12,000 events on 800 backgrounds
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 NJOBS=40 EVENTS=15 \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 utils/slurm_prod_array.sh
```

The defaults, `P=10` jobs per GPU with `--gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=20 --mem=96G`, are an A100's or A40's share of a node; for other GPUs pass `P` and the `sbatch` options (e.g. V100s: `P=8 … sbatch --cpus-per-task=16 --mem=64G`). The script sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS = cpus / P` itself (and warns below 2). At the 3090's measured rate, that 12,000-event campaign is ~11 GPU-hours, ~2.9 TB of stage-1 files and ~0.9 TB of hadrons.

| variable                                             | default                                             |                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SIF`                                                | `$HOME/xscape_prod.sif`                             | the image                                                                                       |
| `WORK`                                               | `$SCRATCH/xscape_prod`                              | bound to `/work`; writable, shared by the tasks                                                 |
| `PROD`                                               | `auau`                                              | `oo` runs `prod_OO_isr`                                                                         |
| `CAMPAIGN`, `NJOBS`, `EVENTS`, `P`                   |                                                     | campaign name, jobs per task, events per job, jobs at once per GPU                              |
| `EXTRA_ARGS`                                         |                                                     | options for the driver (`run_prod_jet.py` / `run_prod_oo_isr.py`)                               |
| `BINDS`                                              |                                                     | more binds, e.g. `"$PWD/xml:/xml"` for your own XML                                             |
| `TAG_PREFIX`                                         | the production's                                    | file names, e.g. `PbPb_0_30_seed`                                                               |
| `SEED_MODE`                                          | `registry`                                          | `ranges` with `SEED_BASE`: task t runs seeds `SEED_BASE + t·NJOBS …`, no cross-node lock needed |
| `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC`, `LBT_CACHE`, `STAGGER`, `USE_MPS` | `block`, `/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin`, 12, 0 | the launch settings (`LBT_CACHE=none`, `STAGGER=0` to turn off)                                 |
| `CHECK_DEPOSITION`                                   | 1                                                   | after the jobs, flag jobs whose droplets per event fall below half the median                   |

- **Output:** `WORK/CAMPAIGN/t000/`, `t001/`, … with one shared seed registry `WORK/CAMPAIGN/seeds_used.tsv`. The script checks that file locks work across nodes, or use `SEED_MODE=ranges`.
- **Restarting:** submit the same command again; each task skips its finished jobs. A task that runs out of time resumes.
- **Time:** at ~25 s per event in a loaded job, a 15-event job takes ~6–7 min; allow 2× on V100s. Longer jobs (30 or 45 events) amortise the start-up better.
- **Memory:** SLURM counts the page cache of the HDF5 files being written; if tasks are killed near the limit, raise `--mem` by ~10–15 % rather than lowering `P`.
- **Disk:** one fast GPU can write more than an OSDF upload takes (an L40S up to ~0.7 TB/h with pair files). Use `--particlize-only` unless the hydro history is needed, and `upload_follow.py` ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/#uploading-while-a-production-runs)).
- **O+O:** `PROD=oo CAMPAIGN=OO_c1 EXTRA_ARGS="--bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file" sbatch --mem=40G utils/slurm_prod_array.sh`.

### Stage 2 on CPU nodes

[`utils/slurm_hadronize.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/slurm_hadronize.sh) hadronizes the campaign with the same image, without a GPU: task *t* runs `run_hadronize.py` on `WORK/CAMPAIGN/t<ttt>/`, the directory of stage-1 task *t*, one process per core.

```bash
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 \
  HAD_ARGS="--oversample 400 --oversample-bg per-pthat-bin --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 utils/slurm_hadronize.sh
```

- Defaults: `--cpus-per-task=16 --mem=32G`; `HAD_ARGS` defaults to `--oversample 400 --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8`. **Keep `HAD_ARGS` the same for every task and resubmission.**
- `PROD=oo` hadronizes the O+O bulk (`--tags bulk_bg` is added); `INPUTS="/work/…"` takes other inputs (directories, particlize files or quoted globs, as paths inside the container).
- Memory ~1.6–1.7 GB per process: ask for ~2 GB per core. One process does ~340 Au+Au events/h at 500 oversamples, so ~6–7 cores keep up with 2,000 events/h of stage 1.

## Several GPUs in one machine

MUSIC always uses the first GPU it sees, and `run_jobs.sh` doesn't assign GPUs: on a machine with several GPUs, run **one campaign per GPU**, each with its own `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (or its own container), OUTDIR and campaign name. OUTDIRs side by side share the seed registry.

**Ready-made for Docker on two GPUs:** [`utils/launch_2gpu.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/launch_2gpu.sh) starts one container per GPU, each running `run_jobs.sh` with MPS, guards the disk and can upload every finished job to the OSDF while the campaign runs. [`utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh) does the same for O+O. Run them from `utils/` of a js-contrib checkout:

```bash
cd js-contrib/utils
# Au+Au with the defaults: 10 jobs per GPU, 3 threads, shared LBT tables, staggered start,
# blocking CUDA sync; 60 jobs x 45 events (a multiple of 20 jobs)
IMAGE=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
nohup ./launch_2gpu.sh 60 45 0 /data/camp_pth3 --campaign pth3 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 \
    --write-particlize both > /data/camp_pth3.log 2>&1 &

# O+O, hadron files only (defaults: 8 jobs per GPU, 3 threads, MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block, MPS)
nohup ./launch_2gpu_oo.sh 64 100 0 /data/OO_had --campaign had1 \
    --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file > /data/OO_had.log 2>&1 &
```

```text
./launch_2gpu.sh [options] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB [FIRST_SEED] [OUTBASE] [driver / run_jobs.sh options]
```

- **NJOBS** is the total: GPU0 gets the first half, GPU1 the rest. Output goes to `OUTBASE/gpu0/` and `OUTBASE/gpu1/`, with a shared seed registry. With `FIRST_SEED 0` both directories hold files of the same names (different seeds): keep the directories.
- **Options before NJOBS:** `--lbt-cache FILE` (Au+Au default `/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin`, made first if missing, ~1 min; `none` turns it off), `--stagger S` (Au+Au default 12; `0` off), `--min-free SIZE` (the disk guard: stops both containers below SIZE free, default `50G`), and the upload options `--upload REMOTE`, `--delete none|pair|all`, `--keep-free SIZE`, `--verify-every N` ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/#uploading-while-a-production-runs)).
- **Environment:** `IMAGE`, `JOBS_PER_GPU` (default 10; O+O 8), `OMP_THREADS` (default 3), `WORKDIR` (mounted as `/work`, default `$HOME/prod_test`), `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC` (default `block`), `TAG_PREFIX`. For an image older than 2026-10-10: `JOBS_PER_GPU=8 OMP_THREADS=4 ./launch_2gpu.sh --lbt-cache none --stagger 0 …`.
- **Stop** with Ctrl-C or `kill` (both containers and the uploader stop); **resume** with the same command.

Measured on 2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores, 125 GB) with the campaign setting: **2,160 events/h** for Au+Au at 10 jobs per GPU, 105 GB host memory peak; **13,728 events/h** for O+O with hadron files only. Details: [`utils/README_launch.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/README_launch.md).

**By hand, or with Apptainer** (one container for all GPUs, no `--mps`):

```bash
apptainer exec --nv --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif bash -c '
  trap "kill \$(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null; wait" INT TERM
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --stagger 12 --campaign AuAu_gpu0 24 45 0 /work/AuAu/gpu0 --write-particlize both &
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --stagger 12 --campaign AuAu_gpu1 24 45 0 /work/AuAu/gpu1 --write-particlize both &
  wait'
```

Under SLURM, if `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is already set (e.g. `2,3`), use those numbers.

## Monitoring a campaign

[`utils/jobmon.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/jobmon.py) reads what the jobs write (their logs, `.json` summaries and the `run_jobs.*` markers) and shows jobs done / running / failed, events, events/h, the ETA, disk per event, the failed jobs with their last log lines, the deposition check, edge hits, skipped events and the most frequent warnings. It works on Docker, SLURM and Mac output alike, during a run or after.

```bash
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1                  # OUTBASE: its gpu0/, gpu1/, ... (or t000/, ...) are taken
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --njobs 100      # count the jobs not started yet too
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --watch          # live view, every 10 s
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --tui            # terminal UI: sort, filter, a job's details and live log
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --all            # every job; exit code 1 if one failed or is flagged
```

It needs only the standard library; `--watch` uses `rich` if installed and `--tui` needs `textual` (both in the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md)). For a workshop, the TUI runs in a browser: `textual serve "utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --tui"` (package `textual-dev`).

- A job counts as running while its driver process is alive (on the machine that runs the jobs, containers included); on another machine, while its log changed in the last 15 min (`--stale`).
- The drivers' `event … done in` lines reach the log in blocks, so event counts jump by ~10–15 at a time; `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` in the jobs' environment avoids it. The s per event are exact.

**The deposition check.** Once, in ~250 campaign jobs, all events of one job lost almost no jet energy (1–5 droplets per event instead of 13–34), with a correct background and no warning in the log; the same seed alone was normal. Check every campaign for it:

```bash
utils/check_deposition.py /work/AuAu_a                     # every job summary below it
utils/check_deposition.py /data/c1/gpu0 /data/c1/gpu1      # one campaign in two directories
```

It flags a job whose droplets per event fall below half the campaign's median (`--fraction`) and exits 1 if one is flagged. To redo it, move its files (`<stem>.*`) out of OUTDIR and run the campaign's command again. `slurm_prod_array.sh` runs it on each task's directory.

## Checking a run

In a job log, `OUTDIR/<stem>.log`:

| line                                                                                     | means                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[MUSIC-GPU] CUDA device: <GPU name> (cc X.Y, …)`                                        | the hydro runs on that GPU                                                                                                                                 |
| `[MUSIC-GPU] OMP wait policy: passive (max threads N)`                                   | the thread settings arrived                                                                                                                                |
| `[MUSIC-GPU] host sync: block`                                                           | `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block` arrived                                                                                                                            |
| `LBT: wrote the table cache …` / `LBT: tables mapped read-only from …`                   | the LBT cache works (`grep -L "mapped read-only" OUTDIR/*.log` lists jobs without it)                                                                      |
| `late step: delta_tau 0.02 -> 0.05 fm/c at step 130 …`                                   | MUSIC's late time step is on                                                                                                                               |
| `restart MUSIC_2 starts from MUSIC_1's state …` / `restart OFF: …`                       | the MUSIC_2 restart, on or off with the reason                                                                                                             |
| `… done in … s` per event                                                                | the speed: events/h = jobs × 3600 / s per event                                                                                                            |
| `No CUDA device found`, `falling back to CPU`                                            | **no GPU**: ~7–10× slower and systematically different (~0.2 %). Don't add that output to a GPU campaign                                                   |
| `PairH5Writer: event i: the jet leg has e = … on the transverse edge of the output grid` | fluid above freeze-out reached the stored box's edge (`diag/{bg,jet}_hit_edge`); a few per campaign are expected, frequent ones mean the grid is too small |

Each job also writes `<stem>.json` (seed, events written, settings, `events_hit_edge`, `droplets_total`), and a campaign ends with `OUTDIR/run_jobs.finished`.

## Troubleshooting

| symptom                                                          | cause and fix                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `./run_jobs.sh: No such file` (Apptainer)                        | no `--pwd "$PROD"`; or call `$PROD/run_jobs.sh`                                                                          |
| `--outdir: give OUTDIR as the argument after FIRST_SEED`         | OUTDIR is the 4th argument of `run_jobs.sh`, not an option                                                               |
| `Read-only file system: …/seeds_used.tsv`                        | OUTDIR's parent isn't writable: put OUTDIR one level inside a bound directory (`/work/out`)                              |
| only one job runs with `-j 2`                                    | NJOBS is 1: `-j` only limits how many run at once                                                                        |
| `No CUDA device found` / jobs much slower                        | no GPU visible: `--nv` / `--gpus`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, or per-campaign MPS on several GPUs                           |
| `kernel launch … failed: no kernel image is available`           | the image lacks this GPU's architecture (e.g. V100 with a `cu130` image): use `cu124` or `cu126`; discard that output    |
| `--mps: could not start the MPS daemon`                          | MPS doesn't work in this container or site: drop `--mps`                                                                 |
| jobs killed (OOM)                                                | plan ~7 GB per Au+Au job plus ~8 GB per node: lower `-j`, use `LBT_TABLE_CACHE` and `--stagger`, or ask for more `--mem` |
| busy-spinning threads, the libgomp warning                       | `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive` before launching                                                                               |
| the GPUs stay ~60 % busy whatever `-j`                           | expected: the cores per GPU set the rate. More cores per GPU help, more jobs don't                                       |
| one job's events have far fewer droplets than the rest           | the rare failure of the deposition check: redo that job                                                                  |
| `unrecognized arguments: --late-dtau` (or `--no-music2-restart`) | an older image without the option: drop it                                                                               |
| a failed job                                                     | its `OUTDIR/<stem>.log`; rerun the same command (finished jobs are skipped)                                              |

More cases: [`docs/README_2stage.md`, §7](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/README_2stage.md#7-troubleshooting).

# Data on the OSDF

Productions are shared on the **OSDF**, the Open Science Data Federation of the OSG: a national network of data origins and caches, reached through the Pelican platform. Data sit on an *origin* under a *namespace*; clients ask a *director* for the closest cache and read from it with plain HTTP. For us that means: one place where a production made on a cluster, a workstation or a Mac can go, from which anyone can download it, or read just the part of a file they need without downloading it, from any machine and without an account. js-contrib's namespace is **`osdf:///fno4hic`**. Reading it is public; writing needs a login.

What is there

Today the namespace holds example and test productions. In the future, besides the example files, training data sets (for the ML/FNO surrogates) and physics simulation productions will be made available there.

The test data named in this documentation:

| path                                    | content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test/AuAu_0_10_jet_pth10-40_eta06_c1/` | the ROOT files of an Au+Au jet campaign (pT̂ 10–40 GeV, 68 files, 2.1 GB), with its campaign file                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `test/h5_read_test/`                    | a small Au+Au hadron file, to try reading in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `test/OO_test/`                         | the hadron files of an O+O `oo_workflow` run, read in place by the notebook `pythonic/oo_analysis.ipynb`                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `LHC/zjet_viz/`                         | two Pb+Pb Z+jet events with their full hydro evolution (pair file, 0.93 GB), hadron files and movies: the example for [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/#example-data-a-pbpb-zjet-event-on-the-osdf) of the medium and the jet wake                                            |
| `RHIC/AuAu_dijet_viz/`                  | one Au+Au 0–10 % dijet event (p̂T 30–40 GeV) with its full hydro evolution (pair file, 233 MB), hadron files and four movies: the example for [`full_event_pyvista.py`](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/#example-data-an-auau-dijet-event-on-the-osdf), from the colliding nuclei to the hadrons |

## The transfer tool: `js_osdf.py`

[`utils/remote_transfer/js_osdf.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/remote_transfer/js_osdf.py) lists, downloads, uploads and removes whole productions, single files or patterns, and picks the files by kind. It runs from a js-contrib checkout and makes its own Python environment on its first run (in `~/.cache/js_osdf/venv`; a `python3` ≥ 3.9 with `venv` and access to PyPI, a few seconds), so it needs no conda env or venv of yours:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib.git
cd js-contrib/utils/remote_transfer
./js_osdf.py ls                     # the namespace: one folder per production
```

Keep it next to `transfer_core.py`, which it imports. Every command takes remote names as `NAME`, `osdf:///fno4hic/NAME` or `/fno4hic/NAME`.

### On a Mac: the xscape wheel

The [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) (0.2.0 or later) has the tool as a command, `xscape-osdf`, with the same commands and options, and `upload_follow.py` as `xscape-upload-follow`. They run in the wheel's environment, which has pelicanfs and google-crc32c: no checkout, no environment in `~/.cache/js_osdf`, nothing to install.

```bash
source ~/.venvs/xscape-0.2.0/bin/activate
xscape-osdf ls test                                    # as ./js_osdf.py ls test below
xscape-osdf download AuAu_c1 --what h5 --to ~/data
xscape-osdf login                                      # once, for uploads
xscape-upload-follow ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/out AuAu_c1 --follow
```

In the examples below, `xscape-osdf` stands for `./js_osdf.py` on the Mac.

## Browsing

```bash
./js_osdf.py ls                                  # the top level
./js_osdf.py ls test                             # a folder
./js_osdf.py ls test -r                          # every file below it
./js_osdf.py ls AuAu_c1 --what h5                # a production's files of one kind, with sizes
./js_osdf.py du                                  # space per top-level folder, and the total
./js_osdf.py du AuAu_c1 -d 2 --sort size         # below a folder, two levels, largest first
```

`AuAu_c1` stands for a production folder; `ls` shows what is there.

## Downloading

```bash
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what h5 --to /scratch            # -> /scratch/AuAu_c1/
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what root --to /scratch          # only the ROOT files
./js_osdf.py download 'AuAu_c1/*_000[1-5]_*' --to /scratch/few   # a pattern (quoted): a few jobs
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what h5 --to /scratch --dry-run  # what would come, and how much
```

The kinds go by file name:

| `--what`        | files                                                                              | for                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `h5`            | `<stem>_particlize.h5`, `<stem>_hadrons_*.h5`, the hadronization logs              | the hadron analyses: `HadronFileReader` needs the particlize files next to the hadron files, and `h5` brings them along |
| `root`          | `<stem>_hadrons.root`, `<campaign>_campaign.root`                                  | ROOT analyses alone: complete on their own                                                                              |
| `pair`          | `<stem>.h5`, the hydro (~0.17–0.29 GB per event), with its `.json`, `.xml`, `.log` | the hydro, the wake observables, FNO training                                                                           |
| `all` (default) | everything in the folder                                                           |                                                                                                                         |

- **Resumable and checked.** Files already there with the same size and CRC32C are skipped, so an interrupted download finishes when the command runs again. Each file is written as `<file>.part` and renamed only when its size and checksum are right.
- **Where they go:** a folder to `--to/<folder>/`, files and patterns to `--to/<file>`.
- `-j N` transfers N files at once (default 4). Measured: ~69 MB/s down from a workstation.
- `--what` takes a comma list (`h5,root`).

## Reading files in place

In the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md) (pelicanfs is installed by default), in the production container and in the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) (from 0.2.0), `osdf://` paths can be read without downloading: pelicanfs finds a cache for the path and reads by byte ranges, so only the parts asked for travel. Both examples read public test files and run as they are:

```python
import uproot
c = uproot.open("osdf:///fno4hic/test/AuAu_0_10_jet_pth10-40_eta06_c1/pth10-40_eta06_c1_campaign.root")
sigma = c["windows"].arrays(["sigma_mb"], library="np")["sigma_mb"]   # the pT-hat windows' cross sections

import fsspec, h5py, hdf5plugin                   # hdf5plugin: the Blosc filter of the HDF5 files
fs = fsspec.filesystem("osdf")
with fs.open("/fno4hic/test/h5_read_test/AuAu_0_10_jet_st1_t000_0001_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5", "rb",
             cache_type="blockcache", block_size=2**20) as fo, h5py.File(fo, "r") as f:
    so = f["hadrons/sample_offsets"][:]
    p = f["hadrons/p"][so[3]:so[4]]               # one oversample's momenta (E, px, py, pz)
```

- **Pass `cache_type="blockcache", block_size=2**20`** for HDF5: fsspec's default read-ahead re-fetches overlapping ranges when HDF5 jumps back to its metadata. With 1 MB blocks, one oversample of a 100 MB hadron file moved 6.3 MB instead of 31.5 MB.
- **Time:** the first open in a process takes ~1–1.5 s (pelicanfs finds a cache); after that, one oversample ~0.1–0.2 s.
- **When to download instead:** for whole productions and for anything read more than once (in place, every pass goes over the network again). `HadronFileReader`, `ParticlizeFile`, `run_h5toROOT.py` and the `analysis/` scripts take local paths only.
- Inside the production container the `pelican` command line does the same for single files: `pelican object get osdf:///fno4hic/… /work/…`.
- **`AttributeError: 'Client' object has no attribute 'info'`** (or `list_files`): pelicanfs up to 1.5.0 does not work with aiowebdav2 1.x (released 2026-11-02), so environments installed since then cannot open `osdf://` URLs in uproot or list folders. Fix: `pip install "aiowebdav2<1"`. js-contrib's requirement files pin it.
- A first, hands-on look at pelicanfs (browsing, uproot, h5py, downloading) is [tutorial 01](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/tutorials/pyjetscape/01_check_setup/index.md), section 2.

What the files hold and how to read them: [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/index.md), [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md), [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md).

## Uploading

Writing to `/fno4hic` needs write access to the namespace: a browser login, or a bearer token. **Whatever is uploaded can be read by everyone.**

```bash
./js_osdf.py login              # once: prints a link; log in and approve in any browser
./js_osdf.py status             # who, the scopes, the time left of the token and the login
./js_osdf.py upload /data/AuAu_c1 --what h5 --dry-run       # what would go
./js_osdf.py upload /data/AuAu_c1 --what h5                 # -> osdf:///fno4hic/AuAu_c1/
./js_osdf.py upload /data/out --what root --as AuAu_pth10-40_v1   # another folder name
./js_osdf.py rm -r AuAu_c1 --dry-run                         # what would be removed
```

- **The login** lasts 15 days (renewals don't extend it): log in again before a long run would pass that date. It is kept in `~/.config/js_osdf/web/` and used by every later command. `logout` revokes it. A bearer token works too (`--token-file`, `$BEARER_TOKEN_FILE`, …).
- **Uploads** of a directory go to `osdf:///fno4hic/[PREFIX/]<directory name>/` (`--as NAME` for another name, `--prefix` for a parent folder). Only the files directly in the directory are sent, not its subdirectories: upload `gpu0/`, `gpu1/` or `t000/`, … one by one (with `--as CAMPAIGN/gpu0`) or use `upload_follow.py` below.
- **Unfinished files are left out:** HDF5 files whose `complete` attribute is false (a job still writing) and `*.part` files.
- **Checked:** Pelican reports sizes but no checksums, so after each upload `js_osdf.py` checks the size at the origin and records size and CRC32C in a manifest in the remote folder; downloads are checked against it. Don't run two uploads into the same folder at once.
- **`rm`** asks first (`--yes` doesn't; `--dry-run` lists all). Removed files can't be brought back.

Measured: ~80 MB/s up from a workstation, 4 or 8 files at once alike.

### Uploading while a production runs

A campaign can write faster than a local disk holds. [`utils/upload_follow.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/upload_follow.py) uploads each job as soon as its `<stem>.json` says complete and, if asked, deletes the local copies after a verified upload, so the local disk no longer limits the campaign:

```bash
utils/upload_follow.py /data/AuAu_a AuAu_a                      # one pass, upload only
utils/upload_follow.py /data/AuAu_a AuAu_a --follow --delete pair   # while the campaign runs
touch /data/AuAu_a/.upload_final       # when the campaign is done: a last pass, then it exits
```

| option                                     |                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--delete none` (default) / `pair` / `all` | after a verified upload, delete nothing / `<stem>.h5` (the hydro) / also `<stem>_particlize.h5`       |
| `--keep-free SIZE`                         | with `pair`/`all`: delete only while the disk has less than SIZE free, the oldest uploads first       |
| `--verify-every N`                         | before deleting, download every Nth file and compare it byte by byte (default 20; 0: never)           |
| `--follow`                                 | repeat every `--interval` s (default 60) until `OUTBASE/.upload_final` appears or `--follow-pid` ends |

- **Verified** means: the origin holds a file of the local size, the manifest's CRC32C matches the local file, and every Nth file was downloaded and compared. The `.json`, `.log` and `.xml` files are never deleted (`run_jobs.sh` needs the `.json` to skip finished jobs).
- **It runs on the host**, next to Docker or on a node that sees a SLURM campaign's directories, from a js-contrib checkout (on a Mac with the xscape wheel: `xscape-upload-follow`, no checkout); any directory of `run_jobs.sh` output directories works (`OUTBASE/<sub>/` → `REMOTE/<sub>/`). Its state survives restarts (`OUTBASE/upload_state.json`, log in `OUTBASE/upload.log`).
- **With `launch_2gpu.sh`**, `--upload REMOTE --delete pair` starts it with the campaign ([Clusters](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/#several-gpus-in-one-machine)). `launch_2gpu.sh --upload` refuses to start without a login.
- Hadronization output is uploaded afterwards: `js_osdf.py upload OUTBASE/gpu0 --as REMOTE/gpu0 --what h5,root`.

**What to move where.** The particlize files are self-contained (surfaces, partons, shower initiators), so hadronization on another cluster and the analysis need only `--what h5`; the large pair files (`--what pair`) only go where the hydro is used, e.g. FNO training.

## Google Cloud Storage

[`js_gcs.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/remote_transfer/js_gcs.py), next to `js_osdf.py`, has the same commands and options for a Google Cloud Storage bucket (default `gs://test_fno`). The bucket is not public: reading and writing need a service-account JSON key (`--key-file`, `$JS_GCS_KEY_FILE` or `$GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`). The analysis environment reads `gs://` paths with `--with-gcs`.

```bash
./js_gcs.py upload /data/AuAu_a --what pair -j 8     # -> gs://test_fno/AuAu_a/
./js_gcs.py download AuAu_a --what root --to /scratch
```

On a Mac with the xscape wheel the command is `xscape-gcs`. Unlike `xscape-osdf` it keeps its own environment in `~/.cache/js_gcs` (google-cloud-storage is not in the wheel), made on its first run.

All options, credentials and the tests: [`utils/remote_transfer/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/remote_transfer/README.md).

# Analyse

# Analyse

A production leaves behind HDF5 files: the hydro evolution of every event, the freeze-out surfaces and partons that hadronization starts from, and the hadrons themselves, plus ROOT copies of the hadrons if you made them. This section shows how to read each kind, how to combine many production files into one data set with the right statistics, and how to go from there to spectra, jets, the jet-induced wake and the O+O observables. Start here if you have production files in hand, your own or downloaded, and want physics out of them.

None of the analysis needs X-SCAPE, a GPU or the production container. Everything on these pages runs in a plain Python environment; ROOT is needed only for the C++ route.

Work in progress: examples, not vetted physics results

The physics analysis scripts, notebooks and their implementations in this section (spectra, jets and jet-hadron correlations, the wake observables, bulk and flow observables such as vₙ{2} and v₂(p_T), the O+O and Z+jet analyses) are work in progress and need further vetting: definitions, corrections, centrality selection and the comparisons with published data have not been checked to the standard of a publication. They are meant mainly as **examples of how to use the simulation outputs** for an analysis. Validate any result, against the experiments' exact procedures and against independent code, before you rely on it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P["production job<br/>(GPU)"] --> PAIR["stem.h5<br/>hydro pair"]
  P --> PART["stem_particlize.h5<br/>surfaces, partons"]
  PART --> HAD["hadronize.py<br/>(CPU)"]
  HAD --> H["stem_hadrons_{bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag}.h5<br/>(+ extra_frag with --extra-hard)"]
  H --> ROOT["run_h5toROOT.py"] --> R["stem_hadrons.root<br/>campaign_campaign.root"]
  PAIR --> A1["h5py, wake_observables.py,<br/>jet_wake.ipynb"]
  H --> A2["HadronFileReader,<br/>FastJet, notebooks"]
  R --> A3["uproot, RDataFrame,<br/>HadronFileReader.h"]
```

## 1. Pick an environment

| environment                          | use it for                                                                                                                    | set up                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **the analysis venv** (recommended)  | every HDF5 file, the ROOT files through uproot, FastJet in Python, the notebooks, `run_h5toROOT.py`                           | [Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md)                                                                                     |
| **the analysis venv + ROOT** (conda) | the above plus PyROOT, RDataFrame, the C++ macros and FastJet in C++                                                          | [Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md), and [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md) |
| **the Mac wheel** (Apple Silicon)    | the same environment that runs X-SCAPE also analyses; on any other computer `pyjetscape[analysis]` installs the readers alone | [Mac (xscape wheel)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md)                                                                                                |
| **the production container**         | re-hadronizing stored surfaces (`hadronize.py`: more oversamples, other iSS settings), which needs X-SCAPE                    | [Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md)                                                                                        |

The venv installs PyJetscape's pure-Python readers (`jetscape.hadrons_h5`, `jetscape.particlize_h5`, ...), h5py with `hdf5plugin` (the files are Blosc-compressed), uproot, awkward, scikit-hep `fastjet`, matplotlib and Jupyter, and it sets `MUSIC_EOS_TABLE` for converting energy density to temperature.

Always `import hdf5plugin`

The production files are compressed with Blosc-zstd. h5py reads them only after `import hdf5plugin`; without it every dataset read fails with `OSError: Can't synchronously read data`. The PyJetscape readers import it for you.

## 2. Get the files

- **Your own run:** the job writes everything into its output directory, one set of files per job (`<stem>.h5`, `<stem>_particlize.h5`, ...); `hadronize.py` adds the hadron files next to them. See [Au+Au jets](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md), [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md) and [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md).
- **Shared productions:** campaigns are published on the OSDF under `osdf:///fno4hic`, public to read. `js_osdf.py` downloads a whole campaign or only the kind of file an analysis needs (`--what h5` for the hadron analyses, `--what root`, `--what pair`), and small files can be read in place without downloading. See [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md).

## 3. A first analysis

The charged-hadron pT spectrum of the background events of a whole campaign, at `$|\eta| < 0.5$`, each event averaged over its oversamples:

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader

edges = np.linspace(0, 4, 41)                                  # pT bins [GeV]
with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:               # the production files in there
    print(r.n_files, "files,", r.n_events, "events, tags", r.tags())
    mid = lambda ev, info: ev.charged & (np.abs(ev.eta) < 0.5)   # charged, |eta| < 0.5
    dn, err = r.hist("bulk_bg", "pt", edges, mask=mid, per_event=False)

pt, w = 0.5 * (edges[1:] + edges[:-1]), np.diff(edges)
plt.errorbar(pt, dn / w, err / w, fmt="o")                     # per event: d^2N/dpT deta
plt.yscale("log"); plt.xlabel(r"$p_T$ [GeV]"); plt.ylabel(r"$dN_{ch}/dp_T\,d\eta$")
plt.savefig("pt_spectrum.png")
```

`hist` returns, per bin, the count per event (each event first averaged over its own oversamples, then over the events) and its error. Replace `"bulk_bg"` with `"bulk_jet"` for the events with the jet's wake, `"jet_frag"` for the jet's own hadrons, or `"extra_frag"` for the fragments of the event's other hard scatterings (productions with `--extra-hard`). [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md) explains all of it.
