# What a production writes

Every production job writes a small set of files that share one name, the **stem** (`AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001`, `OO_isr_c1_0007`, ...). This page describes each kind: what it holds, how it is laid out, and how big it is. It also says what one "event" means at hadron level, which settings must match before files are combined, and how to look inside any file. Read it once before your first analysis; the statistics of oversamples in particular affect every result.

**Why HDF5, and why one file per job.** The hydro evolution is a large 4D array per event; HDF5 stores it chunked (one chunk per event and τ frame) and compressed, so a single frame reads without the rest. Every file carries its provenance as attributes: the job's XML, the grid, the seed and the software build. Jobs are never merged: a campaign is a directory of production files, and the readers open them side by side as one data set.

## 1. The files at a glance

The Au+Au jet production (two hydro legs per event) writes, per job:

| file                                              | made by                                  | holds                                                                                                              | size per event                                       | read with                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `<stem>.h5`, the **pair file**                    | the production job                       | both hydro legs on the output grid: `arr` (jet leg), `arr_bg` (background); the droplets, the showers, diagnostics | ~170 MB with 15 jets per background, 285 MB with one | h5py, FNO4d's loader, `wake_observables.py` |
| `<stem>_particlize.h5`                            | the job, with `--write-particlize`       | both freeze-out surfaces (32 columns per cell), the final partons, the shower initiators, the event table          | ~90 MB (15 jets per background)                      | `ParticlizeFile`                            |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5`                      | `hadronize.py`                           | iSS on the jet leg's surface: bulk + wake, N oversamples per event                                                 | ~0.2 MB per oversample at full precision             | `HadronFileReader`                          |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`                       | `hadronize.py`                           | iSS on the background's surface, once per background                                                               | as above                                             | `HadronFileReader`                          |
| `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5`                      | `hadronize.py`                           | the fragmented surviving partons, M fragmentations per event; with extra hard scatterings the trigger's alone      | small                                                | `HadronFileReader`                          |
| `<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5`                    | `hadronize.py`, only with `--extra-hard` | the fragments of the event's other hard scatterings, M fragmentations per event, with `scatterings/`               | small                                                | `HadronFileReader`                          |
| `<stem>_hadrons.root`, `<campaign>_campaign.root` | `run_h5toROOT.py`                        | the three hadron tags as RNTuple or TTree, one entry per oversample; event table, cross sections, provenance       | 0.9 × the HDF5 hadron files                          | uproot, RDataFrame, `HadronFileReader.h`    |
| `<stem>.json`, `.xml`, `.log`                     | every job                                | the job summary (seed, events, droplets, edge hits), the exact job XML, the log                                    |                                                      | `json`, an editor                           |

The sizes are for the Au+Au campaign setting (three pT̂ windows, five jets per window and background, partons at `$|y| < 0.6$`): pair + particlize file together 0.243 GB per event, 0.097 GB with `--particlize-only` (no pair file).

Other productions write a subset or a variant:

| production                                                | files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Au+Au hydro only (`prod_AuAu_0_10`)                       | `AuAu_0_10_*.h5` with `arr` only (~140 MB per event)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Au+Au **hadrons only** (`run_prod_jet.py --hadrons-only`) | the three hadron files and the undecayed `_primary` bulk files, written in the job; no pair and no particlize file; the event record sits in the jet files' `units/`                                                                                                      |
| O+O with ISR (`prod_OO_isr`)                              | one hydro per event (`OO_isr_*.h5`, ~17 MB), a particlize file (~10 MB), the jet hadrons and optionally the bulk hadrons made in the job; see [O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md)                                                         |
| Z+jet (Pb+Pb)                                             | hadrons-only jobs, as above, with the Z and its leptons in the event record; see [Z+jet and other systems](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/zjet-other/index.md)                                                                                               |
| any jet production with `--extra-hard`                    | the same files plus `<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5` and the extras' records; minimum bias (`--hard none`) has no `jet_frag`; see [below](#the-events-other-hard-scatterings) and [Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md) |

### Which files an analysis needs

| analysis                                               | files                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| hadron spectra, the wake at hadron level, jets         | the particlize file and the three hadron files of every production file (hadrons-only jobs: the hadron files); or the ROOT files alone        |
| the wake in the fluid, the energy balance, the deposit | the pair files (and the particlize files)                                                                                                     |
| FNO training                                           | the pair files, or the hydro-only files                                                                                                       |
| more oversamples, other iSS settings                   | the particlize files, and `hadronize.py` in the [container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md) on a CPU node |

The particlize files are self-contained: a hadron analysis never needs the large pair files. With the OSDF downloader, `--what h5` fetches exactly the particlize and hadron files ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)).

## 2. Hydro pair files

**Why pairs.** The jet production runs MUSIC twice on the same initial condition: once without the jet (the background, MUSIC_1), and once with the energy the jet deposits (the jet leg, MUSIC_2). Both legs are bit-identical until the first droplet arrives, so `arr − arr_bg` is the jet's effect on the medium and nothing else: no pairing of separate runs, no event-by-event fluctuations to subtract. How to use them: [Hydro and hadrons together](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hydro-hadrons/index.md).

| dataset                               | shape                                      | content                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `arr`                                 | `(nevents, 4, nx, ny, neta, ntau)` float32 | the **jet leg** (MUSIC_2). Channels `energy_density` [GeV/fm³], `vx`, `vy`, `vz` (Cartesian lab velocities)                                                                    |
| `arr_bg`                              | as `arr`                                   | the **background** (MUSIC_1)                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ntau_freezeout`, `ntau_freezeout_bg` | `(nevents,)`                               | frames written per leg; every frame from there on is 0                                                                                                                         |
| `tau_freezeout`, `tau_freezeout_bg`   | `(nevents,)`                               | when each leg's hydro ended [fm/c]                                                                                                                                             |
| `source/droplets`, `source/offsets`   | `(M, 8)`, `(nevents + 1,)`                 | the droplets MUSIC_2 received: `tau, x, y, eta, E, px, py, pz`; event i is rows `offsets[i]:offsets[i+1]`                                                                      |
| `shower/`                             |                                            | the shower graphs (partons, vertices, initiators), read with `jetscape.showers`                                                                                                |
| `diag/`                               | `(nevents,)` each                          | `E_droplets`, `n_droplets`, `bg_id`, `frames_identical`, boundary and edge flags, `tau0_music`, `eloss_tstart`, `wall_s`; with pT̂ windows `pthat_bin`, `pthat`, `event_weight` |

- **The grid** is in the attributes: `x_min`, `dx`, `nx` (and `y_*`, `eta_*`), `tau_min`, `dtau`. The production default (`grid_fno.yaml`) is 64 × 64 × 32 cells: x, y from −12.2 to 12.2 fm in steps of 0.3875 fm, η_s from −4.84 to 4.84 in steps of 0.3125, τ = 0.5 + k · 0.1 fm/c. MUSIC's own grid is recorded in the `*_MUSIC` attributes.
- **Read frame by frame.** Each chunk is one event and one τ frame (~2 MB): `f["arr"][i, ..., k]` is fast, a single cell's whole history reads every chunk.
- **The legs freeze out at different times.** The deposit reheats the jet leg, by 1–2 fm/c in 0–10 % Au+Au. After the background has frozen out, `arr − arr_bg` is the jet leg's whole medium, not a wake: compare only frames below both `ntau_freezeout` values.
- **Shared backgrounds.** When several events share one background (`--reuse`, pT̂ windows), `arr_bg` is an HDF5 virtual dataset over `arr_bg_store`, so each background is stored once. Read `arr_bg`, never the store. Copy such files whole (`cp`, `rsync`, `h5repack`): copying only the `arr_bg` dataset into another file gives a view without its data, which reads as zeros.
- **No gridded source.** There is no `source/S`: MUSIC evaluates the liquefier's kernel per cell and step, so only the droplets are stored.

## 3. Particlize files

The input to hadronization, stored instead of hadrons so that hadronization can run later, on CPUs, as often as needed (`jetscape.particlize_h5`):

| group               | content                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `surface/jet/cells` | MUSIC_2's freeze-out surface, `(N, 32)` float32, one unit per event: exactly the fields iSS reads                                                                  |
| `surface/bg/cells`  | MUSIC_1's, one unit per **new** background; `events/bg_unit` says which unit an event used                                                                         |
| `partons/data`      | the final partons the jet hadronization receives, `(K, 14)`: shower, pid, pstat, E, px, py, pz, t, x, y, z, mass, col, acol                                        |
| `initiators/data`   | each event's shower-initiating partons, `(J, 11)`: shower, pid, pstat, px, py, pz, E, x, y, z, t                                                                   |
| `events/`           | per event: `bg_id`, `bg_unit`, `bg_key`, `n_cells_jet`, `n_cells_bg`, `n_partons`, droplet energies, MUSIC's τ₀, boundary flags; with windows `pthat_bin`, `pthat` |
| attributes          | `music_input` (iSS reads the EoS from it), `T_fo`, `pair_file`, `file_uuid`, the provenance                                                                        |

- **Surface columns** (`SURFACE_COLUMNS`): `tau, x, y, eta, ds0..ds3, u0..u3, e, T, P, nB, nQ, nS, muB, muQ, muS`, the 10 components of π^{μν} and `Pi`. Lossless: the framework's surface cells are float.
- **Parton status:** 0 shower, 1 recoil, −1 hole, −11/−13/−17 went into the droplets (never hadronized), 22 photon. The jet hadronization takes 0, 1, 22 and −1.
- **A broken leg shows here:** a background with far more or fewer cells than its jet leg did not freeze out ([Hadrons, bad runs](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/#6-bad-runs)).

Reading one event:

```python
from jetscape.particlize_h5 import ParticlizeFile, SURFACE_COLUMNS

with ParticlizeFile("AuAu_0_10_jet_c1_0001_particlize.h5") as pf:
    cells    = pf.surface("jet", 0)          # (N, 32) float32: MUSIC_2's surface, event 0
    cells_bg = pf.surface("bg", 0)           # the background event 0 used (events/bg_unit)
    partons  = pf.partons(0)                 # (K, 14)
    ini      = pf.initiators(0)              # (J, 11)
    n_cells  = pf.events("n_cells_jet")      # a column of the per-event table
    T_fo     = cells[:, SURFACE_COLUMNS.index("T")]
```

Particlize files from before the initiators were added have no `initiators/` group; `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/add_initiators.py` copies them in once from the pair files.

## 4. Hadron files

`hadronize.py` (or the job itself, in hadrons-only mode) writes one file per **tag** (`jetscape.hadrons_h5`, format `xscape/hadrons`):

| tag          | from                                                                                                                  | one unit is                                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `bulk_jet`   | iSS on the jet leg's surface: bulk + wake                                                                             | an event                                           |
| `bulk_bg`    | iSS on the background's surface: bulk                                                                                 | a background (shared by the events that reused it) |
| `jet_frag`   | Colorless hadronization of the surviving partons (O+O: iColored, in the job); with `--extra-hard` the trigger's alone | an event                                           |
| `extra_frag` | only with `--extra-hard`: Colorless hadronization of the other hard scatterings' surviving partons                    | an event                                           |

Each file keeps every sample apart:

| dataset                        | content                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hadrons/pid`, `hadrons/pstat` | int32, one row per hadron                                                                                    |
| `hadrons/p`                    | float32 `(n, 4)`: E, px, py, pz [GeV]                                                                        |
| `hadrons/x`                    | float32 `(n, 4)`: t, x, y, z [fm]; absent with `--no-x`                                                      |
| `hadrons/sample_offsets`       | where each sample (oversample or fragmentation) starts                                                       |
| `hadrons/unit_offsets`         | where each unit's samples start                                                                              |
| `units/`                       | per unit: `unit`, `event`, `n_samples`, `seed`, `n_cells`; hadrons-only and O+O jobs: the whole event record |
| `initiators/`                  | `bulk_jet`, `jet_frag`: each event's shower initiators                                                       |

**Choices made at hadronization, recorded in the files.** `--keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8` rounds the stored momenta and positions (58 % of the disk; the recommended campaign setting); `--eta-max X`, `--charged` and `--no-x` store only part of the hadrons. All three tags get the same selection, so jet − background stays complete inside it. They change only what is stored: the same seeds give the same hadrons, and `hadronize.py --force` without them recreates the full files from the particlize file. The attributes `eta_max`, `charged_only`, `positions` and each dataset's `keep_mantissa_bits` record them; `HadronFileReader.precision(i)`, `.eta_max()` and `.selection()` read them back. Full option list: [`prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md).

### What an event is

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  BG["background b<br/>(MUSIC_1 fluid)"] -->|"bulk_bg, unit b:<br/>samples 0..N_bg-1"| GB["G_b^k"]
  BG --> E1["jet event i<br/>(its own MUSIC_2 fluid)"]
  BG --> E2["jet event i' (same background)"]
  E1 -->|"bulk_jet, unit i:<br/>samples 0..N-1"| J["J_i^k: bulk + wake"]
  E1 -->|"jet_frag, unit i:<br/>fragmentations 0..M-1"| F["F_i^(k mod M)"]
```

- **A jet event** at hadron level is oversample k of `bulk_jet` plus fragmentation k mod M of `jet_frag`. Its background is sample k of `bulk_bg`, unit `events/bg_unit` of that event.
- **Oversamples are not independent collisions.** The N oversamples of an event are independent Cooper–Frye samplings of **one** fluid. Average each event over its samples first, then over events, and take errors per event. `HadronFileReader` does both.
- **Events that share a background** (`--reuse`, pT̂ windows) are correlated through it. Per-window results and jet − background are fine; spectra stitched over windows have correlated errors.
- **Correlated sampling** (`hadronize.py --correlated`): sample k of the jet leg and sample k of its background share most hadrons, so jet − background is ~8 times less noisy at `$|\eta| < 1$`. Only the paired error (the spread of the per-sample differences) is then right; `jet_minus_background` uses it automatically.
- **An empty surface** (MUSIC stopped at the grid boundary) gives a unit with no samples; the readers skip such events.

The ROOT files have the same structure, one entry per oversample: [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md).

### The event's other hard scatterings

Productions with `--extra-hard` ([Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md)) have each event's other hard scatterings, the **extras**. Their wakes are in `bulk_jet`, so `bulk_jet − bulk_bg` is the response to all scatterings; their fragments are in `extra_frag`; `jet_frag` stays the trigger's alone. A jet event at hadron level is then oversample k of `bulk_jet` + fragmentation k mod M of `jet_frag` + fragmentation k mod M of `extra_frag`.

| where                                                           | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| per event: pair `diag/`, particlize `events/`, hadron `units/`  | `n_extra`, `extra_mu` (= N_coll σ/σ_NN), `extra_E`, `extra_pt` (summed E and scalar pT of the extras' handed-over partons)                                                                                                  |
| `scatterings/data` + `offsets` (pair, particlize, `extra_frag`) | one row per scattering, columns `scatter, pthat, code, x, y, n_partons, E, pt`; the trigger's first (scatter 0; none with `--hard none`); `code` is Pythia's process code, x, y [fm] the binary collision                   |
| `initiators/scatter` (particlize, `extra_frag`)                 | each shower initiator's scattering, aligned with `initiators/data`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `<stem>_hadrons_extra_frag.h5`                                  | the layout of `jet_frag` (unit = event, `--n-frag` samples), plus `scatterings/`, the extras' `initiators/`, `partons/` (hadrons-only jobs) and `hadrons/scatter` (with `--extra-hadronize per_scattering`)                 |
| attributes                                                      | `extra_hard`, `extra_no_trigger`, `extra_pthat_min`, `extra_sigma`, `extra_sigma_err`, `extra_sigma_nn`, `extra_warmup`, `extra_fixed_n`, `extra_seed`, `extra_rng_seed`; `prod_extra_*`; `extra_hadronize` on `extra_frag` |
| `<stem>.json`                                                   | `extra_hard`, `extra_pthat_min`, `extra_sigma(_err)`, `extra_sigma_nn`, `n_extra_total`                                                                                                                                     |

A minimum-bias file (`--hard none`) has no `jet_frag` and no trigger row in `scatterings/`. Files without extras have none of these: their layout is unchanged. Do not combine files with and without extras, or with different thresholds (`extra_pthat_min`), in one data set.

## 5. Provenance: the job record

Every job keeps its exact inputs, so a file can always be traced and reproduced:

| where                                                                                                 | what                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<stem>.json`                                                                                         | the job summary: seed, events written, droplets, edge hits, skipped events, cross sections     |
| `<stem>.xml`, attribute `prod_user_xml`                                                               | the job's XML, verbatim                                                                        |
| `prod_grid_yaml`                                                                                      | the output grid                                                                                |
| `prod_seed`, `prod_reuse`, `prod_hard`, `prod_build`, `prod_host`                                     | seed, background reuse, hard process, software build, machine                                  |
| `pthat_bins`, `pthat_bin_sigma_gen`, `pthat_bin_sigma_err`, `pthat_bin_n_accepted`, `pthat_bin_seeds` | the pT̂ windows and each window's Pythia cross section [mb], written when the job ends          |
| `music_input`, `hadronize_xml`                                                                        | MUSIC's input and the hadronization settings                                                   |
| `file_uuid` (particlize), `source_uuid` (hadron files)                                                | the link between a hadron file and the run it came from: `HadronFileReader` refuses a mismatch |

The pair files and the particlize files carry the same `prod_*` attributes.

## 6. Settings to check before combining files

None of these shows in the data arrays. Files that differ in one of them belong in different data sets:

| setting                                                                                           | why it matters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | where it is recorded                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **MUSIC's late time step** (Δτ 0.02 → 0.05 fm/c from τ = 3 fm/c, on by default in current images) | the stored frames stay at 0.1 fm/c, so the files look alike; but the medium differs at the 10⁻³ level, the cell-level wake by ~5 % below ~1 fm. Hadron observables agree within ±2 %. Don't mix late-step and constant-step files in one training set or comparison | `<late_delta_tau>` in the job XML (`prod_user_xml`); absent or 0: constant step                             |
| the image or build                                                                                | MUSIC on the GPU and on the CPU differ at 2 × 10⁻³: one image per campaign                                                                                                                                                                                          | `prod_build`, `prod_host`; the campaign's notes                                                             |
| the output grid                                                                                   | 64 × 64 × 32 at ±12.2 fm, or the earlier 65 × 65 × 33 at ±10 fm: never in one training set                                                                                                                                                                          | `prod_grid_yaml`; `nx`, `dx`, ...                                                                           |
| hadron precision and selection                                                                    | `--keep-bits-*`, `--eta-max`, `--charged`, `--no-x`: one setting per campaign                                                                                                                                                                                       | `HadronFileReader.precision(i)`, `.eta_max()`, `.selection()`; the reader warns on a mix                    |
| correlated sampling                                                                               | the errors of jet − background must be paired                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `HadronFileReader.correlated`                                                                               |
| pT̂ windows, parton rapidity cut, reuse                                                            | each window has its own cross section; events sharing a background are correlated                                                                                                                                                                                   | `pthat_bins`, `pthat_bin_sigma_gen`, `parton_ymax`, `prod_reuse`; `events/bg_unit`                          |
| the liquefier normalisation and the LBT double counting                                           | older pair files gave MUSIC_2 the wrong droplet energy (only a rerun fixes the jet leg) or counted absorbed LBT partons twice (`fix_lbt_double_counting.py` repairs the partons)                                                                                    | pair file: `liquefier_normalize_on_hydro_grid` = 1 for fixed files; `lbt_double_count_fix` on repaired ones |

The settings of every production file of a campaign:

```python
import glob, h5py, hdf5plugin, yaml              # hdf5plugin registers the Blosc filter
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

for path in sorted(glob.glob("/path/to/campaign/**/*_particlize.h5", recursive=True)):
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as f:
        A = f.attrs
        late = ET.fromstring(A["prod_user_xml"]).findtext(".//Hydro/MUSIC/late_delta_tau")
        grid = yaml.safe_load(A["prod_grid_yaml"])["grid"]
        print(path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], "| seed", A["prod_seed"],
              "| late_delta_tau", late.strip() if late else "absent (constant step)",
              "| grid x", grid["x"], "| reuse", A.get("prod_reuse"))
```

The details behind the late time step: [`docs/REPORT_FINAL_OPTIM.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/REPORT_FINAL_OPTIM.md); the liquefier normalisation: [`docs/SOURCE_NORMALIZATION.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/SOURCE_NORMALIZATION.md).

## 7. Looking inside any file: `h5_inspect.py`

[`utils/h5_inspect.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/h5_inspect.py) prints every group and dataset with its shape, dtype, storage and attributes. For the hydro files it adds a summary that decodes the conventions: the output and MUSIC grids, the axes, the per-event freeze-out, the ragged `*offsets` groups with their columns, the `diag/` vectors, and it flags inconsistencies. It needs only h5py and numpy, and reads nothing from the large datasets unless asked:

```bash
python utils/h5_inspect.py AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5                  # tree + summary
python utils/h5_inspect.py AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 --no-tree        # summary only
python utils/h5_inspect.py AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 --attr prod_user_xml   # one attribute in full
python utils/h5_inspect.py AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 --stats --event 0      # min/max/mean, NaN/inf of event 0
python utils/h5_inspect.py AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5 --json > meta.json
```

For the HDF5 command-line tools (`h5dump`, `h5ls`) on Blosc data, point them at the plugin: `export HDF5_PLUGIN_PATH=$(python -c "import hdf5plugin; print(hdf5plugin.PLUGIN_PATH)")`.

# Hadrons

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

This page shows how to read the hadron files of a whole campaign as one data set, fill histograms with the right per-event statistics, pull out single events, weight pT̂ windows by their cross sections, and spot bad runs. The tool for almost all of it is `HadronFileReader` from `jetscape.hadrons_h5`; lower-level readers and the Pythonic `HadronArray` are at the end, for when you need one file, one sample or awkward arrays. It applies to the Au+Au jet productions (two stages or hadrons-only jobs), the Z+jet productions and the productions with extra hard scatterings or minimum bias; O+O hadron files made in the job by the O+O with ISR production are read differently ([O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/index.md)).

The file layout and what an event is: [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/#4-hadron-files).

## 1. Open a campaign

```python
import numpy as np
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader

r = HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign")       # or: with HadronFileReader(...) as r:
print(r.n_files, "files,", r.n_events, "events, tags", r.tags())
```

`source` can be:

- **a directory:** every production file in it, i.e. every `*_particlize.h5`, and every hadrons-only job (its `*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5`). Subdirectories are **not** searched.
- **a glob pattern** (quoted, of particlize or hadron files): the way to read a campaign spread over subdirectories, e.g. the per-GPU output of a multi-GPU run: `HadronFileReader("/data/zjet_c00/gpu*/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")`.
- **a list** of stems or particlize paths.

Events are numbered globally, in the sorted order of the files: `r.locate(g)` gives (file index, local event), `r.global_event(file, local)` the reverse, and `r.stems` lists the files.

**What it checks on open:**

- a hadron file whose recorded `source_uuid` is not its particlize file's `file_uuid` (renamed, or from another run) is refused (`check_uuid=False` overrides);
- mixed precisions, η cuts, charged-only or no-position files give warnings: results are then right only for what all files hold;
- a background that appears in two production files (two campaigns over the same seeds) gives a warning; `r.duplicate_backgrounds()` lists them.

## 2. Histograms, totals and the wake

`hist`, `total` and `jet_minus_background` do the statistics for you. For every event, the samples of its unit are histogrammed and divided by that unit's number of samples; these per-event means are then averaged over events. So every event counts the same, even when files were hadronized with different `--oversample`, and the errors are per event (compound-Poisson per event, added over events).

```python
def lead(info):
    """phi and pseudorapidity of the event's hardest shower-initiating parton."""
    ini = info.initiators()                     # (K, 11): shower, pid, pstat, px, py, pz, E, ...
    px, py, pz = ini[np.argmax(np.hypot(ini[:, 3], ini[:, 4])), 3:6]
    return np.arctan2(py, px), np.arcsinh(pz / np.hypot(px, py))

def dphi(ev, info):                             # azimuth relative to the leading parton
    return np.mod(ev.phi - lead(info)[0] + np.pi / 2, 2 * np.pi) - np.pi / 2

def soft_charged(ev, info):
    return ev.charged & (ev.pt > 0.2) & (ev.pt < 4) & (np.abs(ev.eta) < 1)

with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    # names of EventHadrons attributes: per-event sample means, averaged over events
    pt, pt_err = r.hist("bulk_bg", "pt", np.linspace(0, 3, 31), mask="charged")
    n_mid, n_err = r.total("bulk_jet", mask=lambda ev, info: ev.charged & (np.abs(ev.eta) < 1))

    # the wake: <jet leg> - <its own background>, event by event
    bins = np.linspace(-np.pi / 2, 3 * np.pi / 2, 17)
    wake, wake_err = r.jet_minus_background(dphi, bins, mask=soft_charged)
    full, _ = r.jet_minus_background(dphi, bins, mask=soft_charged, fragments=True)  # + jet_frag
```

- **`values`, `mask`, `weights`** are either names (an attribute of `EventHadrons`: `pid`, `pstat`, `p`, `x`, `E`, `px`, `py`, `pz`, `pt`, `eta`, `y`, `phi`, `charged`, `sample`; for `mask` also `"charged"` or a species, `"pi+"`, `"K-"`, `"p"`, `"pbar"`, `"pi"`, `"K"`, `"p+pbar"`), or callables `f(ev, info)` returning one value per hadron. A tuple of names (or a callable returning a tuple) gives an N-dimensional histogram.
- **Callables get the event's `info`** (`EventInfo`: `event`, `stem`, `local_event`, `bg_unit`, `seed`, `pthat_bin`, `pthat`, `n_coll`, `z`, `initiators()`), which jet-relative observables need: above, Δφ to the event's leading initiator.
- **Names are faster.** With names only, a background shared by several events is binned once and counted for each of them. For a callable that does not use `info`, pass `per_event=False` for the same single pass; the result is identical.
- **`events=`** restricts any of them to a subset, e.g. one pT̂ window.
- **`jet_minus_background`** uses only events whose jet leg *and* background have samples, each against its own background. `fragments=True` adds the jet's own hadrons, and the extra hard scatterings' if the campaign has them (`extras=False` leaves those out).

Which error

For files hadronized with `--correlated`, `jet_minus_background` takes its error from the spread of the per-sample differences (`paired=True`, chosen automatically: `r.correlated`), the only right error when the legs share hadrons. The default compound-Poisson error treats every hadron as independent; resonance daughters in one bin make it ~20 % too small for soft multiplicities, which `paired=True` also avoids for independent legs with equal sample counts.

## 3. A worked example: multiplicity and spectra

The charged dN/dη of the background and of the jet events, the identified spectra at `$|y| < 0.5$`, and the wake's charged multiplicity, for one campaign:

```python
import numpy as np
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader

eta_e = np.linspace(-5, 5, 41)
pt_e = np.linspace(0, 3, 31)
with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    # dN_ch/deta, per event (each event: the mean over its oversamples)
    bg, bg_err = r.hist("bulk_bg", "eta", eta_e, mask="charged")
    jet, jet_err = r.hist("bulk_jet", "eta", eta_e, mask="charged")
    dndeta_bg = bg / np.diff(eta_e)

    # identified dN/dpT at |y| < 0.5 (width 1 in y)
    spectra = {}
    for s in ("pi+", "K+", "p"):
        mid_y = lambda ev, info, s=s: ev.species(s) & (np.abs(ev.y) < 0.5)
        h, e = r.hist("bulk_bg", "pt", pt_e, mask=mid_y, per_event=False)
        spectra[s] = (h / np.diff(pt_e), e / np.diff(pt_e))

    # the wake's charged hadrons at |eta| < 1, and the jet's own
    mid = lambda ev, info: ev.charged & (np.abs(ev.eta) < 1)
    wake, wake_err = r.jet_minus_background(None, None, mask=mid, per_event=False)
    n_frag, n_frag_err = r.total("jet_frag", mask=mid, per_event=False)
print("dN_ch/deta at eta = 0:", dndeta_bg[len(dndeta_bg) // 2])
print("wake N_ch(|eta| < 1):", wake[0], "+-", wake_err[0], "| fragments:", n_frag)
```

With `values=None, bins=None`, `jet_minus_background` returns the difference of the totals as a one-bin array. For a 2D map in the jet frame, pass a callable returning a tuple, e.g. `lambda ev, info: (ev.eta - lead(info)[1], dphi(ev, info))`, and a tuple of bin edges.

## 4. Single events

```python
with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    ev = r.jet_event(0, 17)          # global event 0, oversample 17 + its fragmentation
    ev["pid"], ev["p"], ev["x"]      # p = (E, px, py, pz); ev["origin"]: 0 bulk, 1 fragment
    bg = r.background_event(0, 17)   # oversample 17 of the background event 0 used
    info = r.event_info(0)           # stem, local_event, bg_unit, seed, pthat_bin, initiators()
    n, m = r.n_oversamples(0), r.n_frag(0)
    for ev in r.iter_jet_events(0):  # every oversample of event 0
        ...
```

`jet_event(e, k)` pairs oversample k with fragmentation k mod `n_frag(e)`; `frag_sample=` picks another, `fragments=False` leaves them out. These are the inputs for jet finding ([Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/index.md)).

### The event's other hard scatterings

Campaigns made with `--extra-hard` ([Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md)) have a fourth tag, `extra_frag`: the fragments of the event's other hard scatterings. **The extras belong to the event, not to the trigger.** By default the full event is `bulk_jet + jet_frag + extra_frag`, and "the event without its trigger" (B) is `bulk_bg + extra_frag`; the trigger's truth (e.g. the Z–hadron signal `bulk_jet − bulk_bg + jet_frag`) stays the trigger's. A campaign without `extra_frag` reads exactly as before.

```python
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader
import numpy as np

with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    r.has_extras()                               # True: the campaign has extra_frag
    sc = r.event_info(0).scatterings()           # (S, 8): scatter, pthat, code, x, y, n, E, pt
    print(sc[sc[:, 0] > 0, 1])                   # the extras' pTHat (the trigger is scatter 0)
    ev = r.jet_event(0, 0)                       # bulk_jet + jet_frag + extra_frag
    extras_only = ev["origin"] == 2              # origin 0 bulk, 1 jet_frag, 2 extra_frag
    bins = np.linspace(0, 20, 41)
    full, err = r.jet_minus_background("pt", bins, mask="charged", fragments=True)
    trig, err = r.jet_minus_background("pt", bins, mask="charged", fragments=True, extras=False)
    h, e = r.hist("extra_frag", "pt", bins, mask="charged")      # the extras' fragments alone
```

`jet_event(..., extras=False)` leaves them out of a single event. A **minimum-bias** campaign (`--hard none`) has no `jet_frag` and no trigger; analyses that need a trigger (the Z+jet and Z–hadron map steps, `qa.py`, `wake_iso.py`) refuse it. For its bulk observables see [Bulk and flow](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/bulk/index.md). The per-analysis switches are on [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#7-worked-examples-the-zjet-campaign-analyses) and [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md).

## 5. pT̂ windows and cross sections

Campaigns with several pT̂ windows per background (`--pthat-bins`) have one Pythia, and one cross section, per window. Each window's histogram is a per-event average, so the windows can have different event counts; multiply each by its cross section to stitch them:

```python
with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    r.pthat_bins                                   # (K, 2): the windows
    edges = np.linspace(0, 40, 41)
    spec, var = np.zeros(40), np.zeros(40)
    for k in range(len(r.pthat_bins)):
        h, e = r.hist("jet_frag", "pt", edges, mask="charged", events=r.pthat_bin_events(k))
        sigma, _ = r.pthat_bin_sigma(k)            # mb, after the parton-y cut
        spec += sigma * h                          # each window: per-event mean x its sigma
        var += (sigma * e) ** 2                    # jet_frag: windows independent
```

`spec` is then dσ/dpT per bin [mb]. `pthat_bin_sigma(k)` combines the files' Pythia estimates, weighted by their accepted events; `pthat_bin_acceptance(k)` is the parton-rapidity cut's acceptance. The windows share their backgrounds, so for the bulk tags the errors of different windows are correlated: the simple sum of variances above is right for `jet_frag` only.

## 6. Bad runs

Two rare failures show up in the data, not in the logs. Check for them before an analysis:

- **A leg that never froze out.** Its background has ~3 times the freeze-out cells and ~11 times the hadrons of its jet leg. Compare `n_cells_bg / n_cells_jet` (particlize file's `events/`): `wake_hadrons.py`, `hadron_distributions.C` and the C++ `HadronFileReader.h` drop events where it is off by more than 20 %. In the job logs, `grep -l "Maximum allowed time reached" DIR/*.log` finds such jobs.
- **A job whose jets lost almost no energy** (once in ~250 campaign jobs): its droplets per event fall far below the campaign's. `utils/check_deposition.py` reads every job summary and flags it (exit code 1):

```bash
python utils/check_deposition.py /path/to/campaign              # every <stem>.json below it
python utils/check_deposition.py /data/c1/gpu0 /data/c1/gpu1    # one campaign, two directories
```

Move a flagged job's files away and rerun the campaign command, which redoes the job.

## 7. Lower-level readers

For one file, one sample, or a whole small file in memory:

```python
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFile, JetEvents, Hadrons

with HadronFile("<stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5") as hf:       # random access, nothing loaded
    one = hf.sample_event(0, 17)                            # unit (event) 0, sample 17: pid, pstat, p, x
    ini = hf.initiators(0)                                  # the event's shower initiators
with JetEvents.from_stem("<stem>") as je:                   # the three files + particlize of one job
    ev = je.jet_event(0, 17)                                # bulk_jet sample 17 + a fragmentation

h = Hadrons.from_h5("<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")            # a whole file in memory
dn, err = h.hist(h.eta, np.linspace(-1, 1, 5), mask=h.charged)   # per sample
```

`Hadrons` carries `pt`, `eta`, `y`, `phi`, `charged`, `sample`, `unit` as arrays (in float64, about 2.4 times the file's memory) and `hist` / `total` averaged per sample. `units=` reads only some units.

### The Pythonic `HadronArray`

`jetscape.HadronArray` holds a hadron file as flat arrays with sample offsets, without derived columns, and turns it into awkward arrays of `vector` four-momenta on demand, for selections and FastJet's array interface:

```python
import jetscape as js

bulk = js.HadronArray.from_h5("<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")
had = bulk.to_awkward(by_unit=True)            # units x samples x hadrons, Momentum4D records
charged = had[js.select(had, "charged")]
mid = abs(charged.eta) < 0.5
```

It needs no X-SCAPE build and also reads file objects (e.g. a file streamed from the OSDF). More in [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md).

## 8. Scripts and notebooks for hadrons

|                                                                                                                                                                                 | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb) | η, φ, pT of background, background + wake, fragments and the wake, in the lab and relative to the jet; checks the correlated-sampling flags (`HADRON_DIR`, `MAX_EVENTS`, `PAIRED`)                                                                                         |
| [`analysis/wake_hadrons.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/wake_hadrons.py) + `wake_hadrons.ipynb`                    | one pass over a campaign: the wake per event in the jet frame, ΔR profiles, identified spectra, totals → `wake_hadrons.h5`; then the figures. See [Hydro and hadrons together](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hydro-hadrons/#4-the-wake-at-hadron-level) |

**Threads and memory.** `HadronFileReader` is one Python process, reading one production file at a time and only the units it needs: the four events of two seed files with 500 and 100 oversamples (~11 M hadrons) take 2.7 s. A background of 2000 oversamples is ~14 M hadrons, ~1.5 GB with the derived kinematics. For more speed, split a campaign by `events=` over processes.

**Reading in place from the OSDF.** `HadronFileReader` takes local paths only; download the campaign first ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)). Single files can be read in place with h5py or `HadronArray` through `fsspec`.

# Jets with FastJet

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

This page shows how to find jets in the production hadrons with FastJet from Python: the conventions the notebooks and analyses share, the classic (SWIG) interface with jet areas and ρA background subtraction, embedding a jet into a background it never touched, charged and full jets, and the array (awkward) interface. It ends with the Z+jet, Z+hadron and dijet Δη analyses as worked examples of a complete campaign analysis. Use it once you can read hadrons ([Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md)).

**What you need.** scikit-hep `fastjet` from PyPI, which is in the analysis venv: it ships the FastJet library itself and offers both interfaces. For FastJet in C++ (ROOT macros, fjcontrib), see [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/#5-fastjet-in-c).

## 1. Why the model's events are good for jets

Every Au+Au and Pb+Pb jet event comes with its **twin without the jet**: the background leg, the same fluid without the jet's energy (see [What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/#what-an-event-is)). Per oversample k there are three events to cluster:

| event                | hadrons                                                                | tests                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **bkg**              | `bulk_bg` sample k                                                     | ρ, random cones, combinatorial (fake) jets                     |
| **bkg + jet**        | `bulk_bg` sample k + `jet_frag` sample k mod n_frag                    | embedding: the jet on a background it did not touch, ⟨δpT⟩ = 0 |
| **bkg + wake + jet** | `bulk_jet` sample k + the same `jet_frag` sample (`r.jet_event(e, k)`) | the full event, with the medium response                       |

Comparing the last two isolates what the medium response does to a jet; comparing the reconstructed jets with the fragments alone measures the subtraction.

## 2. Conventions

The notebooks and the snippets below use one set of choices; change them deliberately:

- **Particles:** `$|\eta| < 1.5$`, pT > 0.15 GeV, charged by default, clustered as **massless** (E = |p|), so that rapidity equals pseudorapidity and the ghosts cover the acceptance exactly.
- **Jets:** anti-kT, R = 0.4, `$|\eta_\text{jet}| < 1.5 - R$`; active areas with explicit ghosts (ghost area 0.005).
- **ρ:** the median of pT/A of the kT jets (R = 0.4) in `$|\eta| < 1.5 - R$`, without the two hardest, with `set_use_area_4vector(False)`: the scalar area that pT − ρA uses. Without it FastJet 3 divides by the 4-vector area's transverse part, which gives a ρ about 1 GeV larger.
- **`user_index`** tags each particle with its row in the sample; offsetting the fragment rows tells a jet's fragment content exactly.
- **Weights:** every event counts once, so each oversample of an event weighs 1/(n · N_events) with n its oversamples; multiply by σ_k/N_k for cross sections ([Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/#5-pt-windows-and-cross-sections)).

Ghost positions are random

The Python bindings cannot set FastJet's ghost seed, so the ghosts get new random jitter at every clustering: areas and ρ change slightly from run to run. `jet_fastjet.ipynb` §4 measures by how much.

## 3. The classic interface, with ρA subtraction

The whole jet event of every oversample, clustered with areas, ρ from the kT jets, and the subtracted spectrum per event:

```python
import numpy as np
import fastjet as fj
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import CHARGED, HadronFileReader

ETA_MAX, R = 1.5, 0.4
JET_DEF  = fj.JetDefinition(fj.antikt_algorithm, R)
KT_DEF   = fj.JetDefinition(fj.kt_algorithm, R)
AREA_DEF = fj.AreaDefinition(fj.active_area_explicit_ghosts, fj.GhostedAreaSpec(ETA_MAX, 1, 0.005))
RHO_SEL  = (~fj.SelectorNHardest(2)) * fj.SelectorAbsRapMax(ETA_MAX - R)
JET_SEL  = fj.SelectorAbsRapMax(ETA_MAX - R) * fj.SelectorPtMin(10.0)
CHARGED_PID = np.array(CHARGED)

def pseudojets(ev, charged=True, pt_min=0.15):
    """Massless PseudoJets of one sample; user_index = the hadron's row in the sample."""
    E, px, py, pz = np.asarray(ev["p"], dtype=np.float64).T
    pt = np.hypot(px, py)
    eta = np.arcsinh(pz / np.maximum(pt, 1e-12))
    keep = (np.abs(eta) < ETA_MAX) & (pt > pt_min)
    if charged:
        keep &= np.isin(np.abs(ev["pid"]), CHARGED_PID)
    out = []
    for i in np.flatnonzero(keep):
        pj = fj.PseudoJet(px[i], py[i], pz[i], np.hypot(pt[i], pz[i]))
        pj.set_user_index(int(i))
        out.append(pj)
    return out

r = HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign")
pt_sub, weight = [], []
for e in r.events():
    n = r.n_oversamples(e)
    for k in range(n):
        parts = pseudojets(r.jet_event(e, k))               # bkg + wake + jet
        cs = fj.ClusterSequenceArea(parts, JET_DEF, AREA_DEF)
        bge = fj.JetMedianBackgroundEstimator(RHO_SEL, KT_DEF, AREA_DEF)
        bge.set_use_area_4vector(False)
        bge.set_particles(parts)
        rho = bge.rho()
        for jet in fj.sorted_by_pt(JET_SEL(cs.inclusive_jets())):
            pt_sub.append(jet.pt() - rho * jet.area())
            weight.append(1.0 / (n * r.n_events))           # per event: mean over its samples
spectrum, edges = np.histogram(pt_sub, np.arange(-20, 104, 4.0), weights=weight)
```

A raw R = 0.4 jet in a 0–10 % Au+Au event carries ρπR² of background, 25–30 GeV for charged hadrons, so the subtraction is not optional. Cost: 20 oversamples of ~7,000 hadrons (the charged ones at `$|\eta| < 1.5$` clustered), anti-kT with areas and ρ, take 0.4 s.

**Charged or full jets.** `pseudojets(ev, charged=False)` keeps neutral hadrons too: full jets need every hadron, which hadronizing with `--charged` would have dropped (check `r.selection()`). The notebooks switch with `PARTICLES=charged` or `PARTICLES=full`.

## 4. Embedding: a jet on a background it did not touch

Cluster the background sample plus the event's fragments, and keep track of which constituents are fragments through `user_index` (continuing the block above):

```python
def embedded(r, e, k):
    """bulk_bg sample k of event e's background + the event's fragments (no wake)."""
    bg = r.background_event(e, k)
    full = r.jet_event(e, k)
    frag = full["origin"] == 1                              # 0 bulk, 1 fragment
    return {"pid": np.concatenate([bg["pid"], full["pid"][frag]]),
            "p": np.concatenate([bg["p"], full["p"][frag]])}, len(bg["pid"])

ev, n_bg = embedded(r, 0, 0)
parts = pseudojets(ev)
cs = fj.ClusterSequenceArea(parts, JET_DEF, AREA_DEF)
for jet in fj.sorted_by_pt(JET_SEL(cs.inclusive_jets())):
    frag_pt = sum(c.pt() for c in jet.constituents() if c.user_index() >= n_bg)
```

The reference is the jet of the fragments alone: match the embedded jet to it, and pT,emb − pT,ref is the subtraction's offset and resolution (δpT). Repeating the same with `r.jet_event(e, k)`, the full event with the wake, shows what the medium response adds inside the cone. Random cones in `r.background_event(e, k)` give the background's fluctuations.

## 5. The array interface (awkward)

One `ClusterSequence` call clusters all samples of a unit in C++, with no Python loop (continuing the first block: `np`, `CHARGED_PID`, `r`):

```python
import awkward as ak, vector, fastjet as fj
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFile
vector.register_awkward()

def samples(path, unit, n=None):
    """The samples of one unit as samples * var * Momentum4D (massless)."""
    with HadronFile(path) as hf:
        u = hf.unit_index(unit)
        s0, s1 = int(hf.unit_offsets[u]), int(hf.unit_offsets[u + 1])
        s1 = s1 if n is None else min(s1, s0 + n)
        so = hf.sample_offsets[s0:s1 + 1]
        p = hf.f["hadrons/p"][so[0]:so[-1]].astype(np.float64)
        pid = hf.f["hadrons/pid"][so[0]:so[-1]]
    rec = ak.zip({"px": p[:, 1], "py": p[:, 2], "pz": p[:, 3],
                  "E": np.linalg.norm(p[:, 1:], axis=1),
                  "charged": np.isin(np.abs(pid), CHARGED_PID)}, with_name="Momentum4D")
    return ak.unflatten(rec, np.diff(so))

info = r.event_info(0)
ev = samples(f"{info.stem}_hadrons_jet_frag.h5", info.local_event)      # the jet hadrons alone
ev = ak.to_packed(ev[(abs(ev.eta) < 1.5) & (ev.pt > 0.15) & ev.charged])
cs = fj.ClusterSequence(ev, fj.JetDefinition(fj.antikt_algorithm, 0.4))  # all samples at once
jets = cs.inclusive_jets(min_pt=10.0)                                     # samples * jets
cons = cs.constituent_index(min_pt=10.0)                                  # indices into ev
```

`jetscape.HadronArray.from_h5(path).to_awkward(by_unit=True)` gives the same jagged arrays without writing `samples()` yourself ([Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/#the-pythonic-hadronarray)).

|     | supported                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| yes | inclusive and exclusive jets, constituents and their indices (`constituent_index` stands in for `user_index`), fjcontrib's SoftDrop, Lund declusterings, energy correlators and N-subjettiness |
| no  | areas, background estimators, `Selector`s, `user_index`                                                                                                                                        |

So the array interface is ideal for the jet hadrons alone, for pp, and for substructure; in the heavy-ion background, use the classic interface for the subtraction, or add explicit ghosts as particles by hand, which `jet_fastjet_awkward.ipynb` §6 does. A batch with explicit ghosts is large: cluster it in chunks. 100 samples cluster in 0.2 s.

## 6. The notebooks

| notebook                                                                                                                                                   | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`jet_fastjet.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/jet_fastjet.ipynb)                 | classic interface: the spectrum and fragmentation function of the jet hadrons alone; is the area right (tiling, πR², ghost size); ρ with and without the two hardest kT jets, random cones; the spectrum with and without ρA; embedding δpT for bkg + jet and bkg + wake + jet |
| [`jet_fastjet_awkward.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/jet_fastjet_awkward.ipynb) | the same with the array interface, plus exclusive jets, SoftDrop, Lund planes, energy correlators, N-subjettiness, and areas with hand-made ghosts                                                                                                                             |

```bash
HADRON_DIR=/path/to/campaign MAX_EVENTS=200 MAX_OVERSAMPLES=100 \
  jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/jet_fastjet.ipynb
```

## 7. Worked examples: the Z+jet campaign analyses

The Pb+Pb Z+jet campaigns (0–30 % Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV, hadrons-only jobs with the Z in the event record, a pp reference from `run_prod_vacuum.py`) are analysed against three CMS measurements. Each is written up step by step, from the downloaded files to the figures, in Python on the HDF5 files (route A) and with C++ map steps on the ROOT files (route B, see [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/#6-the-zjet-analyses-in-c)). They share a design worth copying for any campaign analysis:

- **A map step, then a final stage.** The map step reads every production file once and writes a small per-file summary (a "pool" of per-event histograms, or a tree of jets); the final stage computes everything else from those summaries in seconds to minutes. A new figure never needs another pass over the hadrons.
- **A ladder of steps** from the model-only ideal (using the event's twin without the jet) to an emulation of the experiment's procedure. The difference between two steps is what the added ingredient costs.
- **Jackknife errors over blocks of hydro backgrounds:** events that share a background are correlated, so the blocks are backgrounds, not events.
- **Weights:** the window cross section over its events, times N_coll in Pb+Pb.

Reading multi-GPU output

A campaign run on two GPUs sits in `gpu0/` and `gpu1/`. The readers do not search subdirectories: give Python a quoted glob, `"$DATA/gpu*/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5"`, and convert both directories into one ROOT directory for C++.

### Z+jet: CMS 1702.01060

Δφ_jZ, x_jZ = pT,jet/pT,Z, ⟨x_jZ⟩ and R_jZ (jet partners per Z) with anti-kT R = 0.3 jets, pT > 30 GeV, `$|\eta| < 1.6$`. S are the Z–jet pairs of the Z's own event; B, the fake jets from background fluctuations, is subtracted:

| step | jets of the Z event (S)                                                             | subtracted (B)                                                                                            |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | the fragments alone, smeared with CMS's resolution: the reference, a model quantity | none                                                                                                      |
| 2    | the whole event, ρA-subtracted                                                      | the jets of the Z's **own** background (`bulk_bg`, sample k against sample k)                             |
| 3    | the whole event, ρA-subtracted                                                      | the jets of 40 `bulk_bg` samples of the 20 other backgrounds closest in N_coll: CMS's minimum-bias mixing |

With extra hard scatterings, B also holds their jets ([below](#with-the-events-other-hard-scatterings)).

Steps 2 and 3 are the model's version of the measured observable. Step 2 repeated on the embedded event (the same fragments in `bulk_bg` sample k, no wake) gives "what the wake does to the jets" with very small errors, since both share everything else. In short (route A):

```bash
DATA=/data/zjet_c00     # the campaign: gpu0/, gpu1/ with <stem>_hadrons_*.h5
PP=/data/zjet_pp        # the pp reference of run_prod_vacuum.py
ANA=/data/ana_c00       # the outputs (private)
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet
./get_hepdata.sh                                                    # CMS's HEPData, once
python zjet_jets_map.py "$DATA/gpu*/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" $ANA/jets_py/pbpb --files 0:13   # map, in slices
python zjet_jets_map.py "$PP/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" $ANA/jets_py/pp
python zjet_jets_qa.py --pbpb $ANA/jets_py/pbpb --pp $ANA/jets_py/pp --outdir $ANA/figures --tag _c00
python zjet_jets.py --pbpb $ANA/jets_py/pbpb --pp $ANA/jets_py/pp --outdir $ANA/figures --tag _c00 --blocks 100
```

The map step clusters every oversample (anti-kT, explicit ghosts on a fixed grid, ρ per jet from the kT jets in a strip `$|y - y_\text{jet}| < 1$`), embeds the fragments into `bulk_bg`, throws random cones and clusters every background sample. On the 9,600-event campaign (2 × RTX 3090 box) it took ~0.37 s per Pb+Pb oversample in one process. Read the jet QA first (subtraction, areas, response, geometry, fakes), then pp against CMS's pp, then steps 1 to 3. Full walk-through: [`ANA_Zjet.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/ANA_Zjet.md).

### Z–hadron correlations: CMS 2507.09307

Charged hadrons around the Z in Δφ and Δy, per Z: S (the Z with the tracks of its own event) minus B (the Z with the tracks of other Z events, 10 per Z in CMS). What remains is the Z-correlated yield: the jet's fragments at Δφ ≈ π and the medium response, including the wake's depletion near the Z. Here the model's twin makes the exact answer available:

| step | mode       | S − B                                                                                                           |
| ---- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | factorized | (`bulk_jet` − `bulk_bg`) + fragments, sample by sample: the reference, compared with data directly              |
| 2    | all        | the full event against the pooled density of all events: the **closure test** of the mixing method on the model |
| 3    | cms10      | 10 partner events from 10 other backgrounds: CMS's procedure                                                    |
| 4    | strict     | one Z per background, one oversample: an experiment's statistics, to compare the errors                         |

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet          # DATA, PP, ANA as in the Z+jet block
python qa.py map "$DATA/gpu*/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" $ANA/qa_py/pbpb --jobs 8      # QA, both analyses
python qa.py map "$PP/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" $ANA/qa_py/pp
python qa.py plot --pbpb $ANA/qa_py/pbpb --pp $ANA/qa_py/pp --outdir $ANA/figures --tag _c00
python mix.py --pbpb "$DATA/gpu*/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" --vacuum "$PP/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5" \
    --pools $ANA/pools --hists '' --jobs 8 --outdir $ANA/figures --tag _c00   # all four steps
```

One `mix.py` run writes the pools (once) and computes all four steps, the checks and the jackknife. Two details matter in the model: every hydro background has its event plane near φ = 0 (the impact parameter is always along x), so `mix.py` rotates each background by its own random angle (an exact symmetry; `--no-rotate` keeps them as produced); and steps 3 and 4 never take a partner from the Z's own background, which shares its fluid. Full walk-through: [`ANA_Zhadron.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/ANA_Zhadron.md); every mode written out: [`MIXING_MODES.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/MIXING_MODES.md); every cut of the paper and its setting in production and analysis: [`README_zjet_2507.09307.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/README_zjet_2507.09307.md).

### The η-separated dijet wake: CMS HIN-25-012

CMS compared dijet–hadron correlations for dijets with a large rapidity gap (R_asym) and a small one (R_sym) to see the diffusion wake. The same analysis runs on the Z+jet campaigns with the Z as jet1 (`$|y_Z| < 1$`, pT,Z > 60 GeV) and the leading R = 0.4 jet above 30 GeV as jet2. It builds on the Z–hadron pools and the jets at R = 0.4, and its final stage is [`dijet/deta.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/dijet/deta.py):

```bash
RUNS=contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/runs    # data/ and figures/ per campaign (git-ignored)
OPT="--pools $RUNS/zjet_c00/data/mix/pbpb --vacuum-pools $RUNS/zjet_pp/data/mix/vacuum \
   --jets $RUNS/zjet_c00/data/jets_r04 --pp-jets $RUNS/zjet_pp/data/jets_r04 --run zjet_c00"
python contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/dijet/deta.py $OPT --tag _c00
```

It reports the model's truth (wake + fragments), the wake alone, the experiment-like full event, and closure contents that must come out flat, next to CMS's HEPData. With the Z as jet1 the comparison with CMS is a shape reference, not like for like. Full walk-through, including the map steps at R = 0.4: [`ANA_Deta.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/dijet/ANA_Deta.md).

### With the event's other hard scatterings

A campaign made with `--extra-hard` ([Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md)) has the event's other hard scatterings above p₀ (15 GeV for Pb+Pb) in `extra_frag`. Without them, B holds only the fake jets of the bulk's fluctuations, while CMS's minimum-bias events also hold the other scatterings' jets. **The extras belong to the event, not to the trigger**, so every map step takes them by default:

| analysis                               | with the extras (default)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | without                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Z+jet (`zjet_jets_map.py`, `zjets`)    | S = `bulk_jet` + `jet_frag` + `extra_frag`; B = `bulk_bg` + the event's `extra_frag` (per event, collection `bgx_*`), for B_own (step 2) and B_mixed (step 3, the Z events on the nearest backgrounds), the embedding and the random cones; the reference jets of step 1 stay the trigger's | `--no-extras` / `--extras 0` |
| Z–hadron (`mix.py`, `zhadron_pools`)   | the full events (and so the mixing partners) carry their extras; the Z-correlated yield `bulk_jet − bulk_bg + jet_frag` stays the trigger's; step 1 is unchanged, steps 2–4 get the extras' noise                                                                                           | `--no-extras` / `--extras 0` |
| QA (`qa.py map`, `zqa`), `wake_iso.py` | `extra_frag` as a source, `n_extra`, `nch*_extra`; the measured event's noise includes the extras                                                                                                                                                                                           | `--no-extras` / `--extras 0` |
| dijet Δη (`deta.py`)                   | jet2 is the leading jet of the full event, so the fake jet2 includes the extras' jets; takes everything from the map steps                                                                                                                                                                  | via the map steps            |

Map a campaign one way: pools and jet outputs with and without the extras do not combine. With `--no-extras` the outputs are exactly those of files without extras, and files without `extra_frag` give the same outputs as before, bit for bit. Minimum-bias files (`--hard none`) have no Z and are refused. B now has the scatterings above p₀ but still no minijets below it. Details: the *Extra hard scatterings* sections of [`ANA_Zjet.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/ANA_Zjet.md), [`ANA_Zhadron.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/zjet/ANA_Zhadron.md) and [`ANA_Deta.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/dijet/ANA_Deta.md).

Results not public yet

The Z+jet and dijet results are not public: write their outputs (`--outdir`, `runs/`) outside the repository or in its git-ignored `runs/` directory.
