# Hydro and hadrons together

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

The Au+Au and Pb+Pb jet productions store each event twice in the fluid, with and without the jet, and both legs again at hadron level. This page shows how to use that: read a hydro pair and take the difference as the wake, follow the wake through a whole campaign, connect the hadron files to the pair's events, measure the wake in hadrons, walk through one event from energy density to hadrons with `jet_wake.ipynb`, and judge how well hadrons made from the stored hydro history (what an FNO prediction would give) reproduce MUSIC's own. You need the pair files (`<stem>.h5`) for the fluid side; the hadron side needs only the particlize and hadron files.

## 1. Why a pair, and what the difference is

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  IC["one initial condition<br/>(3D MC-Glauber strings)"] --> M1["MUSIC_1<br/>background"] --> BG["arr_bg"]
  M1 --> EL["Matter + LBT<br/>in MUSIC_1's medium"] --> LQ["liquefier<br/>droplets"]
  IC --> M2["MUSIC_2<br/>same strings + droplets"] --> J["arr"]
  LQ --> M2
```

The jet loses energy in the background's medium (MUSIC_1); the liquefier turns what it loses into droplets, and a second MUSIC run (MUSIC_2) gets the same initial condition plus those droplets. Both legs are bit-identical until the first droplet is deposited, so `$\Delta e = e_\text{jet} - e_\text{bg}$` is the jet's effect on the medium (the wake, with its excess and its depletion) and nothing else. There are no event-by-event fluctuations to subtract, and no pairing of separate runs. The physics behind it: [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md).

Two things to keep in mind:

- **The legs freeze out at different times.** The deposit reheats the jet leg, by 1–2 fm/c in 0–10 % Au+Au. After the background has frozen out, `arr − arr_bg` is the jet leg's whole medium: use only frames below both `ntau_freezeout` values.
- **The jet leg ignores late droplets.** Energy deposited after MUSIC_2 has stopped never enters the fluid (`diag/E_droplets_late`).

## 2. Reading a pair

```python
import os
import h5py, hdf5plugin, numpy as np            # hdf5plugin: without it Blosc data won't read

with h5py.File("AuAu_0_10_jet_c1_0001.h5", "r") as f:
    A = f.attrs
    x   = A["x_min"]   + A["dx"]   * np.arange(A["nx"])      # cell centres [fm]
    y   = A["y_min"]   + A["dy"]   * np.arange(A["ny"])
    eta = A["eta_min"] + A["deta"] * np.arange(A["neta"])
    tau = A["tau_min"] + A["dtau"] * np.arange(f["arr"].shape[-1])   # 0.5, 0.6, ... fm/c

    i, k = 0, 40                                   # event 0, frame tau = 4.5 fm/c
    jet = f["arr"][i, :, :, :, :, k]               # (4, nx, ny, neta): e, vx, vy, vz
    bg  = f["arr_bg"][i, :, :, :, :, k]            # the same collision without the jet
    de  = jet[0] - bg[0]                           # the wake in e [GeV/fm^3]
    live = min(f["ntau_freezeout"][i], f["ntau_freezeout_bg"][i])   # frames where both legs live

    o = f["source/offsets"]
    droplets = f["source/droplets"][o[i]:o[i + 1]]   # tau, x, y, eta, E, px, py, pz
    E_dep = droplets[:, 4].sum()                   # = diag/E_droplets[i]

    # e -> T with MUSIC's hotQCD table (columns e, P, s, T); the venv sets MUSIC_EOS_TABLE
    tab = np.fromfile(os.environ["MUSIC_EOS_TABLE"], dtype="<f8").reshape(-1, 4)
    tab = tab[np.argsort(tab[:, 0])]
    T = np.interp(jet[0], tab[:, 0], tab[:, 3])    # GeV; T_fo = 0.15 at e = 0.234
```

- **Read frame by frame.** Each chunk is one event and one τ frame; a frame is ~2 MB.
- **The grid** (cell centres, steps) is in the attributes; the production grid is 64 × 64 × 32, ±12.2 fm in x and y, ±4.84 in η_s, every 0.1 fm/c from τ = 0.5 fm/c.
- **The showers** that made the droplets are in `shower/`, read with `jetscape.showers` (`fates`, `segments`, `to_milne`).
- **A campaign to one τ length:** `python contribs/PyJetscape/python/jetscape/repad_h5.py FILES` grows `arr` and `arr_bg` in place (a metadata resize), for loaders that need equal shapes.
- **FNO training:** FNO4d's `read_3d_data_hdf5(files, h5_key="arr"/"arr_bg", unique_bg=...)` reads many pair files lazily; `unique_bg` drops the repeated backgrounds of a reuse campaign.

### FastHydro's `PairBrowser` (optional)

With FastHydro's readers installed (`setup_analysis_env.sh --with-fasthydro`), a pair file opens in a browser that checks the premise and answers the common questions:

```python
from fasthydro.browse import PairBrowser

with PairBrowser("AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5") as p:
    print(p.summary(0))      # identical IC?, first differing frame, droplets, deposited E, freeze-out times
    de = p.diff(0, 20)       # arr - arr_bg, energy density, frame 20: (nx, ny, neta)
```

More about FastHydro and its notebooks: [FastHydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fasthydro/index.md). 3D views and movies of a pair file (`wake_pyvista.py`, `hydro_jet_particles_pyvista.py`): [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md).

## 3. The wake in the fluid, for a whole campaign

[`analysis/wake_observables.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/wake_observables.py) reads each pair file once and writes a small `wake_observables.h5`; the notebook makes the figures from it alone, so a new figure never needs another pass over the data:

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis
python wake_observables.py /path/to/campaign -j 10 -o /path/to/campaign/wake_observables.h5
WAKE_OBS=/path/to/campaign/wake_observables.h5 jupyter lab wake_observables.ipynb
```

| table       | content                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `showers`   | per initial parton: kinematics, vertex, heading in or out of the fireball, angle to the background's ψ₂, the energy bookkeeping from the shower graph, and the medium along its path (path length above T_c, ∫T², ∫T³, ...) |
| `droplets`  | position, four-momentum, the shower it came from, background T and v at the deposit                                                                                                                                         |
| `events`    | pT̂ window and cross section, ψ₂ and ε₂, freeze-out times, energy totals                                                                                                                                                     |
| `evolution` | P^μ and S of both legs through every τ surface (ideal-fluid T^{μν} with MUSIC's EoS), and the cumulative droplet four-momentum                                                                                              |
| `jetframe`  | the stacked wake about the leading-deposit leg's source, in (Δη, Δφ)                                                                                                                                                        |

It takes ~1 min for 300 events at `-j 10`, with ~0.5 GB extra per process for reading ahead. It also flags legs that never froze out (the hottest cell of a leg's last frame above 1.5 e_fo) and leaves those events out of the figures.

**How faithful is the stored wake?** The output grid is coarser than MUSIC's (0.3875 fm against 0.3 fm, 0.3125 against 0.2 in η_s). A comparison on 6 events (pT̂ 50–70 GeV) of the same Δe on MUSIC's grid and on the output grids found: the wake's net energy within ~1 % of MUSIC's; its shape at scales of 0.5 fm and up within ~10 %; peaks at 0.76 of MUSIC's height; and a ~30 % point-by-point loss that every resampling has, even one at MUSIC's own spacing shifted by half a cell. The background is unaffected (0.2 %). Details: [`docs/Wake_grid_comparison.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/Wake_grid_comparison.md).

## 4. The wake at hadron level

### Matching hadron files to the pair's events

All files of one job share its stem and its event order. Event i of the pair file is event i of the particlize file, unit i of `bulk_jet` and of `jet_frag`; its background in `bulk_bg` is unit `events/bg_unit[i]` of the particlize file (backgrounds are stored once, so their numbering is not the events'). In the pair file `arr_bg[i]` already resolves a shared background. `HadronFileReader` numbers events over the whole campaign, and its `event_info` leads back to the job and the local event:

```python
import h5py, hdf5plugin, numpy as np
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader
from jetscape.particlize_h5 import ParticlizeFile

with HadronFileReader("/path/to/campaign") as r:
    for g in r.events():
        info = r.event_info(g)                         # the job (stem) and the event in it
        i = info.local_event
        with h5py.File(f"{info.stem}.h5", "r") as f:   # the pair file of the same job
            live = min(f["ntau_freezeout"][i], f["ntau_freezeout_bg"][i])
            E_dep = f["diag/E_droplets"][i]            # energy handed to MUSIC_2 [GeV]
            k = live - 1                               # the last frame where both legs live
            de = f["arr"][i, 0, ..., k] - f["arr_bg"][i, 0, ..., k]
        with ParticlizeFile(f"{info.stem}_particlize.h5") as pf:
            cells = pf.events("n_cells_bg")[i] / pf.events("n_cells_jet")[i]   # ~1, else a bad leg
        # the same event at hadron level: the wake's energy at |eta| < 1
        dE, dE_err = r.jet_minus_background(None, None, mask=lambda ev, inf: np.abs(ev.eta) < 1,
                                            weights="E", events=[g])
        print(f"event {g}: {E_dep:.1f} GeV deposited, wake in hadrons {dE[0]:.1f} +- {dE_err[0]:.1f} GeV")
```

### Jet minus background, in hadrons

At hadron level the wake is ``` $\langle$``bulk_jet``$\rangle - \langle$``bulk_bg``$\rangle$ ```: each event's oversample average of its jet leg minus that of its own background, then averaged over events. `HadronFileReader.jet_minus_background` does exactly that, with the right error for correlated sampling ([Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/#2-histograms-totals-and-the-wake)). The jet event is that plus the fragments (`fragments=True`). Jet-relative observables use the event's shower initiators (`info.initiators()`) as the jet axis.

For a campaign, [`analysis/wake_hadrons.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/wake_hadrons.py) does the same in one pass and writes `wake_hadrons.h5`, which `wake_hadrons.ipynb` turns into figures together with `wake_observables.h5`:

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis
python wake_hadrons.py /path/to/campaign -j 10 -o /path/to/campaign/wake_hadrons.h5
WAKE_HAD=/path/to/campaign/wake_hadrons.h5 WAKE_OBS=/path/to/campaign/wake_observables.h5 \
  jupyter lab wake_hadrons.ipynb
```

- Per event and relative to the leading initiator: the (Δη, Δφ, pT) map of charged hadrons, ΔR profiles, identified spectra at `$|y| < 1$` near and away side, and totals (N, E, pT, ...) per `$|\eta|$` band; ~3.5 min for 300 events at `-j 10`.
- **Correlated files** (`--correlated`, or `--common-seeds`): the events of one background are not independent, so it also stores the jet leg and the wake as means over `--batches` (default 10) aligned blocks of samples, and the notebook takes the errors from their spread. On a 1005-event campaign with 15 events per background this cut the wake's errors 4–8 times.
- **Bad runs** are checked first, from the pair file, the hadron multiplicities and the logs; flagged events are not histogrammed unless `--keep-flagged`.
- **Stored hadrons:** with files hadronized at `--eta-max`, every "all η" result is only within that cut; the script records and warns about it.

**What it found** on a 285-event 0–10 % Au+Au campaign at pT̂ 10–40 GeV: the wake's hadrons carry 1.01 ± 0.13 ± 0.18 of the energy MUSIC_2 received; fragments (minus beam remnants) plus wake give 1.006 of the initial partons' energy. The wake has thermal chemistry and a harder spectrum than the background (⟨pT⟩ 0.85 against 0.54 GeV), peaks along both jets with no significant depletion behind them, and brings back 20 % of the leading leg's deposit inside R = 0.4 and 70 % inside 1.5. Details: [`analysis/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/README.md).

Beam remnants in the fragments

Colorless hadronization closes colour-unpaired strings with remnant quarks of `$\sqrt{s}/6$` = 33 GeV along the beam. That energy is not the jet's, and the strings to a remnant spread hadrons across all Δη, so no rapidity cut removes them. `wake_hadrons.ipynb` takes them out of the energy balance.

## 5. One event, end to end: `jet_wake.ipynb`

[`prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/jet_wake.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/jet_wake.ipynb) follows one pair from the energy density to the hadrons. It needs only numpy, h5py, matplotlib and scipy (and `jetscape` for the hadron section):

| section | shows                                                                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1–3     | the data, a check that both legs start identical, the dijet: several showers, several sources, each droplet assigned to a leg |
| 4–5     | Δe in the transverse plane and in (η, φ), re-centred on the jet                                                               |
| 6–7     | how big, how much, how wide; whether the front sits where a Mach cone would                                                   |
| 8       | freeze-out: the jet extends the medium's lifetime                                                                             |
| 10      | the same event at hadron level: bulk_jet − bulk_bg in (Δη, Δφ) about the leading leg, the energy at (                         |
| 11      | the energy balance: initial partons = surviving partons + deposited energy                                                    |

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
WAKE_H5=/path/to/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 jupyter lab jet_wake.ipynb
```

`WAKE_H5` names the pair file; the hadron section looks for `<stem>_particlize.h5` and the three hadron files next to it and prints the commands that make them if they are missing. `MUSIC_EOS_TABLE` gives the EoS for c_s². The shipped example (seed 1) shows a Mach-cone-like pattern behind the source, a wake whose hadrons return the deposited energy within errors (18.1 ± 2.7 GeV at `$|\eta| < 1$`, 24.6 ± 5.6 GeV at `$|\eta| < 2$`, for 25.0 GeV deposited), and a medium lifetime extended by 1.1 fm/c. One event shows the shape and the mechanism, not an average.

## 6. Hadrons from the stored hydro history

The pair files keep only e, vx, vy, vz on the output grid, with no viscous fields. That is all a neural operator (FNO) trained on them would predict. Such a history can only be hadronized through a freeze-out surface **found in it**, sampled **without viscous corrections**. The study in [`hydro_hist_vs_surface/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/hydro_hist_vs_surface) measures how far those hadrons are from the correct ones: iSS on MUSIC's own surface, with π^{μν} and Π. Same events, same `hadronize.py` settings, same seeds; only the surface changes:

| variant        | surface                                             | viscous corrections | isolates             |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| `ref`          | MUSIC's                                             | shear + bulk δf     | the correct answer   |
| `ref_no_shear` | MUSIC's, π^{μν} = 0                                 | bulk only           | shear δf             |
| `ref_no_bulk`  | MUSIC's, Π = 0                                      | shear only          | bulk δf              |
| `ref_ideal`    | MUSIC's, π^{μν} = Π = 0                             | none                | all of δf            |
| `hist`         | Cornelius on the stored history, T from MUSIC's EoS | none                | + the coarse history |

### Running it

It needs an X-SCAPE build with iSS and PyJetscape (as for `hadronize.py`; see [Source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md)), and a production directory made with `run_prod_jet.py --write-particlize both` plus its reference hadrons:

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/hydro_hist_vs_surface
PYTHON=$(which python) ./run_study.sh /path/to/production       # all variants, resumable
HVS_SUMMARY=/path/to/production/hist_vs_surface/summary.npz jupyter lab hydro_hist_vs_surface.ipynb
```

`run_study.sh [DATA [OUT]]` builds each variant's particlize files (`make_surfaces.py`), hadronizes them (`run_hadronize.py`) and summarizes everything into one small `summary.npz` (`analyze.py`). The hadronization settings must be the reference's: pass them as `HADRONIZE_OPTS` if they differ from the default `--oversample 100 --n-frag 50 --correlated --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8`. Other knobs: `HADRONIZE_J`, `VARIANTS`. On the GB10 (20 cores) 4 files × 25 events took 2 h 12 min and 51 GB, most of it the surface search in the history (~31 s per leg). Because the variants keep the reference's seeds and the sampling is correlated, variant − reference is far less noisy than either.

### What it found

(0–10 % Au+Au, pT̂ 50–70 GeV, 100 events; shifts relative to `ref`, mid-rapidity.)

- **The surfaces agree to 2 %:** 0.981 of MUSIC's freeze-out volume, same position and timing, but less of the fastest fluid.
- **For the bulk, the missing viscous corrections dominate,** not the coarse history:

| observable  | all δf off (`ref_ideal`) | history on top | **total (`hist` − `ref`)** |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------- |
| dN_ch/dη, ( | \\eta                    | \<0.5)         | −0.4 %                     |
| dN/dy p + p̄ | −29.3 %                  | +1.0 %         | **−28.6 %**                |
| ⟨pT⟩ π      | +13.5 %                  | −1.2 %         | **+12.1 %**                |
| v₂{2}       | +6.5 %                   | −3.0 %         | **+3.3 %**                 |
| v₃{2}       | +21.4 %                  | −4.9 %         | **+15.4 %**                |

Bulk δf sets the yields and spectral shapes, shear δf the flow harmonics.

- **The jet wake: δf cancels, the history loses about 10 %.** ΔE at `$|\eta| < 1$` is 24.0 ± 1.2 GeV with `ref` and 21.5 ± 1.1 GeV with `hist`; the deficit is a scale, not a change of shape (per-event correlation 0.97, same Δφ shape), and is already in the surfaces.
- **So:** dN/dη and the wake's shape can be taken from a history as it is (the wake's size ~10 % low); spectra, identified yields, ⟨pT⟩ and v_n cannot (5–30 % off, almost all of it missing δf). A single weight table w(species, pT) corrects yields and ⟨pT⟩ to within 0.3 %, one scale fixes the wake and v₂, but v₃ per event needs δf restored at the surface.

The study also lists its limits (the output grid ends at `$|\eta_s|$` = 5, where the medium is still above T_sw, so forward hadrons are missing) and next steps. Full write-up: [`hydro_hist_vs_surface/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/hydro_hist_vs_surface/README.md).

- The live FNO hydro these files train: [Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md).
- Making pair files: [Au+Au jets (two stages)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md).

# O+O

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

This page is for the analysis of O+O collisions at 200 GeV with initial-state radiation, from the `prod_OO_isr` production: what one event is, what its per-event record holds, how to load a campaign, how to weight it (pT̂-window cross sections, N_coll), the checks to run, and recipes for multiplicity, centrality, flow from the oversamples and jets. O+O differs from the Au+Au jet production in ways that change the analysis: there is no background twin, every event is hard-triggered, and the hadrons are usually made in the job. Running the production: [O+O with ISR](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/oo-isr/index.md).

## 1. What an O+O event is

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  IS["3dMCGlauber<br/>O16 positions"] --> H["PythiaIsrGun<br/>hard scattering at one binary collision"]
  H --> ISR["ISR (iMATTER),<br/>backward in time"]
  ISR --> S["strings from what<br/>the hard pair left"]
  S --> M["MUSIC<br/>one hydro per event"]
  M --> E["Matter + LBT<br/>in MUSIC's medium"]
  E --> JH["iColored:<br/>jet hadrons"]
  M --> SP["iSS:<br/>bulk hadrons"]
```

What matters for an analysis:

- **One MUSIC run per event, no background leg.** The medium response to the jet is part of the bulk and cannot be separated from it: there is no jet − background.
- **Every event is hard-triggered:** exactly one hard scattering, at a binary collision drawn uniformly. The geometry is sampled as in minimum-bias collisions within the b range, but in nature the hard-process rate grows with N_coll: weight with N_coll for the geometry of hard events (§6).
- **The hard partons' momentum is taken from the strings** (the default): the bulk loses what the hard pair and its remnants carry. That biases a multiplicity-based centrality towards peripheral, more so at small N_part.
- **The jet hadrons are the whole hard nucleon pair:** the dijet showered by Matter + LBT, the ISR emissions, Pythia's MPI partons and the pair's beam remnants, hadronized together by iColored. Their pstat is mostly 1000 (the gun's mark, which the shower's daughters keep); that does not mean "unshowered".
- **Events without a medium:** when the hard collision is the only one, no string is made: no evolution, Matter showers in vacuum, the bulk unit is empty (`has_medium` 0). In 0–80 % (b < 5.6 fm) that is ~5 % of the events, mostly with N_coll = 1.
- **Centrality comes from b.** For O+O at 200 GeV with this Glauber setup, the b percentiles are 10 % 1.91, 20 % 2.71, 40 % 3.84, 60 % 4.71, 80 % 5.59 fm; the production's default b < 3 fm is about 0–24 %.

## 2. The files

Each job writes, next to each other (stem `OO_isr_<campaign>_NNNN` or `OO_isr_seedNNNN`):

| file                          | holds                                                                                           | when                                                                  | size per event        |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `<stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5`  | the jet hadrons, one sample per event; `units/` with the whole event record (§3); `initiators/` | always (unless `--no-jet-hadrons`)                                    | small                 |
| `<stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5`   | the bulk (iSS), N oversamples per event                                                         | `--bulk-hadrons N` in the job, or later `hadronize.py --tags bulk_bg` | ~13 kB per oversample |
| `<stem>_particlize.h5`        | MUSIC's freeze-out surface (one unit per event), the final partons, the initiators              | default; not with `--no-particlize`                                   | ~10 MB                |
| `<stem>.h5`                   | MUSIC's evolution (e, vx, vy, vz) on `grid_oo.yaml`, `diag/`                                    | default; not with `--no-hydro-file`                                   | ~17 MB                |
| `<stem>.json`, `.xml`, `.log` | the job summary (cross sections, skipped events), the job XML, the log                          | always                                                                |                       |

The usual production setting is **hadron files only** (`--bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file`), 0.13 MB per event; the bulk can then not be resampled later. Download a campaign with `js_osdf.py download <campaign> --what h5` ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)).

Unit i is event i, and `HadronFileReader` does not apply

Unit i of the jet file and unit i of the bulk file are the same event. Hadron files made in the job have no `source_uuid`, so `HadronFileReader` and `run_h5toROOT.py`, made for the Au+Au pairs, refuse them. Read them as in §5 (or with `Hadrons` / `HadronFile` / `HadronArray`), and convert them to ROOT as in §13.

## 3. The per-event record

`units/` of the jet file (and of an in-job bulk file), `diag/` of the hydro file and `events/` of the particlize file carry the same columns:

| column                                                             | meaning                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unit`, `event`                                                    | the unit (row), the event's number in the job (skipped events leave gaps in `event`)                        |
| `pthat`, `pthat_bin`                                               | the hard scattering's pT̂ and its window                                                                     |
| `sigma_gen`, `sigma_err`                                           | Pythia's running cross-section estimate at that event [mb]; use the per-window file attributes instead (§6) |
| `glauber_b`, `glauber_npart`, `glauber_ncoll`, `glauber_nstrings`  | the geometry                                                                                                |
| `has_medium`, `hydro_row`                                          | 1 if the event has a medium; its row in `<stem>.h5` (−1: none)                                              |
| `isr_sub_{E,px,py,pz}_{proj,targ}`, `isr_sub_E_total`              | what the ISR handed over for subtraction from the projectile (+z) and target (−z) nucleon                   |
| `remnant_E_{proj,targ}`, `remnant_pz_{proj,targ}`                  | the hard pair's remnants, which go to the jet hadronization                                                 |
| `strings_E_total`, `strings_pz_net`                                | what MUSIC's strings carry (NaN without a medium)                                                           |
| `parton_y_lead`, `parton_pt_lead`, `parton_y_sub`, `parton_pt_sub` | the two hardest partons of the hard process after the ISR                                                   |
| `tau0_music`                                                       | MUSIC's start time                                                                                          |
| `n_samples`, `seed`, `n_cells`                                     | per file: the unit's samples, its seed, the surface cells (bulk file)                                       |

Per event, exactly: `strings_E_total + isr_sub_E_total + remnant_E_proj + remnant_E_targ = Npart √s_NN / 2`.

## 4. Settings to check before combining files

| setting                            | why                                                                                                                                             | where                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `subtract_hard_momentum`           | 1 (default) or 0 (`--no-subtraction`, a reference that counts the hard pair's energy twice)                                                     | attribute of every file; `.json`                                                                  |
| the b range, √s                    | e.g. `O+O 200 GeV, b in [0.0, 3.0] fm`                                                                                                          | the `system` attribute                                                                            |
| MUSIC's late time step             | the freeze-out surface is 0.20 % larger and the bulk +0.05 % against a constant step: one setting per campaign                                  | `<late_delta_tau>` in the job XML (`<stem>.xml`, or `prod_user_xml` of the hydro/particlize file) |
| energy loss                        | Matter + LBT (current default) or Matter alone (`--matter-only`, and older campaigns)                                                           | the `eloss` attribute (absent: Matter alone)                                                      |
| jet colour handling                | the jet hadrons differ between campaigns with and without colour tags in the energy loss; `<colour_closure>` must be the same across a campaign | `units/colour_partons` present or not; the `jet_hadronization_xml` attribute                      |
| pT̂ windows, parton rapidity cut    | the cross section per window                                                                                                                    | `pthat_bins`, `pthat_bin_sigma_gen`, `pthat_bin_acceptance`, `parton_ymax`                        |
| bulk oversamples, hadron selection | `--eta-max`, `--charged`, `--no-x`, `--keep-bits-*`                                                                                             | `n_samples`, `eta_max`, `charged_only`, `positions`                                               |
| skipped events                     | a few per campaign in older builds                                                                                                              | `events_skipped` in the attributes and the `.json`                                                |

```python
# the settings of every job of a campaign
import glob, h5py, hdf5plugin
for p in sorted(glob.glob("/path/to/OO_c1/**/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5", recursive=True)):
    with h5py.File(p, "r") as f:
        A = f.attrs
        windows = A["pthat_bins"].tolist() if "pthat_bins" in A else "none"
        print(p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], "|", A["system"], "| subtraction", A["subtract_hard_momentum"],
              "| skipped", A.get("events_skipped"), "| windows", windows)
```

The late step is recorded only in the job XML, which hadron-only jobs keep next to the files: `grep late_delta_tau OO_c1/*.xml`.

## 5. Reading a campaign

The hadron files are small, so a whole campaign fits in memory as flat arrays: one event table, and one array per hadron quantity with the global event index and the sample of each hadron:

```python
import glob
import h5py, hdf5plugin, numpy as np
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import CHARGED, pseudorapidity

def read(path):
    """units/ and the hadrons of one file; 'event' = the unit's position, 'sample' within it."""
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as f:
        units = {k: f["units"][k][:] for k in f["units"]}
        attrs = dict(f.attrs)
        so, uo = f["hadrons/sample_offsets"][:], f["hadrons/unit_offsets"][:]
        p, pid = f["hadrons/p"][:].astype(np.float64), f["hadrons/pid"][:]
    n_had = np.diff(so)
    unit_of_sample = np.repeat(np.arange(len(uo) - 1), np.diff(uo))
    h = {"event": np.repeat(unit_of_sample, n_had),
         "sample": np.repeat(np.arange(len(n_had)) - uo[:-1][unit_of_sample], n_had),
         "pid": pid, "E": p[:, 0], "px": p[:, 1], "py": p[:, 2], "pz": p[:, 3]}
    return units, attrs, h

def load(campaign):
    """Every finished job (its .json) of a campaign: one event table, bulk and jet hadrons."""
    stems = sorted(p[:-5] for p in glob.glob(f"{campaign}/**/*.json", recursive=True))
    ev, bulk, jet, n0 = [], [], [], 0
    for i, stem in enumerate(stems):
        u, attrs, hj = read(f"{stem}_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")      # the event record: always here
        ub, _, hb = read(f"{stem}_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")          # in the job or hadronize.py
        assert len(ub["unit"]) == len(u["unit"])                # unit i = event i in both
        u["n_samples_jet"] = u.pop("n_samples")
        u["n_samples_bg"] = ub["n_samples"]                     # 0: no medium
        u["file"] = np.full(len(u["unit"]), i)
        for k in ("pthat_bin_sigma_gen", "pthat_bin_n_accepted"):   # per window, this file
            u[k] = np.tile(np.atleast_1d(attrs.get(k, np.nan)), (len(u["unit"]), 1))
        hj["event"] += n0
        hb["event"] += n0
        ev.append(u), jet.append(hj), bulk.append(hb)
        n0 += len(u["unit"])
    cat = lambda parts: {k: np.concatenate([x[k] for x in parts]) for k in parts[0]}
    ev, bulk, jet = cat(ev), cat(bulk), cat(jet)
    for h in (bulk, jet):
        h["pt"] = np.hypot(h["px"], h["py"])
        h["eta"] = pseudorapidity(np.stack([h["E"], h["px"], h["py"], h["pz"]], axis=1))
        h["phi"] = np.arctan2(h["py"], h["px"])
        h["charged"] = np.isin(np.abs(h["pid"]), CHARGED)
    return ev, bulk, jet

ev, bulk, jet = load("/path/to/OO_c1")
n_ev = len(ev["unit"])
```

On a test campaign (2,991 events, 10 bulk oversamples) this loads 5.5 M bulk and 0.35 M jet hadrons in ~1 s. Only finished jobs (with a `.json`) are read, so it also works while a campaign runs.

**The Pythonic alternative:** `jetscape.HadronArray.from_h5(path).to_awkward(by_unit=True)` gives events × oversamples × hadrons as awkward arrays; the notebook `pythonic/oo_analysis.ipynb` does an O+O analysis that way, streaming the files of a public test run from the OSDF ([The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md)).

## 6. Weights and statistics

**Cross sections.** Each pT̂ window is its own Pythia; each file records per window `pthat_bin_sigma_gen` [mb] (after the parton-rapidity cut) and `pthat_bin_n_accepted`. Combine the files weighted by their accepted events:

```python
first = np.unique(ev["file"], return_index=True)[1]          # one row per file
sig, n_acc = ev["pthat_bin_sigma_gen"][first], ev["pthat_bin_n_accepted"][first]
sigma_k = (n_acc * sig).sum(0) / n_acc.sum(0)                 # mb per window
k = ev["pthat_bin"]
N_k = np.bincount(k, minlength=len(sigma_k))                  # events per window

w_hard = sigma_k[k] / N_k[k]             # sum over events = sigma of the hard process [mb]
SIGMA_NN = 42.0                          # mb, inelastic NN at 200 GeV
w_coll = ev["glauber_ncoll"] * sigma_k[k] / SIGMA_NN / N_k[k]   # per O+O collision in the b range
```

| weight                       | normalises to                                                                        | use                                                                   |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| none (per event, per window) | per hard event of that window                                                        | shapes and ratios within a window                                     |
| `w_hard`                     | dσ/dX of the hard process [mb], summed over windows                                  | spectra stitched over windows                                         |
| `w_coll`                     | the yield per O+O collision in the b range, assuming the hard rate ∝ N_coll σ_k/σ_NN | comparisons with measured per-event yields; ratios to a p+p reference |
| `ev["glauber_ncoll"]` alone  | the geometry of hard events                                                          | ⟨N_part⟩, multiplicities "for events with a jet"                      |

The N_coll weight matters because the events are hard-triggered with one hard scattering whatever the geometry: unweighted, peripheral events are over-represented. In the 0–80 % test campaign it moves the bulk's dN_ch/dη at `$|\eta| < 0.5$` from 28.3 (unweighted) to 36.7 (N_coll-weighted).

**Statistics.**

- **Events are independent:** there is no shared background. Different windows are independent samples.
- **The bulk oversamples of one event sample one fluid:** average each event over its samples (`n_samples_bg`), then over events, and take errors from the spread of the per-event values.
- **The jet hadrons are one sample per event.** Combining them with each bulk oversample makes N correlated copies of the event: weight each by 1/N.
- **`n_samples_bg` is 0 for events without a medium:** their bulk is empty, not missing. Keep them unless the analysis needs a medium.

## 7. Checks

```python
E_beam = ev["glauber_npart"] * 200.0 / 2                     # Npart sqrt(s_NN) / 2
E_sum = (ev["strings_E_total"] + ev["isr_sub_E_total"]
         + ev["remnant_E_proj"] + ev["remnant_E_targ"])
med = ev["has_medium"] == 1                                  # no medium: strings_E_total is NaN
print(np.max(np.abs(E_sum[med] - E_beam[med]) / E_beam[med]))   # test campaign: 3e-9
print("without a medium:", 1 - med.mean())                   # 4.9 % in 0-80 %
```

- **Skipped events:** `events_skipped` in every file's attributes and the `.json` (with the error).
- **The b range:** `glauber_b` must stay inside the `system` attribute's range.
- **Windows:** `np.bincount(ev["pthat_bin"])` should be about equal (event i uses window i mod K).

## 8. Multiplicity and spectra

Per event: the bulk's sample mean plus the event's jet hadrons:

```python
n_samp = ev["n_samples_bg"]
mid_b = bulk["charged"] & (np.abs(bulk["eta"]) < 0.5)
mid_j = jet["charged"] & (np.abs(jet["eta"]) < 0.5)
dn_bulk = np.bincount(bulk["event"][mid_b], minlength=n_ev) / np.maximum(n_samp, 1)
dn_jet = np.bincount(jet["event"][mid_j], minlength=n_ev)
dndeta = dn_bulk + dn_jet                                    # |eta| < 0.5: width 1
w = ev["glauber_ncoll"]
mean = np.average(dndeta, weights=w)                         # test campaign: 36.7
err = np.sqrt(np.sum(w**2 * (dndeta - mean)**2)) / w.sum()
```

A pT spectrum is the same with `np.histogram(..., weights=1/n_samp[event])` per hadron and the event weights on top; `hard_sub_compare.ipynb` has a complete, weighted version with errors from the per-event spread.

## 9. Centrality

An experiment classifies events by a multiplicity, not by b. `hard_sub_compare.ipynb` §2 shows how: an estimator from charged hadrons at `$3.1 < |\eta| < 3.9$` (like RHIC's beam-beam counters), from **one** bulk sample (one collision's fluctuations) plus the jet hadrons; class boundaries from a reference without a hard scattering's effect; then each event classified by what an experiment would count. The hard-momentum subtraction makes events with a hard scattering look more peripheral, the more so at small N_part: compare classes defined this way, not by b, with data.

## 10. Flow from the oversamples

Pairs of hadrons from **different** oversamples of one event correlate only through the fluid (its flow and geometry): no resonance-decay or momentum-conservation pairs within one sample. That gives v_n{2} of the events' own fluids, without that non-flow:

```python
def vn2(h, n, n_samples, mask):
    """v_n{2} from pairs of hadrons in different oversamples of the same event."""
    m = mask & (n_samples[h["event"]] >= 2)
    e, s, q = h["event"][m], h["sample"][m], np.exp(1j * n * h["phi"][m])
    key = e * 100000 + s                                     # (event, sample)
    uk, inv = np.unique(key, return_inverse=True)
    Qs = np.bincount(inv, weights=q.real) + 1j * np.bincount(inv, weights=q.imag)
    Ms = np.bincount(inv).astype(float)
    ev_of = uk // 100000
    Q = np.bincount(ev_of, weights=Qs.real) + 1j * np.bincount(ev_of, weights=Qs.imag)
    M = np.bincount(ev_of, weights=Ms)
    num = np.abs(Q)**2 - np.bincount(ev_of, weights=np.abs(Qs)**2)   # sum over a != b of Q_a Q_b*
    den = M**2 - np.bincount(ev_of, weights=Ms**2)                    # number of such pairs
    ok = den > 0
    return np.sqrt(num[ok].sum() / den[ok].sum())

sel = bulk["charged"] & (np.abs(bulk["eta"]) < 1) & (bulk["pt"] > 0.2) & (bulk["pt"] < 3)
v2 = vn2(bulk, 2, ev["n_samples_bg"], sel)       # test campaign (0-80 %, unweighted): 0.031
```

- The pairs are weighted by their number; for an N_coll-weighted average, weight `num` and `den` per event.
- Ten oversamples give ~45 sample pairs per event, enough for v₂; v₃ needs more oversamples.
- A pseudorapidity gap between the two hadrons (as in data) is a mask on each sample's Q.

## 11. Jets

The full event at hadron level is one bulk oversample plus the jet hadrons. Clustering bulk sample 0 with them:

```python
import fastjet as fj
JET_DEF = fj.JetDefinition(fj.antikt_algorithm, 0.4)

def pseudojets(h, idx):        # massless, as on the FastJet page
    return [fj.PseudoJet(px, py, pz, np.hypot(pt, pz))
            for px, py, pz, pt in zip(h["px"][idx], h["py"][idx], h["pz"][idx], h["pt"][idx])]

acc_b = bulk["charged"] & (np.abs(bulk["eta"]) < 1.5) & (bulk["pt"] > 0.15) & (bulk["sample"] == 0)
acc_j = jet["charged"] & (np.abs(jet["eta"]) < 1.5) & (jet["pt"] > 0.15)
by_b = np.split(np.flatnonzero(acc_b), np.searchsorted(bulk["event"][acc_b], np.arange(1, n_ev)))
by_j = np.split(np.flatnonzero(acc_j), np.searchsorted(jet["event"][acc_j], np.arange(1, n_ev)))
lead_pt = np.zeros(n_ev)
for e in range(n_ev):
    parts = pseudojets(bulk, by_b[e]) + pseudojets(jet, by_j[e])
    jets = fj.sorted_by_pt(fj.SelectorAbsRapMax(1.1)(
        fj.ClusterSequence(parts, JET_DEF).inclusive_jets(5.0)))
    lead_pt[e] = jets[0].pt() if jets else 0.0
```

- **Background:** the O+O bulk is small; ρA subtraction works as in [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#3-the-classic-interface-with-a-subtraction) (areas with explicit ghosts, ρ from kT jets).
- **All oversamples:** cluster bulk sample k plus the jet hadrons for every k and weight each by 1/N: the jet hadrons are the same in all of them.
- **Relative to the hard partons:** the initiators of event (file i, unit u) are in the jet file, `HadronFile(path).initiators(u)` → `(K, 11)`, columns `shower, pid, pstat, px, py, pz, E, x, y, z, t`; the two hardest partons after the ISR are also in `parton_{y,pt}_{lead,sub}`.
- **A p+p reference** with the same chain (ISR, Matter in vacuum, iColored) is not part of the production.

## 12. The hydro and particlize files

With the default outputs:

- **`<stem>.h5`:** `arr` `(nevents, 4, 64, 64, 32, ntau)` on `grid_oo.yaml` (x, y ±9.84 fm and η_s ±4.84 in steps of 0.3125), τ = 0.5 + k · 0.1 fm/c, `diag/` with the record of §3. Only events with a medium have a row: an event's row is its `hydro_row`. Read it as the Au+Au pair files ([Hydro and hadrons together](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hydro-hadrons/#2-reading-a-pair)), without `arr_bg`.
- **`<stem>_particlize.h5`:** `surface/bg` (one unit per event), the final partons and the initiators; `ParticlizeFile` reads it. It is the input for more bulk hadrons later, in the container or an X-SCAPE build:

```bash
contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_hadronize.py /work/OO_c1 -j 8 --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100
```

`hadronize.py` refuses `jet_frag` on these files: the O+O jet hadrons are made in the job.

## 13. ROOT

`run_h5toROOT.py` and `HadronFileReader.h` expect the Au+Au layout (they stop on O+O with `KeyError: 'seed'`). For O+O, convert each tag with the single-file converter and write the event record next to it:

```python
import glob, subprocess, sys
import h5py, hdf5plugin, numpy as np, uproot

CONV = "contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/root_export/hadrons_to_root.py"
for jf in sorted(glob.glob("/path/to/OO_c1/**/*_hadrons_jet_frag.h5", recursive=True)):
    stem = jf[: -len("_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")]
    for tag in ("bulk_bg", "jet_frag"):                     # one ntuple per tag, one entry per sample
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, CONV, f"{stem}_hadrons_{tag}.h5",
                        "-o", f"{stem}_{tag}.root", "--no-x"], check=True)
    with h5py.File(jf, "r") as f:                           # the event record (jet file)
        ev = {k: f["units"][k][:] for k in f["units"]}
        win = {k: np.atleast_1d(f.attrs[k]) for k in ("pthat_bin_sigma_gen", "pthat_bin_n_accepted")
               if k in f.attrs}
    with h5py.File(f"{stem}_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5", "r") as f:  # unit i = event i in both files
        ev["n_samples_bg"] = f["units/n_samples"][:]
    ev["n_samples_jet"] = ev.pop("n_samples")
    with uproot.recreate(f"{stem}_events.root") as out:
        out["events"] = {k: v.astype(np.float64 if v.dtype.kind == "f" else np.int64)
                         for k, v in ev.items()}
        if win:
            out["windows"] = {k: v.astype(np.float64) for k, v in win.items()}
```

It writes, per job, `<stem>_bulk_bg.root` and `<stem>_jet_frag.root` (one entry per sample: `event`, `unit`, `sample`, `pid[n]`, `pstat[n]`, `E/px/py/pz[n]`) next to the inputs, and `<stem>_events.root` (`events`, one entry per unit; `windows`). An RDataFrame macro for the N_coll-weighted bulk dN_ch/dη on these files is [`docs/analysis_snippets/oo_dndeta.C`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/analysis_snippets/oo_dndeta.C): `root -l -b -q 'oo_dndeta.C+("/path/OO_c1/OO_isr_c1_0001")'`. More on ROOT: [ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/index.md).

# Bulk and flow

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

The bulk tools in [`example/analysis/bulk/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk) compute, per event, the charged multiplicity Nch, the mean transverse momentum [pT] and the two-particle flow vₙ{2} with an η gap. They do it for the full event, for its parts, and as the paired difference to the jet-free background, with class averages and jackknife errors. They work on every production with hadron files: Au+Au, Pb+Pb, O+O, Ne+Ne, with or without a trigger, with or without [extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md). Their main use is the question the minimum-bias mode was made for: what do the extra hard scatterings (and a trigger's wake) do to Nch, [pT] and vₙ?

Like the other readers they need only the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md).

## 1. What is computed

Charged hadrons (`hadrons_h5.CHARGED`, which includes e and μ), 0.2 < pT < 3 GeV by default. Each event is evaluated for four **compositions**:

| composition | hadrons                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `full`      | `bulk_jet` + `jet_frag` + `extra_frag`: the whole event |
| `no_extras` | `bulk_jet` + `jet_frag`                                 |
| `bulk_jet`  | the bulk with every wake                                |
| `bulk_bg`   | the jet-free twin                                       |

A missing part is empty: without extras `full` = `no_extras`; minimum-bias files have no `jet_frag`.

| per event | definition                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nch`     | hadrons with (                                                                                                                                              |
| `pt`      | [pT] = ΣpT / N in that window, per oversample, then the mean over the oversamples                                                                           |
| `pt_var`  | the variance of [pT] over the oversamples (one sample's noise)                                                                                              |
| `c`, `w`  | the two-subevent pair sum Re(Qₙᴬ Qₙᴮ\*) and its pair count Mᴬ Mᴮ, means over the oversamples; A: −η_flow < η < −Δη/2, B: Δη/2 < η < η_flow (default 0.5 < ( |

| per class          | definition                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nch`, `dnch_deta` | ⟨nch⟩ and ⟨nch⟩ / (2 η_max)                                                                                                                      |
| `pt`               | ⟨[pT]⟩                                                                                                                                           |
| `sigma_pt`         | the spread of the events' [pT] (still contains each average's sampling noise)                                                                    |
| `sigma_pt_dyn`     | √(sigma_pt² − ⟨pt_var / K⟩): the fluid's event-by-event [pT] fluctuation, with the sampling noise removed using the K oversamples (NaN with one) |
| `sigma_pt_one`     | √(sigma_pt_dyn² + ⟨pt_var⟩): the spread with one sample per event, as an experiment sees it                                                      |
| `c2`, `c3`         | ⟨⟨2⟩⟩ₙ = Σ c / Σ w (multiplicity-weighted)                                                                                                       |
| `v2`, `v3`         | vₙ{2, (                                                                                                                                          |

And the **paired differences** to the background, `delta_full`, `delta_no_extras` and `delta_bulk_jet` (composition − `bulk_bg`, over the events that have both):

|                 | definition                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dnch`, `rdnch` | ⟨nch − nch_bg⟩, and that over ⟨nch_bg⟩                                                           |
| `dpt`           | ⟨[pT] − [pT]\_bg⟩                                                                                |
| `dc2`, `dc3`    | ⟨⟨2⟩⟩ₙ − ⟨⟨2⟩⟩ₙ,bg: the change of the correlator; it adds up, and it exists where vₙ{2} does not |
| `dv2`, `dv3`    | vₙ{2} − vₙ{2}\_bg                                                                                |

**The flow vector's kick.** The extras also move each event's flow vector in a random direction. Per paired difference the tools give `kick{n}` = √⟨|ΔVₙ|²⟩, measured as ⟨Re(ΔqₙᴬΔqₙᴮ\*)⟩ across the η gap so that the sampling noise drops out; `rkick{n}` (relative to vₙ{2}); `align{n}` = 2⟨V·ΔV⟩, the change along the existing flow (dilution or push); and `r{n}`, the correlation of the flow vectors with and without the extras. The per-hadron ⟨⟨2⟩⟩ changes by exactly align + kick², so the random and the systematic part come apart. On the 60-event Pb+Pb 0–10 % pilot (p₀ = 15 GeV): kick₂² = (3.1 ± 3.0)·10⁻⁶ (|ΔV₂| ≈ 0.002, ~4 % of v₂), kick₃² consistent with 0, r₂ = 0.9991 ± 0.0009.

**What a difference means** depends on the production:

- **Minimum bias** (`--hard none --extra-hard`): `delta_bulk_jet` is the extras' wakes, `delta_full` their wakes and fragments.
- **Triggered with extras:** the trigger's and the extras' together. Compare with the same seeds run without `--extra-hard` (the trigger and the background are bit-identical) to separate them.
- **Without extras:** the trigger's wake (`delta_bulk_jet`) and fragments (`delta_full`).

Each event also records N_coll, the number of extras and their summed E and pT (from `extra_frag`'s `scatterings/`).

## 2. Statistics

- **Oversamples** are independent Cooper–Frye samplings of the same fluid, not independent collisions ([What an event is](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/#what-an-event-is)). Each is treated as one physical event: pairs and [pT] are formed within one sample, so decay non-flow is included, as in data. The per-event values are means over the oversamples, and every event weighs the same whatever its number of oversamples. The legs may have different numbers of oversamples, since only per-event means are differenced.
- **Paired difference:** both legs are averaged over the same events and differenced in every jackknife replica, so the errors keep the legs' correlation. With correlated sampling (`--correlated`) sample k of `bulk_jet` and of its `bulk_bg` share their random numbers and the difference is low-noise. Without it the legs are independent samplings, and a difference of a few per mille needs many samples.
- **Errors:** delete-one-block jackknife over **backgrounds**, not events. Events sharing a background (`--reuse`) are left out together; with `--reuse 1` the unit is the event. More than `--max-blocks` (100) units are grouped into contiguous blocks.
- **Classes:** a list of events, an N_coll range, or N_coll percentiles (largest first). This is a centrality proxy from the Glauber collision, not multiplicity classes, which matter in small systems.
- **Weights:** every event weighs the same. That is right for minimum-bias and single-window files; `--pthat-bins` campaigns would need the window weights, which are not applied.
- Hadron files written with an `--eta-max` smaller than the cuts reach are refused.

## 3. The command line

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk
python bulk_obs.py out_had/                                  # every production file in it
python bulk_obs.py "OUTBASE/gpu*/*_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5" --ncoll-classes 0 10 30 50 100 \
       --out bulk.json --table bulk_events.npz
python bulk_obs.py out_had/ --eta-max 0.5 --flow-eta-max 2.4 --eta-gap 2 --harmonics 2 3 4
python bulk_obs.py out_had/ --workers 8                     # 8 processes, the same results
```

| option                       | default     |                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source ...`                 |             | directories, quoted globs or files (several allowed)                         |
| `--eta-max`                  | 0.8         | (                                                                            |
| `--pt-min`, `--pt-max`       | 0.2, 3.0    | GeV                                                                          |
| `--eta-gap`                  | 1.0         | Δη between the two subevents                                                 |
| `--flow-eta-max`             | `--eta-max` | outer edge of the subevents                                                  |
| `--harmonics`                | 2 3         | n of vₙ{2}                                                                   |
| `--events`                   | all         | global events, `0:100` or `3,5,9`                                            |
| `--ncoll-min`, `--ncoll-max` |             | an N_coll range                                                              |
| `--ncoll-classes`            |             | N_coll percentile edges, e.g. `0 10 30 50 100`                               |
| `--max-blocks`               | 100         | jackknife blocks (at most)                                                   |
| `--out`                      |             | the class results, `.json` or `.npz`                                         |
| `--table`                    |             | the per-event table, `.npz`                                                  |
| `--quiet`                    |             | no table on the screen                                                       |
| `--workers`                  | 1           | processes for the per-event pass (0: all CPUs); the same results as with one |

**In parallel.** The per-event pass is the slow part; `--workers N` (in Python `event_table(..., workers=N)`) reads the events in N processes, in contiguous chunks cut where the hydro background changes, so a shared background is still read once. The table, and so every result, is the same as with one process. On the GB10, 200 Pb+Pb 0–10 % events with 40 oversamples took 87 s with one process and 14 s with `--workers 8`. Scripts that call `event_table` with workers need the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard (the processes are spawned).

The output on a 3-event minimum-bias O+O test job (one oversample, uncorrelated, so σ_dyn is NaN and the vₙ are noise; it shows the layout, not physics):

```text
1 production file(s), 3 events, tags bulk_jet, bulk_bg, extra_frag
  no jet_frag in (some) files (minimum bias): full = bulk_jet + extra_frag
  bulk_jet / bulk_bg sampled correlated: False
  oversamples per event: bulk_jet [1], bulk_bg [1];  N_coll 36-43;  extras per event 2.33, extra_E 927 GeV

== all: 3 events, 3 jackknife blocks
                       <Nch>            dNch/deta          <[pT]> GeV        sigma([pT])   ...   v2{2}
full                201.7 +- 26          126 +- 16       0.6656 +- 0.019   0.03209 +- 0.017 ...  0.08748 +- 0.029
bulk_bg             197.7 +- 19        123.5 +- 12       0.6524 +- 0.019   0.03325 +- 0.024 ...  nan
                        dNch           dNch/Nch_bg        d<[pT]> GeV        dc2 = d<<2>>  ...
delta_full              4 +- 15      0.02024 +- 0.078   0.01324 +- 0.0087  0.01226 +- 0.0038 ...
```

`--out bulk.json` holds `cuts`, `sources`, `tags`, `extras`, `correlated` and `classes`: per class, per composition and per difference, every quantity as (value, jackknife error).

## 4. In Python

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk")
from flow import Cuts, event_table, select, class_averages
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronFileReader

with HadronFileReader("out_had") as r:
    t = event_table(r, Cuts(eta_max=0.8, pt_min=0.2, pt_max=3.0, eta_gap=1.0))
    # t = event_table(r, Cuts(), workers=8)    # the same table from 8 processes
res = class_averages(t, select(t, n_coll_percent=(0, 10)))
res["full/v2"], res["bulk_bg/v2"]               # (value, jackknife error)
res["delta_full/dnch"], res["delta_bulk_jet/dc2"]
```

`flow.py` is the library (`Cuts`, `event_table`, `select`, `class_averages`; the definitions are in its docstring), `bulk_obs.py` its command line. The tests on synthetic events recover an imposed v₂ = 0.08 (0.0802 ± 0.0011), v₃ = 0.04, [pT] and its dynamical spread.

## 5. A recipe: what the extras do to the bulk

Minimum bias, correlated legs, a few oversamples, then the paired differences per N_coll class:

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_10_seed ./run_jobs.sh -j 4 --campaign mb_x 20 30 0 out_mb_x \
    --user-xml ../config/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid ../config/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --hard none --extra-hard --hadrons-only --oversample 10 --correlated
cd ../analysis/bulk
python bulk_obs.py ../../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/out_mb_x --ncoll-classes 0 50 100 --out mb_x.json
# delta_bulk_jet/dc2, dpt, rdnch: the extras' wakes;  delta_full: + their fragments
```

Scale the threshold to see the dependence on p₀ (`--extra-pthat-min 20`, `15`, `10`, same seeds: the backgrounds are the same). For O+O and Ne+Ne, use `OO_5360_jet.xml` / `NeNe_5360_jet.xml` with `grid_oo.yaml`, and check dN_ch/dη and v₂{2} against the LHC data first ([O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/#oo-and-nene-at-536-tev)).

## 6. Histograms and jets of a minimum-bias campaign

For figures beyond the class averages, `extra_hard_hists.py` makes one pass over a minimum-bias extras campaign and writes, per event, η, φ, φ − Ψ₂ and pT of the charged hadrons and anti-kT R = 0.4 jets without subtraction (charged and all hadrons), together with the extras' scatterings and initiators. It does this for the bulk, bulk + wakes and bulk + extras, and it keeps the sums for v₂(p_T) of charged hadrons with three estimators: ALICE's v₂{2, |Δη| > 1} in |η| < 0.8, the same with |Δη| > 1.5, and ⟨cos 2(φ − Ψ₂)⟩ relative to the jet-free background's plane (no non-flow from the extras). Two notebooks draw them with jackknife errors over the hydro backgrounds, and compare v₂(p_T) in two N_coll halves of the 0–10 % sample ("0–5 %", "5–10 %") with ALICE's v₂{2, |Δη| > 1} ([arXiv:1804.02944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02944)) and with CMS's v₂{SP} up to 100 GeV ([arXiv:1702.00630](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00630)). `./get_hepdata.sh` fetches the data once into `../runs/hepdata/`; `v2pt.py` holds the estimators and the data readers.

```bash
./get_hepdata.sh                                              # ALICE + CMS v2(pT), once
python extra_hard_hists.py --prod /path/to/campaign --out hists.npz --workers 12
```

|                                                                                                                                                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--prod`                                                                                                                                                          | the campaign directory (its `*_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--out`                                                                                                                                                           | the `.npz` (default `../runs/pbpb_extra_hard/data/extra_hard_hists.npz`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--workers`                                                                                                                                                       | processes (default 12); they take contiguous event ranges, about `--chunks-per-worker` (default 4) each, so the cores stay busy to the end. The output is the same as with one range per file (`--chunks-per-worker 0`). 1,000 Pb+Pb events × 40 oversamples: 302 s with 20 workers on the GB10 (10 fast and 10 efficiency cores) |
| [`v2pt.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk/v2pt.py)                                                 | v₂(p_T) from the sums, the event-plane resolution, the HEPData tables                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`extra_hard_bulk_jets.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk/extra_hard_bulk_jets.ipynb)           | the figures and ratios (numpy + matplotlib), and v₂(p_T) against ALICE and CMS                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`extra_hard_bulk_jets_hist.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/bulk/extra_hard_bulk_jets_hist.ipynb) | the same with `hist` + mplhep: a jackknife `block` axis, rebinning, a `Mean` profile                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
