# ROOT and C++

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

Most analyses in the field are written in ROOT. This page shows how to turn a hadronized campaign into ROOT files, read them with or without ROOT (uproot, RDataFrame), loop over events in C++ with the header-only `HadronFileReader.h`, cluster jets with FastJet's C++ library, and run the C++ map steps of the Z+jet analyses. The ROOT files hold the hadrons and the event information only; the hydro stays in HDF5 (read it with h5py, also from PyROOT).

## 1. Set up

| need                                                 | environment                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| converting (`run_h5toROOT.py`), reading with uproot  | the analysis venv; it writes with uproot, or with ROOT when PyROOT imports                              |
| RDataFrame, the macros, `HadronFileReader.h`, PyROOT | ROOT **≥ 6.34** (RNTuple) next to the venv                                                              |
| FastJet in C++                                       | conda-forge `fastjet-cxx` (FastJet, `fastjet-config`) and `fastjet-contrib` (fjcontrib) in the ROOT env |

conda gives ROOT and its Python, and the venv is made from that Python:

```bash
conda create -n root -c conda-forge "root>=6.34"           # RNTuple needs ROOT >= 6.34
conda activate root
conda install -c conda-forge fastjet-cxx fastjet-contrib   # only for FastJet in C++
./utils/analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh ~/.venvs/js_analysis_root --system-site-packages
```

Then `source ~/.venvs/js_analysis_root/bin/activate` has PyROOT. For the `root` prompt and compiled macros, `conda activate root` first: without it ACLiC does not find the system headers (`'assert.h' file not found`). Details: [Analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md).

## 2. Convert a campaign: `run_h5toROOT.py`

[`run_h5toROOT.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_h5toROOT.py) turns every hadronized production file into one ROOT file, plus one campaign file:

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
python run_h5toROOT.py /path/to/campaign -j 4                        # RNTuple, next to the inputs
python run_h5toROOT.py /path/to/campaign -j 4 --format ttree         # TTree, for ROOT < 6.34
python run_h5toROOT.py /path/to/campaign -j 4 --out-dir root --no-x --charged --eta-max 1
python run_h5toROOT.py /path/to/campaign --dry-run                   # the plan only
python run_h5toROOT.py /data/c00/gpu0 /data/c00/gpu1 -j 8 --out-dir /data/root/c00   # several directories into one
```

| option                               |                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-j N`                               | files in parallel; ~80 B per hadron of the largest tag each (~3.5 GB for a 15-event file at 400 oversamples)                |
| `--format {rntuple,ttree}`           | RNTuple (default): 0.9 × the HDF5 size, ~1.8 times faster to read than a TTree; needs ROOT ≥ 6.34 to read                   |
| `--writer {auto,root,uproot}`        | `auto`: ROOT if PyROOT imports (16–24 % smaller files), else uproot                                                         |
| `--out-dir DIR`                      | where the ROOT files go (default: next to the inputs)                                                                       |
| `--no-x`, `--charged`, `--eta-max X` | leave out positions (40 % of the bytes), neutral hadrons, (                                                                 |
| `--tags`                             | a subset of `bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag,extra_frag` (default: all a file has; `extra_frag` only with extra hard scatterings) |
| `--campaign-file NAME` / `none`      | the campaign file's name, or none                                                                                           |
| `--force`                            | redo files already converted                                                                                                |

A file is converted once its particlize file and every tag's hadron file are complete (hadrons-only jobs: their hadron files). Outputs are written to `.part` and renamed, so rerunning finishes an interrupted pass and skips what is done. The 20-file test campaign took 2 min 40 s at `-j 4`.

**Check a conversion** against the HDF5 files, every hadron bit for bit, the event record, the windows and the cross sections (exit 1 on a difference):

```bash
python root_export/check_h5_vs_root.py /path/to/campaign /path/to/root --campaign /path/to/root/c1_campaign.root
```

### What is in the files

**Per production file, `<stem>_hadrons.root`:**

| object                            | one entry per | content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bulk_jet`, `bulk_bg`, `jet_frag` | oversample    | `event`, `unit`, `sample`, `bg_unit`, `n`, `pid[n]`, `pstat[n]`, `E/px/py/pz[n]` (GeV), `t/x/y/z[n]` (fm; not with `--no-x`)                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `extra_frag`                      | fragmentation | with extra hard scatterings only: the fragments of the event's other hard scatterings, the same layout. A minimum-bias file (`--hard none`) has no `jet_frag`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `events`                          | event         | the particlize file's `events/`, `sigma_file_mb`, `n_samples_*`, `seed_*`, the initiators `ini_*[...]`; with extra hard scatterings also `n_extra`, `extra_mu`, `extra_E`, `extra_pt`, `n_samples_extra`, `seed_extra`, the scatterings `scat_*[...]` (the trigger's first) and the extras' initiators `xini_*[...]` |
| `windows`                         | pT̂ window     | `pthat_lo/hi`, this file's `sigma_mb`, `sigma_err_mb`, `acceptance`, counts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `provenance`                      | –             | JSON: every setting, seed, XML and EoS behind the file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**`<campaign>_campaign.root`:** `windows` with the campaign's `sigma_mb`, `sigma_err_mb`, `acceptance`, `n_events` and **`weight_mb = sigma_mb / n_events`**; `files` with `event_offset` per file (global event = `event_offset[file] + event`, the numbering of the Python `HadronFileReader`); `provenance`.

**Why one entry per oversample:** one entry per event would hold ~2.8 M hadrons at 400 oversamples, and one entry per hadron loses the event. One entry per oversample reads like an MC event. Remember that the oversamples of an event are samplings of one fluid, not independent events ([What a production writes](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/files/#what-an-event-is)).

**One file at a time.** `root_export/hadrons_to_root.py <stem>_hadrons_<tag>.h5 -o out.root` converts a single hadron file (the same `--format`, `--writer`, `--no-x`, `--eta-max`, `--charged` options); the O+O files are converted that way ([O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/#13-root)). The format study behind the defaults: [`root_export/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/root_export/README.md).

## 3. Reading without ROOT: uproot

```python
import uproot, awkward as ak, numpy as np

f = uproot.open("AuAu_0_10_jet_c1_0001_hadrons.root")
jet = f["bulk_jet"].arrays(["event", "sample", "pid", "px", "py", "pz"], entry_stop=100)
pt = np.hypot(jet.px, jet.py)                     # jagged: samples * hadrons
ev = f["events"].arrays()                         # awkward: the ini_* columns are jagged
ini_pt = np.hypot(ev.ini_px, ev.ini_py)
c = uproot.open("pth10-40_c1_campaign.root")
if "windows" in c:                                # pT-hat-window campaigns only
    w = c["windows"].arrays(["sigma_mb", "weight_mb"])
```

- Read `events` as awkward (the default): `library="np"` fails on the jagged initiator columns.
- `np.isin` does not take jagged arrays; flatten and unflatten for a species mask:

```python
CHARGED = [211, 321, 2212, 3222, 3112, 3312, 3334, 11, 13]        # jetscape.hadrons_h5.CHARGED
b = f["bulk_jet"].arrays(["event", "pid", "px", "py", "pz"])
eta = np.arcsinh(b.pz / np.hypot(b.px, b.py))
charged = ak.unflatten(np.isin(np.abs(ak.flatten(b.pid)), CHARGED), ak.num(b.pid))
n_mid = ak.sum(charged & (abs(eta) < 1), axis=1)  # charged at |eta| < 1, per oversample
```

- In the venv, uproot also reads files in place over `osdf://`, e.g. `uproot.open("osdf:///fno4hic/<campaign>/<file>.root")` ([Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md)).

## 4. In ROOT

### RDataFrame

A cross-section-weighted spectrum of the jet leg, every event the mean over its oversamples:

```cpp
ROOT::RDataFrame w("windows", "pth10-40_c1_campaign.root");
auto wt = *w.Take<double>("weight_mb");             // per window
ROOT::RDataFrame ev("events", "RUN_0001_hadrons.root");
auto nsamp = *ev.Take<int>("n_samples_jet");        // per event
auto bin   = *ev.Take<int>("pthat_bin");
ROOT::RDataFrame jet("bulk_jet", "RUN_0001_hadrons.root");
auto h = jet.Define("w", [&](int e) { return wt[bin[e]] / nsamp[e]; }, {"event"})
            .Define("pt", "sqrt(px*px + py*py)")
            .Histo1D({"pt", "", 100, 0, 5}, "pt", "w");
```

TTree and RNTuple read the same way. `ROOT::EnableImplicitMT(n)` runs it on n threads.

### `HadronFileReader.h`

[`analysis_root/HadronFileReader.h`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/HadronFileReader.h) is the header-only C++ counterpart of the Python reader. It finds an event's entries in the three ntuples and returns their hadrons as `std::vector<Hadron>`:

| call                   | the hadrons of                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `r.bkg(e, k)`          | the background (MUSIC_1): sample k of the background event e used                                 |
| `r.bkg_dep(e, k)`      | the jet leg (MUSIC_2): background + deposition                                                    |
| `r.bkg_dep_frag(e, k)` | the whole jet event: `bkg_dep(e, k)` + fragmentation k mod `n_frag(e)`                            |
| `r.frag(e, j)`         | fragmentation j of the surviving partons (with extra hard scatterings: the trigger's)             |
| `r.extra(e, j)`        | fragmentation j of the event's extra hard scatterings (files with extras only)                    |
| `r.bkg_extra(e, k)`    | B, the event without its trigger: `bkg(e, k)` + the extras' fragmentation k mod `n_extra_frag(e)` |

```cpp
#include "HadronFileReader.h"
using namespace hadrons_root;

HadronFileReader r("/path/to/campaign");    // every *_hadrons.root, + its *_campaign.root
r.set_charged_eta(1.0);                     // optional filter while reading
for (long e : r.select_events()) {          // hadronized events, flagged ones left out
  const EventInfo &info = r.info(e);        // pthat_bin, bg_unit, initiators, leading(), weight_mb
  const int n = r.n_oversamples(e);
  for (int k = 0; k < n; ++k)
    for (const Hadron &h : r.bkg_dep_frag(e, k)) { /* h.pt(), h.eta(), h.phi(), h.p4(), h.origin */ }
}
```

- **Source:** a directory (without its subdirectories) or one `*_hadrons.root` file, or a `std::vector<std::string>` of files. For multi-GPU output, convert all subdirectories into one directory with `--out-dir`.
- **`EventInfo`:** `pthat_bin`, `pthat`, `bg_unit`, sample and cell counts, `weight_mb`, the `initiators` and `leading()`, `n_coll`, the trigger Z (`z`), and `flagged()`: the background has more than 20 % more or fewer freeze-out cells than the jet leg, so one surface is not a freeze-out surface. `select_events()` leaves those out.
- **Normalisation:** a hadron of `bkg_dep` or `bkg_dep_frag` weighs w_e / `n_oversamples(e)`, of `bkg` w_e / `n_bg_samples(e)`, of `frag` w_e / `n_frag(e)`, with w_e = 1/N per event or σ_k / N_k for the cross section. Errors per event, not per sample; for `--correlated` files pair `bkg_dep(e, k)` with `bkg(e, k)`.
- **Cross sections:** `sigma_mb(k)`, `weight_mb(k)` come from the campaign file, or are combined from the files' `windows` tables when there is none.
- **Extra hard scatterings** ([Extra hard scatterings](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/extra-hard/index.md)): they belong to the event, so `bkg_dep_frag(e, k)` adds the extras' fragmentation (`Hadron::origin` 2, `kExtra`) whenever the file has them. `r.set_extras(false)`, or `bkg_dep_frag(e, k, j, false)`, reads every event as without them; `has_extras(file)`, `with_extras(e)`. `EventInfo` gains `n_extra`, `extra_mu`, `extra_E`, `extra_pt`, `scatterings` and `extra_initiators` (`initiators` stay the trigger's). A minimum-bias file has no `jet_frag`: its full event is `bulk_jet` + `extra_frag`.
- **PyROOT:** `ROOT.gInterpreter.Declare('#include "/path/HadronFileReader.h"')`, then `ROOT.hadrons_root.HadronFileReader(...)`.
- **Speed:** the whole jet event of every oversample of one event with 500 oversamples (3.5 M hadrons) takes 0.24 s compiled. It gives the same hadrons as the Python reader on the HDF5 files, event by event.

### The macros

```bash
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root
root -l -b -q 'read_hadrons.C+("/path/to/campaign")'                       # per event
root -l -b -q 'read_hadrons.C+("/path/to/campaign", -1, true)'             # dsigma/dX [mb]
root -l -b -q 'hadron_distributions.C+("/path/to/campaign", -1, false, true, 1.0, "out.root", 8)'
```

| macro                    | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `read_hadrons.C`         | the reader by example: pT spectra and Δφ to the leading initiator, per source (`bkg`, `bkgdep`, `full`, `frag`) and for the wake (`bkgdep − bkg`). Arguments: `dir, window = -1, xsec = false, eta_cut = 1.0, out, max_samples = -1`                                              |
| `read_hadrons.ipynb`     | the same, one step per cell, in ROOT's C++ notebook kernel (`HADRON_DIR`, `HADRON_OUT`, `MAX_SAMPLES`); needs `pip install metakernel` in the env                                                                                                                                 |
| `hadron_distributions.C` | η, φ, pT of every source and of the wake, with RDataFrame, multithreaded; with extra hard scatterings a source `extra`, and `full` includes it. Arguments: `dir, window = -1, xsec = false, charged = true, eta_cut = 1.0, out, threads = 1, keep_flagged = false, extras = true` |

`hadron_distributions.C` reproduces `HadronFileReader.hist` / `jet_minus_background` on the HDF5 files bin for bin: a 285-event campaign takes 21 s with 8 threads, against ~6 min in Python. Its errors are those of independent sampling; for the paired error of correlated files use the Python `jet_minus_background`. Full reference: [`analysis_root/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/README.md).

## 5. FastJet in C++

With FastJet's C++ library next to ROOT, `HadronFileReader.h` hands the hadrons straight to FastJet. This macro clusters the whole jet event of every oversample with the conventions of [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#2-conventions) and fills the raw and ρA-subtracted spectrum:

```cpp
// jets_fastjet.C: anti-kT jets with rho*A subtraction on the ROOT files of run_h5toROOT.py
#include "HadronFileReader.h"

#include <fastjet/ClusterSequenceArea.hh>
#include <fastjet/Selector.hh>
#include <fastjet/tools/JetMedianBackgroundEstimator.hh>

#include <TFile.h>
#include <TH1D.h>

void jets_fastjet(const char *dir = "out_root", double eta_max = 1.5, double R = 0.4,
                  int max_samples = 20) {
  using namespace hadrons_root;
  HadronFileReader r(dir);
  r.set_charged_eta(eta_max);                    // charged hadrons at |eta| < eta_max only

  const fastjet::JetDefinition jet_def(fastjet::antikt_algorithm, R);
  const fastjet::JetDefinition kt_def(fastjet::kt_algorithm, R);
  const fastjet::AreaDefinition area_def(fastjet::active_area_explicit_ghosts,
                                         fastjet::GhostedAreaSpec(eta_max, 1, 0.005));
  const fastjet::Selector rho_sel =
      (!fastjet::SelectorNHardest(2)) * fastjet::SelectorAbsRapMax(eta_max - R);
  const fastjet::Selector jet_sel =
      fastjet::SelectorAbsRapMax(eta_max - R) * fastjet::SelectorPtMin(5.0);

  TH1D h_raw("h_raw", ";p_{T,jet} (GeV);dN_{jet}/dp_{T} per event", 60, -20, 100);
  TH1D h_sub("h_sub", ";p_{T,jet} - #rho A (GeV);dN_{jet}/dp_{T} per event", 60, -20, 100);

  const std::vector<long> events = r.select_events();      // hadronized, flagged ones out
  for (long e : events) {
    const int n = std::min(r.n_oversamples(e), max_samples);
    const double w = 1.0 / (double(events.size()) * n);    // per event: mean over its samples
    for (int k = 0; k < n; ++k) {
      std::vector<fastjet::PseudoJet> parts;
      for (const Hadron &h : r.bkg_dep_frag(e, k))           // bulk (bkg + wake) + fragments
        if (h.pt() > 0.15) parts.emplace_back(h.px, h.py, h.pz, h.p());   // massless
      fastjet::ClusterSequenceArea cs(parts, jet_def, area_def);
      fastjet::JetMedianBackgroundEstimator bge(rho_sel, kt_def, area_def);
      bge.set_use_area_4vector(false);                       // rho = median of pT / A
      bge.set_particles(parts);
      const double rho = bge.rho();
      for (const fastjet::PseudoJet &jet : jet_sel(cs.inclusive_jets())) {
        h_raw.Fill(jet.pt(), w);
        h_sub.Fill(jet.pt() - rho * jet.area(), w);
      }
    }
  }
  h_raw.Scale(1.0, "width");
  h_sub.Scale(1.0, "width");
  TFile out("jets_fastjet.root", "RECREATE");
  h_raw.Write();
  h_sub.Write();
}
```

The file is in [`docs/analysis_snippets/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/docs/analysis_snippets), with `jets_main.cxx`, a `main` that calls it.

**ACLiC:**

```bash
conda activate root                         # the env with ROOT and fastjet-cxx
AR=/path/to/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root
root -l -b -q \
  -e "gSystem->AddIncludePath(\"-I$AR -I$CONDA_PREFIX/include\"); gSystem->Load(\"libfastjet\"); gSystem->Load(\"libfastjettools\")" \
  'jets_fastjet.C+("/path/to/campaign")'
```

**g++:**

```bash
cd docs/analysis_snippets                   # jets_main.cxx includes jets_fastjet.C; AR as in the ACLiC tab
g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -I$AR jets_main.cxx $(root-config --cflags --libs) \
    $(fastjet-config --cxxflags) $(fastjet-config --libs) -lROOTNTuple -o jets
./jets /path/to/campaign
```

- `fastjet-config` takes one query at a time: `--cxxflags` and `--libs` separately.
- **fjcontrib:** add `-lfastjetcontribfragile` (conda-forge `fastjet-contrib`) and include e.g. `<fastjet/contrib/SoftDrop.hh>` or `ConstituentSubtractor.hh`; in a macro, `gSystem->Load("libfastjetcontribfragile")`.
- **Cross sections:** replace `w` with `info.weight_mb / n` (or `r.sigma_mb(k) / N_k / n` for a subset of events, as `read_hadrons.C` does).
- **Embedding:** cluster `r.bkg(e, k)` plus `r.frag(e, k % r.n_frag(e))` for the jet on a background it did not touch; the fragments have `Hadron::origin == kFrag`, which can go into the PseudoJets' `user_index`.
- One event with 20 oversamples of ~7,000 hadrons took 21 s, ACLiC compilation included, on the GB10.

## 6. The Z+jet analyses in C++

[`analysis_root/zjet/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/zjet) holds the C++ map steps of the Z+jet analyses ([Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#7-worked-examples-the-zjet-campaign-analyses)). Each has a Python twin and agrees with it value for value; the final stage is the same Python for both:

| program         | map step                                                                                                 | output per production file                        |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `zqa`           | the QA: a table per Z event and per-source hadron histograms                                             | `<stem>_qa.root`, drawn by `qa.py plot`           |
| `zhadron_pools` | the Z–hadron pool (CMS 2507.09307)                                                                       | `<stem>_pool.root`, read by `mix.py --pbpb-pools` |
| `zjets`         | every oversample clustered with FastJet, ρA-subtracted, with embedding and random cones (CMS 1702.01060) | `<stem>_jets.root`, read by `zjet_jets.py`        |

```bash
# DATA (the campaign), PP (the pp reference) and ANA (the outputs) as on the FastJet page
cd contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/zjet && make     # root-config and fastjet-config on PATH
P=../../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
python $P/run_h5toROOT.py $DATA/gpu0 $DATA/gpu1 -j 8 --out-dir $ANA/root/pbpb \
    --campaign-file $ANA/root/pbpb/zjet_c00_campaign.root
python $P/run_h5toROOT.py $PP --out-dir $ANA/root/pp --campaign-file $ANA/root/pp/zjet_pp_campaign.root
./zjets $ANA/root/pbpb $ANA/jets_cxx/pbpb --files 0:13        # in slices, in parallel
./zjets $ANA/root/pp $ANA/jets_cxx/pp
cd ../../analysis/zjet
python zjet_jets.py --pbpb $ANA/jets_cxx/pbpb --pp $ANA/jets_cxx/pp --outdir $ANA/figures --tag _c00_cxx
python check_cxx.py jets $ANA/jets_py/pbpb $ANA/jets_cxx/pbpb | tail -1      # against the Python map step
```

With extra hard scatterings all three take them into the full event by default and keep the trigger's truth as it is; `zjets` also writes B's jets per oversample (`bgx_*`: `bulk_bg` + the event's extras), `zhadron_pools` the extras' density (`R_extra`), `zqa` their histograms. `--extras 0` gives the outputs of files without extras ([Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/#with-the-events-other-hard-scatterings)).

`zjets` took 0.12 s per Pb+Pb oversample on the test set, at ~0.35 GB per process. `make FASTJET_PY=<the fastjet wheel's package directory>` builds against the pip `fastjet` wheel instead of a system FastJet, so both routes use the same FastJet. Options and details: [`analysis_root/zjet/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis_root/zjet/README.md).

## 7. Troubleshooting

| symptom                                                               | cause and fix                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| ROOT can't open an RNTuple                                            | ROOT < 6.34: convert with `--format ttree`                                                                               |
| `ValueError: cannot convert <RecordArray …> into np.ndarray` (uproot) | `events` read with `library="np"`; read it as awkward                                                                    |
| `UnboundLocalError: … 'low'` (uproot)                                 | a TTree with truncated floats written by ROOT ≥ 6.38: write those with ROOT < 6.38, or without `--bits-*`                |
| `'assert.h' file not found` (ACLiC)                                   | `conda activate` the ROOT env before compiling                                                                           |
| `fastjet/ClusterSequenceArea.hh: No such file` (ACLiC)                | `gSystem->AddIncludePath("-I$CONDA_PREFIX/include")`, or install `fastjet-cxx`                                           |
| `Error: You can only make one query at a time`                        | `fastjet-config --cxxflags --libs`: call it twice                                                                        |
| ROOT's C++ notebook kernel dies at start                              | `pip install metakernel` in the env; deactivate other venvs first                                                        |
| `run_h5toROOT.py`: `KeyError: 'seed'`                                 | O+O hadron files made in the job: convert them as in [O+O](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/oo/#13-root) |

# Notebooks

Work in progress

The analysis scripts and notebooks on this page are work in progress and need further vetting; they are meant mainly as examples of how to use the simulation outputs. See the [note on the analysis section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md).

Every notebook sits next to the code or the production it belongs to; this page is the index. Each one reads its inputs from environment variables (the defaults are in its first code cell), so the same notebook runs on the shipped example files, on your own run or on a downloaded campaign. Most are committed with their outputs, so they can be read on GitHub before running anything.

## Running a notebook

Set the notebook's variables, then open it in Jupyter or run it headless:

```bash
source ~/.venvs/js_analysis/bin/activate                  # the analysis venv
HADRON_DIR=/path/to/campaign jupyter lab contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb
HADRON_DIR=/path/to/campaign jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace \
    contribs/PyJetscape/example/analysis/tutorials/hadron_distributions.ipynb
```

The notebooks name the kernel they were saved with; in the venv choose `Python 3 (ipykernel)`, or the kernel registered with `setup_analysis_env.sh --kernel NAME` (for VS Code or another JupyterLab). On the Mac, the xscape environment runs them too, from your copy of the examples ([Mac (xscape wheel)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md)); from 0.2.0 it has pelicanfs, so the notebooks that read from the OSDF need nothing extra.

**Environments** in the tables: *venv* = the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md) (no X-SCAPE, no ROOT); *venv + ROOT* = the same with ROOT ≥ 6.34 ([ROOT and C++](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/root/#1-set-up)); *X-SCAPE* = an environment that runs X-SCAPE: the [Mac wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) or a [source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

# Python

# Python

js-contrib's Python interface, PyJetscape, lets you run X-SCAPE events from Python, read what every module produced as numpy arrays while the event is still in memory, and put modules of your own, written in Python, into the chain. Use it when the productions' command-line scripts are not enough: for a study of your own, for a notebook, for machine learning, or to try a new physics module without touching C++. Why this matters for ML is on [Python and machine learning](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/python-ml/index.md).

## The three layers

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["Your script or notebook"] --> B["Pythonic layer<br/>per_event, final_parton_array(), HadronArray,<br/>to_awkward, select, @js.module"]
    B --> C["jetscape package (pure Python)<br/>drivers, HDF5 writers and readers,<br/>PyFNOHydro, utils"]
    C --> D["pyjetscape_core (pybind11)<br/>X-SCAPE's C++ classes with their C++ names"]
    D --> E["X-SCAPE + MUSIC4GPU, iSS, Pythia, ..."]
```

- **`pyjetscape_core`** is the compiled extension: pybind11 bindings of X-SCAPE's classes (`JetScape`, `JetScapePerEvent`, `Parton`, `FourVector`, `PartonShower`, the module base classes, MUSIC, iSS access, ...) with their C++ names and argument order, so C++ code ports line by line. Every module base class has a *trampoline*: a Python subclass runs as a real JETSCAPE module.
- **The `jetscape` package** is pure Python around it: event-loop drivers (`jetscape.run_jetscape`), the HDF5 writers and readers of the productions, `PyFNOHydro`, conversion helpers (`jetscape.utils`), and `jetscape.paths` / `JobDir`, which find the X-SCAPE tree and give each run a working directory. The HDF5 readers work without the compiled extension; `jetscape.HAS_CORE` says whether it is there.
- **The Pythonic layer** is installed onto the bound classes by `import jetscape`: numpy record arrays instead of column indices, hadrons as one array per field, awkward views with `vector` kinematics, an event loop that is a context manager, and modules that declare their XML parameters. It only adds names, so code written against the bare bindings keeps working.

In code, `import jetscape as js` gives the package and the Pythonic layer; the bound classes themselves are in `jetscape.pyjetscape_core`:

```python
import jetscape as js                         # package + Pythonic layer
from jetscape import pyjetscape_core as core  # the bound C++ classes: core.JetEnergyLoss, core.FourVector, ...
```

PyTorch: import it first

`torch` and the compiled extension each bring an OpenMP runtime; the one loaded second can crash the process. When you use PyTorch, `import torch` **before** `import jetscape`. On macOS `import jetscape` does this for you if PyTorch is installed.

## Where you get it

**Container:**

The production image `jhputschke/xscape-prod` has `pyjetscape_core` and the `jetscape` package on `PYTHONPATH`, plus the analysis packages (awkward, vector, FastJet, Jupyter). PyTorch is not included. Copy the examples out of the read-only image once:

```bash
mkdir -p work
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  xscape-examples /work/examples
```

Details: [Production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md).

**Mac (xscape wheel):**

The `xscape` wheel (X-SCAPE with MUSIC4GPU for Metal, and the compiled `pyjetscape_core`) and the `pyjetscape` wheel (the `jetscape` package) install into one Python environment; `import jetscape` finds the compiled core there. PyTorch is not included. Copy the examples with

```bash
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
```

Details: [Mac (xscape wheel)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md).

**Source build:**

Build X-SCAPE (branch `contrib`) with js-contrib and the bindings. `-DUSE_MUSIC=ON` and `-DUSE_3DGlauber=ON` are required (the bindings use MUSIC's wrapper, iColoredHadronization and iMATTER):

```bash
cmake .. -DUSE_MUSIC=ON -DUSE_ISS=ON -DUSE_3DGlauber=ON \
         -DUSE_JS_CONTRIB=ON -DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON
make -j pyjetscape_core
pip install -e ../external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape   # or "...PyJetscape[fno,root]"
python -c "import jetscape; print(jetscape.HAS_CORE)"               # True
```

The extension must be built for the Python you run it with. Details: [Source build (conda)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

With only the [analysis environment](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/analysis-env/index.md) (no X-SCAPE build) you can read and analyse every production file, but not run events.

## A first event from Python

This runs one O+O event through the whole chain (3D MC-Glauber, Pythia with initial-state radiation, MUSIC, Matter + LBT, hadronization) with the user XML of the Pythonic example, `pythonic/oo_workflow.xml` in the copied examples, and prints what the jet left behind:

```python
import numpy as np
import jetscape as js

with js.JobDir("out_first", "oo_workflow.xml") as job:          # a private working directory
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml, n_events=1) as driver:
        for i in driver.events():                                # results are in memory here
            partons = driver.energy_loss_manager.final_parton_array()   # numpy records
            jet = driver.hadronization_manager.hadron_array()          # HadronArray
            print(f"event {i}: {len(partons)} final partons,",
                  f"leading parton pT {np.hypot(partons['px'], partons['py']).max():.1f} GeV,",
                  f"{len(jet)} jet hadrons")
```

On an M3 Max (Metal) this takes about 16 s and prints a line like `event 0: 17 final partons, leading parton pT 9.2 GeV, 116 jet hadrons`.

- `js.JobDir(out_dir, user_xml)` copies the XML to `out_dir/`, points its relative paths at the X-SCAPE build, and runs inside `out_dir/work/<name>`, because MUSIC, 3dMCGlauber and iSS read and write files in the current directory. Write your own outputs to absolute paths.
- `js.per_event(...)` as a context manager runs `Init()` on entry and `Finish()` on exit; `driver.events()` yields once per event, after the event ran and before its memory is freed.

A longer version that writes the hadrons to files is `pythonic/oo_workflow.py` (`python oo_workflow.py --events 3 --seed 7 --outdir out_oo`).

## Three ways to drive a run

|                 | how                                                       | modules come from                                                              | event loop |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| A, from the XML | `jetscape.run_jetscape.run_automatic(main_xml, user_xml)` | the XML (C++ factory, plus registered Python modules)                          | C++        |
| B, by hand      | `run_manual(main_xml, user_xml, modules=[...])`           | a Python list; the user XML sets `<enableAutomaticTaskListDetermination>false` | C++        |
| C, per event    | `js.per_event(main_xml, user_xml, tasks=None)`            | the XML, or `tasks=[...]` as in B                                              | Python     |

Mode C is the one to use for analysis and for anything that reads results: only there is each event's data still in memory when your code runs.

## Pages in this section

- [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md): running events, the result arrays, hadrons, awkward, FastJet, showers.
- [Writing modules in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md): your own hard process, energy loss, hadronization, afterburner or writer, with a worked example.
- [Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md): a PyTorch Fourier neural operator as the hydro module.
- [FastHydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fasthydro/index.md): MC-Glauber and a 3+1D hydro solver in PyTorch, with jet-deposition pairs.
- [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md): the medium and the parton shower in PyVista.

The full reference of the bindings and the package is [`contribs/PyJetscape/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/README.md); all examples are listed in [`contribs/PyJetscape/example/README.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/README.md).

# The Pythonic interface

The Pythonic interface is the layer of PyJetscape you will use most. It runs X-SCAPE events in a Python loop and hands you each event's partons, hadrons and showers as numpy record arrays, awkward arrays with four-vector kinematics, or Python objects, ready for numpy, FastJet and histogramming. Use it for any study that reads what the modules produce: a script of your own, a notebook, or a small production. It is installed by `import jetscape` and only adds names to the bound C++ classes, so scripts written against the bare bindings keep working and keep their output. Where to get it: [Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/#where-you-get-it).

## Quick start

```python
import fastjet
import jetscape as js

with js.per_event("jetscape_main.xml", "my_user.xml") as driver:
    for i in driver.events():
        partons = driver.energy_loss_manager.final_parton_array()   # numpy records
        jet = driver.hadronization_manager.hadron_array()          # HadronArray
        h = jet.to_awkward()                                        # samples x hadrons
        charged = h[js.select(h, "charged") & (abs(h.eta) < 2)]
        jets = fastjet.ClusterSequence(charged, fastjet.JetDefinition(
            fastjet.antikt_algorithm, 0.4)).inclusive_jets(min_pt=5.0)
        print(i, len(partons), "partons;", jets.pt.tolist())
```

The complete worked example is [`example/pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/example/pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb): three O+O events through the whole chain, the hadrons written to files and read back, spectra with errors, FastJet. Its simulation half is the script `oo_workflow.py` (`--xml`, `--events`, `--seed`, `--outdir`), a template for a production of your own.

**Requirements.** The bound classes need the compiled `pyjetscape_core`. Records and `HadronArray` need only numpy (they also work on files without a build); `to_awkward()` needs `awkward` and `vector`, `select()` needs `particle`, jets need the `fastjet` Python package, and the hadron files need `h5py`. All are in the container image, the Mac wheel's environment and the analysis environment; awkward and vector are imported only when used.

## Conventions

- **Names.** A method ending in `_array()` returns numpy data for the current event (`final_parton_array()`, `hadron_array()`, `edge_array()`). A plain noun returns objects (`showers`, `nodes`). Properties (`info`, `showers`, `momentum`, `last_random_seed`) take no parentheses.
- **Four-vectors.** Momentum is `(E, px, py, pz)`, position `(t, x, y, z)`, everywhere: records, `HadronArray.p` / `.x`, the hadron files, `FourVector.comp(i)`. Two older calls keep their own order: the bound constructor `FourVector(x, y, z, t)` (for a momentum `FourVector(px, py, pz, E)`) and `FourVector.to_list()`.
- **Units.** GeV and fm (fm/c), as in X-SCAPE.
- **Flat first, nested on request.** Every `_array()` is flat numpy plus offsets, the form the files use; `to_awkward()` gives the nested view.

## Running events

```python
with js.per_event(main_xml, user_xml) as driver:     # Init() and ExecInit() on entry
    for i in driver.events():                         # ExecPerEvent() ... ClearPerEvent()
        ...                                           # this event's results are in memory
                                                      # Finish() on leaving the block
```

`js.per_event(main_xml=None, user_xml=None, tasks=None, n_events=None)` returns a `JetScapePerEvent` driver:

- `tasks=[...]` adds a pipeline built by hand, in order; without it the XML's task list is used.
- `n_events` overrides `<nEvents>`.
- `driver.events(n=None, on_error=None)` yields the event index after the event ran and before it is cleared. `n` caps the count; `break` clears the current event. With `on_error(i, exc)`, an event in which a module throws (for example Matter's rare "minus log of sudakov negative") is reported, cleared and skipped, as the productions do; without it the exception propagates.

The run's modules are driver properties (`None` when absent):

| property                | what                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `energy_loss_manager`   | the final-state `JetEnergyLossManager` (in ISR runs, not the ISR chain's) |
| `hadronization_manager` | the `HadronizationManager`                                                |
| `soft_particlization`   | the first `SoftParticlization` (iSS)                                      |
| `hydro`                 | the hydro module                                                          |
| `initial_state`         | the initial state                                                         |

Anything else: `driver.GetTaskList()` and, for sub-tasks, `task.GetTaskList()`.

**Run in a working directory of its own.** MUSIC, 3dMCGlauber and iSS read inputs from and write side files to the current directory, and X-SCAPE's XMLs contain paths relative to the build. `js.JobDir` handles that for a script or notebook anywhere on disk:

```python
with js.JobDir("out", "my_job.xml") as job:      # out/my_job.xml; runs in out/work/my_job
    with js.per_event(job.main_xml, job.user_xml) as driver:
        ...                                       # write your outputs to absolute paths
```

It copies the user XML to `out/`, makes its `../` paths absolute, copies `music_input`, links the build's tables, changes into `out/work/<name>` and back, and removes that directory after a run without an exception (`keep=True` keeps it). The build is found through `jetscape.paths`: `$JETSCAPE_BUILD`, else `<X-SCAPE>/build_gpu`, where X-SCAPE is `$XSCAPE` or the tree the package sits in. In the container `XSCAPE=/opt/X-SCAPE` is set, so scripts run unchanged in and out of it.

## The results of an event

Each method wraps a function of the bindings, and returns numpy copies or arrays taken over from C++, so the results stay valid after the event is cleared.

| class                                   | member                                                                       | returns                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JetEnergyLossManager`                  | `showers`                                                                    | list of `PartonShower`, one per shower                                                              |
|                                         | `final_parton_array()`                                                       | final-parton records (what hadronization receives)                                                  |
|                                         | `initiator_array()`                                                          | the partons that started each shower                                                                |
| `SoftParticlization` (iSS)              | `hadron_array()`                                                             | `HadronArray`, one sample per oversample                                                            |
|                                         | `use_compact_output(on=True)`                                                | from the next event on, hadrons as arrays (about 8x less memory)                                    |
|                                         | `set_number_of_samples(n)`, `set_next_random_seed(seed)`, `last_random_seed` | oversamples and seeds                                                                               |
|                                         | `primary_array()`                                                            | the undecayed hadrons (iSS `<keep_primaries>`), or `None`                                           |
| `HadronizationManager`, `Hadronization` | `hadron_array()`                                                             | `HadronArray` of the jet hadrons                                                                    |
|                                         | `hadronize(partons, seed=None)`                                              | hadronize stored partons again                                                                      |
|                                         | `last_random_seed`                                                           | the jet hadronization's last seed                                                                   |
|                                         | `colour_audit()`, `colour_totals()`, `set_colour_closure(mode)`              | iColoredHadronization's colour bookkeeping, on builds that have it (`hasattr(had, "colour_audit")`) |
| `HardProcess`                           | `parton_array()`, `info`                                                     | hard partons, hardest first; dict with `pthat`, `sigma_gen`, `sigma_err`, `event_weight`            |
| `InitialState`                          | `info`                                                                       | dict with `n_coll`, `n_part`, `centrality` (what the module reports)                                |

Compact output is taken once

After `use_compact_output()`, `hadron_array()` takes iSS's arrays over without a copy, so call it **once per event**. Without compact output it copies and can be called again.

## Record arrays

The small per-event tables are numpy structured arrays (`jetscape.records`): `rec["px"]` instead of `rec[:, 4]`. Each holds exactly the values of the older column array it reorders.

| dtype                | from                         | fields                                                           |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FINAL_PARTON_DTYPE` | `final_parton_array()`       | `shower, pid, pstat, E, px, py, pz, t, x, y, z, mass, col, acol` |
| `INITIATOR_DTYPE`    | `initiator_array()`          | `shower, pid, pstat, E, px, py, pz, t, x, y, z`                  |
| `EDGE_DTYPE`         | `PartonShower.edge_array()`  | `src, tgt, pid, pstat, E, px, py, pz, t, x, y, z`                |
| `NODE_DTYPE`         | `PartonShower.node_array()`  | `id, t, x, y, z`                                                 |
| `HARD_PARTON_DTYPE`  | `HardProcess.parton_array()` | `pid, E, px, py, pz, pt, y`                                      |

Records work with the usual tools: `rec[rec["pstat"] >= 0]`, `np.unique(rec["shower"])`, `np.hypot(rec["px"], rec["py"])`, `pandas.DataFrame(rec)`. Converters for arrays from files: `final_parton_records(rows)`, `final_parton_rows(rec)`, `initiator_rows(rec)`, ... in `jetscape.records`.

## HadronArray

One event's hadrons (or a whole file's), **one array per field**, grouped into samples: one per iSS oversample, one for a jet hadronization.

| attribute        |                          |                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pid`, `pstat`   | (n,) int32               |                                                                          |
| `p`              | (n, 4) float32           | E, px, py, pz                                                            |
| `x`              | (n, 4) float32 or `None` | t, x, y, z                                                               |
| `mass`           | (n,) float32 or `None`   | `None` when read from a file                                             |
| `sample_offsets` | (n_samples + 1,) int64   | sample `s` is rows `sample_offsets[s]:sample_offsets[s+1]`               |
| `info`           | dict                     | e.g. the seed; after `from_h5`: `units`, `unit_offsets`, `attrs`, `path` |

`len(h)`, `h.n_samples`, `h.sample_counts`; `h.to_dict()` gives the dict the hadron writer takes; `h.to_awkward(...)` the nested view; `h.to_hadrons()` a `hadrons_h5.Hadrons` for its histogram helpers.

**Memory.** `HadronArray` wraps the arrays the bindings return without a copy and stores no derived columns: pt, eta, phi and rapidity are computed by `to_awkward()` when you ask for them. `to_hadrons()` computes them all in float64 (about 2.4x the memory); use it for histograms, not to hold many events.

## Nested views: `to_awkward`

`js.to_awkward(obj, position=False, charge=False, by_unit=False)`, also `HadronArray.to_awkward(...)`:

| input                                          | result                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `HadronArray`                                  | samples x hadrons, on the same buffers |
| `HadronArray.from_h5(...)` with `by_unit=True` | units (events) x samples x hadrons     |
| final-parton or initiator records              | showers x partons                      |
| edge, node, hard-parton records                | a flat array of records                |

The records are `vector` `Momentum4D` objects, so kinematics come on demand:

```python
import awkward as ak

h = driver.soft_particlization.hadron_array().to_awkward()
h.pt, h.eta, h.phi, h.rapidity, h.mass          # jagged, the shape of h
mid = h[abs(h.eta) < 0.5]
dndeta = ak.mean(ak.num(mid), axis=0)            # mean over the oversamples
```

- `position=True` adds a nested `h.position` (`Vector4D`: `h.position.t`, `h.position.rho`). It is nested on purpose: `vector` would read flat fields named t, x, y, z as the coordinates of the momentum.
- `charge=True` adds the PDG charge.
- A stored mass appears as the field `rest_mass`; `h.mass` is `vector`'s, computed from E and p.
- `ak.flatten(a, axis=1)` merges units x samples into samples; `ak.num(a, axis=k)` counts.

## Selecting species: `select`

```python
js.select(h, "pi+")                          # one PDG name
js.select(h, ["K+", "K-"])                   # any of several
js.select(h, "charged")                      # a class
js.select(h, ["p", "p~", "Lambda", "Lambda~"])
```

The result is a boolean mask of the input's shape (jagged for awkward input, so `h[js.select(h, "charged")]`). Classes: `charged`, `neutral`, `hadron`, `meson`, `baryon`, `strange`; names as the `particle` package spells them (`pi0`, `K(S)0`, `Sigma+`, `Omega-`, ...). Each distinct pid is looked up once.

`"charged"` and `hadrons_h5.CHARGED`

`select(..., "charged")` takes every pid with a nonzero PDG charge, resonances included. `hadrons_h5.CHARGED`, used by `Hadrons.charged` and the analysis scripts, lists the stable charged hadrons and leptons. They agree on decayed hadrons and differ only on files that keep undecayed primaries.

## Hadron files

The productions' hadron files (`jetscape.hadrons_h5`) take a `HadronArray` per unit (event) and give one back:

```python
from jetscape.hadrons_h5 import HadronH5Writer
from jetscape.records import initiator_rows

with HadronH5Writer("x_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5", tag="bulk_bg", n_samples=20) as bulk_w, \
     HadronH5Writer("x_hadrons_jet_frag.h5", tag="jet_frag", n_samples=1,
                    initiators=True) as jet_w:
    for i in driver.events():
        iss, had = driver.soft_particlization, driver.hadronization_manager
        bulk_w.append_unit(iss.hadron_array().to_dict(), unit=i, event=i,
                           seed=iss.last_random_seed)
        jet_w.append_unit(had.hadron_array().to_dict(), unit=i, event=i,
                          initiators=initiator_rows(driver.energy_loss_manager.initiator_array()))
```

Keywords besides the hadrons (`event=`, `seed=`, `pthat=`, ...) become the file's per-unit table. Reading:

```python
h = js.HadronArray.from_h5("x_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")          # every unit, stored fields only
h.info["units"]["seed"]                                      # the per-unit table
a = h.to_awkward(by_unit=True)                               # units x samples x hadrons
first = js.HadronArray.from_h5("x_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5", units=[0])
```

For whole campaigns, with event-averaged histograms and compound-Poisson errors, use `hadrons_h5.HadronFileReader` and `Hadrons`: [Hadrons](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/hadrons/index.md).

## Jets with FastJet

FastJet's Python package clusters jagged awkward arrays directly: one call for every event, or every oversample.

```python
import awkward as ak
import fastjet

jdef = fastjet.JetDefinition(fastjet.antikt_algorithm, 0.4)

# the jets of every event (a jet file: events x hadrons)
h = js.HadronArray.from_h5(jet_path).to_awkward()
acc = h[abs(h.eta) < 2]
jets = fastjet.ClusterSequence(acc, jdef).inclusive_jets(min_pt=5.0)   # events x jets
leading = ak.firsts(jets[ak.argsort(jets.pt, ascending=False)])

# charged jets
ch = acc[js.select(acc, "charged")]
ch_jets = fastjet.ClusterSequence(ch, jdef).inclusive_jets(min_pt=3.0)

# every oversample of every event (bulk: units x samples x hadrons)
b = js.HadronArray.from_h5(bulk_path).to_awkward(by_unit=True)
per_sample = ak.flatten(b, axis=1)                                     # samples x hadrons
bulk_jets = fastjet.ClusterSequence(per_sample[abs(per_sample.eta) < 2],
                                    jdef).inclusive_jets(min_pt=5.0)
bulk_jets = ak.unflatten(bulk_jets, ak.num(b, axis=1))                 # units x samples x jets
```

The jagged call gives the same jets as a loop over the samples. Jets are `vector` records too (`.pt`, `.eta`, `.phi`, `.m`); `constituent_index()` maps them back to hadrons. Areas, background subtraction and embedding are on [Jets with FastJet](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/jets/index.md).

## Particles and four-vectors

`FourVector` iterates, indexes and converts in `comp()` order (t, x, y, z) = (E, px, py, pz), compares by value, and pickles:

```python
import numpy as np
from jetscape import pyjetscape_core as core

v = core.FourVector.momentum(10.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0)    # E, px, py, pz
E, px, py, pz = v
np.asarray(v)                                         # array([10., 1., 2., 3.])
v == core.FourVector(1, 2, 3, 10)                     # True (the constructor is x, y, z, t)
```

Because `==` compares values, a `FourVector` is not hashable; use `tuple(v)` as a key.

Particles (`Parton`, `Photon`, `Hadron`) gain `momentum` and `position` (FourVector copies) and keyword factories that take any 4-sequence:

```python
p = js.make_parton(21, momentum=(50, 50, 0, 0), position=(0.5, 0, 0, 0),
                   stat=0, label=0, color=101, anti_color=102)
g = js.make_photon(momentum=(5, 0, 0, 5))
h = js.make_hadron(211, momentum=p.momentum, position=p.position, stat=1)   # PDG mass
E, px, py, pz = p.momentum
t, x, y, z = p.position
```

The bound methods stay methods (`p.pt()`, `p.eta()`). For properties, wrap a particle: `from jetscape.particles import view; view(p).pt`. Each is one call into C++ (about 1.4 µs), so for many particles use the arrays.

A particle's `t()` is its time

`x()`, `y()`, `z()`, `t()` of a particle are its position. A parton's virtuality is `virtuality()` (C++ `Parton::t()`).

## Parton showers

```python
for shower in driver.energy_loss_manager.showers:
    for parton in shower:                              # the partons (graph edges)
        end = shower.end_node(parton)
        if end.is_one_to_two:
            print(parton.pid(), "splits at t =", end.position.t(),
                  "z =", end.split_z, "kt =", end.split_kt, "dR =", end.split_delta_r)
    edges = shower.edge_array()                        # EDGE_DTYPE records
    nodes = shower.node_array()                        # NODE_DTYPE records
```

`PartonShower` iterates over its partons and has `nodes`, `start_node(p)`, `end_node(p)`, `edge_array()` and `node_array()`; it has no `len()`, so an empty shower is still true in `if shower:`. A `ShowerNode` has `id`, `vertex`, `position`, `parents`, `children`, `split_z`, `split_kt`, `split_delta_r`, `is_one_to_two` and `is_end`. Showers and partons are C++ objects of the event: use them inside the loop. The record arrays are copies and outlive it.

## Cost and memory

Measured on a GB10:

|                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| iSS, 972,215 cells, 1000 oversamples (7.0M hadrons), resident memory after the step / peak | dict from the bindings 686 / 916 MB; `HadronArray` 686 / 915 MB (no copy); `to_awkward()` + `.pt` 761 / 915 MB; `Hadrons` 1241 / 1240 MB |
| a Python energy-loss module, 715,438 calls (500 events)                                    | 3.73 s against 3.70 s before the Pythonic layer (+0.9 %)                                                                                 |
| one bound method call (`p.pt()`, `view(p).pt`)                                             | about 1.4 µs                                                                                                                             |

## Pitfalls

- **Read results inside the event loop.** Call the `_array()` methods inside `for i in driver.events():`. Their numpy results outlive the event; C++ objects (showers, partons) do not.
- **No surface, no iSS hadrons.** An event without a medium (O+O with no string) has no freeze-out surface; check `len(driver.hydro.surface_to_numpy())` before `hadron_array()`, as `oo_workflow.py` does.
- **Field names and `vector`.** Do not add fields named t, x, y, z, `tau`, `rho`, `phi`, `eta`, ... to a Momentum4D record; `vector` reads them as coordinates. Use nested records.
- **Bound classes are in `pyjetscape_core`.** `import jetscape as js` re-exports only some of them (`js.JetScapePerEvent`, `js.JetScapeSignalManager`, `js.FluidDynamics`, ...). For the others write `from jetscape import pyjetscape_core as core` and `core.FourVector`, `core.JetEnergyLoss`, `core.Parton`.
- **ISR runs** have two energy-loss managers; `driver.energy_loss_manager` is the final-state one.
- **Import `torch` before `jetscape`** when you use PyTorch (see [Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/index.md)).

The full guide, with every member, the guarantees of the layer and a side-by-side table of the old and new calls: [`contribs/PyJetscape/PYTHONIC.md`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/contribs/PyJetscape/PYTHONIC.md).
