# GPU acceleration

The viscous hydrodynamics is the most expensive part of an X-SCAPE heavy-ion event, and js-contrib runs it on the GPU with **MUSIC4GPU**, a port of MUSIC to CUDA (NVIDIA) and Metal (Apple Silicon). This page explains what runs on the GPU and what does not, how closely the GPU results agree with CPU MUSIC, what throughput to expect on the machines it was measured on, and the launch settings that give that throughput. Read it before you plan a campaign or pick hardware. To launch jobs, see [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).

## What runs on the GPU

MUSIC4GPU is a **direct port of MUSIC 3.1**: the same equations and the same numerical scheme (KT flux, Newton reconstruction, second-order Israel–Stewart viscous evolution). It adds no new physics. Two back ends share the same compute kernels and host code, and are chosen when MUSIC is built:

| back end  | hardware                                                            | used by                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CUDA**  | NVIDIA GPUs, discrete (V100 … H100, RTX) and Grace-Blackwell (GB10) | the [production container](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/container/index.md), source builds on Linux |
| **Metal** | Apple Silicon (M1 or later)                                         | the [Mac wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md), source builds on macOS                  |

When a configuration is supported, the **whole per-cell hydro time step runs on the GPU**: ideal evolution and reconstruction, shear stress and bulk pressure, velocity gradients, temperature-dependent η/s and ζ/s, the regulator, and the integration of the hydro source terms. The X-SCAPE productions (zero net baryon density, 3+1D grid) fall entirely inside it. Configurations outside it fall back to the CPU path, correct but slower: baryon diffusion, vorticity terms, a finite-μB EOS or μB-dependent shear.

Everything else in the event runs on the CPU:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  IC["3D MC-Glauber strings<br/>CPU"] --> M1["MUSIC_1: background<br/><b>GPU</b>"]
  H["Pythia hard process<br/>CPU"] --> E["Matter + LBT<br/>CPU"]
  M1 --> E
  E --> L["CausalLiquefier droplets<br/>CPU"]
  L --> M2["MUSIC_2: jet leg<br/><b>GPU</b>"]
  M1 --> S["freeze-out surfaces<br/>CPU, OpenMP"]
  M2 --> S
  S --> W["HDF5 writers<br/>CPU"]
  W --> P["iSS particlization,<br/>hadronization<br/>CPU (stage 2)"]
```

- **On the CPU:** the initial state, Pythia, the jet energy loss (Matter, LBT), the liquefier's droplets (the source is evaluated on the CPU and integrated on the GPU), the freeze-out surface search (Cornelius), the HDF5 output, and the whole second stage: iSS particlization and hadronization. Stage 2 needs no GPU at all, so it runs on CPU nodes.
- **One GPU per MUSIC.** MUSIC uses the first GPU it sees, so a machine with several GPUs runs one campaign per GPU (each with its own `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`).
- **The CPU path is still there.** `MUSIC_FORCE_CPU=1` runs the double-precision CPU path of the same binary, for validation.

The GPU is no longer the bottleneck

After the speed-ups, an Au+Au jet event on an RTX 3090 needs about **2 GPU-seconds but about 35 host core-seconds** (24 core-seconds for a job alone); the GPU computes for about 2 s of a 15 s event ([where the time goes](#where-an-events-time-goes)). On a discrete GPU the host cores, not the GPU, set the rate. That is why the launch settings below are mostly about cores and threads, and why several jobs share one GPU.

### Precision choices

- **Single precision on the GPU.** The kernels compute in FP32 (CUDA builds with `--use_fast_math`); the CPU path computes in double precision. Apple GPUs have no FP64, so Metal stays FP32. An FP64 build option has been assessed but not built.
- **Vacuum cells at rest.** In FP32, dilute vacuum cells could reach large u⁰ and stall an evolution. MUSIC4GPU puts vacuum cells (e < 10⁻⁵ fm⁻⁴, u⁰ > 10) at rest and zeroes non-finite viscous fields with a warning; `MUSIC_ABORT_ON_NONFINITE=1` stops the run instead.
- **The reconstruction solvers stop at float resolution.** No switch; the change is at the level of float rounding.
- **A larger time step late in the evolution** (on by default in the production XMLs): Δτ = 0.02 → 0.05 fm/c from τ = 3 fm/c, with the stored frames and freeze-out checks kept every 0.1 fm/c, so the output format does not change. It roughly halves the MUSIC steps and changes the medium at the 10⁻³ level, below the GPU-vs-CPU difference. The wake field differs cell by cell by ~5 %, almost all at scales below ~1 fm; at hadron level no change is seen within ±2 %. Keep **one setting per campaign**; `--late-dtau 0` gives a constant step.

## How close is the GPU to CPU MUSIC?

**Method.** The same Au+Au 0–10 % jet job (6 jet events on 3 backgrounds, PythiaGun p̂T 50–70 GeV, Matter + LBT + liquefier) was run twice with identical options, once on the GPU and once with `MUSIC_FORCE_CPU=1`. Only MUSIC's arithmetic differs. The comparison goes cell by cell through the hydro fields, then the freeze-out surfaces, then hadrons: iSS was run on both paths' surfaces with the same seeds and correlated sampling, so the hadrons are identical wherever the surfaces agree and the difference is measured with little noise. It was done with CUDA on a GB10 and repeated with Metal on an M3 Max.

**Result.** The two paths agree to about 0.2–0.3 %, with identical freeze-out times. The small remaining difference is systematic, and the same with CUDA and Metal:

| quantity                                               | GPU vs CPU                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| freeze-out times (all 9 MUSIC runs)                    | identical                      |
| energy density above freeze-out, energy-weighted       | Δe                             |
| temperature                                            | ΔT                             |
| energy above freeze-out / in the dilute fluid below it | −0.3 % / +0.4 %                |
| freeze-out volume                                      | −0.19 %                        |
| charged hadrons                                        | **−0.20 ± 0.02 %**             |
| ⟨pT⟩, v₂, v₃, momentum anisotropy                      | equal within errors            |
| jet wake (events with the same showers)                | fields 0.1–1 %, integrals ~1 % |

**What it means.**

- **Within one campaign the difference is negligible**: far below model and tuning uncertainties.
- **Between paths it is a normalization offset** that does not average out (it has the same sign in every event). Keep a campaign, and an FNO training set, on one path; don't mix in CPU-fallback jobs; and name the path when you compare with CPU or published MUSIC results.
- **Single events can differ in their jets.** A 3×10⁻⁴ change in the temperature is enough to send Matter and LBT down another random sequence, so the same seed may give a different shower. Compare the two paths statistically.
- **Limits:** 6 events, one centrality, one p̂T window. A large campaign compared with the CPU build has not been done.

Full details: [MUSIC_CPU_vs_GPU.md](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/MUSIC_CPU_vs_GPU.md). The physics of the productions themselves is on [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md).

## Headline numbers

Measured on specific machines

These numbers come from a handful of machines and code states, and they change as the code does. Each one is given with its hardware and settings. Re-measure on your own hardware before you size a campaign.

The productions:

- **Au+Au jets, campaign setting:** `prod_AuAu_0_10_jet` (two stages: MUSIC_1 background, then MUSIC_2 with jet deposition) with `--pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both`: one background per 15 jet events, pair file and particlize file written. An "event" is a jet event.
- **O+O, hadron files only:** `prod_OO_isr --bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file` (bulk hadrons made in the job, nothing else kept).

The rates are events per hour for the whole machine, from the campaign's makespan.

### GPU vs CPU MUSIC

How much faster a production runs on the GPU than on MUSIC's CPU path (`MUSIC_FORCE_CPU=1`, same binary, same events) on the **same machine**. These are speed-ups over each machine's own CPU, not a comparison between GPUs. Two numbers answer different questions:

- **Single event:** one job alone on the machine, GPU against CPU path. This is what a user running a few events sees.
- **Whole machine:** each path with as many jobs at once as pays, best events/h against best events/h. This is what a campaign sees.

Single event: one job alone, GPU vs CPU pathWhole machine: best events/h, GPU vs CPU pathRange

Speed-up of the GPU over MUSIC's CPU path on the same machine. Hover a bar for the measured times and rates; the numbers are in the table below.

|                            | 2 × RTX 3090, Threadripper 3960X (24 cores)                | GB10 (20 Arm cores, one integrated GPU)   | M3 Max (12 performance + 4 efficiency cores, Metal) |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| code and setting           | current `cu124` image, Au+Au campaign setting (2026-10-23) | code of 2026-10-03 to 10-08               | code of 2026-09 to 10-10                            |
| one job alone, CPU path    | 60.9 s/event (59 events/h)                                 | 230 s/event                               | 302 s/event                                         |
| one job alone, GPU         | 11.3 s/event (319 events/h)                                | 32 s/event                                | 28 s/event                                          |
| **single-event speed-up**  | **5.4×**                                                   | **7.2×**                                  | **10.8×** (12.8× in a September test)               |
| CPU path, machine full     | 4 jobs × 12 threads: 62 events/h (1.05× one job)           | not measured; 1.0–1.1× assumed            | not measured; 1.05–1.25× assumed                    |
| GPU, machine full          | 10 jobs per GPU, MPS: 2,846 events/h (8.9× one job)        | 6 jobs, MPS: 205 events/h (1.74× one job) | 3 jobs: 284 events/h (1.69× one job)                |
| **whole-machine speed-up** | **~46×** (35× counting job startup and ramp-up)            | **~11–13×**                               | **~15–17×**                                         |

The whole-machine speed-up is the single-event speed-up times what concurrent jobs add on the GPU, divided by what they add on the CPU path. The two differ this much because:

- **One GPU job leaves the machine mostly idle.** On the 3090 box a job alone keeps the GPU 18 % busy and 4.4 of 48 threads. More jobs fill the spare GPU and cores: 20 jobs (10 per GPU) give 8.9× the rate of one.
- **One CPU-path job already fills the machine.** MUSIC's OpenMP loops keep 42 of 48 threads busy, so 4 jobs × 12 threads gain only 5 %.
- **The 3090 box gains most** because it has two GPUs and 24 fast cores, so 20 jobs fit. Its rate is now limited by the CPUs (22 of 24 cores busy, GPUs 62 % busy). The GB10 and the M3 Max each have one integrated GPU, which is ~85 % busy at 3–6 jobs; more jobs add nothing.

The GB10 and M3 Max numbers are older

Their CPU/GPU pairs come from the 2026-10-08 comparison (6 events, two per background, MUSIC's own grid); their concurrent-job gains from a setting with a new background every event and p̂T 50–70 GeV. Both predate the GPU-side speed-ups of 2026-10-11/12 (on the M3 Max a job alone got 43 % faster), while the CPU path gained only the late time step, so their speed-ups today are probably higher. One CPU-path and one GPU job with the current code (~15 minutes per machine) would settle them.

- **The CPU path is a fair reference.** It takes the late time step, but MUSIC_2 starts from τ0 instead of restarting from MUSIC_1's state, which is how a CPU production would run. Both paths gave the same p̂T values and droplet counts.
- **MUSIC alone** gains more than the whole event. Per time step: 9.1× on the 3090 (vs 48 threads), ~5.2–5.5× on the GB10 (vs 20 threads), 5.0× on the M3 Max (vs 12 threads). One O+O event (wall time, indicative): ~3.5×, ~5.5× and ~8×.

### Where an event's time goes

The stages of one Au+Au event at the campaign setting, for **one job alone on the 3090 box**, same image on both paths (measured 2026-10-23 and 10-25). Stage 1 is the GPU job; stage 2 is iSS on the saved freeze-out surfaces, run later on CPU cores. Times are per event in a 15-event job, so the background's hydro counts one fifteenth.

| per event, one job alone                     | GPU, 3 threads (campaign) | GPU, 48 threads         | CPU path, 48 threads    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------- |
| jet-leg hydro (MUSIC_2)                      | 8.24 s                    | 5.14 s                  | 51.52 s                 |
| GPU kernels                                  | 2.07 s (GPU 25 % busy)    | 1.80 s (GPU 35 % busy)  | –                       |
| CPU work around them                         | 6.17 s (1.8 cores)        | 3.34 s (7.6 threads)    | 51.52 s (45.5 threads)  |
| background hydro (MUSIC_1 + copy), ⅟₁₅       | 1.00 s                    | 0.36 s                  | 3.78 s                  |
| Pythia + Matter + LBT + liquefier            | 0.13 s                    | 0.14 s                  | 0.13 s                  |
| pair file writer                             | 4.34 s                    | 4.36 s                  | 4.18 s                  |
| particlize file writer                       | 1.32 s                    | 1.27 s                  | 1.27 s                  |
| **stage 1**                                  | **15.0 s** (hydro 61 %)   | **11.3 s** (hydro 49 %) | **60.9 s** (hydro 91 %) |
| stage 2, one core: iSS (400 oversamples)     | 6.45 s                    | 6.45 s                  | 6.45 s                  |
| stage 2, one core: jet fragmentation + files | 0.86 s                    | 0.86 s                  | 0.86 s                  |
| **both stages**                              | **22.3 s**                | **18.6 s**              | **68.2 s**              |

Inside the jet leg's hydro (`MUSIC_PROFILE=1`, 3 threads): the RK steps, where the host waits for the kernels, take 1.96 s; putting the string and droplet source terms on the grid (CPU, OpenMP) 2.93 s; the freeze-out surface 2.64 s (Cornelius 1.93 s, on the CPU after a copy from the GPU); packing and copying the frames 0.35 s; init and other 0.36 s.

- **The GPU computes for about 2 s of a 15 s event.** The rest of the hydro is CPU work around the kernels, which runs in parallel: 48 threads cut it from 6.2 to 3.3 s, while the GPU part stays at ~2 s.
- **Matter + LBT take 0.13 s per event, under 1 %,** including Pythia and the liquefier, the same on both paths.
- **The writers take 5.6 s on one core,** as long as the GPU-path hydro with 48 threads; the pair file alone 4.3 s (reading the frames, resampling, HDF5). `--particlize-only` skips it.
- **Counting stage 2 lowers the single-event speed-up from 5.4× to 3.7×** (18.6 s against 68.2 s), since iSS costs the same on both paths. Stage 2 usually runs on a CPU cluster (`slurm_hadronize.sh`), where 4–5 cores keep up with 2,160 events/h; on the 3090 box itself it would cost ~17 % of stage 1's rate (~38× instead of 46× over the CPU path, an estimate).

iSS in stage 1?

Today the hydro (GPU and CPU parts) is about half of a stage-1 event. iSS at 400 oversamples adds ~7.3 s on one core, about as long as the hydro, so moving it into stage 1 drops the hydro to 30–40 % of the event if the job still writes its files (22.3 s and 18.6 s per event above). It stays near half only without the writers (`--hadrons-only`, ~16.6 s and ~13.0 s) or with few oversamples (1–10 oversamples cost mostly a fixed ~2.6 s per surface). But `--hadrons-only` writes no pair file, so there is no hydro history for FNO training and no surfaces to sample again. On a full 3090 box, already CPU-limited, iSS in stage 1 costs ~17 % of the rate either way. These rows add measured stage times; they were not run as jobs.

### Other speed-ups that matter

A pair event once took ~184 s on the GB10. Much of the way to today's rates came from the CPU side, with bit-identical output:

- **MUSIC's host work:** the string source fill skips empty steps and bins strings by transverse reach (15.3 → 5.9 s per event); the jet source is prepared once per step and the liquefier evaluates only droplets that can deposit (pair event 184 → 60 s).
- **Parallel freeze-out surface:** the surface search runs η-slices in parallel with OpenMP, deterministic across thread counts (9.6 → 1.2 s per event).
- **MUSIC_2 restarts from MUSIC_1's state** at the step before the first droplet, instead of re-running the early evolution (two-stage job −19 % wall time, on by default).
- **iSS:** the per-surface fixed cost fell from ~16.5 s to ~4 s, and the sampling loop was repacked; `hadronize.py` on both legs at 500 oversamples now takes ~10.6 s on one core (8.8 s with `--correlated`), against ~58 s before.
- **HDF5 writers and memory:** Blosc-zstd compression and a background stored once for all its jet events take the pair file from 400 to 170 MB per event (15 jets per background); reading the legs one frame at a time and a slim copy of the hydro history for the jets took a job's memory from ~20 GB to ~6–7 GB.
- **Shared LBT tables** (`LBT_TABLE_CACHE`): one read-only copy of LBT's 0.66 GB of tables for all jobs on a machine.

The complete list, with what is and is not bit-identical: [OPTIMIZATION_CHANGES.md](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/OPTIMIZATION_CHANGES.md).

## Recommended launch settings

None of these settings changes the output; they only change how fast a campaign runs. They are **not built into the scripts**, because the best values depend on the machine's balance of cores, GPU and memory. These are the measured best values:

| setting                         | 2 × RTX 3090 (per GPU, Docker) | GB10                                  | M3 Max (Metal)                    | SLURM cluster (`slurm_prod_array.sh`)               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| jobs at once (`run_jobs.sh -j`) | Au+Au 10, O+O 8                | Au+Au 4, O+O 8                        | Au+Au 3                           | `P=10` (default; see the per-GPU table)             |
| `OMP_NUM_THREADS`               | 3                              | Au+Au 5, O+O 2                        | 5                                 | `cpus-per-task / P`, at least 2 (set by the script) |
| `OMP_WAIT_POLICY`               | `passive`                      | `passive` (no measurable effect here) | `passive`, with `KMP_BLOCKTIME=0` | `passive` (set by the script)                       |
| `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC`               | `block`                        | `block`                               | – (CUDA only)                     | `block` (default)                                   |
| CUDA MPS (`--mps`)              | yes, one daemon per container  | yes, natively (not in a container)    | – (CUDA only)                     | off (`USE_MPS=0`), never tried on a cluster         |
| `LBT_TABLE_CACHE`               | yes (Au+Au)                    | optional (−0.6 GB per job)            | yes                               | yes (Au+Au, default path)                           |
| `--stagger`                     | 12 s (Au+Au)                   | –                                     | no gain                           | 12 s (Au+Au, default)                               |

**What each setting does:**

- **Jobs per GPU.** One job alone leaves the GPU idle much of the time, so several jobs share it. Size the number by the cores (~2–3 per job) and host memory (plan ~7 GB per Au+Au job, 5 GB with `--particlize-only`; ~1.5–2 GB per O+O job). If a node gives fewer cores per GPU, lower `-j`, not the threads per job.
- **`OMP_NUM_THREADS` ≈ cores / jobs.** By default every job starts one OpenMP thread per core, and several jobs then oversubscribe the cores. On the M3 Max, `-j 3` with default threads gave only 1.1× one job; with the cores split, 1.6×. **For one job alone, leave it unset**: on the GB10, fewer threads made a single job 24 % slower.
- **`OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive`:** idle OpenMP threads sleep instead of spinning and stealing cores from the other jobs.
- **`MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block`:** the host thread sleeps while it waits for the GPU instead of spinning, ~30 % less CPU per event at the same throughput. The job log says `[MUSIC-GPU] host sync: block`.
- **CUDA MPS** lets the kernels of several jobs run side by side instead of taking turns: +5–7 % on the 3090s, +12.5 % on the GB10 at 4 jobs. Try without it first; if the GPU is under ~60 % busy it won't help. The MPS daemon does not start inside a container on the GB10, and two daemons in one container hang the second GPU's jobs: use one container per GPU.
- **`LBT_TABLE_CACHE=FILE`:** all jobs map one read-only copy of LBT's tables: −0.6 GB and 6–11 s of start-up per Au+Au job (on the M3 Max, start-up 14.5 → 3.0 s). Put the file on local disk, one file per LBT-tables version, not in the container's `/dev/shm`. O+O runs no LBT.
- **`run_jobs.sh --stagger S`:** the first jobs start S seconds apart so that their memory peaks don't coincide (−11 GB at 20 jobs on the 3090 box).
- **`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`** is set by the drivers; more threads don't help.

**NVIDIA GPU, ~12 cores per GPU:**

One RTX 3090-class GPU, Au+Au campaign setting (one `run_jobs.sh` per GPU):

```bash
mkdir -p /scratch/lbt_cache
OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/scratch/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 10 --mps --stagger 12 60 45 0 out_c --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 \
  --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
```

With Docker on two GPUs, `utils/launch_2gpu.sh` (Au+Au) and `utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh` (O+O) start one container and one MPS daemon per GPU, with the settings above as their defaults (Au+Au: 10 jobs and 3 threads per GPU, the LBT cache, `--stagger 12`).

**GB10:**

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 4 --mps 20 25 0
```

For O+O: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2` and `-j 8 --mps`.

**Mac (Metal):**

```bash
export LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/path/on/local/disk/lbt_tables_v1.bin
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign test 20 25 0 ~/xscape/prod/out
```

`-j 4` with 4 threads was not better than `-j 3`. `--mps` and `MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC` don't apply. Keep the Mac awake for long campaigns (`caffeinate -i ./run_jobs.sh ...`).

Let the wizard write the command

[`utils/prodwizard.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/prodwizard.py) takes a production preset and a machine (`2x3090`, `gb10`, `m3max`, or a SLURM cluster with V100, A40, A100 or L40S) and writes the launch command with these settings, with estimates of events/h, duration, disk and memory. It never starts jobs.

Disk can become the limit

At 2,160 Au+Au events/h with the pair file, the 3090 box writes ~525 GB/h, more than the ~290 GB/h an upload to the OSDF takes. If you don't need the hydro history, use `--particlize-only` (0.097 instead of 0.243 GB per event) or a large local disk.

**On another machine,** measure: one job alone first (is the GPU mostly idle?), then a short sweep of `-j` with and without MPS, with `OMP_NUM_THREADS ≈ cores / jobs`. Use the same seeds in every run and compare events/h by makespan. If the GPU stays below ~75 % busy while the cores are full, the machine is host-limited: more cores per GPU pay, more jobs don't. How to launch and monitor: [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md).

## Cost on HPC

None of the cluster GPUs has been run yet. Scaling the measured 3090 and GB10 numbers by GPU speed and cores per GPU gives these **estimates** for the Au+Au campaign setting, per GPU:

| GPU             | jobs per GPU | cores per GPU | host memory per GPU | expected Au+Au events/h | limit                  |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------- |
| V100 (16/32 GB) | 8            | 12–16         | 64 GB               | 700–950                 | GPU                    |
| A40 (48 GB)     | 10–12        | 16–24         | 90–100 GB           | 1,100–1,400             | cores at 16, GPU at 24 |
| A100 (40/80 GB) | 10–12        | 16–24         | 90–100 GB           | 1,000–1,500             | GPU or cores           |
| L40S (48 GB)    | 18–22        | 24–32         | 135–165 GB          | 2,000–2,900             | cores                  |

For NSF ACCESS resources, on well-sized nodes every option gives about **15–25 Au+Au events per ACCESS credit**: faster GPUs cost proportionally more per hour. An H100 pays off only with at least ~24 cores per GPU; with 16 it runs at an A100's rate. About **50,000–55,000 credits** of GPU time make a million Au+Au events. Storage (100–240 TB for those files) is the larger request. The first choice is NCSA DeltaAI (GH200, 72 Grace cores per H100, about 19–22 events per credit), the second NCSA Delta A40. Details, including Slurm settings per resource: [REPORT_CLUSTER_ACCESS.md](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/docs/REPORT_CLUSTER_ACCESS.md).

### Speed-up per GPU against the CPU path

A cluster hands out a GPU together with a share of a node's cores and memory, so the useful number is events/h per GPU against the CPU path on that same share. The 3090 column is measured; the NCSA Delta columns are **estimates** (nothing has run on Delta), and Delta's smaller memory share gives lower rates than the table above.

| per GPU                                                                | 2 × RTX 3090 box (measured)                  | Delta A40 or A100 40 GB, 4-GPU node (estimate)                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| share of the node                                                      | 12 Zen 2 cores (24 threads), ~62 GB          | 16 Milan cores, 62.5 GB (one GPU's charge on a 64-core, 256 GB node)                                                        |
| jobs per GPU                                                           | 10, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=3`                      | 8 with the pair file, 10 with `--particlize-only`; OMP 2; memory sets this                                                  |
| GPU path, events/h                                                     | 1,423 (1,080 by makespan), pair + particlize | 800–1,100 with the pair file, 1,000–1,400 with `--particlize-only`; limited by memory, then cores, so the A100 adds nothing |
| CPU path on the same cores, events/h                                   | 31 (half of the 62 measured on 24 cores)     | 47–62 (16 cores × 2.6 events/h per Zen 2 core × 1.15–1.5 for Milan)                                                         |
| **speed-up per GPU**                                                   | **46×** (35× by makespan)                    | **13–23×** with the pair file, **16–30×** with `--particlize-only`                                                          |
| one GPU replaces                                                       | ~550 Zen 2 cores (~420 by makespan)          | ~200–470 Milan cores                                                                                                        |
| events per ACCESS credit                                               | –                                            | 12–16 (pair), 15–21 (`--particlize-only`) at the A100 rate; about twice that on A40s if they cost half                      |
| **cost per event against Delta CPU nodes** (3.0–3.9 events per credit) | –                                            | **3–5× cheaper** (pair, A100 rate); up to 8–14× (`--particlize-only`, A40 at half rate)                                     |

- **Delta's per-GPU speed-up is lower than the 3090 box's** (13–30× against 35–46×): its 62.5 GB share holds only 8–10 jobs, too few to keep the GPU busy, and the CPU path does better on 16 newer cores than on 12.
- **The speed-up per credit is the per-GPU speed-up divided by ~4.2,** because Delta charges a GPU-hour (66.7 credits, cores included) about 4.2× the 16 core-hours of the same cores. The A40 is charged below the A100 rate, but Delta does not publish the factor.
- **Stage 2 changes little:** 7.3 core-s per event, about 0.002 credits on Delta CPU, against ~0.05–0.08 credits per event of GPU time.
- **Assumptions:** ~5 GB per job with `--particlize-only` and ~7 GB with the pair file; 25–35 s per event in a loaded job; 45-event jobs; a Milan core 1.15–1.5× a Zen 2 core for both paths; the A40's GPU time per event 1.0–1.2× the 3090's, the A100's 0.9–1.4×. The CPU path's rate per Milan core is not measured; its hydro is bandwidth-heavy and could scale less well.
- **Delta's 8-GPU A100 nodes** (more memory per GPU; check before planning) would lift the memory limit: ~1,100–1,700 events/h per GPU, about 18–36× the CPU path.
- **One short benchmark settles it:** one A40 at `-j 8` and `-j 10`, plus one CPU-path job on 16 cores (REPORT_CLUSTER_ACCESS.md §7).

- [Why js-contrib](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/why/index.md) and [the physics of the productions](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md).

# Python and machine learning

X-SCAPE is a C++ framework. js-contrib opens it to Python, not as a wrapper that runs a finished binary, but down to the module level: Python can drive the event loop, read every intermediate result as numpy arrays, and replace any stage of the simulation with a class of its own. This page explains why that matters for heavy-ion physics and what you can do with it today; the [Python section](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/index.md) shows how.

## Why Python

**Machine learning lives in Python.** Neural networks are trained, evaluated and changed in PyTorch. A surrogate model that is only usable after it has been exported, frozen and re-linked into C++ is slow to iterate on. With js-contrib a PyTorch model can be a JETSCAPE module: it receives the initial condition from the framework, predicts the medium, and Matter, LBT and iSS run on its prediction as they would on MUSIC.

**Hydro surrogates need hydro.** A Fourier neural operator (FNO) learns the map from an initial condition to the full space-time evolution of the medium. In 2+1D it reproduces MUSIC orders of magnitude faster ([Phys. Rev. C 113, 014904 (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1103/jsh8-6tm7)). Training it, and the 3+1D and jet-deposition models that follow, takes many MUSIC evolutions in a format a training code reads directly. The productions write exactly that.

**Jets in a medium need pairs.** To learn how a jet changes the medium, a model needs the same event twice: once without the jet and once with its deposited energy, on an identical initial condition. Then `arr - arr_bg` is the jet's effect and nothing else. The two-stage productions (MUSIC, GPU) and FastHydro (a fast solver written in PyTorch) both write such pairs.

**Physics modules are faster to prototype in Python.** An idea for an energy-loss kernel or a hadronization model can be written as a Python class in an afternoon and run inside the full event, next to the C++ modules, without recompiling X-SCAPE. Once it works, it ports to C++ line by line, because the Python interface keeps the C++ names and argument order.

**Analysis is in numpy, awkward and FastJet.** Hadrons, partons and showers come out of an event, or out of the production files, as numpy arrays and nested awkward arrays with four-vector kinematics, ready for `fastjet` and histogramming.

## What works today

| you want to                                                                                | use                                      | page                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| run events from Python and read every result as numpy                                      | `pyjetscape_core` and the Pythonic layer | [The Pythonic interface](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/pythonic/index.md)   |
| replace a stage (hard process, energy loss, hadronization, ...) with your own Python class | the module base classes, `@js.module`    | [Writing modules in Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/modules/index.md) |
| run a PyTorch FNO as the hydro, live, while you train it                                   | `PyFNOHydro`                             | [Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md)        |
| make large samples of jet-deposition pairs fast, on CPU, CUDA or Apple MPS                 | FastHydro                                | [FastHydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fasthydro/index.md)               |
| produce FNO training data with the real MUSIC + jet chain on GPUs                          | the Au+Au jet production                 | [Au+Au jets (two stages)](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/auau-jet/index.md)     |
| analyse hadrons and jets from the production files                                         | `HadronArray`, awkward, FastJet          | [Analyse](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/analysis/index.md)                         |
| look at the medium and the shower in 3D                                                    | the PyVista scripts                      | [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md)    |

Python modules run in the container and with the Mac wheel as they are: no compiler is needed. PyTorch is needed only for `PyFNOHydro` and FastHydro.

# Publications and citing

If you publish results made with js-contrib, cite the repository and the papers of the physics modules your results depend on. This page lists them by stage of the simulation, says which ones belong to which production, and gives a citation for js-contrib itself. Every arXiv number below links to the paper's abstract page. For BibTeX entries, look up the arXiv number on [INSPIRE-HEP](https://inspirehep.net). Which module does what is explained in [The physics](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/about/physics/index.md).

## How to cite js-contrib

js-contrib has no DOI and no paper of its own. Cite:

1. **the repository:** <https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib>;
1. **the JETSCAPE framework paper** ([arXiv:1903.07706](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07706)), always;
1. **the papers of the modules you used**, from the table below and the lists on this page.

```bibtex
@misc{js-contrib,
  author       = {Putschke, Joern and others},
  title        = {{js-contrib}: contributions for the {JETSCAPE}/{X-SCAPE} framework},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib}},
  year         = {2026}
}
```

Add the version you used (a release tag or commit, and the container tag or the Mac wheel version) in the text or a footnote. Every production file records the XML it was made with, which is the precise record of the physics settings.

### Which papers for which production

| you use                                 | cite                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| any js-contrib production               | the [JETSCAPE framework](#framework); [3D MC-Glauber](#initial-state); [MUSIC](#hydrodynamics-and-equation-of-state) and the [HotQCD EoS](#hydrodynamics-and-equation-of-state); [Cornelius, Cooper–Frye and iSS](#freeze-out-and-particlization) |
| Au+Au, Pb+Pb or Z+jet with jets         | in addition: [PYTHIA 8](#hard-process); [MATTER, LBT and the multistage approach](#jet-energy-loss); the [CausalLiquefier](#energymomentum-deposition)                                                                                            |
| O+O with ISR                            | in addition: the [X-SCAPE small-system papers](#framework); [PYTHIA 8](#hard-process); [MATTER and LBT](#jet-energy-loss)                                                                                                                         |
| FNO hydro (FnoHydro, PyFNOHydro)        | in addition: [FNO and the FNO hydro paper](#machine-learning)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| jets reconstructed with FastJet         | [FastJet and anti-`$k_t$`](#jet-reconstruction)                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| SMASH run on the stored primary hadrons | [SMASH](#hadronic-transport)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

# Contribs and repositories

## The contribs

js-contrib is organised like fastjet-contrib: each contrib lives in its own folder under [`contribs/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs) and is switched on separately.

| Contrib                                                                                    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                      | Build                                                                            | Extra dependencies                                             | Docs on this site                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [PyJetscape](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/PyJetscape)       | pybind11 bindings (`pyjetscape_core`), the `jetscape` Python package with the Pythonic layer, Python modules, the `PyFNOHydro` trampoline, the production drivers and examples  | C++ (`-DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON`); already built in the container and the Mac wheel | pybind11; h5py, hdf5plugin, pyyaml; PyTorch optional (`[fno]`) | [Python](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/index.md), [Run](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/index.md) |
| [FnoHydro](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/FnoHydro)           | Fourier-neural-operator hydrodynamics as a C++ module through LibTorch, plus the bulk ROOT I/O library                                                                          | C++ (`-DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON`)                                                    | libtorch (~2 GB), ROOT                                         | [Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/index.md)                                          |
| [FastHydro](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/FastHydro)         | MC-Glauber initial state and a fast 3+1D Milne finite-volume hydro solver, with the MATTER + LBT → CausalLiquefier jet-deposition workflow and paired background/jet evolutions | pure Python, reuses PyJetscape                                                   | PyTorch, scipy, h5py, pyyaml                                   | [FastHydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fasthydro/index.md)                                                 |
| [Visualization](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/contribs/Visualization) | 3D PyVista rendering of the hydro evolution, resampled from Milne to Cartesian coordinates, with a jet parton-shower overlay                                                    | pure Python, reuses PyJetscape                                                   | pyvista, scipy, vtk, imageio (`imageio-ffmpeg` for `.mp4`)     | [3D visualization](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/visualization/index.md)                                      |

FastHydro and Visualization have no CMake build of their own. They read the framework through the PyJetscape bindings and so need a current `pyjetscape_core`.

## The pieces of a working setup

| Component          | Repository / image                                                                                 | Role                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| X-SCAPE            | [JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE), branch `contrib`                          | the framework and the C++ physics modules (MATTER, LBT, liquefier, hadronization, …)                                                                            |
| MUSIC4GPU          | [jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU](https://github.com/jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU), branch `XSCAPE`                   | MUSIC viscous hydro with CUDA and Metal back ends                                                                                                               |
| iSS                | [jhputschke/iSS](https://github.com/jhputschke/iSS), branch `sampling_omp`                         | Cooper–Frye particlization (oversampling, SMASH-ready output, correlated sampling on threads)                                                                   |
| 3D MC-Glauber      | [jhputschke/3dMCGlauber](https://github.com/jhputschke/3dMCGlauber), branch `cap_hard_quark_draws` | the initial state                                                                                                                                               |
| LBT tables         | [JETSCAPE/LBT-tables](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/LBT-tables)                                      | LBT's scattering tables (fetched by `get_lbtTab.sh`, or `xscape-fetch-data lbt` with the wheel)                                                                 |
| js-contrib         | [jhputschke/js-contrib](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib)                                  | this package: bindings, drivers, productions, tools, analysis                                                                                                   |
| Production images  | [`jhputschke/xscape-prod`](https://hub.docker.com/r/jhputschke/xscape-prod)                        | everything above, built, for Linux with NVIDIA GPUs (amd64 and arm64)                                                                                           |
| Development images | `jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev`                                                                      | the build environment without sources, for a source build on Linux with NVIDIA GPUs                                                                             |
| Mac wheel          | [jhputschke/xscape-macos](https://github.com/jhputschke/xscape-macos)                              | everything above, built for Apple Silicon with Metal, installed with uv                                                                                         |
| FNO models         | [Zenodo record 16647726](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16647726)                                  | the trained FNO hydro models and their training data ([Live PyTorch FNO hydro](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/python/fno/#where-the-models-come-from)) |

The X-SCAPE scripts `external_packages/get_*.sh` clone MUSIC4GPU, iSS and 3D MC-Glauber at pinned commits. When you update X-SCAPE, run them again so the pins take effect. See [Source build](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/source/index.md).

## Versions that belong together

| js-contrib | X-SCAPE          | MUSIC4GPU                               | Mac wheel |
| ---------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `main`     | `contrib` (head) | `XSCAPE` (pinned by `get_music4gpu.sh`) | v0.2.0    |

The container images and the Mac wheel are built from one consistent set of commits, so there is nothing to match by hand. With a source build, keep js-contrib `main` together with X-SCAPE `contrib`.

# Tools

The [`utils/`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/tree/main/utils) folder holds the tools around the simulations. They help you plan a production, watch it run, check its files, and move them. Each one is a plain script, and `--help` lists all of its options.

On a Mac: commands of the xscape wheel

From 0.2.0 the [xscape wheel](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/install/mac/index.md) ships `utils/` and has the tools as commands, run in the wheel's environment with the same options (`--help` shows them under the command's name). `xscape-utils DEST` copies `utils/` to read or adapt.

| command                   | script                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `xscape-prodwizard`       | `prodwizard.py` (machine `mac_wheel`)                                            |
| `xscape-jobmon`           | `jobmon.py`                                                                      |
| `xscape-check-deposition` | `check_deposition.py`                                                            |
| `xscape-h5-inspect`       | `h5_inspect.py`                                                                  |
| `xscape-osdf`             | `remote_transfer/js_osdf.py`, in the wheel's environment (no `~/.cache/js_osdf`) |
| `xscape-upload-follow`    | `upload_follow.py`, likewise                                                     |
| `xscape-gcs`              | `remote_transfer/js_gcs.py`, with its own environment in `~/.cache/js_gcs`       |
| `xscape-selftest`         | `container/image_check.py --analysis`, plus the LBT tables                       |

## Planning: `prodwizard.py`

You choose a production preset and a machine. The wizard writes the launch command with the settings measured on that machine. It estimates events per hour, duration, disk and memory (each marked measured or estimated) and checks the plan. **It never starts jobs.**

```bash
python utils/prodwizard.py --list                                  # presets and machines
python utils/prodwizard.py --preset auau_jet --machine 2x3090 --events 2000
python utils/prodwizard.py --preset oo_hadrons --machine slurm_a100 --events 10000 --save launch_oo.sh
python utils/prodwizard_tui.py                                     # the same as an interactive wizard (Textual)
```

| Presets                                                                                       | Machines                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auau_jet`, `auau_particlize_only`, `auau_hadrons_only`, `oo_hadrons`, `oo_full`, `pbpb_zjet` | `2x3090`, `gb10`, `m3max`, `mac_wheel`, `slurm_v100`, `slurm_a40`, `slurm_a100`, `slurm_l40s` |

`m3max` is a Mac with a js-contrib checkout and the `fno_env_mlx` conda environment. `mac_wheel` is a Mac with the xscape wheel: the commands activate `$VIRTUAL_ENV` (default `~/.venvs/xscape`), run `run_jobs.sh` in your copy of the examples, `$XSCAPE_EXAMPLES` (default `~/xscape/examples`), and watch it with `xscape-jobmon`. Run inside the wheel's environment, the wizard picks `mac_wheel` by itself; the settings are the M3 Max's.

```bash
xscape-prodwizard --preset auau_jet --machine mac_wheel --events 300    # on a Mac with the wheel
```

## Launching

| Script                                                                                                                                                                                         | What it does                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run_jobs.sh` (in each production folder)                                                                                                                                                      | runs a campaign of jobs with unique seeds, several at a time on one GPU; see [the productions](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/index.md) |
| [`launch_2gpu.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/launch_2gpu.sh), [`launch_2gpu_oo.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh) | one Docker container per GPU on a two-GPU machine, a disk guard, and optional upload to the OSDF while it runs                                       |
| [`slurm_prod_array.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/slurm_prod_array.sh)                                                                                          | stage 1 (hydro + jets) as a SLURM array in the production container, one GPU per task; `PROD=oo` for O+O                                             |
| [`slurm_hadronize.sh`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/slurm_hadronize.sh)                                                                                            | stage 2 (hadronization) as a SLURM array on a CPU partition                                                                                          |

See [Clusters, GPUs and monitoring](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/clusters/index.md) for how they fit together.

## Monitoring: `jobmon.py`

`jobmon.py` watches a running (or finished) campaign using only what the jobs already write (logs and `.json`). It reports jobs done, running and failed, events per hour, ETA, disk per event, the machine's GPUs and memory, and the most frequent warnings. It also flags failed jobs with their last log lines.

```bash
python utils/jobmon.py out/                 # one summary; exit code 1 if a job failed or is flagged
python utils/jobmon.py out/ --watch         # live view, refreshed every 10 s
python utils/jobmon.py out/ --tui           # terminal UI: sortable job table, live log, problems tab
xscape-jobmon out/ --tui                    # the same with the Mac wheel
```

[`check_deposition.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/check_deposition.py) flags Au+Au jet jobs whose deposited droplets per event fall below half the campaign's median. This is a rare failure that leaves no log message.

## Inspecting files: `h5_inspect.py`

`h5_inspect.py` lists every group and dataset of an HDF5 file with its shape, dtype, storage and attributes. For the js-contrib hydro formats it also summarises the grid, the axes, the freeze-out, the `shower/`, `source/` and `diag/` tables, and flags inconsistencies. It needs only h5py and numpy.

```bash
python utils/h5_inspect.py out/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5           # summary + tree
python utils/h5_inspect.py FILE.h5 --stats [--event 0]              # per-feature min/max/mean, NaN/inf
python utils/h5_inspect.py FILE.h5 --attr prod_user_xml             # one attribute in full
xscape-h5-inspect FILE.h5                                           # the Mac wheel's command
```

## Comparing files: `h5_compare.py`

[`h5_compare.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/h5_compare.py) compares two HDF5 files, or every `*.h5` of the same name in two directories. It is the check after a change that should not alter the output: run the same job with the same seed before and after, and compare.

```bash
python utils/h5_compare.py A.h5 B.h5                               # datasets and attributes that differ
python utils/h5_compare.py before/ after/ --ignore-stamps          # two directories; run stamps skipped
python utils/h5_compare.py A.h5 B.h5 --ignore 'diag/*' --no-attrs  # skip by pattern; datasets only
python utils/h5_compare.py A.h5 B.h5 --rtol 1e-6                   # floats may differ by 1e-6 (relative)
python utils/h5_compare.py A.h5 B.h5 -q && echo same               # exit code: 0 same, 1 different, 2 error
```

The comparison is bit-exact unless you give a tolerance: a dataset is the same only if shape, dtype and every byte agree. For a dataset that differs, the script prints how many values differ, the largest absolute and relative difference, and the index of the first one. For an attribute it prints both values.

For example, a hadron file against a copy with three momenta, one cell count and one attribute changed:

```text
datasets:   10 in A, 10 in B; 8 identical, 2 differ
  hadrons/p        3 of 1438404 values differ, max |a-b| 9.83e-06, max rel 1e-05, first at [1000, 0]
  units/n_cells    1 of 1 values differ, max |a-b| 1, max rel 1.01e-06, first at [0]
attributes: 25 in A, 27 in B; 24 identical, 1 differ
  @oversample      only in B: 101
ignored:    2 (-v lists them)
AuAu_0_10_jet_pth10-40_eta06_c1_0013_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5: DIFFERENT (3 differences)
```

Two runs of the same job never agree in everything: the wall times, the UUIDs that tie the files of a job together, the host name and the dates differ. `--ignore-stamps` skips these (`*wall_s*`, `*@*uuid*`, `*@prod_host`, `*@created`, `*@updated`). `--ignore PATTERN` skips more; a dataset is named by its path (`diag/wall_s`) and an attribute by `PATH@NAME` (`@nevents` for a file attribute). Large datasets are read in blocks, so evolution files of several GB need about 1 GB of memory. The script needs only h5py and numpy, plus hdf5plugin for Blosc-compressed files.

## Moving files: OSDF and Google Cloud Storage

| Script                                                                                                              | What it does                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`remote_transfer/js_osdf.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/remote_transfer/js_osdf.py) | `ls`, `du`, `download` and `upload` for the Pelican namespace `osdf:///fno4hic` (reading is public; writing needs a token) |
| [`remote_transfer/js_gcs.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/remote_transfer/js_gcs.py)   | the same commands for a Google Cloud Storage bucket                                                                        |
| [`upload_follow.py`](https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/utils/upload_follow.py)                     | uploads a campaign's finished jobs to the OSDF **while it runs**, and can delete the verified uploads locally              |

Both transfer scripts select files by kind (`--what pair|h5|root|all`), skip files that are already there, and check every transfer by size and CRC32C. Each one builds its own Python environment on first use; the Mac wheel's `xscape-osdf` and `xscape-upload-follow` use the wheel's environment instead. See [Data on the OSDF](https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/run/osdf/index.md).

# X-SCAPE changes since 2.1

The same table is in the X-SCAPE repository as [`RELEASE_NOTES.md`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/blob/contrib/RELEASE_NOTES.md).

Changes on the `contrib` branch ([`ef19d7f7`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/ef19d7f7), 2026-11-12) relative to the X-SCAPE 2.1 release (tag [`v2.1`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/tree/v2.1), 2026-03-05). The third-party packages X-SCAPE fetches (iSS, 3dMCGlauber, MUSIC, trento, the LBT tables) are included. MUSIC4GPU's own changes are not listed here; see [jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU](https://github.com/jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU).

Fixes to code that was added after 2.1 are folded into the feature that added it.

- [Physics bug fixes](#physics-bug-fixes): change the physics output of existing setups.
- [Technical bug fixes](#technical-bug-fixes): crashes, hangs, memory, build and log noise. The output is unchanged.
- [Enhancements and new features](#enhancements-and-new-features): new or opt-in. Unless a row says otherwise, the defaults reproduce 2.1.

## Physics bug fixes

| Component                     | Fix                                                                                                                                                                          | Effect in 2.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | PR / commit                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Liquefier                     | A free-streaming parton that the liquefier absorbs is marked as absorbed (status -11). Before, it kept status 0/1.                                                           | The parton was deposited in the medium and hadronized too. In two test jobs this double-counted 3% and 13% of the initial energy (issue [#156](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/issues/156)).                                                                    | [#154](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/154)                                                                          |
| Liquefier                     | Each droplet is normalized on MUSIC's grid. Droplets at the hard vertex are deposited.                                                                                       | MUSIC received 0.004 to 6 times a droplet's 4-momentum. 40% of 0-10% Au+Au events were off by more than 20%. Vertex droplets got eta = 0/0 = NaN and were never deposited. On by default; `<normalize_on_hydro_grid>0` restores the old source.                     | [#155](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/155)                                                                          |
| CausalLiquefier               | The causal diffusion is solved in the frame of the Bjorken flow at the droplet's eta_s (`<frame>bjorken`, the new default), not in the lab's Cartesian frame.                | Away from midrapidity the deposit landed closer to midrapidity than the droplet (by about 0.4 units at                                                                                                                                                              | eta_s                                                                                                                         |
| Liquefier / MUSIC wrapper     | The jet source's hydro dtau is set for every initial condition, not only without a pre-equilibrium module.                                                                   | With string or pre-equilibrium initial conditions the droplet source was evaluated about 2.6 times too often. The hadronic liquefier's dtau stayed -1, so every droplet was deposited at every step.                                                                | [#146](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/146)                                                                          |
| Energy loss / MUSIC wrapper   | `FluidDynamics::hydro_tau_0` and `hydro_tau_max` are initialized. MUSIC sets the energy-loss start time to its tau0, also when pre-equilibrium is kept in memory.            | Matter, LBT and AdS/CFT read the start time as 0 in practice, so `<tStart>` had no effect. **Behaviour change:** medium-modified energy loss now starts at the hydro tau0.                                                                                          | [#174](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/174)                                                                          |
| Matter                        | No qhat table lookup at a negative index (ISR partons start at t < 0).                                                                                                       | Garbage qhat values, results that changed between runs with the same seed, and segfaults (O+O with ISR).                                                                                                                                                            | [`8c975d37`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/8c975d37) ([#171](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/171))      |
| Colour tags (Matter, iMATTER) | Colour tags come from one counter per event.                                                                                                                                 | Matter's tags overlapped between showers: 85% of O+O events and 67-83% of pp Z+jet events had a tag used twice. Pythia joined colour lines across showers without a warning. Affects colour-aware hadronization only (iColored, Colored); kinematics are unchanged. | [#181](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/181)                                                                          |
| iColoredHadronization         | Holes and liquefier partons are no longer handed to Pythia as ordinary partons. The tag-pairing loop no longer reads past the end of its vector. `pythia.next()` is checked. | A failed fragmentation wrote the input partons out as hadrons. Now the event throws.                                                                                                                                                                                | [`ad1095be`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/ad1095be) ([#182](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/182))      |
| MUSIC wrapper                 | MUSIC's `reRunHydro` flag is reset for every event, with a warning when the grid edge is hit.                                                                                | After one event touched the transverse grid edge, every later event of that MUSIC instance stopped at its first freeze-out check, silently.                                                                                                                         | [`ca8dd84a`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/ca8dd84a) ([#141](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/141))      |
| MUSIC wrapper                 | `EOS_to_use` is written before MUSIC is constructed.                                                                                                                         | The first MUSIC instance in a process ran with whatever EOS the input file still held.                                                                                                                                                                              | [`a1753327`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/a1753327)                                                             |
| SurfaceFinder                 | The flow is built as u = gamma (1, v). Lattice cells are counted with `floor(L/d + 1e-4)`.                                                                                   | u.u was 1 - v^4 (13% short at v = 0.7). The last cell in tau, x, y and eta was dropped: on a 4x4x2 grid the surface covered 26 of 32 fm^2. HybridHadronization uses only ratios of u, so u did not change its output.                                               | [`88099402`](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/commit/88099402)                                                             |
| MUSIC (CPU)                   | Bulk Pi in the eta-direction flux: `W_eta_p` / `W_eta_m` take `Pi_p` / `Pi_m` (they were swapped).                                                                           | Wrong bulk-viscous contribution to the eta flux.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [MUSIC `9a304fb`](https://github.com/MUSIC-fluid/MUSIC/commit/9a304fb) ([#138](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/138)) |
| MUSIC (CPU)                   | Charge source terms (`turn_on_QS`) use the coordinate factor instead of tau. `CoorType` can be set from X-SCAPE.                                                             | Wrong charge sources in Cartesian mode; Cartesian mode could not be selected from X-SCAPE.                                                                                                                                                                          | [MUSIC `3bc760d`](https://github.com/MUSIC-fluid/MUSIC/commit/3bc760d) ([#138](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/138)) |

## Enhancements and new features

### Event generation

| Component    | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | PR                                                   |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| PythiaGun    | `<pTHatBins>`: several pTHat windows per run, each with its own Pythia, seed and cross section.                                                                                                                                              | [#152](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/152) |
| PythiaGun    | `<partonYMax>`: rapidity cut on the handed-over partons; the cross section is scaled by the acceptance.                                                                                                                                      | [#153](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/153) |
| PythiaGun    | Z+jet: `<trigger>Z` with lepton acceptance cuts, `<minPartons>`. Final-state leptons are handed over and pass through energy loss like photons.                                                                                              | [#173](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/173) |
| PythiaGun    | `<extraHard>`: the event's other hard scatterings, each with its own stream; minimum-bias mode.                                                                                                                                              | [#187](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/187) |
| ISR          | `<Hard><ISR>` in the XML task list builds the PythiaIsrMUSIC chain. `<JetHadronization><name>iColored`. PythiaIsrGun gets `<pTHatBins>`. The subtracted hard momentum is reported, with a warning for `Subtract_hard_momentum` other than 1. | [#164](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/164) |
| PythiaIsrGun | `<partonYMax>` / `<partonYMode>`: rapidity cut on the two hard partons.                                                                                                                                                                      | [#165](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/165) |
| PGun         | `<rapidity>` and `<phi>` of the parton (both 0 as before); `<points>`: several (pT, y) points in one run, event i takes point i mod K.                                                                                                       | [#189](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/189) |

### Energy loss and hadronization

| Component                          | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | PR                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Matter, LBT, iColoredHadronization | Colour flow: Matter's recoils and holes keep their colour flow, LBT partons carry colour tags, and iColoredHadronization closes colour lines that end in the medium (`<colour_closure>`, default `reconnect`). See `README_ColourFlow.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [#182](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/182)                                                       |
| Energy loss (Matter, LBT)          | `<Eloss><nThreads>`: the showers of an event run in parallel on OpenMP threads (N threads, or -1 for `OMP_NUM_THREADS`). Off by default (`0`, output unchanged). When on, every shower gets random streams and colour tags of its own and droplets are flushed in the serial order: the output does not depend on the thread count, but a seed gives other (equally valid) showers than with `0`. Runs serially, with a warning, unless all energy-loss modules declare support (Matter, LBT), showers run per event and there is no hadronic medium; ISR stays serial. O+O with ISR at 4 threads: energy loss 18 to 6.2 s per 40 events, jobs 13% faster; no gain in Au+Au jet jobs. | [#191](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/191)                                                       |
| Matter                             | `<tStart_at_point>`: apply the start-time cut at the point where it is used (default off).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [#183](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/183), [#184](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/184) |
| LBT                                | `LBT_TABLES_PATH` / XML: table location configurable. `LBT_TABLE_CACHE`: tables in one block, shared read-only between jobs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | [#130](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/130), [#163](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/163) |
| Hadronization                      | Reproducible re-hadronization: `SetNextRandomSeed` / `GetLastRandomSeed` for iSS and Colorless, `<reseed_per_event>` for Colorless and iColored, and iColored's `<store_input>` / `HadronizeInput`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | [#148](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/148), [#172](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/172) |
| Liquefier                          | Only droplets that can deposit in the current step are evaluated. When none can, MUSIC skips the jet source (output unchanged).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | [#141](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/141), [#144](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/144) |

| CausalLiquefier                    | `<frame>fluid`: the diffusion in the rest frame of the background fluid where the droplet was made (the droplet stores that cell's velocity and energy density). Opt-in; a droplet without a usable fluid takes the Bjorken frame.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [#189](https://github.com/JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE/pull/189)                                                       |
